articles.title: Preoperative imaging for localising hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands in primary hyperparathyroidism: An umbrella review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate preoperative localisation of hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands enables minimally invasive parathyroidectomy (MIP) in primary hyperparathyroidism (pHPT). This umbrella review summarises more than a decade of meta-analytic evidence on preoperative localisation imaging. METHODS: Twenty-eight systematic reviews (published 2012-2025) were identified through a PubMed search and assessed within a predefined inclusion period (2011-2026). The analysis covered ultrasonography (US), [99mTc]Tc-methoxyisobutylisonitrile ([99mTc]Tc-MIBI) scintigraphy with single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT), four-dimensional CT (4D-CT), and [11C]methionine and [18F]fluorocholine positron emission tomography/CT (PET/CT). Pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and detection rate (DR) were extracted, using histopathology and, where available, postoperative biochemical cure as reference standard. RESULTS: Pooled sensitivity/specificity was 80%/77% for US and 84%/87% for [99mTc]Tc-MIBI scintigraphy. Detection rates were 84-88% for SPECT/CT, 74% for SPECT alone, and 70% for planar scintigraphy. Multiphase CT achieved 73% per-quadrant and 81% per-side sensitivity; after negative or inconclusive scintigraphy, 4D-CT reached 71% sensitivity and 81% PPV. [11C]methionine PET/CT sensitivities ranged from 77 to 86%. Radiolabelled choline ([11C]choline and [18F]fluorocholine) PET performed best (pooled sensitivity 95%, PPV 97%, DR 91%). [18F]fluorocholine outperformed [99mTc]Tc-MIBI scintigraphy (96% vs. 54% per patient), [11C]methionine (92% vs. 80% per lesion, indirect comparison) and 4D-CT (92% vs. 85% per patient). In the largest choline meta-analysis (1,716 patients), pooled sensitivity was 93.8% and the surgical cure rate 92.8%. CONCLUSION: Among currently available techniques, [18F]fluorocholine PET/CT provides the highest diagnostic accuracy for preoperative localisation of hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands. It consistently surpasses conventional scintigraphy and 4D-CT in sensitivity while entailing lower radiation exposure.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Clinical value of 18F-FDG-PET/CT-detected immune-related adverse events in oncological immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can induce immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including subclinical inflammatory toxicities detectable by 18F-FDG PET/CT. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the organ distribution, diagnostic utility, and prognostic significance of PET-detected irAEs (PET-irAEs) in patients with cancer. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science and Embase was conducted through September 2026. Studies reporting on PET-detected irAEs and clinical outcomes in human participants treated with ICIs were included. Data were summarized via narrative synthesis. No formal meta-analysis was performed; organ-site events were aggregated descriptively by cancer type. RESULTS: PET-irAEs displayed cancer-specific organ profiles: bladder cancer showed thyroid (34%) and gastrointestinal (28.3%) enrichment; non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) was characterized by gastrointestinal (50%) and pulmonary (19.5%) involvement and melanoma exhibited a heterogeneous multisystem distribution. Evidence regarding the predictive and prognostic significance of PET-irAEs remains inconsistent. Although several studies have demonstrated associations between PET-irAEs and favorable treatment responses or survival outcomes, others have reported no statistically significant relationships. Interpretation of the available evidence is limited by small sample sizes, the lack of adjusted analyses, and susceptibility to selection bias, residual confounding, and time-dependent bias. CONCLUSION: 18F-FDG PET/CT shows promise as an important tool for the early detection and monitoring of immune-related toxicities. However, the utility of PET-irAEs as imaging biomarkers for predicting treatment response and prognosis requires further validation in large-scale prospective studies.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Yttrium-90 resin microsphere radioembolization for post-liver transplantation recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma: a dual-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Liver transplantation (LT) is an important treatment modality for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but recurrence after LT remains a major challenge with limited therapeutic options. Although yttrium-90 (Y-90) transarterial radioembolization (TARE) is now widely used for HCC, data on its efficacy in recurrent HCC after LT-particularly with resin microspheres-remain scarce. This study aimed to investigate the safety and efficacy of resin microsphere‑based TARE in patients with recurrent HCC following LT. METHODS: Consecutive patients with recurrent HCC after LT who underwent Y-90 TARE using resin microsphere between August 2022 and August 2026 at two Chinese centers were retrospectively enrolled. Tumor response was assessed using localized and overall modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST). The main outcomes assessed were overall survival (OS) from TARE; additional outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), adverse events (AEs), and prognostic factors. Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and univariate Cox proportional-hazards regression were used. RESULTS: Twelve patients (1 female, 11 males; median age 60.5 years) were included. At recurrence, 91.7% (11/12) had multifocal lesions, 75.0% (9/12) had bilobar involvement, and 41.7% (5/12) had extrahepatic metastasis. The best localized ORR was 50.0% (6/12; 95% CI 21.1-78.9%), with 1 patient (8.3%) achieving complete response (CR), 5 (41.7%) achieving partial response (PR), and 5 (41.7%) having stable disease (SD); 1 patient (8.3%) was not evaluable (NE). No grade 3-4 adverse events occurred within 1 month after TARE; grade 1-2 events occurred in 33.3% (4/12). Median OS and PFS following Y‑90 TARE were 10.0 months (95% CI, 5.0-12.0) and 5.7 months (95% CI, 1.8-6.8), respectively. Local responders (CR + PR) had longer OS than non-responders (SD + NE, 11.0 vs. 5.7 months; P = 0.032). Tumor absorbed dose ≥ 100 Gy was likewise associated with longer OS (11.0 vs. 5.7 months; P = 0.023). In exploratory univariate Cox regression analysis, local tumor response (HR = 0.20, 95% CI, 0.04‑1.02, P = 0.052) and higher tumor absorbed dose (HR = 0.10, 95% CI, 0.01-1.05, P = 0.055) showed borderline protective effects. CONCLUSION: Resin‑microsphere Y-90 TARE achieved favorable local tumor control with acceptable safety in patients with recurrent HCC after LT. Localized mRECIST-defined response and higher tumor absorbed dose were associated with improved survival. These exploratory findings require validation in larger multicenter cohorts.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: PET/CT radiomics integrating tumour and whole-body composition enhances prognostic prediction in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a multicentre study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate an integrated PET/CT‑based radiomic model that combines tumour characteristics and whole‑body composition features for predicting progression‑free survival (PFS) in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study included 477 patients with pathologically confirmed ESCC who underwent pretreatment [¹⁸F]FDG‑PET/CT. Patients were allocated to training (n = 294), internal validation (n = 74), and external validation (n = 109) cohorts. Primary tumours and whole‑body composition components, including skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, intermuscular adipose tissue and spine, were automatically segmented on PET/CT images. Radiomic features were extracted from both tumour and body‑composition regions. Feature selection and model development were performed using machine learning approaches. A composite clinical-tumour-body composition model was constructed and compared with clinical and tumour‑radiomic models. RESULTS: The integrated model showed superior prognostic performance over individual models, achieving C‑indices of 0.802 (95% CI: 0.770-0.832), 0.716 (95% CI: 0.639-0.797), and 0.732 (95% CI: 0.660-0.796) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The corresponding AUCs for 3‑year PFS prediction were 0.895 (95% CI: 0.858-0.930), 0.831 (95% CI: 0.727-0.923), and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.639-0.895). The model stratified patients into high‑ and low‑risk groups, with significantly different PFS between the two strata across all cohorts (log‑rank P < 0.05). Decision curve analysis supported the clinical utility of the integrated model. CONCLUSIONS: A PET/CT‑based radiomic model integrating clinical, tumour, and whole‑body composition features provides robust, externally validated postoperative prognostic stratification for ESCC. This approach may facilitate individualised risk assessment and inform treatment decision‑making.

articles.title: Role of MRI in Evaluating Lower Genitourinary Trauma: A Pictorial Review.
articles.abstract: Diagnosis and management of lower genitourinary trauma presents substantial challenges to the complex anatomy and functional diversity of the affected organs. Imaging plays a critical role in accurately assessing the injury location and severity, guiding clinical decisions, and improving patient outcomes. US, CT, and conventional urethrography and cystography are commonly used for the initial assessment of patients with lower genitourinary trauma. MRI, with its superior soft-tissue contrast resolution and direct multiplanar imaging capability, is invaluable in selected cases of lower genitourinary trauma. MRI has a complementary role in diagnosis of acute penile fractures and testicular injuries when US findings are inconclusive, as MRI effectively delineates the tunica albuginea of the corpora of the penis as well as the testicles. Disruption of the tunica albuginea is an indication for immediate surgical repair. Traumatic urethral injuries can lead to strictures and disruptions, which often necessitate delayed reconstructive surgery. MRI has an adjunctive role in conventional urethrography and provides detailed anatomic information about the urethra and periurethral structures such as urethral stumps, urethral gap length, periurethral fibrosis, displacement of the prostate and rectum, fistulas, false channels, fractures and avulsions of the corporal bodies, and fluid collections such as hematoma, urinoma, and abscess. Bladder rupture with surrounding fluid collection can be identified at MRI, although confirmatory CT or conventional cystography may be necessary. Furthermore, MRI with and without intravenous contrast material is helpful for diagnosis of suspected partial segmental thrombosis of the corpus cavernosum. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license. Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Role of Cryoablation in Breast Cancer: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer treatment has progressively evolved toward less invasive, more personalized therapeutic strategies that maintain oncologic efficacy while minimizing morbidity. Cryoablation, a percutaneous image-guided technique, has emerged as a promising alternative to surgery in selected patients with breast cancer. Initially explored in patients unfit for surgery or those declining operative management, cryoablation is now supported by growing evidence demonstrating favorable local control rates for older women with low-risk, early-stage breast cancer. Ongoing trials are further investigating these findings and evaluating whether cryoablation may exert immunomodulatory effects that enhance systemic antitumor immunity. If so, this may provide a rationale for combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and cancer vaccines. The authors examine the technical principles of cryoablation, summarize clinical outcomes from key studies, and explore its role in special populations including elderly patients and those declining surgery. Ongoing research will determine how cryoablation can be integrated into standard breast cancer treatment as part of a broader movement toward therapeutic de-escalation. ©RSNA, 2026 See the invited commentary by Mitchum and Ward in this issue.

articles.title: Imaging of Pediatric Pancreas Revisited: Spectrum of Diseases and Diagnostic Clues.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic disease in pediatric patients includes a diverse range of congenital, inflammatory, traumatic, and neoplastic conditions. In this article, the authors provide a comprehensive overview of the imaging features of a broad range of pancreatic diseases in children, highlighting the roles of conventional and advanced imaging techniques while addressing pediatric-specific challenges. A structured review of pediatric pancreatic abnormalities, including the findings of US, CT, MRI with MR cholangiopancreatography, and nuclear medicine studies is presented. In addition, the benefits and limitations of these diagnostic imaging methods, as well as the necessity of a tailored, multimodality imaging paradigm for accurate diagnosis and management of pediatric pancreatic disease, are outlined. Emerging quantitative imaging methods have recently enabled objective evaluation of the pancreas at the cellular and molecular levels by means of assessment of the parenchymal volume, fat fraction, tissue stiffness, and microvascular architecture. In addition, radiomics and artificial intelligence models may enhance diagnostic accuracy by extracting large volumes of quantitative data from medical images to characterize tissue dimensions, morphology, and tissue heterogeneity. The authors provide a comprehensive review of the imaging findings of the most common neoplastic and non-neoplastic pediatric pancreatic diseases and their mimics. Finally, they outline the most common pediatric pancreatic surgical procedures, expected postoperative changes, and potential postsurgical complications to facilitate communication between the surgeon and the radiologist.

articles.title: Prognostic performance of ATA 2015 and ATA 2025 risk stratification systems after radioactive iodine therapy in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The 2025 American Thyroid Association (ATA) guidelines introduced a four-tier risk stratification system replacing the previous three-tier classification. This study compared the performance of the ATA 2015 and ATA 2025 systems in predicting response after first radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 133 consecutive patients who underwent a first RAI therapy, with ≥ 6 months follow-up. Patients were classified according to both ATA 2015 and ATA 2025, adapted to histology. Consistent with ESTIMABL trial criteria, suppressed thyroglobulin (Tg) ≥ 1 ng/mL, structural/functional evidence of disease on imaging, additional surgery or further RAI for persistent disease were considered incomplete response; complete/excellent response was suppressed Tg < 1 ng/mL with no evidence of disease. Discriminative performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and net reclassification improvement (NRI). RESULTS: Median follow-up was 7 months (range 6-24). Incomplete response occurred in 11 patients (8.3%). Neither system showed a monotonic risk gradient (ATA 2015: low 7.1%, intermediate 10.2%, high 5.6%; ATA 2025: low 9.1%, low-intermediate 5.5%, intermediate-high 8.9%, high 13.6%). ATA 2025 showed a non-significantly higher AUC than ATA 2015 (0.582 vs. 0.513, difference 0.070, P = 0.074). NRI significantly favored ATA 2025 (+ 8.2%, P = 0.002), driven entirely by appropriate downgrading of 10 excellent-response patients to lower risk, with no reclassification benefit among patients with incomplete response. CONCLUSIONS: Reclassification analysis showed a significant benefit of ATA 2025 system as compared to ATA 2015 driven by appropriate downgrading of true excellent responders, reducing the risk of overtreatment. Validation in larger, prospective cohorts is needed to confirm whether ATA 2025 improves detection of true incomplete response.

articles.title: [211At]Astatine-based CD117-targeted radioimmunotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate astatine-211-based radioimmunotherapy (211At-RIT) targeting CD117, an antigen found on hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) and blasts on 60-90% of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), for anti-leukemia efficacy and facilitation of allogeneic HSPC engraftment. METHODS: A clinically exploited CD117 antibody (briquilimab [JSP191/AMG-191]) and the anti-mouse CD117 antibody, ACK2, were conjugated with isothiocyanatophenethyl-ureido-closo-decaborate(2-) and radiolabeled with 211At. Biodistribution of CD117 RIT was assessed in flank tumor models in immunodeficient mice. Anti-leukemic efficacy was evaluating in flank and disseminated tumor xenograft models in immunodeficient mice using parental and CD117-engineered human AML cell lines. Haploidentical HSPC engraftment after CD117 RIT was evaluated in immunocompetent mice. RESULTS: CD117 RIT accumulated in CD117+ AML flank tumors. In models with CD117high Kasumi-1 cells, CD117 RIT markedly prolonged survival of immunodeficient mice and, in some, provided apparent cure. Conversely, CD117 RIT was much less effective against CD117low THP-1 cells. Stepwise overexpression of CD117 on THP-1 cells improved the in vivo efficacy of CD117 RIT . Conversely, in our models, CD117 RIT failed to enable the engraftment of haploidentical HSPCs in immunocompetent mice, unlike CD45 RIT or high-dose total body irradiation. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate the anti-leukemic potential of 211At-CD117 RIT but suggest that its efficacy may be limited in cases of low target antigen expression. The latter may also account for its inability to facilitate allogeneic HSPC engraftment. Testing of agents with higher specific activity is necessary to examine how the usefulness of 211At-CD117 RIT can be extended to leukemias expressing lower levels of CD117.

articles.title: FAP-targeted 211At radiotherapy remodels the tumor microenvironment and is associated with enhanced anti-PD-L1 efficacy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)‑positive cancer‑associated fibroblasts contribute to immune exclusion and resistance to checkpoint blockade in the tumor microenvironment (TME). This study evaluated whether 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr, a FAP‑targeted alpha‑emitting radiopharmaceutical, could remodel the TME and enhance responsiveness to PD-L1 blockade. METHODS: Given the complex and immune-excluded microenvironment of lung cancer, we analyzed public datasets to define the clinical and immune context of FAP in this malignancy. 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr was synthesized and characterized for radiochemical purity, stability, FAP‑specific uptake, DNA damage, and PD‑L1 induction. Biodistribution, PET/CT imaging, therapeutic efficacy, histology, immune remodeling, and systemic cytokine profiles (MSD platform) were assessed in LLC/3T3‑FAP tumor‑bearing mice treated with saline, 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr, TPP-1 (a PD-L1-blocking peptide), or combination. RESULTS: FAP was enriched in stromal regions and correlated with advanced stage, reduced CD8⁺ T‑cell infiltration, and immunosuppressive signatures. 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr showed > 95% radiochemical purity, FAP‑dependent uptake, induced γ‑H2AX foci, and upregulated PD‑L1 in vitro. Tumor uptake peaked at 5.63 ± 0.72%ID/g (1 h) and remained 4.53 ± 2.13%ID/g at 24 h. Combination therapy exhibited the most potent tumor growth inhibition, reduced 18F‑FDG uptake, increased PD-L1-specific 68​Ga-TPP-1 uptake, decreased proliferation and angiogenesis, and enhanced CD8⁺ T‑cell infiltration and granzyme B expression. At the immunological level, MSD‑based cytokine analysis revealed that combination therapy induced more extensive alterations in systemic immune modulation than either monotherapy, whereas 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr alone shifted the profile toward pro‑inflammation. No overt organ histopathology or sustained body-weight loss was observed during the assessment period (8 days), while treatment-associated haematological changes (reduced WBC and RBC counts) were detected. CONCLUSION: In the engineered LLC/3T3-FAP model, 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr selectively targets FAP-rich tumor stroma, induces DNA damage and adaptive PD-L1 upregulation, and is associated with a shift of the immune-excluded TME toward a state that is more responsive to PD-L1 blockade. These findings suggest that FAP-targeted alpha radiotherapy may be a promising strategy for TME remodeling and immunotherapy sensitization in preclinical NSCLC models, and support further investigation toward clinical translation in more physiologically relevant systems.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Dual-energy CT for appendicular fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis vs conventional CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Computed tomography (CT) performs well in appendicular fracture detection, yet false-negative and false-positive results remain possible. This meta-analysis compares the performance of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) and CT in diagnosing appendicular fractures. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Included studies compared DECT and CT for appendicular fractures, with magnetic resonance or follow-up as reference. Two reviewers performed data extraction and assessed risk of bias. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated using binomial generalized linear mixed models, while subgroup analyses investigated technical and reader-related heterogeneity. RESULTS: Seven studies including 444 patients were analyzed. Pooled sensitivity was 93.5% (95% CI: 85.5-97.2) for DECT and 89.3% (95% CI: 80.2-94.5) for CT, while pooled specificity was 93.7% (95% CI: 79.8-98.2) and 94.6% (95% CI: 86.2-98.0). No statistically significant differences were found between DECT and CT in either sensitivity (p = 0.075) or specificity (p = 0.639). After excluding fast kV switching systems, DECT sensitivity and specificity increased to 96.5% (95% CI: 90.6-98.7%) and 96.0% (95% CI: 69.6-99.6%). In stress and non-displaced fractures, DECT sensitivity was 93.7% (95% CI: 89.2-95.4) and 93.5% (95% CI: 88.1-97.8), compared to 88.3% (95% CI: 82.8-92.6) and 87.7% of CT (95% CI: 80.2-92.5) CONCLUSION: DECT and CT demonstrated excellent accuracy for appendicular fractures, with overlapping confidence intervals for both pooled sensitivity and specificity. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested numerically higher sensitivity for dual-source and dual-layer systems and in stress and non-displaced fractures. KEY POINTS: Question Does DECT provide superior diagnostic accuracy compared to conventional CT in detecting appendicular fractures across different anatomical sites? Findings DECT showed higher sensitivity than CT for appendicular fractures, with performance improving when excluding fast kV switching systems and demonstrating the greatest advantage in stress and in non-displaced fractures. Clinical relevance DECT offers potential diagnostic advantages compared to convention CT in the evaluation of specific subgroups of patients with appendicular fractures.

National Trends and Projections in Utilization of Emergency Department CT and MRI Across Radiology Subspecialties.
articles.abstract: Background: Prior studies have documented increasing utilization of emergency department (ED) CT and MRI but have generally focused on restricted populations or on individual modalities, anatomic regions, or clinical indications. Purpose: To characterize temporal trends in utilization of CT and MRI across radiology subspecialties in U.S. EDs and to project future such utilization shifts. Methods: This retrospective study used deidentified aggregate EHR data from U.S. healthcare organizations participating in the Epic Cosmos platform. The platform was queried from 2016 to 2025 to identify annual counts for ED encounters and associated CT and MRI events, stratified by subspecialty, age group, and U.S. census region. Utilization was expressed per 100 ED encounters. Quasi-Poisson regression models were used to determine annual percentage change and to project utilization through 2030. Results: The analysis included 431,876,897 ED encounters during the study period. Utilization per 100 encounters for CT increased from 27.3 to 53.9 (annual percentage change, 7.4%), for MRI from 3.6 to 5.4 (4.3%) and for CT and MRI combined from 30.9 to 59.3 (7.1%). The proportion of ED encounters without CT or MRI decreased from 80.0% in 2016 to 66.8% in 2025. Utilization per 100 encounters increased for all subspecialties (6.2-9.1%), age groups (5.0-6.2%), and census regions (5.6-7.6%). Among subspecialties, the contribution to the absolute increase in utilization was greatest for neuroradiology (36.3%) and body imaging (29.0%). Assuming that the trend from 2016 through 2025 remained unchanged through 2030, utilization per 100 encounters was projected to increase further for CT to 78.4, for MRI to 6.7, and for CT and MRI combined to 84.8. In sensitivity analyses, projected utilization per 100 encounters for CT and MRI combined in 2030 was 85.5 when excluding calender years 2020 and 2021 (relating to the COVID-19 pandemic) and 80.6 when modeling based on only years 2022 through 2025. Conclusion: Per-encounter ED utilization of CT and MRI increased substantially from 2016 to 2025; the growth occurred broadly across subspecialties, age groups, and census regions. Clinical Impact: These findings may inform targeted workforce allocation, scanner capacity planning, workflow redesign, and imaging stewardship strategies, to help address evolving ED imaging demands.

articles.title: Prediction of PD-L1 status and characterization of tumor subtype in NSCLC with static and abbreviated dynamic LAFOV [18F]FDG PET.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to assess the potential of abbreviated dynamic [18F]FDG PET imaging using a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) scanner for non-invasive characterization of tumor subtypes and prediction of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) status in treatment-naïve patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: 51 treatment-naïve patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC (34 adenocarcinomas [LUAD], 17 squamous cell carcinomas [LUSC]) underwent a 20-min dynamic [18F]FDG PET/CT acquisition starting 45-min post-injection on an LAFOV system. Parametric images of net influx rate (Ki) and distribution volume (DV) were reconstructed using a direct Patlak approach with patient-specific scaled population-based input functions. PD-L1 tumor proportion score was determined from one histopathologically sampled lesion per patient. RESULTS: PD-L1 positive lesions demonstrated higher SUVmax (16.9 ± 9.6 vs. 11.6 ± 5.7; p = 0.04), Kimax (0.077 ± 0.04 vs. 0.054 ± 0.02; p = 0.03), and DVmax (428.7 ± 253.5 vs. 278.7 ± 145.2; p = 0.02) than PD-L1 negative lesions. LUSC lesions showed higher SUVmax (18.7 ± 8.5 vs. 12.9 ± 8.2; p = 0.008) and Kimax (0.08 ± 0.02 vs. 0.06 ± 0.04; p = 0.02) than LUAD lesions, whereas DVmax did not differ (p = 0.69). In the histopathology-matched LUAD analysis, apparent/optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.74/0.70 for SUVmax/Kimax, 0.71/0.67 for Kimax/DVmax, and 0.75/0.71 for SUVmax/SUVpeak, without evidence of superior discrimination by any model. CONCLUSION: PD-L1 prediction using both static and kinetic [18F]FDG PET parameters was feasible in NSCLC, with comparable performance between SUV- and parametric-based metrics, without evidence of superior discrimination by any model. These preliminary findings require validation in larger independent cohorts. Abbreviated dynamic LAFOV PET/CT enables whole-body assessment of tumor glucose kinetics in a clinically practical protocol.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Immune imaging of thyroid tissue with a 99mTc-labelled anti-PD-L1 nanobody: a first-in-human study with histopathological correlation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This first-in-human study investigated whether scintigraphy with a 99mTc-labelled KN035-derived anti-PD-L1 nanobody could visualise PD-L1-associated uptake in hypofunctional thyroid nodules and whether uptake patterns were related to the predominant PD-L1-positive cell population identified histopathologically. METHODS: Eight patients with scintigraphically hypofunctional thyroid nodules scheduled for thyroidectomy underwent planar scintigraphy and SPECT/CT after intravenous administration of the radiotracer. Tracer uptake was assessed visually and semi-quantitatively using L/T and L/B uptake ratios and was compared with postoperative histopathological findings and qualitative PD-L1 immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: Tracer administration was well tolerated. Intense focal uptake was observed in oncocytic thyroid tumours with predominant tumour-cell PD-L1 staining, whereas intermediate uptake occurred in lesions with predominant macrophage-like PD-L1-positive cells. Absent or minimal uptake was observed in lesions without identifiable PD-L1 staining. Diffuse thyroid uptake was observed in the patient with Hashimoto thyroiditis, with predominant lymphocyte-like PD-L1-positive inflammatory cells on histopathology. L/T uptake ratios differed across the three predefined histopathological categories (Kruskal-Wallis H = 6.25; P = 0.044), although this exploratory finding requires cautious interpretation given the very small group sizes. No diagnostic threshold or screening algorithm was derived from the observed uptake ratios. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory first-in-human study, 99mTc-labelled KN035-derived anti-PD-L1 nanobody scintigraphy was feasible and demonstrated distinct uptake patterns associated with different histopathological PD-L1 staining patterns. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further prospective investigation of PD-L1-targeted molecular imaging to assess the spatial and cellular distribution of PD-L1 in thyroid tissue.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Performance of a mammography-based deep learning risk model across breast cancer tumor phenotypes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Breast cancers have diverse biologic features associated with variable prognoses, treatment selection, and eligibility for targeted therapies. We evaluated the discriminatory performance of an image-only deep learning (DL) breast cancer risk model across diverse tumor phenotypes, including histologic subtypes, grades, molecular profiles, and disease stages. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, multisite study included consecutive women 30 years or older undergoing screening mammography across six sites from 2009 to 2022. A previously validated image-only DL model (Mirai) was used to generate risk scores from screening mammograms. Demographic data were retrieved from electronic health records, and cancers diagnosed within 1 year were identified through linkage to regional and state tumor registries. Discrimination across histologic subtypes, grades, molecular profiles, and stage was evaluated using areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs), with DeLong comparisons. RESULTS: Among 341,921 examinations in 104,472 patients (median age, 59 years [IQR, 51-68]), 1991 cancers were diagnosed, including 1543 (77.5%) invasive cancers and 448 (22.5%) ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). Discrimination was similar for invasive cancer (AUC 0.81; 95% CI: 0.80-0.82) and DCIS (AUC 0.81; 95% CI: 0.79-0.83; p = 0.88) and did not differ between invasive ductal and lobular carcinomas (AUC 0.81 vs 0.78; p = 0.08). Discrimination was robust across grades for both invasive cancer and DCIS (AUC range, 0.79-0.83), molecular profiles (AUC range, 0.77-0.88), and stages (AUC range, 0.71-0.82). CONCLUSION: Screening mammograms contain imaging biomarkers associated with diverse breast cancer phenotypes. An image-only DL risk model demonstrated robust discrimination across histologic subtypes, grades, molecular profiles, and disease stages. KEY POINTS: Question Does an image-only mammography-based deep learning breast cancer risk model (Mirai) demonstrate similar performance across breast cancers with different phenotypes? Findings In a multisite cohort of 341,921 screening mammograms, Mirai demonstrated similar discrimination across invasive cancer and ductal carcinoma in situ and maintained robust performance across histologic subtypes, tumor grades, molecular profiles, and stages at diagnosis (AUC range, 0.71-0.88). Clinical relevance A deep learning breast cancer risk model applied to screening mammography demonstrates robust discriminatory performance across cancers with diverse phenotypes, supporting risk-stratified screening and prevention strategies.

articles.title: Reperfusion status and clinical outcomes in patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion undergoing endovascular treatment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the association between reperfusion status assessed by expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade and clinical outcomes in patients with middle cerebral artery (MCA) M2 occlusion undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patient data were pooled from five randomized controlled trials and a cohort study. Patients with MCA M2 occlusion undergoing EVT were stratified into 3 groups (eTICI 0-2a, eTICI 2b-2c, and eTICI 3). The primary effectiveness outcome was modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score 0-2 at 90 days. Secondary effectiveness outcomes included 90-day mRS score 0-1, 0-3, and ordinal mRS score distribution. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) within 48 h. Multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were performed. RESULTS: Among 599 patients, 308 achieved eTICI 3 reperfusion. Compared with eTICI 0-2a, eTICI 3 was significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-2 in both the adjusted (aOR, 2.94; 95% CI, 1.54-5.60; p = 0.001) and the IPTW model (aOR, 3.49; 95% CI, 2.30-5.30; p < 0.001). eTICI 2b-2c was also associated with higher odds of 90-day mRS 0-2. Similar trends were observed for secondary effectiveness outcomes. After IPTW, eTICI 3 was associated with lower rates of mortality (p < 0.001) and sICH within 48 h (p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with MCA M2 occlusion undergoing EVT, eTICI 3 reperfusion was associated with better functional outcomes. However, the safety of achieving eTICI 3 reperfusion in this population needs further validation. KEY POINTS: Question How is the degree of reperfusion achieved after endovascular treatment associated with 90-day functional outcomes in patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion? Findings In 599 patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion, eTICI 3 was associated with functional independence, whereas associations with mortality and intracranial hemorrhage were less consistent across analytical models. Clinical relevance Among patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion undergoing endovascular treatment, eTICI 3 reperfusion was associated with better functional outcome. The association may inform postprocedural assessment, but the benefit of an additional attempt to achieve eTICI 3 reperfusion needs further study.

articles.title: A plaque heterogeneity score derived from high-resolution vessel wall imaging for identifying stroke-associated vulnerable carotid plaques.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To quantitatively characterize plaque heterogeneity using high-resolution vessel wall imaging (HR-VWI) and to investigate the value of this heterogeneity marker in identifying vulnerable carotid atherosclerotic plaques associated with stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 423 carotid plaques in 341 patients from three medical centers between June 2018 and June 2024 using contrast-enhanced T1-weighted HR-VWI. Plaque voxels were clustered via a Gaussian mixture model, and the spatial distribution patterns of subregions were integrated to compute the plaque heterogeneity score (PHS). A multivariable discriminative model was developed to identify stroke-associated plaques. An age-stratified analysis was further performed to assess the consistency of model performance across age subgroups. RESULTS: Plaques from Center 1 were divided into training (n = 168) and internal validation (n = 72) sets, while Centers 2 (n = 73) and 3 (n = 110) served as external validation cohorts. The integrated model (graphically represented as a nomogram) demonstrated excellent discriminative performance across all datasets, with areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.849-0.865. The model maintained robust discriminative accuracy across age subgroups, with a maximum intergroup AUC difference of 0.041. PHS showed significant incremental discriminative ability (ΔAUC: 0.080-0.112; IDI: 0.089-0.138; all p < 0.05) beyond conventional vulnerability and burden assessments. In external validation set 1, adding PHS to Plaque-RADS improved discrimination (ΔAUC: 0.134; IDI: 0.143; both p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: The PHS effectively quantifies carotid plaque heterogeneity and provides significant incremental value for identifying stroke-associated plaques when integrated with conventional metrics. This interpretable framework holds promise for future clinical translation. KEY POINTS: Question Current identification of stroke-associated carotid plaques relies on qualitative plaque assessment, which is operator-dependent and lacks quantitative measures of plaque heterogeneity. Findings The plaque heterogeneity score independently identified stroke-associated carotid plaques; combined with conventional metrics, it achieved areas under the curve of 0.849-0.865 across multicenter cohorts. Clinical relevance Integrating the plaque heterogeneity score with conventional assessment improves identification of stroke-associated vulnerable carotid plaques, supporting individualized risk stratification and timely preventive decisions in patients with carotid atherosclerosis.

articles.title: Extended MRI versus routine and expert ultrasound in suspected giant cell arteritis: a prospective head-to-head study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Imaging is central to diagnosing giant cell arteritis (GCA). Ultrasound (US) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are widely used, but prospective head-to-head comparisons are limited. OBJECTIVES: To compare extended MRI with routine US for suspected giant cell arteritis and to assess the influence of US expertise. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety-three consecutive patients with suspected GCA underwent US and MRI (median interval 0 days). US assessed the superficial temporal, carotid, subclavian and axillary arteries. MRI additionally evaluated the superficial occipital and vertebral arteries, the thoracic and suprarenal abdominal aorta, and the abdominal aorta. MRI was analyzed (1) restricted to the same vessels as US and (2) including all MRI-assessed vessels (MRI-all). Readers were blinded to clinical data. The reference standard was the final clinical diagnosis after 12 weeks. RESULTS: GCA was confirmed in 45/93 patients. MRI-all vessels showed higher sensitivity than routine US (80% vs. 44%, p < 0.001), with similar specificity (96% vs. 94%). MRI restricted to US-matched vessels also showed higher sensitivity (60% vs. 44%, p = 0.04). Expert US detected 12/15 cases (80%). MRI identified vasculitis in non-US-accessible territories in 9/45 patients (20%). Predictive values reflected the prevalence of the enriched fast-track. CONCLUSIONS: Extended MRI was more sensitive than routine US in this fast-track cohort, whereas expert US achieved comparable sensitivity. Ultrasound remains appropriate when expertise is available; MRI is useful for atypical, large-vessel, or inconclusive cases. KEY POINTS: Question In suspected giant cell arteritis, the diagnostic impact of extended MRI versus routine ultrasound, and the role of ultrasound expertise, remain uncertain. Findings Extended MRI had higher sensitivity than routine ultrasound, but expert ultrasound reached comparable sensitivity; both modalities maintained high overall specificity. Clinical relevance Ultrasound should remain the first line when local expertise is available, while MRI can support atypical, large-vessel, or inconclusive cases.

articles.title: Consistency of diagnostic-to-procedural lesion conspicuity in contrast-enhanced mammography-guided biopsy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether lesion conspicuity remains consistent between diagnostic and biopsy acquisitions in recombined-only lesions undergoing contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM)-guided biopsy, and to identify determinants of reduced procedural conspicuity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 169 consecutive recombined-only lesions undergoing CEM-guided biopsy between October 2019 and September 2025. Lesion conspicuity (LC) was assessed on diagnostic and projection-matched stereotactic scout recombined images using a three-level ordinal scale (low, moderate, or high). Reduced procedural conspicuity was defined as a decrease in LC category. Continuous perceptual variation was assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS). Associations between ordinal LC change (ΔLC) and median VAS were evaluated using Spearman correlation. Multivariable logistic regression using Firth's penalized likelihood method was performed to identify predictors of reduced conspicuity. RESULTS: Procedural LC was maintained or increased in 136/169 lesions (80.5%), whereas reduced conspicuity occurred in 33/169 lesions (19.5%). The same diagnostic and procedural LC category was observed in 111/169 lesions (65.7%). ΔLC correlated with median VAS (Spearman ρ = 0.665; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, non-mass enhancement morphology (adjusted OR 5.10, 95% CI: 1.94-14.06; p < 0.001) was independently associated with reduced conspicuity, whereas marked background parenchymal enhancement demonstrated a positive but statistically non-significant trend (adjusted OR 3.49, 95% CI: 0.97-12.55; p = 0.055). Technical variables were not independently associated. CONCLUSIONS: LC remained largely consistent between diagnostic and procedural acquisitions in most lesions undergoing CEM-guided biopsy. Reduced conspicuity was primarily associated with non-mass enhancement morphology rather than acquisition-related factors. KEY POINTS: Question Does LC remain consistent between diagnostic and biopsy acquisitions during CEM-guided biopsy, and which factors are associated with reduced procedural conspicuity? Findings LC remained stable or increased in most lesions undergoing CEM-guided biopsy, with reduced conspicuity primarily associated with non-mass enhancement morphology. Clinical relevance LC is generally preserved at the CEM-guided biopsy scout acquisition, supporting consistent procedural visualisation of recombined-only lesions.

articles.title: MRI assessment after posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: graft morphology and arthrofibrosis as imaging markers of knee stiffness and residual posterior laxity.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To identify postoperative MRI features associated with knee stiffness and residual posterior laxity in symptomatic patients after posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) reconstruction. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed postoperative knee MRI examinations in patients after PCL reconstruction. Two radiologists graded arthrofibrosis severity (none-mild-moderate-severe) and assessed graft morphology and tunnel positioning. In a subset, posterior translation was quantified on stress radiographs (> 8 mm = increased laxity). Associations between imaging findings and relevant knee stiffness requiring arthrolysis/manipulation under anesthesia or increased posterior laxity were analyzed using Firth's penalized logistic regression. Inter- and intrareader agreements were evaluated with Cohen's kappa (κ) and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). RESULTS: Fifty-three patients (mean age 33.1 ± 11.1 years, 15 females) were evaluated; stress radiographs were available for 43 (81.1%). Arthrofibrosis was present in 25 patients (total 47.1% [mild 26.4%; moderate 9.4%; severe 11.3%]), with nodular cyclops-like lesions in 35.8%. Seventeen patients (32.1%) required arthrolysis or manipulation under anesthesia. Higher arthrofibrosis grade was associated with an increased likelihood of secondary intervention for stiffness (OR 2.67; 95% CI: 1.45, 5.63; p < 0.01). An S-curved graft configuration (24.5%) was significantly associated with increased posterior laxity (OR 6.83; 95% CI: 1.71, 46.9; p < 0.01), but not with patient-reported subjective instability (p = 0.98). Inter- and intra-reader agreements were substantial to almost perfect (κ/ICC 0.71-0.98). CONCLUSION: Higher arthrofibrosis grades on postoperative MRI, including nodular cyclops-like lesions along the intercondylar PCL graft, are associated with clinically relevant stiffness requiring re-intervention. S-curved graft morphology correlates with objective residual posterior knee laxity on stress radiography. KEY POINTS: Question What postoperative MRI features after PCL reconstruction are associated with clinically relevant knee stiffness and residual posterior laxity in symptomatic patients? Findings Higher arthrofibrosis grades were linked to stiffness requiring arthrolysis or manipulation under anesthesia, while S-curved graft morphology correlated with residual posterior laxity on stress radiographs. Clinical relevance Postoperative MRI assessment of arthrofibrosis severity and graft morphology in symptomatic patients after PCL reconstruction revealed distinct imaging features associated with knee stiffness and residual posterior laxity, which may aid clinical evaluation and management.

articles.title: Semi-automated segmentation of 2D T1-defined black holes on 3D T1-weighted gradient-echo images in multiple sclerosis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a semi-automated method for segmenting 2DT1-weighted (T1w) spin-echo (SE)-defined black holes (BHs) on 3DT1w gradient-echo (GRE) images in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS), accounting for the increased sensitivity of the GRE protocol. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty-eight pwMS with 2DT1w SE, 3DT1w GRE, and 3D-FLAIR scans were selected from the Amsterdam MS cohort. A semi-automated 3DT1w BH method (3DBHSeg) was developed in an optimization set (n = 20) using cortical gray matter (cGM)-based intensity thresholding, optimized against manually segmented 2DT1w-defined BHs. Performance was evaluated in a validation set (n = 68) using a hybrid score, incorporating voxel-wise, lesion-wise, and volumetric agreement metrics. Associations between BH volume and EDSS score were assessed using adjusted linear regression models. RESULTS: The optimal threshold for BH segmentation was 0.95 × median(cGM) intensity. In the validation set, median BH volume was 1.54 mL (IQR: 0.80-2.57 mL) for 3DBHSeg and 1.24 mL (IQR: 0.65-2.47 mL) for the 2DT1w reference, with a hybrid score of 0.76, an ICC (absolute agreement) of 0.92 (95% CI [0.87-0.95]), and a mean DSC of 0.59 ± 0.10. The median BH/FLAIR lesion volume ratio was 24.3%. Log-transformed 3DBHSeg volume was associated with EDSS score (B = 0.33, p = 0.04), whereas FLAIR lesion volume was not (B = 0.19, p = 0.30). CONCLUSION: 3DBHSeg enables segmentation of BHs on heavily T1-weighted 3D GRE images in accordance with their definition on mildly T1-weighted 2D SE images, allowing quantification of severe tissue damage in MS. KEY POINTS: Question Black holes reflect areas of severe tissue damage in multiple sclerosis, yet no validated segmentation method exists for contemporary 3D T1-weighted gradient-echo acquisitions. Findings Our method, 3DBHSeg, segmented black holes on 3D T1-weighted images, achieving an ICC of 0.92 and DSC of 0.59 relative to a 2D T1-weighted reference. Clinical relevance 3DBHSeg enables identification of black holes, as originally defined on 2D T1-weighted images, directly on 3D gradient-echo acquisitions, allowing quantification of severe tissue damage associated with clinical disability in multiple sclerosis in the absence of 2D T1 images.

articles.title: Multicenter prospective study comparing ultra-low-dose CT, conventional radiography, and standard-dose CT for fracture detection in traumatology.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare the diagnostic performance of ultra-low-dose CT (ULD-CT) and conventional radiography (CR) for fracture detection in trauma patients, using standard-dose CT (STD-CT) as the reference. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study on diagnostic accuracy was conducted at five centers from October 2019 to September 2023 and included adult participants with suspected fractures of the extremities, pelvis/hip, or thoracolumbar spine. All participants underwent CR, ULD-CT, and STD-CT during the same visit. Blinded radiologists independently assessed fractures and associated abnormalities. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, radiation dose, image quality, and interpretation time were evaluated. RESULTS: Five hundred and thirty-three participants (mean age, 52 ± 22 years; 283 women) were evaluated, including 282 (53%) with fractures. For fracture detection, CR yielded 201 out of 282 true positives (sensitivity: 71% [65-76%]) and 81 out of 282 false negatives (29%), compared with 269 out of 282 true positives (sensitivity: 95% [92-98%]) and 13 out of 282 false negatives (5%) with ULD-CT (p < 0.01). Specificity was 242 out of 251 (96% [93-98%]) for CR and 245 out of 251 (98% [95-99%]) for ULD-CT (p = 0.58). ULD-CT showed higher sensitivity for both articular (154 of 171 (90%) vs. 93 of 171 (54%); p < 0.001) and soft-tissue abnormalities related to trauma (287 of 315 (91%) vs. 184 of 315 (58%); p < 0.001). Effective dose (E) was lower with ULD-CT than with STD-CT (p < 0.01) but higher than with CR, except for distal extremities (p = 0.33). CONCLUSION: ULD-CT demonstrated higher sensitivity than CR for fracture detection, with similar specificity, using standard-dose CT as the reference. KEY POINTS: Question Can ultra-low-dose CT (ULD-CT) improve detection of fractures and associated traumatic abnormalities compared with conventional radiography (CR) while maintaining high diagnostic confidence? Findings ULD-CT showed significantly higher sensitivity than CR for fractures, articular injuries, and soft-tissue abnormalities, with similar specificity. Clinical relevance ULD-CT increased diagnostic confidence and improved detection of fractures and associated traumatic abnormalities compared with CR, potentially reducing missed injuries and the need for additional imaging examinations despite slightly longer interpretation times.

articles.title: Independent evaluation of eight deep learning breast cancer detection algorithms as a second reader and for triage in a UK breast screening cohort.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To benchmark commercial breast cancer detection algorithms for standalone reading, paired reading, and triage in a UK cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Digital mammograms were retrospectively collected from two UK Breast Screening Programme sites (Cambridge and Norwich; 2017), excluding mammograms without two-view images, 3-year follow-up, or algorithm scores. Eight algorithms from five companies were assessed at single-reader specificity as a standalone reader or paired with the first human reader, and in low- and high-suspicion triage scenarios. The reference standard was histopathologically confirmed cancer (screen-detected, interval, or next-round). Performance metrics included AUC, sensitivity, specificity, recall rate, and arbitration rate; noninferiority was assessed at a 5% margin. RESULTS: Of 22,778 mammograms (median age: 59 years; IQR: 54-63), 294 were screen-detected, 151 were interval, and 209 were next-round cancers. AUCs ranged 0.82-0.91; one algorithm was inferior to all others (p < 0.001). As a standalone reader, four algorithms had noninferior sensitivity (range: 47.2-64.5%) versus single reading (62.9%). Paired with the first reader, sensitivities were 64.7-67.4% (all but one noninferior to double reading: 67.9%) and specificities 97.5% (all superior to double reading: 97.1%; all p < 0.001). Low-suspicion triage ruled out 37.4-65.7% of mammograms, missing ≤ 1.0% of screen-detected cancers; high-suspicion triage ruled in 3.6-12.2% of interval and next-round cancers. In combined triage, sensitivity (68.8-71.2%) was superior to double reading for five algorithms and noninferior for the remainder. CONCLUSIONS: Algorithms demonstrated variable standalone performance. When paired with a human reader, all but one were noninferior to double reading; in a combined triage workflow, all were noninferior and several had superior sensitivity. KEY POINTS: Question How do eight commercial deep learning algorithms from five vendors compare as standalone readers, paired with a single reader, and for triage in a UK breast screening cohort? Findings Most algorithms performed comparably and were noninferior in sensitivity to double reading when paired with a single reader, with one consistent underperformer; combined triage was noninferior or superior in sensitivity while maintaining specificity, at the cost of increased arbitration. Clinical relevance Commercial algorithms differ in performance, and newer versions are not necessarily better, supporting independent, head-to-head evaluation before prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Development and validation of a multimodal prediction model incorporating ultrasound-based deep learning and novel serum biomarkers for ovarian tumor diagnosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ovarian tumors are the most prevalent tumor types in the female reproductive system, with ovarian cancer being a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women. Ultrasound and serological tests are commonly used for detecting ovarian tumors in clinical diagnosis. The aims of this study were to utilize deep learning (DL) to extract features from ultrasound (US) images of ovarian tumors and establish an auxiliary diagnosis model based on these images. Additionally, proteomic analysis of the serum from different patient groups was conducted to identify new molecular markers. The combination of serum molecular markers and the DL diagnosis model based on US images was used to construct a new diagnosis and differential diagnosis system for ovarian tumors, providing novel approaches for the early screening and follow-up monitoring of ovarian tumors. METHODS: The imaging cohort included 916 patients (679 development and 237 test patients; 1319 ultrasound images obtained by transabdominal and transvaginal scanning). A separate cohort of 66 patients underwent targeted serum ELISA and multimodal assessment. Five independently seeded patient-level random training/test partitions were used for internal evaluation. The binary task included 53 benign or malignant patients, and the three-class task included all 66 patients. RESULTS: In the imaging study, the reported image-based test-set class-specific accuracies were 89.4%, 89.8%, and 91.3% for benign, borderline, and malignant tumors, respectively. In the serum cohort, five random held-out tests yielded binary mean patient-level accuracy of 66.2% ± 3.5% for DL and 83.1% ± 7.5% for clinical data + DL + LRRFIP1. Three-class mean accuracy was 62.1% ± 5.6% for DL and 66.5% ± 7.5% for the all-marker model. A separate patient-level ROC analysis gave binary AUC 0.883 (95% CI 0.783 to 0.964) for LRRFIP1 fusion and three-class macro-AUC 0.744 (0.655 to 0.831) for all-marker fusion. The accuracy and ROC analyses are reported separately. Recorded ROMA and IOTA decisions provided clinical-reference context for the binary task. CONCLUSION: The multimodal approach showed a higher binary held-out accuracy for LRRFIP1 fusion than for DL alone within the serum cohort. The smaller three-class accuracy difference was not accompanied by a macro-AUC improvement. These internal findings warrant confirmation in larger paired cohorts.

articles.title: Temporal changes in FAPI uptake in subcutaneous U87MG xenografts progression: implications for preclinical FAP-targeted imaging and therapy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Subcutaneous U87MG xenografts are widely employed for the evaluation of FAP-targeted radiopharmaceuticals, despite limited insight into the regulation of FAP expression. In this study, we investigated the temporal changes of FAP using longitudinal PET/CT imaging, biodistribution studies, autoradiography, immunohistochemistry, in vitro co-cultures, pharmacological and theranostic interventions. METHODS: Subcutaneous U87MG xenografts were longitudinally imaged using [68Ga]Ga-DATA5m.SA.FAPI and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2 PET/CT. Ex vivo biodistribution, autoradiography, and species-specific immunohistochemistry were performed across tumor development. Soluble FAP (sFAP) levels were quantified in plasma and conditioned media. Paracrine U87MG-fibroblast communication was investigated in normal and cancer-associated fibroblasts (NF and CAF) co-cultures with or without galunisertib or UAMC1110. The potential involvement of TGF-β signaling was examined in vivo using galunisertib, and exploratory radionuclide therapy was performed using [177Lu]Lu-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2. RESULTS: [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2 PET uptake increased from day 7 to 15 (3.2 ± 0.2 to 9.1 ± 0.9%ID/mL) followed by a decline at day 21 (6.7 ± 1.8%ID/mL). Ex vivo biodistribution supported this increase (13.5 ± 2.5 to 27.8 ± 1.3%IA/g) but showed only a modest decline by day 21 (24.3 ± 1.8%IA/g). Descriptive immunohistochemical analyses showed an apparent increase in human and murine FAP staining across the examined tumor specimens at early and intermediate time points. Galunisertib-treated mice showed numerically lower radiotracer uptake at day 15 (7.5 ± 1.6 vs. 10.5 ± 1.3%ID/mL) (p = 0.0652). In vitro, U87MG-fibroblast interactions induced fibroblast activation, with a 6-fold increase in FAP expression, up to 900-fold IL-6 upregulation and increased sFAP release (472 ± 149 pg/mL), while galunisertib treatment reduced these responses. Radionuclide therapy reduced tumor growth but did not abolish [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2 uptake at day 29. CONCLUSION: FAPI uptake varies as subcutaneous U87MG xenografts progress, and complementary biological analyses provide additional context for interpreting these changes. These results highlight the importance of tumor stage and biological context when evaluating FAP-targeted radiopharmaceuticals in this preclinical model.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Interim residual metabolic burden complements categorical PET assessment in a real-world cohort of PD-1-treated classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Immune-related response patterns may complicate interim FDG PET assessment in Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). We evaluated whether quantitative residual metabolic burden adds prognostic information beyond Lugano/LYRIC-based assessment during PD-1-based therapy. METHODS: This retrospective single-center landmark study included 63 patients with HL who underwent baseline and interim FDG PET/CT during PD-1-based therapy. Interim PET was categorized using a Lugano/LYRIC-based three-level classification. Interim total lesion glycolysis (TLG) was designated as the principal residual-burden metric, with interim metabolic tumor volume (MTV) evaluated as a closely related alternative volumetric measure. Landmark progression-free survival (PFS) was calculated from the interim PET date. Associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox models, incremental model performance, and sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Fifteen PFS events occurred during a median follow-up of 34.2 months. Categorical Lugano/LYRIC assessment, Deauville grouping, and percentage change in SUVmax were not statistically associated with PFS. Higher log-transformed interim TLG (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.97; 95% CI, 1.10-3.55; P = 0.023) and interim MTV (HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.14-3.04; P = 0.013) were associated with higher PFS event hazards. Among 54 patients without definite progression, PFS events occurred in 8 of 25 patients with high interim TLG and 3 of 29 with low interim TLG. Models incorporating quantitative residual burden yielded higher apparent and optimism-corrected C-index point estimates than categorical assessment alone, but internal performance estimates remained variable. CONCLUSION: Higher interim residual FDG-avid burden was associated with less favorable PFS and may complement categorical response assessment, particularly by revealing prognostic heterogeneity among patients without definite progression. The observed improvement in discrimination was exploratory and requires prospective multicenter validation.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in indeterminate renal masses and advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma: clinical utility and management impact in a real-world cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab is a PET radiotracer targeting carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX), a biomarker highly expressed in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Following the high diagnostic accuracy demonstrated in the phase III ZIRCON trial, this study evaluated the real-world clinical performance and management impact of [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in patients with indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Within an early access program, patients with renal lesions of uncertain origin underwent [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT for noninvasive lesion characterization, while patients with advanced ccRCC were imaged for postoperative assessment, recurrence evaluation, or metastatic restaging. Following intravenous administration of 37 MBq (± 10%) [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab, PET/CT was performed on day 5 post-injection. Findings were correlated with histopathology where available, and their impact on clinical management was assessed retrospectively. RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients (22 men, 6 women; mean age, 71 ± 9 years) were included: 18 with indeterminate renal masses (Group A) and 10 undergoing postoperative, metastatic, or restaging evaluation (Group B). In Group A, PET/CT demonstrated CAIX-positive findings in 10/18 patients (56%) and CAIX-negative findings in 7/18 (39%); one patient showed heterogeneous tracer uptake. Histopathological confirmation was available in 11/18 patients (61%). Within this verified subset, patient-level PET/CT findings were concordant with histopathology, with all CAIX-positive patients (6/6) confirmed as ccRCC and all CAIX-negative patients (5/5) confirmed as non-ccRCC or benign. At the lesion level, however, concordance was incomplete in one patient: four CAIX-avid lesions were identified, two of which were confirmed as ccRCC, while the remaining two corresponded to an angiomyolipoma and normal renal parenchyma. PET/CT findings were associated with a subsequent change in the documented management plan in 11/18 patients (61%; 95% CI, 35.7-82.7%). In the exploratory Group B cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT demonstrated the presence or absence of detectable CAIX-avid findings and contributed to therapeutic and surveillance decisions. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT showed concordance with histopathology in the limited verified subset and was associated with changes in clinical management, supporting further prospective evaluation in indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Development and preclinical evaluation of CP021, a CD38-targeted cyclic peptide radiotheranostic platform for multiple myeloma.
articles.abstract: Small and disseminated lesions within the bone marrow remain challenging to detect and eradicate in multiple myeloma (MM), highlighting the need for targeted approaches capable of both sensitive imaging and localized radiation delivery. CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells and represents an established target in MM, but CD38-directed radiopharmaceuticals with rapid tumor targeting and favorable pharmacokinetics remain limited. Here, we developed CP021, a high-affinity CD38-targeting cyclic peptide, and evaluated [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 for PET imaging, together with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 and [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 for targeted radionuclide therapy in preclinical MM models.MethodsDOTA-CP021 was labeled with ⁶⁸Ga or ¹⁷⁷Lu and DOTAM-CP021 with ²¹²Pb. Radiochemical properties, PET imaging, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, dosimetry, therapeutic efficacy, and safety were evaluated in MM xenograft models.ResultsAll radioconjugates showed > 95% radiochemical purity and good stability. [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 demonstrated CD38-dependent tumor uptake; at 60 min, uptake in CD38-high MOLP-8 xenografts was 12.35 ± 1.37%ID/g, 1.8- and 3.1-fold higher than in MM.1 S and U266B1 tumors, respectively. [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 produced activity-dependent tumor growth inhibition and prolonged survival. Repeated [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 further improved tumor control, extending median survival to 36.5 and 47 days at cumulative activities of 0.555 and 1.11 MBq, respectively, versus 16 days with PBS (P < 0.001). No overt treatment-related toxicity was observed.ConclusionCP021 provides a versatile CD38-targeted radiotheranostic platform combining rapid molecular imaging with β- and α-particle therapy. Its performance across radionuclides supports further development for detecting and treating CD38-positive MM lesions.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: First-in-human multiplexed PET demonstrated with two oncological indications: [18F]FDG/[68Ga]DOTATOC in neuroendocrine tumor and [18F]FDG/[18F]FCH in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Dual-tracer ¹⁸F-FDG and ¹⁸F-FAPI PET/CT in cardiac spindle cell sarcoma.
articles.abstract: A 33-year-old woman presented with long-standing abdominal distension and unexplained ascites. Serum CA125 levels were significantly elevated. Abdominal CT revealed a cystic lesion in the left adnexal region with massive ascites. To determine the etiology, 18F-FDG PET/CT was performed after fasting for at least 6 h. The adnexal lesion showed no appreciable FDG uptake, favoring a benign cystic lesion. Unexpectedly,​ heterogeneous hypermetabolism was found along the right heart border. Because the interpretation of cardiac FDG findings may be confounded by physiological or nonspecific myocardial uptake, ¹⁸F-FAPI PET/CT was subsequently performed for further characterization, which revealed a more extensive and conspicuous tracer uptake within the cardiac lesion than FDG PET/CT, more clearly delineating its extent. The patient subsequently underwent partial surgical resection of the cardiac mass with biopsy. Histomorphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings supported the diagnosis of cardiac spindle cell sarcoma with partial myofibroblastic differentiation. This case reports a rare primary cardiac spindle cell sarcoma and highlights the complementary value of FDG and FAPI PET/CT in evaluating primary cardiac malignancies. It also underscores the importance of multimodal imaging in guiding differential diagnosis and clinical management.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: An immunophenotype-guided interpretable subregional radiomics model for predicting local recurrence-free survival in esophageal squamous cell cancer patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to demonstrate tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) subtypes as prognostic factors for local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) and to develop an interpretable, TIME-guided subregional radiomics model for predicting LRFS. METHODS: 986 ESCC patients from three centers were enrolled. For a subset with available biopsies, multiplex immunofluorescence was used to assess CD3, CD8, and PD-L1 expression, defining prognostic TIME subtypes. Pre-treatment contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) images were used for tumor segmentation, intratumoral subregion partitioning and radiomic feature extraction. Features associated with TIME subtypes were selected to build a subregional radiomic signature (Subrad signature) for LRFS prediction using an advanced machine learning framework. This signature was integrated with clinical factors to construct a Clinic-Subregional radiomic model (CliSubrad-M). RESULTS: A "PD-L1-low/TILs-high" TIME subtype was identified as an independent favorable prognostic factor for LRFS (HR = 0.34, P < 0.001). The Subrad signature, comprising seven TIME-related features from various subregions, demonstrated robust predictive performance (C-indexes: 0.631-0.637). The integrated CliSubrad-M (built with Random Survival Forest) achieved the best performance, with C-indexes of 0.702 (training), 0.679 (internal testing), 0.653 (external testing1), and 0.625 (external testing2), significantly outperforming the clinical model (all P < 0.05). The model effectively stratified patients into distinct risk groups with significant differences in LRFS. SHAP analysis confirmed the signature's strong contribution and enhanced model interpretability. CONCLUSIONS: The developed interpretable subregional radiomics model, integrating TIME biology with clinical factors, provides a non-invasive tool for predicting LRFS in ESCC received dCRT.

articles.title: November/December 2026: Vision-Language Models for Axillary Lymph Nodes, Photon-Counting CT for Bladder Cancer, Emergency Department Neuroimaging Utilization, and More.
AI-Driven CT Analysis for Aortic Disease: A Task-Based Systematic Review of Segmentation, Measurement, and Detection Applications.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography (CTA) are central to assessing aortic aneurysm and dissection, but manual segmentation and geometric analysis remain time-consuming and operator-dependent, while evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) is fragmented. This task-based systematic review synthesised AI applications to CT/CTA of the thoracic and abdominal aorta by primary task: segmentation, measurement, or detection and classification. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC were searched from 2015 to September 2026 following PRISMA 2020; the protocol was registered retrospectively (INPLASY2026110004). Segmentation and measurement studies were appraised with CLAIM and detection studies with QUADAS-2/QUADAS-AI, and results were synthesised without meta-analysis. Results: Of 118 included studies (42 segmentation, 38 measurement, 38 detection), half were published since 2024. Median Dice similarity coefficient was 0.90 or higher for the outer wall, lumen and true and false lumina, but 0.86 for intraluminal thrombus and 0.63 for false lumen thrombus. Automated maximum diameter showed a median absolute bias of 0.26 mm (95% limits of agreement about ±5 mm). Detection of aortic dissection reached a median AUC of 0.96-0.97, mostly in enriched samples. External validation was reported in 14%, 34% and 55% of segmentation, measurement and detection studies, 33 of 38 detection studies were at high risk of bias, and only two systems were evaluated prospectively. Conclusions: AI supports technical automation of aortic CT/CTA segmentation and measurement and is progressing toward multistructure geometric phenotyping and clinical decision support, but independent multicentre validation, consecutive cohorts and prospective reader-in-the-loop studies are required before clinical integration. Detection/classification tools require independent diagnostic and workflow validation.

articles.title: Within-Device Exposure-Setting and Voxel-Size Changes in CBCT Alveolar Bone Measurement for Implant Planning: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This review examined whether within-device exposure-setting or nominal voxel-size changes in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) affect linear alveolar bone measurements for implant planning, separating accuracy from agreement. METHODS: Database-specific search strategies and retrieval counts are reported for PubMed/MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection. Study selection is presented in the updated PRISMA flow diagram. The reported International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) identifier is CRD420261361509. Studies were grouped by outcome, protocol contrast, and experimental model. The Quality Assessment Tool for In Vitro Studies (QUIN) appraisal was performed by one reviewer. A revision-stage source and analysis-unit audit led to withdrawal of the planned inverse-variance meta-analyses and their ±0.5 mm equivalence claims; structured study-level synthesis was used instead. RESULTS: Eight studies addressed linear measurements; two additional reports were retained only as methodological context. Seven linear-measurement studies compared protocols within a device, and one compared different devices. All were experimental. In one five-skull study, mean absolute errors were 0.50, 0.46, and 0.51 mm at 40, 20, and 7 s, respectively. A cadaver study reported mean absolute errors of approximately 1.10-1.20 mm. Small mean between-protocol differences sometimes coexisted with impaired anatomical visibility. Repeated observations were not equivalent to independent specimens, and several required sampling variances could not be reconstructed. CONCLUSIONS: Selected within-device protocol changes may preserve average measurements under controlled experimental conditions. The evidence does not establish statistical equivalence, interchangeability of protocol classes, or clinical safety near critical anatomy. Validation in living patients is needed before broad implementation.

Navigating equivocal PI-RADS category 3 prostate MRI with risk-based stratification.
articles.abstract: PI-RADS v2.1 category 3 on prostate MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) represents an intermediate risk category imaging phenotype rather than a uniform clinical risk category contributing to the dilemma in biopsy decision-making. Clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is found in a minority of PI-RADS 3 lesions, yet interobserver agreement is moderate and benign mimics, such as stromal BPH nodules and focal prostatitis are common, so a simple binary interpretation of biopsy versus no biopsy (biopsy avoidance) is inadequate. This review proposes a two-step approach. Step 1 is to confirm that the lesion is truly PI-RADS 3 by addressing image quality (PI-QUAL v2), interpretative variability, and overcall or undercall. Step 2 is to apply clinical risk stratification, in which PSA density (PSAD), treated as a continuum rather than a single cutoff is the most validated modifier, supplemented by biopsy history, PSA kinetics, family history and lesion-level imaging features. Selected low-risk patients can safely avoid immediate biopsy under a structured safety-net surveillance pathway, whereas patients with higher post-MRI risk should undergo targeted sampling with perilesional or systematic cores as appropriate. Population-specific baseline risk, including the higher csPCa prevalence and lower MRI negative predictive value reported in Black men, may alter pathway performance, although validated race-specific thresholds remain uncertain. Emerging tools, including serum and urine biomarkers, quantitative MRI and artificial intelligence, and PSMA PET with the PRIMARY score, may refine this pathway but require different levels of validation before routine use.

articles.title: Postmortem computed tomography findings in drowning: a systematic review of diagnostic usefulness.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Drowning is a challenging forensic diagnosis, and postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) is increasingly used as an adjunct. This systematic review synthesizes PMCT findings in drowning and evaluates the diagnostic usefulness of individual imaging signs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through July 2026 following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Original studies reporting PMCT findings in human drowning cases were included. A study-family approach was used to address cohort overlap, and quality was assessed using a modified Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Data were synthesized narratively (Synthesis Without Meta-analysis). RESULTS: Thirty-two studies (2007-2026) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing approximately 1400 drowning cases. Cohort overlap reduced unique individuals to approximately 900. Paranasal sinus fluid (88-100%) and pulmonary ground-glass opacity (89-100%) were the most frequent findings, but specificity varied with the comparator (0-100% and 0-38%). High-attenuation airway sediment and a three-layer stomach pattern were absent in controls in single studies, whereas frothy airway fluid also occurred in asphyxiation controls. Quantitative approaches showed inconsistent discriminatory ability. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based classification achieved high internal performance but markedly reduced accuracy on external validation. CONCLUSION: PMCT identifies a constellation of supportive findings, but no single sign has validated accuracy sufficient to establish drowning on its own. Discrimination depends on the comparator cause of death. A multi-parametric approach combining qualitative and quantitative assessment is promising, but its superiority over single findings remains unproven and requires external validation. KEY POINTS: Question Which postmortem CT findings are reproducibly reported in drowning, and which of them reliably distinguish drowning from other causes of death in forensic practice? Findings Across 32 studies, sinus fluid and ground-glass opacity were sensitive but non-specific, whereas airway sediment and a three-layer stomach pattern were specific but infrequent. Critical relevance statement Postmortem CT supports but cannot independently establish the diagnosis of drowning; this review gives radiologists a comparator-dependent hierarchy of signs to interpret findings within the autopsy-based investigation rather than relying on any single feature.

Non-Invasive Magnetic Resonance Imaging After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review of DTI-ALPS and Enlarged Perivascular Space Findings.
articles.abstract: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) may lead to a buildup of neurotoxic metabolites in the brain that require clearance by the glymphatic system.
