Non-invasive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methods such as the diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index and enlarged perivascular space (ePVS) quantification post-mTBI are being increasingly adopted despite an incomplete understanding of the biological limitations and methodological considerations of these techniques. To synthesize the current literature and identify knowledge gaps, a comprehensive search was performed using PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials. Human studies written in English between 2000 and 2025 were included, resulting in 18 studies in the final sample. Extracted data included: study design and population, number of participants, time from injury, MRI method, and results. PRISMA reporting guidelines for scoping reviews were followed. Included studies were heterogeneous in study design, choice of study population, time from injury to MRI scan, confounders controlled for, and study results. Decreases in the DTI-ALPS index were reported in studies including mixed injury severities and, in some studies limited to mTBI, while other mTBI-only studies reported increases or no change. ePVS findings were also heterogeneous, with studies reporting either no group differences or higher ePVS measures in injured participants. This scoping review identified three studies that included both DTI-ALPS index and ePVS quantification and determined that these measures may assess distinct biological processes. These results highlight the need for multiparametric, standardized MRI investigations of the glymphatic system post-mTBI.

articles.title: Radiomics and deep learning in locally advanced rectal cancer: linking imaging biology to response-adapted treatment.
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer produces a wide range of tumor responses, and total neoadjuvant therapy and watch-and-wait strategies have made response assessment a central task for radiologists. Morphological MRI criteria detect complete responders with limited sensitivity because fibrosis, edema, and small foci of residual tumor can overlap after treatment. Radiomics and deep learning extract quantitative features beyond qualitative visual assessment. This narrative review examines their biological correlates and reported performance along the treatment pathway. We discuss tumor cellularity, fibrosis, spatial heterogeneity, segmentation, feature extraction, multimodal fusion, baseline prediction, longitudinal assessment, restaging, and recurrence risk. Previously published meta-analyses report summary areas under the curve of approximately 0.85 for MRI-based prediction of pathological complete response; these estimates were not pooled in this review and reflect heterogeneous imaging time points, response definitions, and validation methods. Representative studies are critically appraised using domains drawn from radiomics quality and prediction-model reporting frameworks. Most evidence remains retrospective, and external performance is variable. Imaging heterogeneity, post-treatment segmentation, limited numbers of complete responders, and inconsistent reference standards restrict applicability. Models trained on conventional chemoradiotherapy require evaluation in total neoadjuvant therapy and immunotherapy cohorts, while watch-and-wait models require sustained clinical complete response and local regrowth endpoints. Prospective observational validation should be distinguished from evaluation of model-guided care. Radiomics and deep learning remain investigational decision-support tools whose translation requires independent validation, calibrated risk estimates, workflow integration, and prospective evidence of clinical benefit.

articles.title: Rapid Volumetric Shimming of the Lung in Free-Breathing.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a rapid, free-breathing, automated framework for volumetric lung shimming. THEORY AND METHODS: Seven volunteers were scanned at 0.55, 1.5, and 3 T. First, shimming was performed offline from volumetric B0 field information using a comprehensive set of axial, coronal, and sagittal magnitude and phase images acquired with a 2D echo-shifted gradient echo sequence. A combinatorial search for a sparse selection of slice positions was then performed to yield highly similar shim coefficients. For this sparse set, image post-processing and shimming were performed inline and evaluated on a complete rescan of all volunteers at all fields. Finally, the prospects of dedicated lung-shimming were evaluated at 1.5 T using extended TR regimes for balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP). RESULTS: From the volumetric scans, a fixed sparse selection, consisting of three coronal and two sagittal slice positions, was identified. The sparse set of slice selections resulted in no apparent differences in the shim field as compared to the full set, but data acquisition took only about 15 s (full set: 2-3 min) and shimming was completed in less than 1 min (full set: about 10 min). For all field strengths, shimming offered an increase of at least 30% in the upper limit of TR for artifact-free bSSFP MRI. CONCLUSION: Dedicated volumetric lung shimming is feasible and relaxes TR constraints for artifact-free bSSFP MRI. This offers new prospects for high-resolution imaging, lowering SAR, and reducing acoustic noise from low to high field strengths.

articles.title: Improved Precision of High b-Value In Vivo Cardiac Diffusion Tensor Imaging on a Commercial Ultrahigh Performance Gradient MRI System.
articles.abstract: Cardiac diffusion tensor imaging (cDTI) enables non-invasive assessment of myocardial microstructure, but clinical implementation remains limited by low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the prolonged echo times associated with higher diffusion weighting. Ultrahigh-performance gradients may enable higher b-values while maintaining clinically feasible acquisition times. This study compared cDTI precision at b = 500 and b = 1000 s/mm2 on a commercially available 3 T MRI system equipped with ultrahigh-performance gradients. Twenty healthy volunteers and six patients with cardiac amyloidosis (CA) underwent cDTI at b = 500 and b = 1000 s/mm2 using identical acquisition parameters except for diffusion encoding strength and echo time. Mean diffusivity (MD), fractional anisotropy (FA), and helix angle transmurality (HAT) were calculated. SNR, geometric distortion, and measurement uncertainty were also assessed using bootstrap analysis. Paired statistical comparisons were performed between diffusion weightings in healthy volunteers. In healthy volunteers, b = 1000 s/mm2 produced significantly lower MD (1.42 ± 0.05 vs. 1.51 ± 0.05 × 10-3 mm2/s, p < 0.001) and FA (0.30 ± 0.02 vs. 0.32 ± 0.01, p < 0.001) and greater HAT magnitude (-0.86 ± 0.14 vs. -0.75° ± 0.18°/% transmural depth, p < 0.01) compared with b = 500 s/mm2. Spatial variance was significantly reduced at b = 1000 s/mm2 for MD, FA, and HAT. Uncertainty was reduced for MD, FA, and the first eigenvector. In CA, MD was higher and FA and HAT magnitude were lower than in healthy volunteers at both b-values. In sum, b = 1000 s/mm2 cDTI demonstrated reduced spatial heterogeneity and lower measurement uncertainty compared with b = 500 s/mm2 despite reduced SNR. Higher diffusion weighting may therefore improve the precision and microstructural specificity of cardiac diffusion measurements.

articles.title: Baseline MRI-based prognostic stratification in T3 rectal cancer using the DISTANCED structured report.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic value of baseline MRI characteristics based on the DISTANCED structured report in patients with MRI-defined T3 (mrT3) rectal cancer. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 190 patients with mrT3 rectal cancer who received neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgical resection between December 2014 and June 2023, with a median follow-up of 43 months (range: 2-126 months). Baseline MRI features, clinical characteristics, and follow-up data were assessed. The patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 133) or a validation cohort (n = 57) in a 7:3 ratio. Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for disease-free survival (DFS), which were then used to construct a nomogram in the training cohort. The nomogram was independently validated using the validation cohort. Harrell's concordance index (C-index) and time-independent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were used to evaluate the model's discrimination. For patient stratification, the DFS rates of high- and low-risk patients were calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Baseline MRI-determined lateral lymph node (mrLLN) metastasis, circumference resection margin (mrCRM) involvement, and tumor deposits (mrTDs) were independent predictors of DFS. The nomogram exhibited good discrimination, with a C-index of 0.805 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.713-0.896) in the training cohort and 0.851 (95% CI: 0.743-0.959) in the validation cohort. The model also showed good predictive performance for DFS, with area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of 0.782, 0.764, and 0.814 at the 2-year, 3-year, and 5-year follow-ups, respectively, in the training set, and corresponding values of 0.792, 0.828 and 0.824 in the validation cohort. Our nomogram also divided patients into significantly different high- and low-risk groups. CONCLUSIONS: The assessment of mrLLN, mrCRM, and mrTDs should be employed for prognosis prediction in mrT3 rectal cancer to optimize preoperative risk stratification and personalized treatment.

articles.title: CIRSE Standards of Practice for the Endovascular Treatment of Pelvic Venous Disorders in Women.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelvic venous disorders are frequent, particularly in pre-menopausal multiparous women, but are an underdiagnosed cause of chronic pelvic pain because of the wide range of symptoms they cause. Endovascular treatments are effective, minimally invasive means of treatment. PURPOSE: This document, as with all CIRSE Standards of Practice documents, is not intended to impose a standard of clinical patient care but will recommend a reasonable approach to, and best practice for, performing procedures, in this instance, the endovascular management of patients with pelvic venous disorders. The document will address the underlying pathophysiology, patient preparation including imaging assessment, and the endovascular treatments and their outcomes. METHODS: The writing group was established by the CIRSE Standards of Practice Committee and consisted of five clinicians with internationally recognized expertise in the endovascular treatment of pelvic varices and a research assistant. The writing group reviewed the existing literature on endovascular treatments of pelvic venous disorders, performing a pragmatic evidence search using PubMed to search for publications in English and relating to human subjects published from 2010 to 2026. Relevant older primary sources were included where the data have not been updated. The final recommendations were formulated through consensus. CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapies for pelvic venous disorders are safe and effective, offering symptomatic relief for women suffering from pelvic venous disorders. This Standards of Practice document provides up-to-date recommendations for the performance of these procedures.

articles.title: Opportunistic identification of metabolic syndrome using abdominal CT-derived body composition: a comparative study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare the performance of abdominal CT-based body composition indices, novel simplified indices, traditional measures, and laboratory findings in identifying metabolic syndrome (MetS) under a definition that excludes waist circumference (WC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-center study enrolled 3089 adults between January 2020 and June 2025. Patients were classified into MetS and metabolically healthy groups according to the Guideline for the Prevention and Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes in China (2020 edition). Deep learning tools (TotalSegmentator and BOA) were used to quantify adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and bone at the third lumbar vertebra (L3) level. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were compared using DeLong tests. Subgroup analyses were performed by gender and BMI categories. RESULTS: In total, 3089 patients (median age 63 years [Q1-Q3, 55-71], 1481 men) were evaluated. Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) area at the L3 level had the highest AUC (0.723), outperforming WC (0.689) and BMI (0.605) (all p < 0.001). Its performance was comparable to a multivariable model (AUC 0.723 vs. 0.728, p = 0.067). In subgroup analyses, the VAT area achieved the highest AUC in the normal-weight group (0.745), the obese group (0.680), the male group (0.686), and the female group (0.722). Inflammatory markers, muscle, and bone had lower AUCs (0.55-0.63). CONCLUSIONS: The VAT area is the individual index with the highest discriminatory performance among those evaluated for identifying MetS, comparable to that of complex models. It may be measured opportunistically on routine abdominal CT, and may offer adjunctive value for normal-weight individuals. KEY POINTS: Question The value of quantitative body composition analysis in identifying metabolic syndrome (MetS) remains to be further clarified. Findings Under a waist circumference-free MetS definition, L3 visceral adipose tissue area outperformed novel simplified indices, traditional anthropometric measures, and laboratory biomarkers in total and subgroups. Critical relevance statement Routine abdominal CT can opportunistically measure visceral adipose tissue area at L3 as an adjunctive risk marker, and may aid in identifying MetS in normal-weight individuals, thereby providing guidance for lifestyle interventions.

articles.title: Quantitative and task-based performance of spectral deep learning reconstruction in low-dose dual-layer coronary CT angiography: A phantom study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is an established noninvasive test for coronary artery disease, but balancing image quality and radiation dose remains challenging. Dual-layer spectral CT (DLCT) enables reconstruction of virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) that enhance coronary artery contrast, but are inherently more sensitive to noise, making this trade-off especially critical. Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) improves image quality and enables radiation dose reduction in CCTA, but its performance on spectral reconstructions from dual-layer CT (DLCT) remains unexplored. PURPOSE: This phantom study compares spectral DLR at five different noise reduction strengths with hybrid-iterative reconstruction (hybrid-IR) at one fixed, clinically used noise reduction strength across conventional and VMI at multiple reduced dose levels. METHODS: An anthropomorphic thorax phantom with a coronary insert containing two calcifications (100 and 800 mg CaHA/mL) was scanned on a DLCT system at six dose levels (volumetric CT dose index 12.2-1.4 mGy) using a clinical sequential CCTA protocol. Data were reconstructed with one clinical hybrid-IR protocol, and DLR at five noise reduction strengths (Smoother, Smooth, Standard, Sharp, Sharper) for conventional images and VMI at 7 energy levels (40-70 keV). Image noise, luminal contrast-to-noise ratio (CNRlumen), noise power spectrum means frequency (NPSmean), task transfer function at 50% (TTF50), and detectability index (d') of coronary plaques were assessed. Statistical significance was inferred when 95% confidence intervals did not overlap. RESULTS: At full dose, DLR significantly reduced noise up to 64% in conventional images and 67% in 40 keV VMI, while increasing CNRlumen up to 300% and 230%, respectively, compared with hybrid-IR. DLR Standard, Sharp, and Sharper significantly increased NPSmean by 7%-13% for conventional images and 40 keV VMI, whereas DLR Smoother shifted noise toward lower frequencies, reducing NPSmean by 22%-32%. All DLR strengths significantly improved spatial resolution of calcified plaque, with TTF50 increasing 9%-29% relative to hybrid-IR. VMI at 40 keV with DLR significantly increased d' by 307% for high-density and 283% for low-density calcifications compared to conventional hybrid-IR. At 50% dose reduction, VMI at 40 keV with DLR Smooth improved CNRlumen (+ 46%), and TTF50 (+ 18%) and d' (+ 24%) of the high-density calcification relative to full-dose hybrid-IR 40 keV VMI, whereas confidence intervals overlapped for NPSmean and for TTF50 and d' of the low-density calcification. CONCLUSIONS: On dual-layer CT, spectral DLR outperforms hybrid-IR on both conventional and VMI images in noise, CNR, spatial resolution, and plaque detectability. At 50% dose reduction, DLR Smooth on 40 keV VMI exceeded full-dose hybrid-IR on 40 keV VMI in CNR, and in spatial resolution and detectability of high-density calcifications, with overlapping confidence intervals for noise texture and for low-density calcifications. Patient studies are needed to validate clinical translation.

articles.title: Range and the Radiologist: What Generalism Can Teach Us About Training for an Uncertain Future.
articles.abstract: Radiology training is increasingly shaped by subspecialization, yet more than half of U.S. radiologists still practice predominantly as generalists. David Epstein's Range: Why Generalists Triumph in a Specialized World argues that in complex, unpredictable domains, breadth of experience and analogical thinking produce more adaptable professionals than early, narrow expertise. Although Range has not been explicitly cited in the radiology literature, its thesis maps directly onto tensions the specialty is actively confronting: the generalist-subspecialist workforce balance, the cognitive vulnerabilities introduced by narrow expertise, and the structure of residency education. This perspective connects Epstein's framework to the radiology cognitive bias literature, workforce data, and educational research to argue that preserving cognitive breadth in training is not a concession to generalism but a prerequisite for effective subspecialization. Implications for curriculum design, interdisciplinary education, training environments, debiasing strategies, the clinical year, and generalist foundations are discussed.

articles.title: A Study in Contrasts: A Head-to-Head Comparison of MRI Contrast Phases for Deep Learning Liver Segmentation.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the optimal MRI contrast phase(s) for automated liver segmentation using single-phase and multiphase deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) employing both early- and late-fusion techniques. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 586 hepatocellular carcinoma patients with multi-phasic contrast-enhanced MRI from an institutional database. DCNNs were trained using identical 3D U-Net-derived architectures on single phases and all possible multi-phasic combinations, with early- and late-fusion techniques, resulting in a total of 26 models. The dataset was randomly split into 70/15/15% for training/validation/testing, and performance was quantified by the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC). From a collaborating site, 16 scans were used for external testing. The public LiverHccSeg dataset (n = 17) was used for additional testing. Furthermore, co-registered multiphasic examinations from the public Duke Liver Dataset (DLDS) were used as a third external test set (n = 68). Friedman's test with Dunn-Bonferroni post-hoc tests were used to compare performance across models. The top-performing model of each fusion strategy was defined by the highest Friedman mean rank. RESULTS: The late-fusion DCNN combining arterial, portal-venous, and delayed-phase MRI achieved superior performance across all models in the internal test set (mean DSC: 0.971 ± 0.021, P <.001 for all pairwise comparisons). The best single-phase DCNN used portal-venous phase (mean DSC: 0.970 ± 0.017) and significantly outperformed the best early-fusion DCNN based on a combination of portal-venous-, and delayed phase (mean DSC: 0.966 ± 0.036) (P < .001). The developed DCNNs demonstrated generalizable performance to external data (late-fusion: 0.961 ± 0.014, early-fusion: 0.964 ± 0.009, single-phase: 0.956 ± 0.035), the public LiverHccSeg (late-fusion: 0.911 ± 0.070, early-fusion: 0.898 ± 0.112, single-phase: 0.889 ± 0.109), and DLDS data (late-fusion: 0.907 ± 0.120, early-fusion: 0.873 ± 0.200, single-phase: 0.898 ± 0.134). CONCLUSION: Optimal deep learning liver segmentation performance was achieved through late-fusion of arterial, portal-venous, and delayed-phase MRI and demonstrated generalizable performance to external data. Single-phase segmentation on portal-venous phase remained a computationally efficient alternative with satisfactory performance. The numerical gain from multiphase late fusion was small in terms of mean DSC and was most apparent as reduced variability and improved worst-case performance on external data.

articles.title: Linking Theory of Mind and Cardiac Vagal Regulation: the Integrative Role of the Posterior Cerebellum.
articles.abstract: Interpersonal interactions are fundamentally regulated by Social Cognition, a multifaceted construct encompassing the cognitive and neural processes used to navigate the social environment. Within this overarching architecture, Theory of Mind (ToM), or mentalizing, provides a foundational dual-level framework of implicit and explicit systems. Although these functions traditionally rely on a cortical mentalizing network, recent findings support a cerebellar contribution to ToM processes. Given that the cerebellar computational architecture is suited for the rapid, automated processing of visual social cues, investigating lower-level social decoding offers a unique window into the cerebellar contribution to ToM. Building on this framework, the present research explored the relation between cerebellar morphometry and lower-level ToM in healthy subjects. Participants underwent MRI to assess cerebellar Gray Matter volumes and completed the computerized version of the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET). Since the lower-level mentalizing is closely tied to complex interactions between the Central and Autonomic Nervous Systems (ANS), the present study also examined the relationships between cerebellar volumes and Heart Rate Variability, namely the variations of Root Mean Square of Successive Differences (RMSSD) values across the RMET procedure. Findings revealed that volumes of cerebellar lobules VI, VIIb, Crus II, and vermis IX predicted the RMET accuracy. Furthermore, the volume of vermis IX selectively predicted RMSSD variation during the rest-recovery transition, with smaller vermis IX volumes associated with a sharper, more progressive RMSSD decline. Overall, these data highlight that posterior cerebellar morphometry is associated with RMET performance and cardiac vagal regulation, thus supporting lower-level mentalizing.

articles.title: Insomnia reorganizes large-scale functional connectivity abnormalities in depression: Evidence from functional gradients and neurotransmitter mapping.
articles.abstract: Sleep disorders are one of the most prevalent and clinically important features of depression, yet their impact on the large-scale organization of brain functional abnormalities remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether insomnia reshapes whole-brain resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) abnormalities in depression and alter their hierarchical and neurochemical organization. Resting-state fMRI data were acquired from depressed patients with (INS, n = 32) and without insomnia symptoms (NINS, n = 24), and healthy controls (HC, n = 45). Network-based statistics (NBS) was used to identify altered RSFC subnetworks. We then examined the hierarchical distribution of network abnormalities using the principal functional gradient, assessed clinical relevance, and evaluated their spatial correspondence with neurotransmitter atlas. Results showed that the INS group exhibited more widespread functional connectivity impairments, primarily concentrated in the visual and sensorimotor networks. Moreover, these abnormal connections showed a hierarchical distribution pattern along the principal functional gradient, with lower-level sensory systems more affected than higher-level cognitive networks. Significant differences in node degree were observed in the visual network, and functional connectivity within this network was associated with anxiety scores in the INS group. Spatial similarity analyses revealed overlapping but distinct neurotransmitter profiles across groups, with shared correlations for mGluR5 and stronger μ-opioid-related associations in the INS group. These findings suggest that insomnia symptoms in depression are associated not simply with more severe dysfunction, but with a reorganization of large-scale functional abnormalities toward lower-order sensory systems, characterized by a gradient-dependent connectivity distribution and altered associations with specific neurotransmitter systems, particularly μ-opioid receptors.

articles.title: Neurocomputational Mechanisms Underlying Differential Framing Effects on Generosity and Honesty.
articles.abstract: The framing effect, a robust cognitive bias, demonstrates that human decision-making is influenced by whether outcomes are presented as gains or losses. Nevertheless, substantial debate remains regarding the extent to which loss frames facilitate or inhibit prosocial behaviors, and the neurocognitive processes through which frames drive these divergent effects remain poorly understood. We combined behavioral analyses, computational modeling, and brain imaging to dissect the neurocognitive substrates underpinning framing effects on two distinct forms of prosociality: generosity and honesty. Fifty-three healthy adult participants completed both the Dictator Game (DG), which primarily captures generosity-related considerations, and the Message Game (MG), which involves honesty-related considerations, allowing us to examine how gain versus loss frames affect choices across these two prosocial decision contexts. Behavioral analyses revealed a significant game type × frame interaction, while computational modeling further identified opposite frame-related changes in the generosity-related parameter β and the honesty-related parameter δ, together revealing differential framing effects across prosocial domains. At the neural level, activations in the amygdala and ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) were modulated by frame and game type: both regions showed greater activation for DG in the gain frame and MG in the loss frame than for DG in the loss frame and MG in the gain frame. Moreover, functional coupling between the vmPFC and temporoparietal junction (TPJ) exhibited an interaction effect consistent with the regional activation pattern, while amygdala and TPJ coupling showed a similar interaction trend. Collectively, these findings suggest the involvement of an amygdala-TPJ-vmPFC circuit in framing-related decision-making, with the TPJ potentially participating in interactions between affective and value-related processes that may contribute to differential framing effects on generosity and honesty.

articles.title: Unraveling the interplay between sensory information and semantic architecture in brain concept representation: the role of abstraction.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Understanding how abstract and concrete words are represented in the brain requires disentangling the contribution of sensorimotor information from the organization of semantic knowledge. These dimensions, here referred to as abstractness and abstraction, respectively, are typically confounded, limiting our ability to identify their distinct neural correlates. OBJECTIVES: The present study aimed to dissociate the roles of abstractness and abstraction in word processing by introducing superordinate words as a critical comparison category. METHODS: Behavioral norming and feature production tasks were used to quantify sensory-related properties and semantic architecture, operationalized in terms of generalizability, feature relevance, and representational specificity. These measures informed computational models capturing abstractness, abstraction, sensorimotor content, and distributional similarity. Neural data were acquired using electroencephalography and analyzed with representational similarity analysis to assess model-brain correspondence over time. RESULTS: Behaviorally, superordinate words patterned with concrete words on sensory properties but with abstract words on measures of semantic architecture. In the electrophysiological data, concrete words elicited stronger negativities than both abstract and superordinate words in the N400 and N700 time windows, whereas the contrast between abstract and superordinate words did not reach significance. Representational similarity analysis revealed that, among the models tested, the abstraction model was significantly associated with the neural response patterns in the N400 and N700 latencies, whereas models based on abstractness, sensorimotor or distributional information did not reach the significance threshold. CONCLUSION: Within the participants and stimuli tested, these results indicate that semantic architecture provides a useful framework for understanding the neural dynamics of word processing, alongside sensorimotor grounding. They suggest that abstraction may play a central role in structuring conceptual representations, providing a unifying account that bridges embodied and formal theories of semantic representation.

articles.title: Differential priors guided adaptive multi-scale edge-guided attention for medical image synthesis with stable diffusion.
articles.abstract: AbstractObjective. Diffusion models pretrained on natural images provide a useful basis for medical image synthesis, but preserving lesion structure remains challenging when annotated data are limited. We aim to improve the quality and segmentation utility of mask-conditioned synthetic images.Approach. We propose a structure-aware fine-tuning framework based on Stable Diffusion and ControlNet. Adaptive Multi-scale Edge-Guided Attention (AMEGA)integrates first-order Sobel and second-order Laplacian responses with multi-scale features. A complementary training objective combines foreground and background supervision with adaptive boundary regularization to encourage structural consistency during generation. Main results. Experiments on BMRI, ISIC2016, and Kvasir-SEG evaluate image quality and downstream segmentation. Compared with mask-conditioned SD+ControlNet, the framework reduces dataset-averaged FID by 18.2% and improves mean downstream Dice from 0 . 711 to 0 .736.Significance. Integrating differential features and boundary-aware supervision improves medical image synthesis and supports synthetic-data augmentation under limited annotations.

articles.title: Spectral analysis of dynamic long-axial-field-of-view PET studies: a flexible framework for whole-body multi-organ kinetic quantification.
articles.abstract: Although long-axial-field-of-view (LAFOV) PET systems are increasingly installed worldwide, quantitative analysis of dynamic LAFOV PET remains largely based on compartmental models or graphical methods. This study systematically evaluates and adapts spectral analysis (SA) as a flexible, data-driven framework for multi-organ kinetic quantification. Approach.SA represents the tissue impulse response function as a non-negative combination of exponential components without requiring a predefined compartmental structure. Four implementations were investigated: standard SA, SA with tracer arrival delay correction (SA*), spectral analysis with iterative filter (SAIF), and SAIF with delay correction (SAIF*). The methods were evaluated at both volume of interest (VOI) and voxel levels using dynamic 18F-FDG PET/CT data from 24 cancer patients, including 40 tumor lesions. Main results. Delay correction improved early-phase time activity curve (TAC) fitting and reduced Akaike information criterion (AIC) values across most organs. SA* achieved comparable or better fitting performance than two-tissue compartmental model with delay correction (2C*) in several regions without requiring a predefined compartmental structure. Kinetic parameter estimates showed the highest consistency for Ki, while K1, VT, and vascular contributions exhibited greater method-dependent variability. The resulting spectra revealed distinct kinetic patterns across normal organs and individual tumors. At the voxel level, SA* generated acceptable parametric images without iterative filtering, while SAIF* provided additional signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvements, particularly in some tumor regions.Significance. This first systematic evaluation demonstrates the potential of SA for multi-organ kinetic quantification with dynamic LAFOV PET. Its flexible kinetic representation may be particularly valuable for investigating novel diagnostic and theranostic radiotracers whose whole-body kinetic behavior is not yet fully characterized.

articles.title: A CTA-Based model integrating the rim sign and quantitative plaque features for identification of carotid intraplaque hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate identification of carotid intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH), a key marker of plaque vulnerability, remains challenging on computed tomography angiography (CTA). We aimed to identify CTA-derived features associated with IPH and develop a CTA-based diagnostic model using high-resolution vessel wall imaging (HR-VWI) as the reference standard. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, 469 patients with 1,196 carotid plaques who underwent CTA and HR-VWI within 1 month were enrolled. IPH was defined on HR-VWI. Qualitative CTA features, including the rim sign, and quantitative plaque characteristics derived from artificial intelligence-assisted CTA analysis were assessed. Independent predictors of IPH were identified using multivariable logistic regression. A diagnostic model was developed in a training cohort, and validated internally and externally. RESULTS: IPH was present in 277 of 1,196 plaques (23.2 %). The rim sign (OR, 13.7; 95 % CI, 6.4-29.4), fibro-lipid volume (OR, 1.5; 95 % CI, 1.2-2), and luminal stenosis (OR, 2.2; 95 % CI, 1.6-2.9) were independently associated with IPH (all P < 0.001). Luminal stenosis and fibro-lipid volume showed the highest discriminative performance (AUCs, 0.741 and 0.735), while the rim sign demonstrated high specificity (97.9 %). The combined CTA model achieved AUCs of 0.794, 0.829, and 0.803 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The rim sign, fibro-lipid volume, and luminal stenosis are independent CTA predictors of carotid IPH. Integrating qualitative CTA markers with AI-derived quantitative plaque features enables accurate, noninvasive identification of IPH and may improve CTA-based assessment of carotid plaque vulnerability.

articles.title: Training in primary rectal cancer MRI staging among radiology residents: a multicenter survey study from Romania.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterize radiology residents' training experience and reporting practices in rectal MRI staging in Romania, an Eastern European training environment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicenter, cross-sectional survey with nationwide dissemination was conducted in late 2025. A pretested questionnaire developed by a three-member panel was distributed through the Romanian Society of Radiology and Medical Imaging and residency coordinators. Items addressed demographics, rectal MRI exposure, self-assessed difficulty and confidence, practice context, learning methods, and structured reporting. Spearman's rank correlation assessed the association between residency year and self-reported rectal MRI exposure. RESULTS: Of 160 respondents (estimated survey uptake: 16.0%, 24.7%, or 23.4%, depending on denominator), 142 with prior general MRI experience formed the main analytic cohort. Higher residency year was associated with greater reported rectal MRI exposure (Spearman's rho = 0.527, p < 0.001), although exposure remained limited: approximately 70% of fifth-year residents reported ≤ 30 cases. Confidence was lowest for T4a and EMVI. Practice-context barriers included limited case volume (33.1%) and restricted resident involvement in interpretation (9.2-11.3%). Internet-based platforms (90.1%) and peer-to-peer learning (57.7%) were the dominant learning methods; only 10.6% attended dedicated workshops. Local training activities were rated useful or very useful by 87.3% of respondents. Prior use of structured reporting for rectal MRI was reported by 21.8%. CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter survey suggests a potential training gap in rectal MRI staging during radiology residency in Romania. Reported exposure remained limited even in later residency years, learning was predominantly self-directed, and a minority of respondents reported prior use of structured reporting. KEY POINTS: Question Rectal MRI staging is complex and clinically important, but residents' actual exposure, learning pathways, and structured reporting use during training remain poorly described. Findings A Romanian multicenter survey identified limited rectal MRI exposure, variable confidence across staging tasks, and prior structured reporting use among 21.8% of respondents. Critical relevance statement Identifying limited resident exposure, self-directed learning, and limited prior use of structured reporting supports targeted residency training and more consistent rectal MRI staging practice.

articles.title: Associations of paraspinal muscle proton density fat fraction and T2 mapping with low back pain and lumbar structural degeneration.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate paraspinal muscle degeneration using proton density fat fraction (PDFF) and T2 mapping and to investigate their associations with degenerative spine features and clinical outcomes in low back pain (LBP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospectively recruited cross-sectional study included 86 participants with LBP and 86 controls who underwent q-Dixon and T2 mapping at L4/5. PDFF and T2 values were measured in the multifidus (MF) and erector spinae (ES). Degenerative spine features were assessed. Group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed, adjusting for age, body mass index, and sex, with additional sensitivity analyses incorporating structural variables. RESULTS: After correction for multiple comparisons, PDFF and T2 values in the superficial and whole MF and ES were higher in the LBP group. PDFF and T2 values showed moderate-to-strong correlations within the same muscle (ρ = 0.571-0.743, all q < 0.001). However, pain status was not independently associated with imaging parameters after adjustment, whereas age showed consistent positive associations. Additional multivariable analyses showed that T2 values, but not PDFF, were associated with selected degenerative spine features after adjustment for covariates. Inter-reader reliability was excellent for PDFF and T2, with ICCs of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. CONCLUSION: After adjustment, LBP status was not independently associated with PDFF or T2 values, whereas age was associated with both and selected degenerative spine features were associated with T2 values in exploratory analyses. Given the cross-sectional design, causal relationships among muscle alterations, structural degeneration, and pain cannot be determined. KEY POINTS: Question Do paraspinal muscle proton density fat fraction and T2 values reflect low back pain independently of demographic and lumbar degenerative features? Findings After demographic adjustment, low back pain status was not independently associated with paraspinal muscle proton density fat fraction or T2 values. Critical relevance statement Radiologists should interpret paraspinal muscle proton density fat fraction and T2 values alongside patient demographics, lumbar degenerative findings, and clinical measures rather than as direct imaging markers of low back pain.

articles.title: Performance of LI-RADS to diagnose hepatocellular carcinoma in patients presenting with locally advanced liver disease on CT or MRI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the diagnostic performance of LI-RADS version 2018 in patients at high risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) presenting with locally advanced intrahepatic tumor burden on CT or MRI. METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive CT and MRI exams containing liver lesions from January 1, 2013-December 30, 2022, of patients at high risk for HCC. CT and MRI exams were reviewed independently by eight radiologists who assigned a LI-RADS category to the largest lesion. Pathology served as the exam-level reference standard for HCC diagnosis. Positive predictive value (PPV), sensitivity, and specificity of the LR-5 (definitely HCC) category and combined LR-5 and LR-TIV (tumor in vein) "definitely due to HCC" categories to determine HCC diagnosis were calculated. RESULTS: In 408 patients (340 [83%] men, mean age, 66 years ± 9.6) with 472 exams, 328 (80%) patients had HCC. The PPV for LR-5 alone was 95% (95% CI: 92-99%), with high specificity of 90% (95% CI: 84-97%) and low sensitivity of 48% (95% CI: 43-54%). The PPV of the combined categories was 96% (95% CI: 93-98%), with moderate specificity of 86% (95% CI: 78-94%) and moderate sensitivity of 77% (95% CI: 73-82%). Inter-reader agreement was substantial for LR-5 alone (κ = 0.71 [95% CI: 0.57-0.84]) and moderate for the combined categories (κ = 0.58 [95% CI: 0.40-0.73]). CONCLUSION: Findings in this selected pathology-confirmed cohort support the potential role of imaging-based diagnosis in this setting. Further research in broader, unselected clinical populations is warranted.

articles.title: Limited incremental value of computed tomography-derived body composition indices for preoperative prediction of lymphovascular invasion in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incremental value of computed tomography (CT)-derived body composition indices for preoperative prediction of lymphovascular invasion (LVI) in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 315 patients with pathologically confirmed ccRCC who underwent preoperative multiphasic CT between May 2020 and December 2024. Patients were randomly divided (7:3) into training (n = 223; 81 LVI-positive) and internal validation (n = 92; 28 LVI-positive) cohorts. Postoperative histopathology served as the reference standard for LVI. Clinical characteristics, conventional CT features, and body composition indices were collected. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression were used for predictor selection and model construction. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: The clinicoradiological model included body mass index (BMI; odds ratio [OR], 0.758; p < 0.001), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR; OR, 1.765; p = 0.010), and size (OR, 1.629; p < 0.001). The body composition model included skeletal muscle index (SMI; OR, 0.951; p = 0.005) and total adipose tissue index (TATI; OR, 0.977; p < 0.001); the combined model included all five predictors. In the training cohort, areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) were 0.852, 0.730, and 0.851 for the clinicoradiological, body composition, and combined models, respectively. The combined model did not significantly outperform the clinicoradiological model (p = 0.917). In the internal validation cohort, the clinicoradiological and combined models had AUCs of 0.778 and 0.774, respectively (p = 0.609). In both cohorts, confidence intervals for Brier score differences included zero, indicating no apparent improvement in calibration with the addition of body composition indices. DCA showed no consistent advantage in net benefit. CONCLUSION: Although SMI and TATI are associated with LVI in the standalone body composition model, they provide no clear incremental predictive value beyond the clinicoradiological model. Findings from this cohort support prioritizing multicenter external validation and clinical impact assessment of the more parsimonious clinicoradiological model.

articles.title: Inter-reader reliability and clinical validity of the MRI grading system for lumbar foraminal stenosis among radiologists and clinicians.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the interobserver reliability of the Lee system among radiologists and clinicians. METHODS: A total of 73 patients who underwent MRI of the lumbar spine included. Six interpreters evaluated the degree of lumbar foraminal stenosis (LFS) from the L2-3 to the L5-S1 levels after training the Lee system. A different neurosurgeon assessed the associated clinical manifestations of each patient. The κ statistics were used to analyse the interreader agreement among the radiologists and clinicians. The clinical correlations between stenosis grade and positive clinical manifestations (PCM) were assessed using nonparametric correlation analysis (Spearman's correlation). RESULTS: There was almost perfect agreement between the trainees (κ = 0.96), radiologists (κ = 0.89), and clinicians (κ = 0.82). The agreements between the radiologist and trainee (κ = 0.78) and between the radiologist and clinician (κ = 0.77) were substantial. Correlation analysis between clinical symptoms and grade for the six readers suggested a moderate correlation, with R ranging from 0.619 to 0.662. CONCLUSION: The Lee system for LFS demonstrated substantial to almost perfect inter-reader reliability across radiologists, trainees, and clinicians, regardless of differences in reader experience. Furthermore, each group showed a moderate correlation between MRI grades and patients' clinical symptoms. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: The Lee system for LFS can be applied with substantial to almost perfect inter-reader reliability not only by radiologists but also by trainees and clinicians without radiologic training, supporting its use where subspecialty expertise is unavailable.

articles.title: Volumetric fat fraction quantification of the sacroiliac joint: changes in axial spondyloarthritis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the changes of fat fraction in the sacroiliac joint in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), including both the cartilaginous joint and the posterior ligamentous joint (PSIJ), by using a volumetric analyzing method on proton-density fat fraction (PDFF) maps. METHODS: Patients aged 18-45 years with low back pain that underwent a 3.0 T MRI scan of the sacroiliac joint with additional PDFF maps were retrospectively included. Semi-automatic segmentation of the subcortical region and the PSIJ was performed. Volumetric fat fraction parameters were quantified including histographic analysis. Comparison between axSpA and non-SpA patients was performed. RESULTS: Ninety-three patients including 44 axSpA and 49 non-SpA patients were included. Patients with axSpA had higher mean sacrum PDFF (58.2% vs. 52.5%, p = 0.004). The percentage of bone volume with PDFF ranged from 75% to 100% (i.e. PDFF75100) increased (24.0% vs. 8.9%, p < 0.001), while the percentages of PDFF2550 and PDFF5075 decreased (26.6% vs. 35.6%, p = 0.005, 33.7% vs. 42.0%, p < 0.001). The mean ilium PDFF was not different between groups (p = 0.284), while the percentage of PDFF5075 decreased (39.0% vs. 46.3%, p = 0.033) and the percentage of PDFF75100 increased (20.6% vs.10.6%, p = 0.008). Fat fraction of the PSIJ was not changed in axSpA. The results remained unchanged after correction of age, sex and BMI. CONSLUSIONS: By using a volumetric segmentation method, fat fraction of the cartilaginous sacroiliac joint was changed in axSpA while not the PSIJ. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Changes of the fat fraction of both the cartilaginous and ligamentous sacroiliac joint was described in detail using a semi-automatic segmentation method.

articles.title: X-ray FLASH: Technologies, evidence and challenges to translation.
articles.abstract: The FLASH effect describes the unique radiobiological advantages of ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) exposures in widening the therapeutic window by reducing normal tissue complications while maintaining tumour control. Since 2014, there has been renewed interest in responses to UHDR exposures with many studies demonstrating the FLASH effect in a range of preclinical models using proton and electron sources. In comparison, fewer studies have reported the FLASH effect in response to X-rays due to the challenges of achieving UHDR X-rays. However, several recent innovations have enabled more widespread access to UHDR X-ray sources providing evidence for the X-ray FLASH effect. In this review, we provide an update on recent developments in UHDR X-ray technologies, evaluate current preclinical evidence supporting the X-ray FLASH effect and discuss the challenges and considerations for future translation.

articles.title: 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: pilot study with fibroblast profiling.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is overexpressed on cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), driving an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We report a prospective study integrating ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET-CT with ex vivo CAF subset profiling in treatment-naïve NSCLC. METHODS: 15 patients underwent 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT alongside standard-of-care imaging (Cohort 1: five surgical candidates; Cohort 2: ten advanced-disease patients). Standardised uptake values (SUV) were derived from primary tumour, lymph nodes, mediastinal blood pool (MBP), background lung and metastatic deposits. Plasma collagen remodelling biomarkers (PRO-C3, C3M, C3F, PRO-C11) were measured in 13 patients. Fresh tumour and adjacent non-cancerous lung tissue were samples following surgical resection (n = 5) to allow for CAF subset identification by flow cytometry. RESULTS: 68Ga-FAPI PET demonstrated avid uptake in all primary tumours (SUVmax 3.97-14.01; mean 9.67 ± 2.84) with low background lung signal (SUVmean mean 0.68 ± 0.28; range 0.30-1.27), yielding good tumour-to-background ratios (TBR mean 16.88 ± 9.85; range 8.07-40). Compared with 18F-FDG PET-CT, 68Ga-FAPI upstaged two patients (previously undetected bone and retro-orbital metastases), but demonstrated discordant (negative 68Ga-FAPI) nodal signal in two further patients. Plasma collagen biomarkers were measurable but did not correlate significantly with 68Ga-FAPI SUV (Spearman r ≤ 0.44 for all markers). FAP high CAF subsets (S1 + S5) were higher in tumour compared with matched normal lung and CAF S5 correlates with SUVmax (r = 0.90, p = 0.04). CONCLUSIONS: 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT is feasible and well-tolerated in NSCLC, provides complementary staging information to FDG PET-CT, and reflects tumour FAP biology as evidenced by ex vivo CAF subset enrichment. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET-CT provides complementary staging information to ¹⁸F-FDG PET-CT in treatment-naïve NSCLC and is shown to reflect intratumoral FAP biology directly. This prospective pilot study provides preliminary evidence that ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-46 PET-CT may act as a non-invasive marker of the fibroblast-rich tumour microenvironment in NSCLC, which requires confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Balancing Directions and Averages for Cardiac Diffusion Tensor Imaging Using a Moderate Gradient Performance System.
articles.abstract: Cardiac diffusion tensor imaging (cDTI) is an inherently low signal-to-noise ratio technique while also having long scan times. This generally results in suboptimal image quality, especially for systems with moderate gradient performance, for fixed durations of scan time. The aim of this study was to evaluate several diffusion encoding schemes (DES) on a moderate gradient performance, 3T scanner, while fixing the number of diffusion-weighted images to objectively determine which DES yielded superior results. Spin-echo cDTI protocols spanning six DES were evaluated in healthy subjects (N = 10). Each DES used a combination diffusion directions (N   d i r    ) and signal averages (N   a v g    ). Mean diffusivity (MD), fractional anisotropy (FA), and the helix angle pitch (HAP), plus MD uncertainty ( d  MD), FA uncertainty ( d  FA), and the primary eigenvector uncertainty ( d   e →  1    ) were analyzed for statistical differences (p < 0.05). The technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) method was used to identify which DES yielded superior results. DES with lower N   d i r    /higher N   a v g    had lower FA, d  MD, and d  FA. As N   d i r    increased/N   a v g    decreased, FA, d  MD, and d  FA increased. Inversely, DES with lower N   d i r    /higher N   a v g    had a higher d   e →  1    , while N   d i r    increased/N   a v g    decreased, the d   e →  1    decreased. The HAP had a parabolic trend where both DES with lower N   d i r    /higher N   a v g    and DES with higher N   d i r    /lower N   a v g    were not as steep as DES with moderate N   d i r    /moderate N   a v g    . The DES with moderate N   d i r    (15)/moderate N   a v g    (4) yielded the most superior results. This work provides a framework for evaluating the best DES for cDTI on systems with moderate gradient performance.

articles.title: Quantitative MRI Relaxation Parameters for Hypoxia Assessment in 3D Cancer Cell Spheroids.
articles.abstract: Tumor hypoxia is a major determinant of treatment resistance, yet non-invasive imaging markers that reflect hypoxia-associated changes remain limited. In this study, the associations of quantitative MRI relaxation parameters with size-associated hypoxia were evaluated in three-dimensional HCT116 tumor spheroids, in which hypoxia develops naturally as spheroids grow. Spheroids of four nominal diameters (400, 650, 800, and 1050  μ  m) were generated in microfluidic chips and imaged simultaneously on a clinical 3 T scanner.   T 1  ,  T 2    , and   T 2 ∗    were estimated from inversion-recovery, multi-echo spin-echo, and multi-echo gradient-echo acquisitions using an in-house fitting framework validated with a quantitative MRI system phantom, and   T 2 '    was derived from   T 2    and   T 2 ∗    . Expression of carbonic anhydrase IX (CA-IX), quantified by western blot, was used as a biological proxy for hypoxia. CA-IX expression increased with spheroid size, with the same rank order on all three blots ( p < 0 . 001  ).   T 2    showed the strongest size-dependent change, decreasing from 291 to 236 ms across the size groups (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0 . 002  ; Kendall's   τ b  = - 0 . 39 ,  p < 0 . 001  ), and group-mean   T 2    decreased in close parallel with CA-IX expression (Pearson's r = - 0 . 99  ).   T 1    showed a weaker, non-significant trend, and   T 2 ∗    and   T 2 '    were unchanged, as expected in an avascular model without deoxyhemoglobin. The association between   T 2    and spheroid size was robust to the position of the chips in the scanner. Exploratory multivariable regression and principal component analysis indicated that combining parameters added little information beyond   T 2    alone. These findings identify   T 2    as the relaxation parameter most closely associated with hypoxia-related changes in this controlled spheroid model and support its further evaluation as a quantitative MRI marker of tumor hypoxia.

articles.title: FOCUS: A Frequency Offset Selection Framework for Accelerated CEST MRI Using Adaptive Subset-Level Optimization.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a redundancy-aware frequency offset selection framework for accelerated chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) MRI that reduces acquired saturation frequency offsets while preserving quantitative and classification performance. METHODS: FOCUS, a Frequency Offset selection framework for accelerated CEST MRI Using adaptive Subset-level optimization, was developed to account for inter-offset redundancy beyond individual offset importance. Frequency offset selection was formulated as subset-level optimization, in which candidate subsets were encoded as binary individuals and evaluated by final task performance. An artificial protozoa optimizer-based search scheme was used to explore the subset space, and a deep Q-network adaptively guided the search strategy. FOCUS was evaluated in numerical simulations, in vivo human skeletal muscle phosphocreatine quantification, and glioma molecular subtype classification, and compared with permutation importance analysis, random forest, and channel pruning. RESULTS: Under reduced frequency-offset sampling, FOCUS outperformed existing methods in both CEST quantification and glioma molecular subtype classification. For CEST quantification, FOCUS achieved the lowest root mean square error in simulations and in vivo skeletal muscle experiments, with the highest structural similarity index and peak signal-to-noise ratio in vivo. For glioma classification, FOCUS achieved the best overall performance in predicting isocitrate dehydrogenase mutation and O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation status. CONCLUSION: FOCUS enables redundancy-aware frequency offset selection for accelerated CEST MRI, reducing acquired saturation frequency offsets while preserving quantitative accuracy and classification performance.

articles.title: Region-Adaptive White Matter Tractography Using Microstructure-Informed Diffusion Metrics.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate a region-adaptive tractography framework that integrates multi-scale diffusion metrics, specifically fractional anisotropy (FA), asymmetric index (ASI) from asymmetric fiber orientation distribution functions, and diffusion tensor distribution (DTD)-derived microscopic fractional anisotropy (μFA) to improve anatomical fidelity in complex white matter configurations. METHODS: MS-Track, a rule-based region-adaptive tractography method, was proposed to classify local fiber configurations (parallel, crossing, bending, termination) using FA, ASI, and μFA. Streamline seeding, peak sampling, curvature tolerance, and termination were dynamically modulated according to configuration. Validation was performed on the ISMRM 2015 Tractography Challenge phantom and in vivo data acquired with the DTD protocol from 20 healthy subjects, 20 arteriovenous malformation (AVM) patients, and 2 glioma patients. RESULTS: On the ISMRM 2015 Challenge dataset, a mean Dice coefficient of 0.700 was achieved by MS-Track, with the highest overlap (68.5%) and the lowest overreach (24.0%) among state-of-the-art methods. In AVM patients, reduced fiber density and elevated μFA and ASI were observed in affected tracts. In glioma cases, μFA increased with tumor grade, consistent with histological findings. CONCLUSION: Tractography reliability in complex white matter was improved by MS-Track through the integration of complementary microstructural contrasts. DTD-derived μFA provided additional sensitivity to pathological tissue, supporting potential clinical translation in surgical planning and disease characterization.

articles.title: The 3‑mm peritumoral margin provides optimal prognostic information in soft tissue sarcoma radiomics: a retrospective multi‑sequence MRI study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To construct an integrated prognostic model combining intra‑ and peritumoral radiomics with MRI features for predicting progression‑free survival (PFS) in soft tissue sarcomas (STS). METHODS: This retrospective study included 305 patients with trunk or extremity STS. Radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and peritumoral regions at expansion distances of 3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm on both contrast‑enhanced T1‑weighted (CE‑T1WI) and fat‑suppressed T2‑weighted (FS‑T2WI) sequences. Features were selected via ICC, univariate Cox, and LASSO Cox regression. Prognostic models were constructed by integrating Rad‑scores with significant MRI features, and evaluated using C‑index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed stratified by imaging phenotype (cellular vs. non‑cellular). Correlation analyses between peritumoral Rad‑scores and semantic MRI features were also conducted. RESULTS: The 3‑mm peritumoral expansion yielded the highest predictive performance among the three distances. Integrated intratumoral-peritumoral (3 mm) models from both sequences outperformed single‑region models. The 3‑mm margin consistently demonstrated superior performance in both cellular and non‑cellular phenotypes. The final multimodal model, combining dual‑sequence Rad‑scores with peritumoral enhancement, achieved a C‑index of 0.888 in the validation set. Correlation analyses reveal that peritumoral Rad‑scores are most strongly associated with peritumoral T2 hyperintensity, with differential correlation patterns between CE‑T1WI and FS‑T2WI supporting their complementary roles. CONCLUSIONS: We developed a robust multimodal radiomics model integrating intra‑ and peritumoral (3 mm) features with key MRI characteristics. The optimality of the 3‑mm margin was validated across major STS phenotypes. This non‑invasive tool facilitates personalized risk stratification and may inform adjuvant treatment decisions, supporting clinical translation in STS management.

articles.title: Adnexal cyst pseudoenhancement and optimal attenuation change threshold determination at low keV reconstructions at photon counting CT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate "pseudoenhancement" in adnexal lesions on low kiloelectron volt (keV) virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) at photon-counting CT (PCCT) and to establish optimal attenuation change thresholds for distinguishing enhancing from nonenhancing lesions at each VMI. METHODS: Adult women who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic PCCT and pelvic MRI or ultrasound (US) within 180 days were identified via retrospective PACS search. Adnexal lesions were classified as enhancing or nonenhancing using MRI or US as the reference standard. Quantitative attenuation measurements were obtained using regions-of-interest at VMI levels (70, 67, 60, 55, 50, 45, and 40 keV). "Pseudoenhancement" was defined as ≥ 20 Hounsfield units (HU) increase between the VMI and virtual unenhanced (VUE) images. The diagnostic performance of a 20HU change to define enhancement at each VMI level was assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine optimal thresholds by maximizing the Youden index. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients. RESULTS: Forty-five women (median [IQR] age 46 years [37, 54] ) with 30 nonenhancing and 15 enhancing adnexal lesions were included. No "pseudoenhancement" was observed at 70 or 67 keV; however, "pseudoenhancement" was observed in 3.3% of patients at 60 keV, increasing to 26.7% at 40 keV. Using a 20 HU change to indicate enhancement had 47% sensitivity with 100% specificity at 70 keV and 93% sensitivity with 73% specificity at 40 keV. Optimal attenuation thresholds increased with decreasing energy, from 10.0 HU at 70 keV to 36.3 HU at 40 keV. Notably, at 60 keV, the threshold was 19.1HU. Inter-reader agreement was near perfect (ICC = 0.858, 95%CI = 0.756-0.920). CONCLUSION: "Pseudoenhancement" of adnexal lesions occurs with increasing frequency with decreasing keV below 60 keV, but there was no "pseudoenhancement" at 67 or 70 keV. Energy-specific attenuation thresholds improve adnexal lesion characterization.

articles.title: Fenestration of the Coronary Arteries: CT Angiography Findings.
articles.abstract: Background: Fenestration is a segmental duplication of an artery and is a new entity described in coronary arteries, distinct from dissection. This study aimed to show CT angiography (CTA) findings of fenestrated coronary arteries, along with their possible associations or any accompanying findings. Methods: This was a multicenter study and included examinations from four different institutions. Between the years 2022 and 2025, 5554 patients who underwent coronary CTA without prior coronary catheter angiography and intervention were included in this study. Coronary CTA was acquired using four different multidetector CT scanners. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) examinations were reevaluated for fenestration. Fenestrations were analyzed for morphological type, length, and diameter. Results: In total, 26 of 5554 patients (0.47%) had coronary artery fenestration. Fenestration was observed in 13 left circumflex (Cx) arteries, 8 left anterior descending (LAD) arteries, and 5 right coronary arteries (RCA). Two of the 26 patients underwent catheter angiography. Single-loop-type fenestration was observed in 12 patients, and two patients had multiple-loop fenestrations. There were 12 patients with parallel-type fenestration. Among the patients with fenestrated coronary arteries, myocardial bridging was observed in 5 patients as an associated anomaly. No significant difference was found in the length or diameter of the fenestrated segments. There were no symptoms related to fenestration in our patients. Conclusions: Fenestration of a coronary artery can be demonstrated by CTA and may be associated with myocardial bridging. It is most common in the Cx artery. Fenestration should be differentiated from dissection for clinical implications. Further studies are warranted to understand the importance of this observation.

articles.title: Pretreatment MRI Radiomics for Overall Survival Risk Stratification in Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Cervix: A Development and External Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix (NECC) is a rare malignancy, and pretreatment overall survival (OS) assessment remains limited. We developed and externally validated an MRI radiomics model for OS risk stratification. Methods: This retrospective study included 128 patients: Center 1 served as the development cohort (n = 90), and Center 2 as the independent external validation cohort (n = 38). The model was selected using development data and locked before validation. Evaluation included Harrell C-index, inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted (IPCW) AUC, calibration, Brier score, decision-curve analysis, and survival stratification. Results: The model comprised three intratumoral T2-weighted imaging features fitted using CoxBoost 1.5.2. Its external C-index was 0.737 (95% CI, 0.615-0.850), compared with 0.633 (95% CI, 0.523-0.749) for the revised clinical model; the paired difference was 0.104 (95% CI, -0.018 to 0.226). A nested sensitivity analysis of the automated selection procedure yielded a mean C-index of 0.592 (SD, 0.049). IPCW AUCs were 0.741 (95% CI, 0.562-0.891) at 3 years and 0.763 (95% CI, 0.583-0.919) at 5 years. At 3 and 5 years, calibration intercepts were 0.03 and -0.09, slopes 1.14 and 1.20, and Brier scores 0.202 and 0.195, respectively. Exploratory decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit over selected thresholds. Hazard ratios (HRs; 95% CIs) for high versus low risk were 1.96 (1.06-3.62) and 3.61 (1.39-9.38) in the development and external cohorts, respectively. Corresponding HRs per development-cohort SD increase in the score were 1.83 (1.29-2.60) and 2.42 (1.45-4.04). Conclusions: The pretreatment MRI radiomics model showed external prognostic discrimination for OS in NECC, but superiority over the pretreatment clinical model was not demonstrated. Further independent validation is needed.

articles.title: Hybrid PET/CCTA for Coronary Atherosclerosis: Molecular Targets, Technical Challenges, and Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) characterizes luminal stenosis and plaque morphology, whereas positron emission tomography (PET) can depict biological processes involved in atherosclerosis. Hybrid PET/CCTA enables assessment of tracer uptake in relation to coronary anatomy, but its interpretation and clinical translation remain challenging. This narrative review, based on a non-systematic, topic-focused literature search, examines established and emerging molecular imaging targets, including inflammation, microcalcification, fibroblast activation, hypoxia, angiogenesis, and thrombosis. We discuss tracer-specific evidence, quantitative measurements, reproducibility, and the effects of cardiac and respiratory motion, partial-volume loss, background activity, and image misregistration. We distinguish human coronary findings from evidence obtained in other vascular territories or preclinical studies. We describe an institutional acquisition workflow, accompanied by illustrative FDG and NaF PET/CCTA images showing CCTA-defined coronary atherosclerosis without discernible focal tracer uptake. [18F]NaF has the most extensive human coronary evidence among the tracers reviewed. However, associations between uptake and subsequent events do not establish the benefit of PET-guided management. Tracer uptake alone does not indicate impending plaque rupture, and the absence of uptake does not establish plaque stability. Standardized acquisition and quantification, validation of incremental value beyond contemporary CCTA, and evidence of improved patient outcomes are required before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Intraoperative Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Imaging in Pancreatic Head and Periampullary Surgery: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence imaging is inexpensive and increasingly used in pancreatic surgery, but its evidence base has been appraised only in fragments-one application at a time, or ICG pooled with investigational fluorophores-and never specifically for the pancreatic head and periampullary region. We mapped its intraoperative applications, techniques and reported outcomes. Methods: Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and the Directory of Open Access Journals on 29 July 2026 without date restriction. Two reviewers screened and charted independently, one row per article-by-application combination, and synthesised the findings narratively. Results: Forty-two studies (51 article-by-application combinations, 613 patients) covered six applications: stump perfusion, biliary identification and anastomotic testing, perfusion of reconstructed vessels and the duodenal arcade, tumour detection and margin assessment, lymphatic mapping, and staging laparoscopy. Eighteen were case or technique reports, no randomised trial was identified, and only three studies included a group operated without ICG. Remnant hypoperfusion predicted postoperative acute pancreatitis (80% versus 16%, p = 0.011) and clinically relevant fistula (odds ratio 10.0) in two small prospective cohorts, yet in the largest series (n = 100) a visual score of the pancreaticojejunostomy was reproducible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.76) but discriminated poorly (area under the curve 0.64) and altered no operation. In a single retrospective comparison in duodenum-preserving resection, ICG guidance was associated with less intraoperative bile-duct injury (10% versus 60%, p = 0.009). Conventional doses did not distinguish pancreatic adenocarcinoma from normal parenchyma, whereas second-window imaging made 12 of 13 invasive specimens fluoresce. Dose varied by two orders of magnitude, and no adverse reaction was reported, although tolerability was formally assessed in only nine studies. Conclusions: Intraoperative ICG use in pancreatic head surgery appears safe and feasible. ICG shows key anatomical structures-above all the biliary tree-more reliably than white light alone. Its most promising benefits are the early recognition of an ischaemic pancreatic remnant, with the prospect of preventing postoperative fistula and pancreatitis, and the early identification and protection of the distal bile duct during duodenum-preserving pancreatic head resection.

articles.title: Approach to the Diagnosis and Management of Primary Hyperparathyroidism.
articles.abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is a common endocrine disorder and an important cause of secondary osteoporosis, characterized by excessive or inappropriate parathyroid hormone secretion relative to serum calcium concentrations. Although its clinical presentation has shifted toward asymptomatic and mild biochemical phenotypes, skeletal and renal complications remain clinically relevant and may be overlooked. This narrative review discusses the diagnosis and management of PHPT, emphasizing diagnostic pitfalls, hereditary forms, and skeletal involvement. Biochemical assessment requires careful interpretation of calcium and parathyroid hormone measurements, recognition of preanalytical and immunoassay interference, and differentiation from familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia and secondary causes of elevated parathyroid hormone. Normocalcemic PHPT requires rigorous exclusion of secondary hyperparathyroidism, and evidence guiding its treatment remains limited. Skeletal manifestations range from reduced bone mineral density and impaired cortical and trabecular microarchitecture to osteitis fibrosa cystica, brown tumors, and pathological fractures. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, vertebral fracture assessment, and complementary tools such as trabecular bone score help characterize skeletal involvement beyond bone mass alone. Genetic evaluation in selected patients informs surgical planning, surveillance, and family screening. Parathyroidectomy remains the only curative treatment, whereas localization imaging serves surgical planning rather than diagnostic confirmation. For patients managed without surgery, antiresorptive agents improve bone mineral density, while cinacalcet controls hypercalcemia. Integrating accurate biochemical diagnosis, skeletal and renal assessment, and recognition of hereditary disease supports individualized management and helps avoid unnecessary investigations and inappropriate interventions.

articles.title: Cytomegalovirus Detection and Monitoring After Autologous Haematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Surveillance Strategies and Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Reported cytomegalovirus (CMV) frequency after autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (auto-HSCT) varies widely. We asked how much of that variation reflects how CMV is sought rather than how often it occurs and how often it causes disease. Methods: PubMed, Europe PMC, Embase and Scopus were searched from inception to 12 September 2026. Reports of at least 20 predominantly adult autologous recipients with an extractable CMV outcome were eligible. Virological detection, symptomatic infection, antiviral-treated infection, confirmed end-organ disease and attributed death were pooled separately by random-effects meta-analysis and a binomial-normal mixed model, stratified by monitoring strategy, denominator, and whether the case definition required symptoms. Results: Thirty-eight reports were included. Detection tracked ascertainment: 17.6% (95% confidence interval (CI) 12.7-23.9) under systematic surveillance, 3.9% (95% CI 1.0-14.4) under symptom-triggered testing, and 37.4% (95% CI 29.9-45.6) where the denominator was restricted to seropositive recipients. That difference disappeared once both arms were restricted to reports enumerating laboratory-detected CMV (2.7%; Q = 2.37, p = 0.12), an artefact of case definition. Clinical consequences were uncommon and stable across strategies: end-organ disease 1.8% (95% CI 1.2-2.7), confirmed disease 1.7% (95% CI 1.0-2.9), attributed death 0.8% (95% CI 0.5-1.2). Median first detection was 30-35 days. Heterogeneity was high for detection (I2 75-96%) and absent for death. Conclusions: After auto-HSCT, how often CMV is reported depends mainly on who is tested and how infection is defined, while end-organ disease and attributed death remain uncommon under every strategy. These data support evaluating risk-adapted monitoring rather than universal surveillance.

articles.title: Patent Foramen Ovale and Atrial Septal Defects: A Multimodal Approach to Diagnosis, Prognosis and Closure-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Interatrial communications encompass anatomically and clinically distinct entities, ranging from patent foramen ovale (PFO), resulting from incomplete postnatal septal fusion, to atrial septal defects (ASDs) and extraseptal communications associated with congenital malformations. This narrative review synthesizes the literature, integrating embryology, anatomical classification, multimodality imaging and clinical evidence to support diagnosis, prognostic assessment and closure. Particular attention is given to distinguishing true secundum septal defects from ostium primum defects within the atrioventricular septal defect spectrum, sinus venosus communications and coronary sinus unroofing. Transthoracic echocardiography provides the initial anatomical and haemodynamic assessment; contrast echocardiography and transcranial Doppler assess right-to-left shunting, while transoesophageal and three-dimensional echocardiography define morphology, surrounding structures and procedural feasibility. Cardiac computed tomography complements these techniques by mapping complex malformations and pulmonary or systemic venous connections. In patients with otherwise unexplained ischaemic stroke, PFO causal attribution requires integration of clinical characteristics, neuroimaging findings and shunt features following investigation of competing mechanisms. Large right-to-left shunts and atrial septal aneurysm have the strongest evidence for identifying patients who derive greater benefit from closure, while additional geometric and biomechanical markers remain incompletely validated. ASD management depends primarily on shunt burden, right-heart remodelling and pulmonary vascular status, with paradoxical embolism providing an additional indication for closure when haemodynamically safe. Platypnoea-orthodeoxia, decompression sickness and migraine require indication-specific assessment; evidence does not support routine closure for migraine alone. The proposed diagnostic and decision algorithms organize these complementary assessments into a practical framework for individualized multidisciplinary management while remaining subject to prospective validation.

articles.title: Screening for Obstetric Sepsis: Diagnostic Performance, Competing Thresholds, and the Problem of an Imperfect Reference Standard-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Maternal sepsis contributes substantially to maternal mortality, with recurrent delays in recognition and considerable opportunities for prevention. More than twenty screening tools have been evaluated in obstetric care; their reported performance varies widely, a variation often read as evidence of superiority.
