Results: Median early TBR values were 0.34 (IQR, 0.29-0.36), 0.52 (IQR, 0.43-0.57), and 0.74 (IQR, 0.66-0.83) in the low-, intermediate-, and high-uptake groups, respectively, versus 0.66 (IQR, 0.54-0.77) in controls. Early TBR was significantly lower in the low- and intermediate-uptake groups than in controls (p < 0.001 and p = 0.0066, respectively), whereas the high-uptake group did not differ significantly. Delayed TBR was lower than early TBR (median reduction 30.0%; p < 0.001). Early and delayed TBR measurements were strongly correlated (rs = 0.86, p < 0.001), and 78.2% of patients remained in the same uptake group. Conclusions: Semiquantitative MIBI analysis using a mediastinal background region provides an objective measure of thyroid uptake patterns in AIT. The strong correlation between early and delayed TBR measurements and substantial stability of relative uptake grouping indicate that the two imaging time points provide closely related semiquantitative information. These exploratory findings require external validation before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Videoautopsy-A Minimally Invasive Autopsy Method Using Endoscopic Techniques in Forensic Medicine: Technical Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Minimally invasive autopsy methods using endoscopic techniques such as Videoautopsy are one of the new diagnostic tools in forensic science. However, there is still a lack of papers presenting the step-by-step technique for carrying them out. This article presents the protocol for conducting the test, with particular emphasis on technical parameters and rules for performing the procedure. Methods: The technical feasibility study included 15 corpses, which were examined at the Department of Forensic Medicine of the Medical University of Poznań. The tests were carried out in teams of three, consisting of highly qualified medical professionals. Results: The average body temperature at which the procedure was performed was 17.9 °C. The pressure of the produced pneumoperitoneum was in the range of 11-20 mmHg; moreover, it was produced with the use of carbon dioxide, the flow rate of which was in the range of 0.5-2.0 L/min. In each case, the examination was performed primarily in the supine position and included examination of the abdominal cavity and chest. The average procedure time was 37 min. Conclusions: The key to optimal examination is the proper preparation of the corpse. Based on observations, body temperature could influence the formation of the pneumoperitoneum required to obtain an adequate field of view. Further research is needed to develop minimally invasive autopsy techniques.

articles.title: Predictive Value of Haematological Inflammatory Indices for Disease Activity and Organ Involvement in Systemic Sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease whose activity and severity remain difficult to assess. Although haematological inflammatory indices such as the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR) have been investigated in several inflammatory conditions, data in SSc remain limited. This study aimed to assess their clinical utility as markers of disease activity and severity. Methods: This cross-sectional correlational study included patients diagnosed with SSc who were evaluated for haematological and inflammatory markers, including SII, PLR, NLR, MLR, platelet distribution width (PDW), plateletcrit (PCT), and C-reactive protein (CRP), in relation to disease phenotype, organ involvement, and disease activity, as assessed by a modified European Scleroderma Trials and Research Activity Index (EUSTAR-AI). Group comparisons were performed using independent-samples t-tests on log-transformed data, with multivariable adjustment for age, sex, disease duration, phenotype and immunosuppressive and glucocorticoid therapy, while Pearson and Spearman correlations, linear regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses (with DeLong comparisons of the areas under the curve, AUC) were used to evaluate associations and discriminative performance; multiplicity was addressed with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results: A total of 159 patients with SSc were included. Patients with diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) exhibited significantly higher SII, NLR, and MLR values than those with limited cutaneous disease. SII and NLR were also significantly elevated in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Active disease was associated with higher levels of all major inflammatory indices, while SII and NLR showed significant correlations with pulmonary function parameters, the modified Rodnan Skin Score (mRSS), and the EUSTAR-AI score. In the ROC analysis of SII alone, SII showed moderate discrimination of active disease (AUC = 0.72, 95% CI 0.63-0.80), not significantly different from NLR (0.67) or CRP (0.75). In multivariable regression, SII remained associated with EUSTAR-AI but not with mRSS. After adjustment for age, sex, disease duration, phenotype and treatment, SII remained higher in dcSSc and active disease, whereas the associations with ILD and PAH were no longer significant. Conclusions: SII and NLR were associated with disease activity, the diffuse cutaneous phenotype and, in unadjusted analyses, pulmonary involvement in SSc. SII was independently associated with EUSTAR-AI, but its discriminative ability was moderate and not superior to that of NLR or CRP. These indices may serve as exploratory adjuncts to established activity measures; prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Diagnostic Efficiency of Sequential Tissue Acquisition During Shape-Sensing Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy in a Thoracic Surgery Setting: A Biopsy-Level Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) enables precise navigation to peripheral pulmonary lesions, while intraprocedural imaging can improve assessment of biopsy tool positioning relative to the target. However, successful lesion localization does not necessarily translate into diagnostic tissue acquisition, and little is known about the diagnostic contribution of individual sequential biopsy specimens. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic yield and sequential tissue acquisition during ssRAB at both the lesion and individual specimen level, with particular emphasis on the number of biopsies required to establish a diagnosis. Methods: We performed a retrospective single-center analysis of consecutive thoracic surgical ssRAB procedures using the ION™ Endoluminal System (Intuitive Surgical, Sunnyvale, CA, USA) between August 2024 and March 2026. Procedures performed exclusively for bronchoscopic lesion marking without diagnostic tissue acquisition were excluded. Intraprocedural imaging was performed using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) or C-arm fluoroscopy. Primary outcome measures included specimen-level diagnostic yield, lesion-level diagnostic yield, the biopsy number at which the first diagnostic specimen was obtained, and the diagnostic-to-total specimen ratio per lesion. Results: Eighty-four patients with 118 pulmonary nodules were included. Median lesion diameter was 9.0 mm, and 94 lesions (79.7%) were solid, 10 (8.5%) were subsolid, and 14 (11.9%) were pure ground-glass opacities. CBCT was used in 111 lesions (94.1%) and C-arm fluoroscopy in seven (5.9%). A diagnostic bronchoscopic result was obtained in 101 lesions, corresponding to a lesion-level diagnostic yield of 85.6%. A total of 794 individual biopsy specimens were obtained, of which 487 (61.3%) were diagnostic. The mean diagnostic-to-total specimen ratio per lesion was 0.59 ± 0.39. Among diagnostically successful lesions, the first biopsy specimen was diagnostic in 68/101 cases (67.3%). A diagnosis was established within the first three biopsy specimens in 91/101 lesions (90.1%) and within the first five specimens in 99/101 lesions (98.0%). In two lesions, the first diagnostic specimen was obtained with the eighth biopsy. Conclusions: Although ssRAB achieved a high lesion-level diagnostic yield, diagnostic performance at the individual specimen level was substantially lower. Most successful diagnoses were established within the first three biopsy specimens, while additional sampling continued to provide incremental diagnostic information. These findings highlight the distinction between successful lesion localization and successful tissue acquisition and support a sequential, rather than single-sample, approach to tissue acquisition during ssRAB.

articles.title: Evaluation of IgG Subclass Reference Intervals in Koreans Using Indirect Methods Reveals Lower IgG3 Concentrations.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Reference intervals for IgG subclasses may vary according to age, population, and analytical method. We aimed to evaluate the applicability of manufacturer-provided SPAPLUS reference intervals in a Korean population. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1617 subjects with simultaneous Roche total IgG and SPAPLUS IgG1-IgG4 (2019-2022). Roche total IgG concentrations were compared with the sum of IgG subclasses. Adult reference intervals were indirectly estimated using refineR and kosmic, with sensitivity analysis performed in adults with normal Roche ranges. Results: Of the 1617 subjects, 1482 adults were included in the primary reference interval analysis, of whom 1345 had Roche total IgG concentrations within the manufacturer-provided reference interval. Method comparison in all subjects (n = 1617) showed that the SPAPLUS IgG subclass sum was approximately 9% lower than Roche total IgG. In the primary analysis of all adults (n = 1482), indirect reference interval estimation using refineR and kosmic yielded substantially lower IgG3 intervals (8.2-86.2 and 4.4-124.3 mg/dL, respectively) than the manufacturer-provided interval (21.82-176.06 mg/dL), whereas the estimated intervals for other IgG subclasses varied between methods. IgG4 also showed a higher upper reference limit than that provided by the manufacturer. Similar results were obtained in the sensitivity analysis of adults with normal Roche ranges (n = 1345). Conclusions: Manufacturer-provided SPAPLUS reference intervals were not uniformly applicable to this Korean population, with the greatest discrepancy observed for IgG3. Together with previous reports, our findings suggest that lower IgG3 concentrations may be a characteristic feature of East Asian populations and support the need for population-specific evaluation.

articles.title: Quantifying [18F]FDG Uptake in the Liver, Spleen, Aorta, Bone Marrow, and Superior Vena Cava Using TotalSegmentator on [18F]PET/CT Imaging.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The measurement of radiotracer uptake in specific organs has potential clinical implications. However, manual delineation is time-consuming. We aimed to evaluate the agreement between manual delineation and automatic segmentation by the artificial intelligence model TotalSegmentator for extraction of standard uptake values (SUVs) from [18F]FDG-PET/CT scans for the aorta, spleen, lumbar spine bone marrow, liver, and superior vena cava. Methods: The aorta, spleen, lumbar spine bone marrow, liver, and superior vena cava were segmented manually by trained physicians and automatically by the TotalSegmentator version 2.4 software, and the correlations between SUV values obtained were assessed. Results: We found good agreement between manually and automatically obtained SUVmean values for the aorta (manual/TotalSegmentator: 2.10/2.11), spleen (2.00/1.95), liver (2.53/2.37), lumbar spine bone marrow (1.88/1.85), and superior vena cava (2.02/1.88) with high correlation coefficients across all organs, ranging from 0.93 to 0.99 and high intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.81-0.99. Agreement for SUVmax showed greater variability across the organs which were assessed: agreement was good for the spleen (ICC 0.83) and lumbar spine bone marrow (ICC 0.86), but weak for the aorta (ICC 0.11). Bland-Altman analyses for SUVmean indicated no systematic bias in the aorta or spleen, slight bias in bone marrow, liver, and superior vena cava, and variable bias for SUVmax across all structures. Conclusions: TotalSegmentator provided reliable SUVmean values from the aorta, spleen, lumbar spine bone marrow, liver, and superior vena cava. However, the agreement between manually and automatically obtained SUVmax values was variable, suggesting that additional quality control steps should be applied if using TotalSegmentator for SUVmax extraction.

articles.title: Association of AI-Enhanced Vectorcardiographic Indices with Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease Burden: A Retrospective Single-Centre Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Cardisiography (CSG) is an AI-enhanced vectorcardiographic (VCG) system that reports composite perfusion (p-factor) and structural (s-factor) indices from a short resting recording. Whether CSG output is associated with the angiographic severity of coronary artery disease (CAD) has not been directly tested. Methods: We retrospectively analysed 103 consecutive patients referred for invasive coronary angiography at a single tertiary centre. The extent and severity of coronary artery disease were quantified with the GENSINI score. GENSINI scores were compared between patients with a normal (p-factor 0-1) and an abnormal (p-factor 2-3) CSG p-factor, and across the four ordinal p-factor categories; continuous VCG parameters were correlated with GENSINI on the continuous scale. A composite (p + s) index was examined as an exploratory analysis. Diagnostic accuracy for angiographic CAD was assessed at three severity thresholds (GENSINI > 0, ≥20 and ≥40). Results: Mean age was 57.5 ± 12.7 years and 72% were men. Patients with an abnormal p-factor had a higher GENSINI score than those with a normal p-factor (73.2 ± 51.2 vs. 50.9 ± 46.9; p = 0.034). A graded association between p-factor category and GENSINI burden was supported by a formal trend test (p = 0.007). QRS-T angle, T vector, superposition, p-index and T-wave scatter changed progressively across p-factor categories (all p < 0.001, retained after false-discovery-rate correction). AUCs for angiographic CAD were modest (0.58-0.68). The composite (p + s) > 3 was not associated with GENSINI (p = 0.096). Conclusions: CSG-derived VCG indices were associated with angiographic CAD burden; AUCs were modest. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings before clinical application.

articles.title: Former Third Molar Sockets Often Remain Histopathologically Altered: A Retrospective Study of the Bone Lid and Former Socket Wall in Covered Socket Residua with AI-Based Cell Quantification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: After tooth removal the crest may close before the socket has mineralised, leaving a covered socket residuum (CSR). Third molars are usually removed in young patients, often prophylactically. We examined bone removed at the surgical revision of former third molar sites with a radiologically diagnosed CSR. Methods: Retrospective single-centre study of a selected surgical series. The specimens consisted mainly of the bone lid covering the residuum, whose inner side is formed by the former socket walls, and, where labelled separately, of tissue from its depth. For every section the routine pathology report was coded for a leading finding, and cell nuclei were classified by whole-slide AI analysis without knowledge of the report. Clustering of sections within patients was accounted for with linear mixed models and a patient-level bootstrap. Results: Eighty-three sections from 28 patients (median age 54 years) were analysed. Fifty-one (61.4%; 95% CI 44.3-77.1) carried a distinguishing finding, 53.0% without haematopoietically active marrow, most often marrow fibrosis (14.5%), granulocytic inflammation or osteomyelitis (13.3%) and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate (10.8%). Twenty-one of 28 patients had at least one such section, and 13 of 24 patients with more than one section showed different findings in different sections. Accounting for clustering, the software-estimated lymphocyte, neutrophil, plasma cell and fibroblast fractions differed between categories (Holm-adjusted p = 0.001-0.023), ordered from cell-poor, fibroblast-dominated sections to lymphocyte-rich inflammation. Conclusions: In this selected series of surgically revised CSR, more than half of the sections, mostly from the bone lid and the former socket wall, carried a distinguishing histopathological finding, and the findings varied within the same patient. The AI-derived cell fractions are exploratory software estimates and require validation in this tissue. Whether the handling of the socket at extraction influences these findings is a hypothesis for prospective controlled studies.

articles.title: Can Grayscale Intensity Inform Bone Age Assessment? A Study of Pediatric Hand Radiographs.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hand-wrist radiographs obtained for bone age assessment also record grayscale intensity, but its relation to skeletal maturity is unknown. We examined whether raw grayscale intensity and bone-to-soft-tissue ratios are associated with bone age. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed left hand-wrist radiographs of 104 consecutive children aged 8-12 years (53 girls). One radiologist assessed bone age with the Greulich-Pyle atlas. Grayscale intensity was measured in five osseous regions and a soft-tissue reference, and each osseous value was normalized to it. Results: Raw intensities were higher in boys at every site, including soft tissue, but the ratios did not differ between sexes. Raw intensity showed little correlation with bone age or chronological age (all |r| < 0.10). Ratios correlated weakly with bone age (r = 0.12-0.19) and more weakly with chronological age (r = 0.04-0.12), but the differences were not significant. Two correlations were nominally significant (distal ulna ratio in the whole cohort, r = 0.19; third metacarpal ratio in boys, r = 0.33), but neither remained significant after Holm adjustment. Conclusions: Grayscale intensity provided little information about bone age. The sex difference in raw intensity affected bone and soft tissue alike, and its cause remains uncertain. Region-of-interest repeatability was not assessed.

articles.title: Hospital-Acquired Infections Associated with Sepsis in Intensive Care Unit Patients: Clinical Characteristics, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sepsis caused by hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) remains a major challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), where antimicrobial resistance is widespread. This study examined the clinical characteristics, microbiological patterns, antimicrobial resistance, and outcomes of ICU patients with HAI-associated sepsis in western Romania. Methods: We retrospectively analysed 276 ICU HAI episodes recorded between 2020 and 2025. Cases were classified as septic shock (n = 148), sepsis without shock (n = 68), or no documented sepsis (n = 60). Mortality predictors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and survival analyses. Results: Sepsis occurred in 78.3% of HAI episodes. Patients with septic shock were generally older and more likely to have diabetes, require mechanical ventilation (82.4%), or develop acute kidney injury (64.9%). Among sepsis-associated episodes, 78.7% were polymicrobic. Respiratory (63.9%) and bloodstream (41.7%) infections predominated, with Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Candida species frequently identified. Carbapenem resistance was particularly high in K. pneumoniae (87.5%) and A. baumannii (90.0%). Mortality increased substantially with disease severity, reaching 43.1% without sepsis, 72.3% with sepsis without shock, and 82.6% with septic shock. Sepsis severity, advanced age, and mechanical ventilation independently predicted death. Carbapenem resistance was associated with mortality, potentially reflecting early deaths and incomplete microbiological documentation. Conclusions: HAI-associated sepsis in this ICU population was characterised by frequent polymicrobic infections, extensive antimicrobial resistance, and exceptionally high mortality. These findings highlight the importance of infection prevention, early recognition of clinical deterioration, and improved microbiological surveillance to support timely treatment decisions and better patient outcomes.

articles.title: Association and Discrimination of Admission sAlb/Cr, BAR, and the RIN-IM Score for In-Hospital Acute Kidney Injury: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to compared the associations and apparent discrimination of admission serum albumin-to-creatinine ratio (sAlb/Cr), blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio (BAR), and the previously published Renal-Inflammatory-Nutritional-Metabolic Index (RIN-IM) Score for incident in-hospital acute kidney injury (AKI) and to explore their incremental value beyond clinical characteristics and renal function. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 400 adults hospitalized in an internal medicine department between January 2022 and March 2026. Patients with admission AKI were excluded. An acceptable stable preadmission creatinine and post-index creatinine follow-up were required. Incident AKI was ascertained using KDIGO serum creatinine criteria. Each index was evaluated in a separate logistic regression model adjusted for age, sex, and pre-existing comorbidities. Standalone receiver operating characteristic AUCs were compared using paired DeLong tests with Holm adjustment. Incremental performance was evaluated against a renal reference model incorporating clinical covariates, admission creatinine, and stable preadmission creatinine, with bootstrap internal validation. Results: Incident AKI occurred in 92 patients (23.0%). Adjusted odds ratios per one-unit increase were 0.70 (95% CI, 0.58-0.84) for sAlb/Cr and 1.18 (95% CI, 1.11-1.26) for BAR; the corresponding estimate per one-point increase in RIN-IM was 1.68 (95% CI, 1.45-1.95). Apparent standalone AUCs were 0.788 (95% CI, 0.739-0.837) for sAlb/Cr, 0.826 (95% CI, 0.779-0.873) for BAR, and 0.889 (95% CI, 0.854-0.925) for RIN-IM. RIN-IM had the highest apparent standalone AUC among the three indices. Conclusions: RIN-IM showed a modest incremental improvement in discrimination beyond a model incorporating clinical characteristics and renal function. This improvement does not establish clinically actionable benefit. Independent external validation and prospective assessment of score-guided management are required before routine implementation.

articles.title: Development of a One-Stop Bone Mineral Density Estimation Model Based on Dual-Energy CT with Quantitative Computed Tomography as the Reference Standard.
articles.abstract: Background: This study intended to explore potential diagnostic criteria for bone status evaluation using a dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) material decomposition technique through comparison with quantitative computed tomography (QCT). Methods: In total, 355 patients who underwent abdominal unenhanced and contrast-enhanced (arterial-, venous- and delayed-phase) DECT were randomly divided into training group A with 255 cases and validation group B with 100 cases (sex was coded as 1 for male and 2 for female). Group A was further divided into four groups, a, b, c, d, according to age (<30 years, 30-49 years, 50-69 years, ≥70 years). QCT standard scanning and reconstruction parameters were adopted for the unenhanced phase, while spectral imaging mode was applied for all enhanced phases. The hydroxyapatite (iodine) density (DHAP (iodine)) in the trabecular bone of L1-L3 vertebral bodies was measured and averaged, alongside QCT-derived bone mineral density (BMD). Spearman's correlation test was used to analyze the relationship between DECT and QCT BMD measurements. DHAP (iodine) of osteoporosis, osteopenia and normal vertebral bodies were compared by one-way ANOVA. ROC curves were constructed to determine the optimal diagnostic thresholds of DHAP (iodine) for differentiating the three bone status categories. The correlated fitting curves between DHAP (iodine) and two variables (age and sex) were established separately for each subgroup in group A. The regression formula from group A was used to estimate BMD in group B. The differences between measured and formula-calculated BMD in group B were assessed. Results: DHAP (iodine) of L1-L3 vertebral bodies showed no significant differences across the three contrast-enhanced CT phases (all p > 0.05). In group A, DHAP (iodine) was positively related to QCT BMD (r = 0.968, p < 0.001). The differences in DHAP (iodine) among different age groups were statistically significant (p < 0.001) with no correlation to age in group a (p > 0.05), but negative correlations with age in groups b, c and d (r = -0.399, -0.489, -0.397, all p < 0.05). No significant sex-related correlation was identified in groups a, b and d (all p > 0.05), while a negative correlation with sex was present in group c (r = -0.233, p < 0.05). For patients aged 30 years and above, DHAP (iodine) showed a strong overall inverse correlation with age (r = -0.731, p < 0.001), with no significant correlation between DHAP (iodine) and sex (p > 0.05): DHAP (iodine) = -1.053 * age + 755.517 (2 mg/cm3). There were significant differences in DHAP (iodine) among osteoporosis, osteopenia and normal groups (p < 0.001). For the diagnosis of osteopenia using the threshold DHAP (iodine) ≤ 694.89 (2 mg/cm3), the area under the ROC curve, sensitivity and specificity were calculated as 0.990, 93.50% and 96.60%. The corresponding values for identifying osteoporosis were 0.962, 90.30%, 90.90% and with DHAP (iodine) ≤ 677.93 (2 mg/cm3), respectively. In group B, formula-calculated BMD showed high agreement with measured BMD. Conclusions: The one-stop DECT-based estimation model for vertebral BMD quantification shows technical feasibility and promising diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Three-Dimensional Evaluation of the Relationships Among Mandibular Asymmetry, Osseous Nasal Septal Deviation, and Anterior Nasal Spine Deviation in Orthognathic Surgery Candidates: A Retrospective CBCT Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Craniofacial asymmetry is a multicomponent morphological condition involving anatomical regions to varying degrees. This study examined associations of Menton (Me) deviation with maximum osseous nasal septal deviation, anterior nasal spine (ANS) deviation, and mandibular ramus/body asymmetries in orthognathic surgery candidates. Methods: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included preoperative cone-beam computed tomography records of 61 orthognathic surgery candidates. Sagittal and vertical skeletal characteristics were recorded descriptively. Volumes were reoriented using a pitch-roll-yaw protocol, and a cranial midsagittal reference plane was established. Signed and absolute Me, ANS, and osseous septal deviations and bilateral Co-Go and Go-Me length differences were analyzed. Intraobserver reproducibility was assessed in 10 cases. Correlations underwent Holm adjustment; multivariable analyses used HC3-robust regression. Results: Intraobserver ICCs ranged from 0.913 to 0.991. Absolute Me deviation correlated with maximum osseous septal deviation (ρ = 0.336; Holm-adjusted p = 0.032), with a numerically stronger signed correlation (ρ = 0.513; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). The signed model was significant (R2 = 0.323; adjusted R2 = 0.274; p < 0.001); septal deviation was its only independently associated predictor (B = 0.419; 95% CI, 0.225-0.613; p < 0.001). ANS and mandibular length differences showed no consistent independent associations. Categorical directional analyses were nonsignificant; normalized asymmetry sensitivity analyses yielded similar findings. Conclusions: Me deviation was associated with maximum osseous nasal septal deviation in orthognathic surgery candidates, particularly when directional information was retained. Considering magnitude and direction may characterize this morphological association, but cross-sectional data preclude causal inference and generalizability remains uncertain.

articles.title: TurboRhythmPat and Directed Rhythm Lobish: An Explainable Multi-Selector EEG Model for Recognising Attack and Post-Attack States in Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) advances through attacks and partial recoveries, yet electroencephalography (EEG) has hardly been used to recognise an attack from the period that follows it, and most EEG models neither test unseen patients nor show which rhythm and electrode pair shaped a decision. Methods: We present an explainable model built around TurboRhythmPat, a feature extractor that codes each 15 s, 19-channel segment as 1805 addressable source-rhythm-target routes in five EEG rhythms. Four iterative feature selectors and their six pairwise intersections form ten selector branches, a self-organised k-nearest-neighbour classifier (tkNN) labels every branch, and iterative majority voting fuses the branch outputs. Directed Rhythm Lobish (DRLobish) decodes the routes behind the selected output into rhythm and electrode-pair statements. We analysed 57 recordings from 19 patients recorded during and after an attack and from 19 healthy controls. Results: Under fully nested leave-one-subject-out validation, in which every data-driven choice was made within the training participants, the attack and post-attack recordings of unseen patients were separated with 65.61% segment-level and 76.32% recording-level accuracy, and patient-level accuracy exceeded chance in 13 of 19 patients (Wilcoxon p = 0.0022). The between-person tasks did not exceed chance (37.92%, 52.51% and 33.17%), and the non-nested estimates (85.71% for attack versus post-attack) were inflated by model selection on the test participants. A permutation-based maxT test over all 1805 routes found no route after family-wise correction (smallest adjusted p = 0.076). Conclusions: Because the attack recording always came first, treatment timing was not documented, no dedicated artefact correction was applied, and the controls were older, the differences are not interpreted as relapse-related changes, and larger prospective cohorts are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Quality, Reliability, and Readability of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Information on Peri-Implant Diseases: A Comparative Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The increasing use of dental implants has been accompanied by a rise in peri-implant diseases. As artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbots are increasingly used to obtain health information, this study evaluated the reliability, quality, usefulness, and readability of responses generated by ChatGPT (GPT-4), Copilot (Smart GPT-5), and Gemini (3.0 Flash) to questions about peri-implant diseases. Methods: Thirty-two AI-generated patient-oriented questions about peri-implant diseases were submitted to each chatbot. The responses were evaluated using the Global Quality Score (GQS), a 4-point usefulness scale, the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) tool, the Flesch Reading Ease (FRE), and the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL). Inter-rater agreement before consensus was assessed using single-measure, absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Statistical analyses included the Shapiro-Wilk, Kruskal-Wallis, post hoc Bonferroni, and Spearman correlation tests. Results: ChatGPT and Gemini had higher FRE scores and lower FKGL scores than Copilot (all adjusted p < 0.001). Copilot and Gemini had higher mDISCERN scores than ChatGPT (both adjusted p < 0.001), with no significant difference between Copilot and Gemini (adjusted p = 0.129). GQS and usefulness scores did not differ significantly across chatbots. Across the three chatbots, Spearman correlation coefficients ranged from -0.973 to -0.844 for the correlation between FRE and FKGL scores and from -0.773 to -0.509 for the correlation between GQS and usefulness scores. Conclusions: ChatGPT and Gemini produced easier-to-read responses than Copilot, while Copilot and Gemini scored higher than ChatGPT on mDISCERN. The chatbots showed no significant differences in overall quality or usefulness scores. Given their potential limitations in clinical depth, AI-generated responses should be used only as supplementary educational resources and should not replace professional medical advice.

articles.title: Effects of Topical Products Used on the Facial Region on Intraoral Radiographic Image Parameters: An Exploratory In Vitro PSP Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This exploratory in vitro study evaluated the effects of topical facial products on quantitative pixel-level parameters of intraoral radiographic images under different exposure conditions using a photostimulable phosphor (PSP) system. Methods: Six groups were tested: inorganic sunscreen, organic sunscreen, BB cream, CC cream, silver (Ag) sulfadiazine 1%, and an untreated control. To isolate the individual radiographic signature of each formulation from anatomical confounders, the products were applied at a dose of 2 mg/cm2 to a homogeneous silicone soft-tissue phantom and imaged under three protocols (60 kVp/7 mA/0.080 s, pediatric anterior; 60 kVp/7 mA/0.160 s, adult anterior; 63 kVp/6 mA/0.200 s, adult posterior) with three independent acquisitions per group and protocol (54 images). Six parameters were measured in ImageJ: brightness, uniformity, signal-to-noise ratio, histogram clipping, noise, and uniformity index. Data were analyzed by two-way ANOVA with Dunnett post hoc testing and Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction. Results: Compared to the control, the BB cream showed significant differences in uniformity (higher SD), noise (higher), and uniformity index (higher; i.e., greater uniformity among the ROI means); the CC cream showed significant differences in histogram clipping (higher), noise (higher), and uniformity index (higher) (all BH-adjusted p ≤ 0.011). Silver sulfadiazine increased histogram clipping (BH-adjusted p = 0.002), while the inorganic sunscreen altered the uniformity index (BH-adjusted p = 0.042). The organic sunscreen did not differ from the control in the primary analysis. Neither exposure protocol nor the group-by-protocol interaction reached significance, although the study was powered only for large effects and exposure dependence cannot be excluded. Conclusions: Products containing metal oxides or silver sulfadiazine produced formulation-specific changes in quantitative imaging parameters, whereas the organic sunscreen tested in this study showed no significant difference from the control. This study did not test whether the observed differences are clinically visible or whether software processing can render them visible. The findings serve as a reference for subsequent research involving anatomical phantoms and observer-based studies.

articles.title: Elective Endovascular Treatment of True Splenic Artery Aneurysms According to Aneurysm Anatomy and Arterial Preservation.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate single-center elective endovascular treatment of true (splenic artery aneurysms) SAAs according to aneurysm anatomy, morphology, Shu classification and preservation/occlusion of involved artery. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing elective endovascular treatment of true SAAs, including polar and intraparenchymal branches, between October 2012 and August 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Computed tomography angiography assessed morphology, location, Shu classification, and outflow branches. Techniques included packing, stent-assisted coil embolization, sandwich technique and covered stent-grafting. Thirty-day outcomes included: technical success, post-embolization syndrome, splenic infarction, reintervention, mortality. Follow-up outcomes included: estimated freedom from splenic infarction, from sac reperfusion, from reintervention, and survival. Results: Thirty-four patients with 43 SAAs were included; mean aneurysm diameter was 19.4 ± 8.7 mm, and 8 patients (24%) had multiple aneurysms. Patency-preserving strategies were used in 14 aneurysms (32%), whereas arterial occlusion was performed in 29 (68%). Technical success was 100%. Post-embolization syndrome occurred in three patients (8.8%), and partial splenic infarction in six (17.6%). Five patients (14.7%) required early access-related reintervention. No 30-day deaths or splenectomies occurred. During a mean follow-up of 37.5 ± 35.2 months, two aneurysms developed sac reperfusion requiring aneurysm-related reintervention. No additional splenic infarctions were detected on the available follow-up imaging. Kaplan-Meier estimates of freedom from sac reperfusion and aneurysm-related reintervention were 97%, 97%, and 90% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. Conclusions: Elective endovascular treatment of true splenic artery aneurysms achieved high technical success and favorable observed outcomes. Treatment strategies varied according to aneurysm anatomy, with arterial occlusion frequently performed for distal lesions. Partial splenic infarction occurred without splenectomy. These descriptive findings require confirmation in larger studies with standardized longitudinal follow-up.

articles.title: Prediction of COVID-19 Outcome Using Machine Learning and Clinical Data for North Macedonia.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This retrospective methodological case study evaluated outcome classification in the first 501 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases in North Macedonia (37 deaths; 7.39%). Methods: Six machine learning classifiers were compared with ZeroR and ridge logistic regression using stratified 10-fold cross-validation, supplemented by five repetitions. The primary analysis used 19 demographic, symptom and comorbidity predictors without hospitalization status. Symptom timestamps were unavailable, so performance at initial assessment could not be established. Results: J48 matched the majority-class accuracy of 92.6%; no classifier exceeded it. Naïve Bayes achieved the highest AUROC (0.863), MCC (0.369) and Death-class sensitivity (0.486). Logistic regression achieved AUROC 0.800 (95% CI 0.709-0.891), numerically exceeding five of the six machine learning classifiers; the conventional benchmark was competitive. Its repeated cross-validation AUROC was 0.801 ± 0.003. Bagging had the lowest Brier score (0.058), whereas Naïve Bayes and Random Tree had negative scaled Brier scores despite their discrimination above chance. Including hospitalization increased the Naïve Bayes AUROC to 0.893 and sensitivity to 0.649. Decision curves suggested net benefit at selected thresholds, but uncertainty and miscalibration limit interpretation. Separate exploratory permutation and SHAP analyses of a scikit-learn Random Forest reconstruction identified difficulty breathing, age and cardiovascular disease as prominent contributors; these explanations cannot be attributed directly to the evaluated WEKA ensemble. Conclusions: The contribution is a cohort-specific demonstration of how accuracy, discrimination, calibration and net benefit can support different conclusions, rather than a new algorithm or deployable mortality model. The small event count, uncertain predictor timing and absence of external validation preclude clinical implementation.

articles.title: Report-Supervised Vision-Language Alignment for Label-Efficient Bronchoscopic Finding Recognition.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fine-grained annotation of bronchoscopic findings is costly, whereas every bronchoscopic image is already described in the examination report. This single-centre proof-of-concept study investigated whether routine report text can serve as supervision for bronchoscopic finding recognition. Methods: BiomedCLIP was aligned with the image-caption pairs of the publicly available Bronchoscopy Examination Report Dataset (BERD; 4826 training images) using standard contrastive learning, a caption-aware objective that treats identical captions as positives, and a label-aware reference. The encoders were evaluated on the official test set, excluding three images duplicated from the training set (313 images, 180 patients), for zero-shot recognition of 23 report-derived finding categories, cross-modal retrieval, linear probing with 1-100% of the labelled training patients, and fine-tuning, using a hierarchical patient-level bootstrap and three training seeds. Results: Without training on finding labels, alignment raised zero-shot macro AUPRC from 0.184 to 0.255-0.278 and macro AUC-ROC from 0.59 to 0.77-0.78, and the gain held across ten prompt formulations. Retrieval generalised to captions never seen during training. With 1-25% of the labelled patients, linear probes on report-aligned features outperformed DINOv2, Swin-T and pretrained BiomedCLIP; with 5%, they exceeded DINOv2 and Swin-T trained with all labels. Caption-aware training showed no measurable benefit over standard contrastive training, full fine-tuning did not improve macro F1, and absolute performance remained modest (macro F1 at most 0.32). Conclusions: In this single-centre dataset, report text was an effective source of supervision for recognising report-derived finding categories with few labels; independent reference standards and external validation are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Bilateral Extensive Retinal Dialysis-Associated Macula-On Retinal Detachment and Pupillary Block in a 60-Year-Old Patient After Silicone Oil Removal and SF6 Gas Tamponade.
articles.abstract: Retinal dialysis is an uncommon cause of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD), typically associated with ocular trauma and occurring predominantly in young men. Bilateral extensive retinal dialysis-associated RRD in older patients is particularly rare. Although scleral buckling is a commonly used surgical approach, pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) may be considered in selected cases with complex vitreoretinal pathology.We report a case of a 60-year-old man with bilateral extensive retinal dialysis-associated macula-on RRD. The extent of retinal dialysis was approximately 225° in the right eye and 270° in the left eye. Both eyes demonstrated everted retinal edges, marked peripheral vitreoretinal traction, retinal tissue bridges, and complete posterior vitreous detachment. Bilateral phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation and PPV were performed, including perfluorocarbon liquid-assisted retinal reattachment, relaxing retinectomy, endolaser photocoagulation, and silicone oil tamponade. Three months later, silicone oil was removed and replaced with 25% SF6 gas in both eyes. Three to four days after gas administration, both eyes developed elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), reaching 34 mmHg in the right eye and 36 mmHg in the left eye, accompanied by clinically documented iris bombe, suggesting a possible pupillary-block mechanism. In the right eye, unsuccessful laser peripheral iridotomy necessitated surgical iridectomy and synechiolysis, whereas the left eye was successfully managed with laser peripheral iridotomy and intensive topical IOP-lowering treatment. At one year after the final surgical procedure, the retina remained attached in both eyes. Visual acuity remained stable at 0.9 in the right eye and 0.8 in the left eye. IOP was 18-20 mmHg without ongoing topical IOP-lowering medication. This case describes an unusual bilateral presentation of extensive retinal dialysis-associated macula-on RRD in an older patient, followed by bilateral postoperative pupillary block after silicone oil removal and SF6 gas tamponade. It highlights the importance of postoperative anterior segment assessment and IOP monitoring, including in pseudophakic patients. As a single-case observation, these findings do not establish treatment efficacy or a causal relationship between gas tamponade and pupillary block.

articles.title: Progressive Attenuation of NF-κB p65 Signaling During Penile Lichen Sclerosus Progression: Diagnostic Implications for Histopathological Disease Assessment.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Penile lichen sclerosus (PLS) is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis characterized by progressive sclerosis and fibrosis of the penile glans and foreskin. Histopathological examination remains the reference standard for diagnosis, whereas reliable biomarkers reflecting disease activity and progression remain limited. Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) p65 (RELA), a key regulator of inflammatory and immune signaling, may provide insights into inflammatory processes associated with PLS. This study aimed to evaluate NF-κB p65 expression across different histopathological stages of PLS and explore its potential relevance to histopathological disease staging. Methods: Foreskin specimens obtained during circumcision from 39 patients with histologically confirmed PLS were classified as early, moderate, or severe disease. Each specimen was divided into potentially affected (PA) and potentially unaltered (PH) regions based on macroscopic appearance, with 18 normal foreskin specimens included as controls. All samples underwent hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining and immunohistochemical staining for NF-κB p65. NF-κB p65 immunoreactivity was evaluated semi-quantitatively using the immunoreactive score (IRS), while its subcellular localization was assessed descriptively. Results: Histopathological assessment showed less prominent inflammatory infiltrates in advanced stages of PLS, accompanied by more pronounced fibrotic changes. Descriptive analysis of NF-κB p65 immunohistochemical staining showed a trend toward lower immunoreactivity and less frequent nuclear localization in advanced lesions. However, differences in IRS between disease stages, PA and PH regions, and PLS and control tissues did not reach statistical significance. Histopathological examination also confirmed PLS involvement in all PH regions, indicating that macroscopically unaltered peripheral tissue was not histologically unaffected. Conclusions: The observed changes in NF-κB p65 immunoreactivity and subcellular localization may reflect differences in inflammatory processes across PLS stages; however, the present findings do not establish progressive attenuation of canonical NF-κB signaling. Although NF-κB p65 cannot currently be considered an independent diagnostic or staging marker, its immunohistochemical expression pattern warrants further investigation as a potential complementary marker in the histopathological assessment of PLS. Larger patient cohorts, particularly including more cases of severe disease, and further studies involving quantitative assessment of nuclear localization and NF-κB pathway activity are needed to determine its potential diagnostic relevance. The detection of histopathological involvement in macroscopically unaltered peripheral tissue also highlights the importance of histopathological examination beyond visibly affected areas.

articles.title: Clinicoradiological Predictors of Retro-Orbital Extension in Idiopathic Orbital Inflammation: The Role of Lateral Rectus Thickness as a Potential Imaging Marker.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to investigate the clinicoradiological factors associated with retro-orbital extension and clinical course in idiopathic orbital inflammation (IOI), with particular emphasis on quantitative extraocular muscle measurements as potential predictors of retro-orbital extension. Methods: A total of 32 patients with IOI were stratified according to retro-orbital extension (present n = 18 vs. absent n = 14) and clinical course (subacute n = 8 vs. chronic n = 24). Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings were evaluated. All patients initially received systemic corticosteroid therapy as first-line treatment. Extraocular muscle width and thickness measurements were obtained. ROC analysis was performed to assess diagnostic performance, and forward stepwise logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors. Results: Patients with retro-orbital extension had significantly worse treatment response (complete response: 55.6% vs. 100%, p = 0.016). MRI revealed higher frequencies of lateral rectus involvement (50.0% vs. 14.3%, p = 0.035), soft tissue involvement (94.4% vs. 57.1%, p = 0.011), and optic disc involvement (33.3% vs. 0.0%, p = 0.017) in the extension group. Lateral rectus thickness was significantly greater in patients with extension (4.46 mm vs. 3.42 mm, p = 0.007). ROC analysis identified lateral rectus thickness ≥ 4.125 mm as the best predictor of retro-orbital extension (AUC = 0.786, p < 0.001; sensitivity 61.1%, specificity 92.9%, PPV 91.7%). In stepwise logistic regression, lateral rectus thickness ≥ 4.125 mm remained the sole independent predictor (OR = 20.39, 95% CI: 1.92-216.40, p = 0.012). For the chronic clinical course, only redness (62.5% vs. 12.5%, p = 0.012) and inferior rectus width showed borderline significance (≤10.22 mm, AUC = 0.719, p = 0.050), with no significant predictors in logistic regression. Conclusions: Lateral rectus thickness may serve as a potential imaging marker of retro-orbital extension in idiopathic orbital inflammation, which was associated with lower complete treatment response rates in our cohort. Accordingly, we recommend that patients with lateral rectus thickness ≥ 4.125 mm be evaluated for retro-orbital extension using advanced imaging and undergo close monitoring of treatment response.

articles.title: Analytical Inclusivity of Three Commercial Real-Time PCR Platforms Against Carbapenemase Allelic Variants in Peruvian Clinical Isolates.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Rapid molecular detection of carbapenemase-producing Gram-negative bacilli is crucial for targeted antimicrobial therapy, but regional gene sequence diversity can impair commercial PCR assays. This study evaluated the analytical inclusivity of three commercial real-time PCR platforms (Xpert Carba-R on the GeneXpert system, Galaxy Lite, and Molecular Mouse) against carbapenemase alleles circulating in Peru, including the regionally relevant blaIMP-74 and blaIMP-93 alleles. Methods: We analyzed a positive-enriched challenge panel of 23 non-duplicate clinical isolates previously characterized by whole-genome sequencing (WGS): 10 Enterobacterales and 13 Pseudomonas aeruginosa carrying 26 carbapenemase genes across 12 variants (blaKPC-2/35, blaNDM-1/5, blaOXA-48/181/232, blaVIM-2, and blaIMP-16/18/74/93); inclusivity was calculated per WGS-confirmed target gene, and Molecular Mouse was evaluated on a 16-target subset including at least one representative of each allele. Results: Galaxy Lite detected all carbapenemase alleles evaluated (12/12 alleles; gene-level analytical inclusivity 100%, 26/26 target genes, 95% CI: 86.8-100%). Xpert Carba-R and Molecular Mouse each detected 8 of the 12 alleles (100% of KPC, NDM, OXA-48-like, and VIM alleles), failing to detect any of the four IMP alleles evaluated. Overall gene-level inclusivity was 53.8% (14/26 target genes, 95% CI: 33.4-73.4%) for Xpert Carba-R and 62.5% (10/16 target genes, 95% CI: 35.4-84.8%) for Molecular Mouse. Conclusions: In this small, positive-enriched panel, two of the three commercial PCR panels did not detect the IMP alleles tested, a finding that may be related to primer/probe-target sequence divergence, although this mechanism was not investigated. These results support the local verification of commercial carbapenemase PCR assays against circulating alleles before routine implementation.
authors: Gomez de la Torre Pretell JC

articles.title: Operational Performance and Turnaround Time of a Tuberculosis Diagnosis Laboratory in Panama.
articles.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis relies on the coordinated use of rapid molecular testing, microscopy, culture, and drug-resistance assays. This study evaluated laboratory performance and turnaround time (TAT) across an integrated TB diagnostic workflow in Colón Province, Panama, and compared Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) and auramine-rhodamine microscopy. Methods: A retrospective laboratory-based study included 501 unique patients with positive Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra results between January 2021 and December 2025. The routine workflow included ZN microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, BD BACTEC MGIT 320 culture, and post-culture GenoType MTBDRplus testing. A separate microscopy analysis included 300 specimens with sufficient residual material for paired ZN and auramine-rhodamine staining, using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra as the reference comparator. Results: ZN microscopy was positive in 96.4% (483/501) of Xpert-positive specimens, and ZN positivity increased significantly across Xpert semiquantitative categories (p for trend < 0.001). Among specimens with final positive MGIT cultures, increasing Xpert semiquantitative category was strongly associated with shorter MGIT TAT (Spearman's ρ = -0.728, p < 0.001). Initial MGIT contamination occurred in 5.2% (25/480) of cultures; cultures recovered after contamination had a longer median TAT than those without initial contamination (24 vs. 16 days, p < 0.001). Auramine-rhodamine microscopy showed higher sensitivity than ZN microscopy [96.8% (95% CI, 92.8-98.6) vs. 88.0% (95% CI, 82.0-92.2)] and stronger agreement with Xpert [κ = 0.967 (95% CI, 0.938-0.996) vs. 0.874 (95% CI, 0.819-0.928)]. Conclusions: The integrated laboratory workflow supported rapid initial TB diagnosis while maintaining culture and drug-resistance testing capacity. Molecular bacterial burden was associated with smear positivity and culture TAT, while fluorescence microscopy showed improved performance relative to ZN microscopy. Culture recovery procedures preserved diagnostic yield despite delays related to contamination.

articles.title: CNN-ViT-Based Model Incorporating a Voting-Based Ensemble Method with Future Fusion for Multiple Sclerosis Classification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease affecting the central nervous system and significantly reducing the quality of life. Early detection of the disease is critical for slowing its progression and developing appropriate treatment plans. In recent years, artificial intelligence and deep learning methods have begun to play a significant role in clinical decision support systems, particularly due to their high accuracy rates in the analysis of Magnetic Resonance (MR) images. Methods: In this study, a hybrid model was developed for the automatic classification of MS. Two different architectures were used for feature extraction in the developed model. These architectures were selected from among the most successful architectures out of 10 different Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures. Six different classifiers were used to classify the feature maps obtained in the proposed model and pre-trained models. The application of the VOTE operation in the final stage of the proposed model improved its performance. Results: The proposed model yielded competitive results compared to similar studies in the literature and the CNN and ViT architectures used in this study. The accuracy rate achieved with the proposed hybrid model was 97.28%. Conclusions: These results indicate that the proposed model has the potential to support computer-aided MS detection and may provide a useful framework for clinical decision support systems.

articles.title: AI-Assisted Follow-Up MRI Interpretation in Multiple Sclerosis: Radiology Residents' Diagnostic Confidence and Performance.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are becoming increasingly utilised in everyday radiological practice. Evaluating follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) is challenging. The aim of this study was to assess changes in confidence among four participating radiology residents when evaluating follow-up MRIs of MS patients using Pixyl.Neuro.MS® software. Methods: This retrospective study included 78 MS patients. Previous and new FLAIR images were independently analysed by four residents, first without AI and then in an immediate AI-assisted second reading using Pixyl.Neuro.MS®, a deep-learning lesion-segmentation software. Readers recorded their findings and confidence after each reading and rated the impact and usefulness of AI. The reference standard was defined by a consensus reading of a neuroradiologist and a radiology resident (15 and 4 years of experience). Paired analyses and patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals were used; bootstrap inference was conditional on the four readers. Results: The reference standard identified 24 patients with new lesions. Mean accuracy across readers increased from 84.62% to 90.71% (difference, 6.09 percentage points; 95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 2.24-10.26). Only Reader 3 showed a significant accuracy increase after Holm adjustment (p = 0.025). No accuracy comparison with routine reports was significant after adjustment. Confidence increased for all readers (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Perceived usefulness did not differ significantly between lesion-burden groups. All readers predominantly rated the impact of AI as positive. The second-reading phase was shorter by a mean of 59.35 s (95% bootstrap CI, 51.39-67.07). Conclusions: In these four residents, the AI-assisted second reading was associated with higher confidence and average accuracy. The immediate sequential design prevents separation of AI contributions from familiarity and order effects, and the shorter second-reading phase does not establish an overall workflow time saving.

articles.title: Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Pretrained Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classifiers: A Retrospective External Validation of Seven Models.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chest radiograph classifiers are usually benchmarked within their training distribution, whereas deployment exposes them to new populations, equipment, and labeling conventions. This study quantified out-of-distribution (OOD) performance of seven public pretrained classifiers. Methods: Six DenseNet-121 models and one ResNet-50 TorchXRayVision model were evaluated without fine-tuning on 18,424 Brazilian BRAX studies for seven common labels. The in-distribution (ID) performances of the three models trained on ChestX-ray14 were measured on held-out patients. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) were compared with a paired patient-level bootstrap; calibration, operating points, and subgroups were assessed. Results: OOD macro AUROC was 0.733-0.741 for three models trained with PadChest and 0.652-0.677 for four single-source models (all between-group differences significant). Relative to held-out ID performance, macro AUROC decreased by 6.0-11.4 percentage points. Expected calibration error of default outputs (0.028-0.392) largely reflected score normalization and fell to 0.001-0.003 after recalibration; sensitivity at default operating points was 0.035-0.797. Macro AUROC was lower for anteroposterior than posteroanterior radiographs (0.499-0.605 vs. 0.691-0.796), also within age groups; residual confounding remains possible. Conclusions: In this single Brazilian cohort, ID benchmarks overestimated external performance, and default outputs and operating points did not transfer. Local validation, recalibration, and subgroup-stratified reporting are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Mask-Guided Two-Stage Synthesis and Regional Quantitative Evaluation of Virtual Contrast-Enhanced Thoracic CT.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Virtual contrast-enhanced CT (vCECT) synthesis may support imaging workflows when iodinated contrast administration is undesirable. However, whole-image similarity can obscure errors in localized vascular enhancement. We evaluated a mask-guided two-stage framework that couples spatially targeted enhancement with separate assessment of localization and synthesis. Methods: This retrospective study included 50 patients with 2550 paired thoracic non-enhanced CT (NECT) and contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) slices from radiotherapy simulation. Stage 1 predicted a contrast-region mask from NECT; Stage 2 used this mask to guide residual synthesis, trained with locally blended pseudo-contrast targets. Localization was assessed using segmentation metrics, and synthesis was evaluated against reference CECT over the whole image and reference-mask regions of interest (ROIs). Ablations compared single-stage residual synthesis, predicted-mask guidance, and reference-mask guidance. Results: Mask prediction achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.91. Whole-image peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index were 46.91 dB and 0.96, respectively; ROI values were 34.22 dB and 0.95. Compared with single-stage synthesis, predicted-mask guidance increased ROI PSNR from 18.97 to 34.22 dB and reduced normalized root mean squared error from 0.12 to 0.03. Reference-mask guidance achieved an ROI PSNR of 36.13 dB. Conclusions: Explicit localization improved regional synthesis fidelity in this cohort. The framework links localized CT enhancement to quantitative image-quality evaluation; external and reader-based validation remain necessary before clinical use.

articles.title: Endoscopic OCT with Attenuation Mapping for In Vivo Assessment of "Thin Endometrium" State: A Descriptive Case Series.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: "Thin endometrium" is considered an important factor in infertility and pregnancy loss and in assisted reproductive technology (ART) failure, as it may substantially reduce endometrial receptivity and the likelihood of successful embryo implantation. The chronic nature of these pathological changes and the often-limited effectiveness of therapy due to the variability of treatment approaches complicate the assessment of structural abnormalities of the endometrium at early stages. Methods: In this preliminary study, we applied, for the first time in vivo, endoscopic optical coherence tomography (OCT) with depth-resolved optical attenuation coefficient (OAC) mapping to describe the microstructural features of "thin endometrium." The analysis included four women with reproductive disorders (secretory-phase endometrial thickness ≤ 7 mm on ultrasound) who underwent hysteroscopy followed by pipelle biopsy. Results: OAC maps provided higher contrast than conventional structural OCT images. As a proof-of-concept, we explored an OAC threshold of 15 mm-1, with values above this threshold observed in regions of increased endometrial stromal density, including areas of extracellular matrix deposition and vascular wall fibrosis, in the patients examined. These OAC values are preliminary, descriptive observations and are not validated as diagnostic criteria. Conversely, regions with endometrial glands were characterized by low OAC values (<5 mm-1), while areas of stromal edema showed intermediate values (6-14 mm-1). Moreover, OCT scans and endometrial OAC maps in which the glandular component predominated or was present in a comparable proportion to the stromal component appeared to exhibit a more elongated, longitudinally striped texture compared with endometrium with low glandular content and stromal predominance with fibrotic changes. Conclusions: It can be hypothesized that OCT with OAC mapping may eventually enable in vivo, minimally invasive, real-time assessment of the structural features of "thin endometrium", thus complementing biopsy and, in the long term, contributing to personalized approaches for restoring implantation potential during treatment.

articles.title: Association Between Plasma Homocysteine Levels and Peripapillary Vessel Density in Patients with Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome Without Glaucoma.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The relationship between circulating homocysteine (Hcy) and ocular microvascular alterations in pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PXS) remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between plasma Hcy concentrations and peripapillary vessel density (VD) in patients with PXS without clinically evident glaucoma and controls. Methods: This single-center, cross-sectional observational study with prospective recruitment included three groups: patients with PXS and Hcy < 15 µmol/L, patients with PXS and Hcy ≥ 15 µmol/L, and controls without PXS. Fasting plasma Hcy was measured using chemiluminescent immunoassay. Peripapillary VD was quantified from optical coherence tomography angiography images using ImageJ (version 1.54, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD, USA). Generalized estimating equations accounted for inter-eye correlation and assessed associations adjusted for age, intraocular pressure, and PXS status. PXS-only and single-eye sensitivity analyses were performed. Results: VD analyses included 71 eyes from 60 participants. Mean peripapillary VD was 62.3 ± 7.2%, 54.1 ± 6.4%, and 66.3 ± 6.3% in the respective groups (overall p < 0.001). In the full cohort, each 1 µmol/L increase in Hcy was associated with a 0.30-percentage-point decrease in VD (95% CI, -0.57 to -0.03; p = 0.029). Associations remained inverse but were not statistically significant in the PXS-only analysis (B = -0.25; p = 0.114) or single-eye sensitivity analysis (B = -0.28; p = 0.077). Global retinal nerve fiber layer thickness did not differ significantly among groups. Conclusions: Higher plasma Hcy was associated with lower peripapillary VD in the full cohort, but evidence within PXS remained inconclusive. These exploratory cross-sectional findings do not establish causality or prognostic value and require confirmation in larger longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Structure of the Discretised Complete Blood Count Profile Space: A Reproducible Analysis of 700,000 Records.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Qualitative complete blood count (CBC) profiles, formed by classifying each result relative to its reference interval, underlie rule-based interpretation and autoverification. The structure of the resulting profile space has not been characterised. Methods: We analysed 729,469 adult CBC records from 414,907 patients (14 analytes; Sysmex XN-10; January 2024-May 2025). The results were coded into five ordinal states relative to each record's reference interval. We measured concentration, diversity, algebraic dependence and unobserved richness under three reference interval frameworks and at the patient level. Results: Under the laboratory's limits, the records formed 40,376 distinct profiles. Seven profiles covered half of the records; the all-normal profile covered 42.2%. Removing four algebraically dependent analytes contracted the observed space by 63.0%; their discretised states were not fully determined by the other analytes. New profiles kept appearing, so the tail of the distribution remained open: with the framework held constant, 3.03% of the 2025 records carried a profile that was unseen in 2024 (predicted, 3.06%). Across the frameworks, the number of profiles varied 1.65-fold, but the concentrated head (a few profiles covering most records), the open tail and the contraction (52.3-63.0%) persisted. With one record per patient, the concentration was higher and the tail remained open. Conclusions: In this corpus, the reference framework changed the coordinates of the profile space (the number of profiles and the all-normal share) but not its structural properties. These properties suggest hypotheses for the design of rule-based interpretation systems.

articles.title: Can Panoramic Radiographs Verify Sibling Relationships? A Confound-Matched Diagnostic Accuracy Study Including Dizygotic Twins.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: When unidentified remains lack an ante-mortem record, relatives may be prioritised for DNA testing. Panoramic radiographs (OPGs) are routine dental records, but kinship models can exploit age or acquisition differences. We tested whether calibrated likelihood ratios (LRs) from paired OPGs can rank candidate relatives before DNA testing. Methods: Using 1117 single-centre OPGs of living patients from 560 sibling pairs confirmed by telephone (174 dizygotic twin pairs), eleven verification methods and three fusion models were evaluated by family-disjoint cross-validation against negatives matched for age, sex composition and acquisition signature. An exploratory analysis estimated sibling intraclass correlations (ICC) of 70 automatically measured phenotypes; automated tooth dimensions were compared with blinded manual measurements in 60 radiographs. Results: The primary fusion model had an AUC of 0.516 (95% CI 0.482-0.551) and a log likelihood ratio cost of 1.009; no fusion model, twin or age stratum differed from chance. Age difference alone gave an AUC of 0.778 against unmatched negatives, and adding the fusion score did not improve it. Automated tooth lengths exceeded manual lengths by 36%. Vertical tooth and mandibular dimensions resembled each other within families (held-out ICC 0.269, 95% CI 0.200-0.334), yet a Gaussian LR model gave an AUC of 0.563 and a median LR near 1.03. Conclusions: In this sample, apparent sibling discrimination on OPGs was largely explained by age. A familial resemblance was detectable, but none of the evaluated models showed evidential value, so they should not be used to prioritise relatives. Other populations, measurement methods and post-mortem radiographs were not tested.

articles.title: Postmortem Morphometric Assessment of Regional Adiposity in Relation to Histological Hepatic Steatosis: A Pilot Autopsy Study.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Hepatic steatosis is closely associated with general and visceral adiposity; however, data on its relationship with regional adipose tissue measured directly at postmortem examination remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of hepatic steatosis with body mass index (BMI), abdominal subcutaneous and regional epicardial adipose tissue thickness, and coronary atherosclerosis. Materials and Methods: This pilot autopsy study included 34 adult cases. Abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness and regional epicardial adipose tissue thickness at predefined locations along the left anterior descending (LAD), circumflex (CX), and right coronary arteries (RCA) were measured. Hepatic steatosis was histopathologically graded from S0 to S3, and coronary stenosis from G1 to G4. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were performed, and the associations between regional adipose tissue thickness and hepatic steatosis were further adjusted for BMI and age. Results: Hepatic steatosis was identified in 14 of 34 cases (41.2%). In unadjusted analyses, cases with steatosis had significantly higher BMI (p = 0.001) and greater abdominal (p = 0.014), LAD (p = 0.012), and CX (p = 0.011) adipose tissue thickness. Steatosis grade was positively correlated with BMI (ρ = 0.595; p < 0.001) and abdominal (ρ = 0.470; p = 0.005), LAD (ρ = 0.451; p = 0.007), CX (ρ = 0.488; p = 0.003), and RCA (ρ = 0.432; p = 0.011) adipose tissue thickness. However, the associations between regional adipose tissue thickness and steatosis were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for BMI. No statistically significant associations were identified between hepatic steatosis or regional epicardial adipose tissue thickness and coronary luminal stenosis. Conclusions: Hepatic steatosis was associated with higher BMI and greater regional adipose tissue thickness in unadjusted analyses. However, these associations were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for BMI. These preliminary findings suggest that general adiposity may contribute to the observed relationships, but do not establish an independent association between regional adipose tissue thickness and hepatic steatosis. Larger autopsy studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Association Between "Macular Ischemic Retinal Lesions and Severity of Diabetic Retinopathy".
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To assess the prevalence of different types of retinal ischemic lesions in type 2 diabetic patients without diabetic retinopathy (DR) and with various stages of DR. Methods: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. The presence of retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) lesions, and disorganization of retinal inner layers (DRILs) was identified using optical coherence tomography angiography. Results: Eighty-nine eyes of 89 patients were included. Seventeen (19.1%), 15 (16.9%), 29 (32.6%), and 28 (31.5%) patients had diabetes without DR, mild nonproliferative DR (NPDR), moderate-to-severe NPDR, and proliferative DR (PDR), respectively. The prevalence of all lesions increased significantly with DR severity (p < 0.001). RIPL prevalence rose from 52.9% in eyes without DR to 86.7% in mild NPDR and to 100% in both the moderate/severe NPDR and PDR groups (p < 0.001). Ischemic RNFL lesions were observed in 17.6% of eyes without DR, increasing to 66.7% in mild NPDR, to 86.2% in moderate/severe NPDR, and to 100% in eyes with PDR (p < 0.001). DRIL first appeared in eyes with moderate/severe NPDR (17.2%) and increased to 60.7% in PDR (p < 0.001). Conclusions: RIPLs, RNFL lesions, and DRIL can be considered a continuous spectrum of ischemic retinal injuries reflecting the progression of retinal ischemia in type 2 DR.

articles.title: Granulomatous Gastritis of Uncertain Aetiology in a Patient with Recurrent Serositis and Polyarthralgia.
articles.abstract: Granulomatous gastritis is a rare histopathological pattern of gastric mucosal inflammation associated with a broad spectrum of infectious, inflammatory, systemic, and medication-related conditions. We report the case of a 55-year-old female with a history of recurrent pleuritis, pericarditis, and polyarthralgia, initially accompanied by a right hilar soft tissue mass that regressed following corticosteroid therapy. Despite multiple immunosuppressive treatments and subsequent anakinra and canakinumab treatment, her symptoms persisted, and the underlying systemic disorder remained unresolved. During subsequent gastroduodenoscopy, gastric biopsies revealed moderate chronic, focally active gastritis with multifocal non-necrotizing granulomas in the antral lamina propria. The granulomas consisted of CD68-positive histiocytes, while investigations for infectious agents, including mycobacteria and fungi, yielded negative results. Helicobacter pylori immunohistochemistry was also negative in the antral specimen, although a separate corpus biopsy demonstrated Helicobacter pylori-associated gastritis. In view of the patient's systemic manifestations and histopathological findings, several potential aetiological factors were considered, including Helicobacter pylori infection and medication-induced granulomatous inflammation. However, systemic conditions such as sarcoidosis and Crohn's disease also warrant consideration and further exclusion. None of these potential causes could be definitively established based on the available clinical and histopathological findings. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of granulomatous gastritis and emphasizes the importance of integrating histopathological findings with clinical, radiological, microbiological, and serological data. Granulomas are a histological finding rather than a definitive diagnosis; identifying their underlying cause requires a multidisciplinary approach, particularly when gastric pathology occurs in the setting of unexplained systemic inflammation.

articles.title: Admission Serum 25-Hydroxyvitamin D and Survival in Older Hospitalized Adults with Delirium: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: The prognostic significance of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] among older inpatients with established delirium remains uncertain. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included 184 adults aged ≥65 years with delirium and serum 25(OH)D measured within seven days of admission during the period of 2020-2025. Outcomes were all-cause mortality and hospital length of stay. Vitamin D was modeled continuously in Cox regression; baseline comparisons were exploratory. Results: During follow-up, 47 patients (25.5%) died: 31/120 (25.8%) with 25(OH)D concentrations < 30 ng/mL and 16/64 (25.0%) with concentrations ≥30 ng/mL (log-rank p = 0.731). Median follow-up was 30.4 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier; 95% CI 28.1-34.0). The proportional-hazards-corrected multivariable Cox estimate per 10-ng/mL increase was HR 1.09 (95% CI 0.91-1.30; p = 0.354); the minimally adjusted age-sex-CCI estimate was HR 1.07 (95% CI 0.91-1.26; p = 0.407). Adjusted median length of stay was also not associated with serum 25(OH)D (difference of -0.81 days per 10-ng/mL increase, 95% CI -2.18 to 0.56; p = 0.250). Results were consistent across ward, landmark, spline, ridge-penalized, and additional sensitivity analyses. Other covariate and baseline associations were exploratory. Conclusions: Serum 25(OH)D was not significantly associated with mortality or length of stay in this selected retrospective single-center cohort of hospitalized older adults with documented delirium and timely 25(OH)D measurement. The findings were consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses, although the confidence intervals do not establish equivalence or exclude smaller associations. This study cannot evaluate delirium incidence or the effects of vitamin D supplementation. Substantial cohort exclusions, the moderate sample size, limited mortality events, and unavailable functional and frailty measures restrict generalizability. The null findings are informative within this selected population but should not be generalized beyond it without prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Expert Perspectives on Implementing Rapid Molecular Point-of-Care Testing for Respiratory Infections in Emergency Care: A CFIR-Informed Project Report.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rapid molecular point-of-care testing (mPOCT) can provide respiratory pathogen results within clinically actionable timeframes, yet implementation in emergency departments remains inconsistent. This project report aimed to examine the perceived clinical, operational, and organizational value of rapid mPOCT in emergency respiratory care and to identify key barriers and enablers to its implementation. Methods: A multidisciplinary group of point-of-care testing experts from Germany, France, Saudi Arabia, and the United Kingdom participated in sounding-board discussions, interviews, and questionnaires. Consultation outputs were synthesized from structured notes, descriptive questionnaire summaries, and facilitated discussion, and were then mapped deductively to the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research to structure implementation-related findings. Results: Experts identified rapid mPOCT as a potentially valuable tool for supporting timely diagnosis, targeted treatment, infection-control decisions, patient flow, cohorting, and resource utilization.
