However, implementation was considered to be limited by insufficient awareness of clinical and economic value, the absence of standardized pathways, logistical and information-technology challenges, and fragmented integration into hospital workflows. The group emphasized the need for clearer implementation guidance, stronger evidence generation, improved communication of health-economic value, and closer collaboration among clinical, laboratory, industry, and policy stakeholders. Conclusions: Rapid mPOCT may support emergency respiratory care by providing clinically actionable results within shorter timeframes, but its value depends on local implementation context. Its wider adoption may depend not only on test performance, but also on standardized pathways, organizational readiness, stakeholder engagement, and practical implementation support.

articles.title: Molecular Diagnostic Yield of NGS and MLPA/FISH in Neurofibromatosis Type 1: A Regional Romanian Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) has variable clinical expression and marked allelic heterogeneity. This study assessed the diagnostic yield of molecular testing in a regional Romanian cohort with an initial clinical diagnosis of NF1 and described the clinical features of patients with NF1 molecular findings. Methods: This retrospective study included 77 patients evaluated between 1990 and 2025. We reviewed the use and results of next-generation sequencing (NGS), multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA), and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). Results: Of the 77 patients, 42 (54.5%) underwent molecular testing. NGS was performed in 36 patients, MLPA in 15, and FISH in 7. NGS identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic NF1 sequence variants in 30 of 36 sequenced patients (83.3%), representing 30 of 42 tested patients (71.4%). In one additional patient with a negative NGS result, MLPA detected a suspected intragenic NF1 deletion that was not independently confirmed. Including this finding, the observed yield was 31/36 (86.1%) among sequenced patients and 31/42 (73.8%) among all tested patients. FISH detected no 17q11.2 microdeletions. One patient had an NF1 variant of uncertain significance. Each of the three recurrent NF1 variants was observed within a single family. A homozygous pathogenic MSH6 variant led to the reclassification of one patient as having constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (CMMRD). Conclusions: NGS identified a pathogenic or likely pathogenic NF1 variant in 30 of the 36 sequenced patients. Because access to testing and the methods used varied across the cohort, this proportion applies to the sequenced subgroup. In one child initially diagnosed with NF1, molecular testing established a diagnosis of CMMRD.

articles.title: Prediction of Malignant Upgrade in B3 Breast Lesions: Development of Multiparametric Risk Scoring Model.
articles.abstract: Background: Breast lesions of uncertain malignant potential (B3 lesions) represent a heterogeneous group with variable risks of malignant upgrade, making the choice between surveillance and surgical excision challenging. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a practical multiparametric risk model for predicting malignant upgrade in patients with B3 breast lesions. Materials and Methods: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 356 B3 lesions diagnosed by image-guided 16-gauge core needle biopsy between 2011 and 2025 were evaluated. Of these, 112 were managed with surveillance and 244 underwent surgical excision. Malignant upgrade, defined as ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive carcinoma in the biopsied (index) lesion on the excision specimen, was assessed among excised lesions; carcinomas in a separate focus were analysed separately. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of upgrade, and a simplified risk score was derived from the final model. Model performance was assessed using ROC analysis, bootstrap resampling, and 10-fold cross-validation, with variable selection repeated within each resample and fold. Results: Index-lesion-related malignant upgrade occurred in 46 of 244 excised lesions (18.9%; 13 DCIS and 33 invasive carcinomas); five further carcinomas in a focus separate from the biopsied lesion (2.0%) were analysed separately. Increasing age, high BI-RADS category (4B-5), microcalcifications, atypia on biopsy, and hormone replacement therapy use were independently associated with upgrade; lesion size > 10 mm was not. The full model showed high discrimination (AUC, 0.948; optimism-corrected AUC, 0.930; 10-fold cross-validation AUC, 0.918). The derived 0-16-point score achieved an AUC of 0.945 (optimism-corrected, 0.926) and stratified lesions into low- (0-7 points; 2.8%), intermediate- (8-10 points; 50.0%), and high-risk (11-16 points; 86.2%) groups. The bootstrap-corrected Brier score was 0.082, with a bootstrap-corrected calibration slope of 0.79. Conclusions: A simple risk score integrating routinely available clinical, radiological, and histopathological variables demonstrated high discriminatory performance for malignant upgrade in B3 breast lesions in this selected retrospective cohort. Safe omission of surgery and a reduction in unnecessary procedures have not yet been demonstrated; external and prospective validation is required before this tool can support individualized decision-making.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Urinary Keratin 17 Immunocytochemistry (URO17®) During Hematuria Evaluation: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Urinary biomarkers may assist hematuria risk stratification, but diagnostic performance must be assessed against an appropriate reference standard. We evaluated urinary keratin 17 immunocytochemistry (URO17®) during hematuria evaluation and compared it with urine cytology. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included adults evaluated between August 2019 and March 2026. The analytic cohort comprised 746 specimens from 612 patients. Formal diagnostic accuracy analyses used one result-independently selected specimen per patient in the reference-standard cohort. URO17® positivity was defined as at least 10 keratin 17-positive cells. Sensitivity and specificity were compared using paired McNemar tests; atypical cytology was classified as negative in the primary comparison. Results: The reference-standard analysis included 313 patients, including 20 with histopathologically confirmed urothelial carcinoma. URO17® sensitivity was 90.0% (95% confidence interval, 69.9-97.2), specificity 90.1% (86.1-93.0), and negative predictive value 99.2% (97.3-99.8). Cytology sensitivity was 20.0% and specificity 98.6%. URO17® was 70.0 percentage points more sensitive and 8.5 percentage points less specific (both p < 0.001). Quantitative cell counts yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.938. Patients without reference-standard verification were analyzed descriptively. Conclusions: URO17® demonstrated higher sensitivity but lower specificity than conventional cytology when atypical cytology was classified as negative. The high negative predictive value reflects, in part, the 6.4% cancer prevalence in the verified cohort. Selective verification and the small number of cancer-positive patients limit interpretation. Prospective multicenter validation is needed to define its adjunctive clinical role.

articles.title: Comparison of Actin FSL and Pathromtin SL aPTT Reagents in Patients Receiving Efanesoctocog Alfa: A Retrospective Laboratory Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Efanesoctocog alfa (EFA) is an extended half-life factor VIII (FVIII) concentrate. Although FVIII assay variability in EFA monitoring is established, data on the comparability of activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) reagents remain limited. This study compared Actin FSL and Pathromtin SL in post-infusion EFA samples, assessed lot-to-lot variability, and evaluated aPTT performance in detecting reduced FVIII activity. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study analyzed 106 paired samples from 53 patients receiving once-weekly EFA at trough level, peak level (1 h post-infusion), or follow-up (median 4.0 days). FVIII activity was measured using an Actin FSL-based one-stage clotting assay with FVIII-deficient plasma. aPTT was determined using Actin FSL and Pathromtin SL on Sysmex coagulation analyzers. Method comparison included Passing-Bablok regression and modified Bland-Altman analysis. Results: Pathromtin SL produced longer clotting times (mean bias: 5.2 s, mean relative difference: 13.1%). Both aPTT reagents showed a strong correlation in post-infusion EFA samples (Pearson's r = 0.878). No significant differences in regression slopes were observed across reagent lot combinations; maximum relative inter-lot difference was 6.5%. Using assay-specific cut-offs, both aPTT assays showed 100% sensitivity for detecting FVIII activity < 30% in this cohort. Nevertheless, prolonged aPTT values also occurred at FVIII activity ≥ 30%, indicating limited specificity. Conclusions: Both Actin FSL and Pathromtin SL aPTT assays identified all samples with Actin FSL-based FVIII activity < 30%. However, significantly longer clotting times with Pathromtin SL necessitate assay-specific interpretation in clinical practice. Findings should be interpreted considering the limited sample size, retrospective single-center design and potential methodological dependency.

articles.title: Reappraisal of Blood Markers in Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss Using a Single-Center OMOP Common Data Model: Associations with Onset, Baseline Severity, and Recovery Across Clinical Axes and Sampling Timings.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to reappraise the practice of treating admission-day blood values as a fixed baseline in sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL). Blood markers were grouped into clinical axes A (acute cellular stress), B (reserve/protein), and C (acute-phase response) and tested for associations with onset, baseline pure-tone average (PTA), and recovery at timings E0, Eb, and Δ. Methods: First SSNHL episodes were identified in a single-center OMOP CDM (n = 5311; 2002-2025). Markers were classified into three clinical axes (A/B/C), and sampling timing was separated into E0, Eb, and Δ. Prespecified hypotheses were H1 (onset OR for Eb 36-month NLR, TP, and Glb), H2 (E0 albumin-PTA), and H3 (E0 CAR-PTA). Onset used 1:4 age-sex matched odds ratios; PTA used linear regression; recovery used logistic regression. Exploratory analyses were controlled with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Recovery sensitivity definitions and indication-stratified rematching were applied. Results: Under H1, onset ORs were NLR 1.05 (1.03-1.07), TP 0.81 (0.73-0.90), and Glb 0.83 (0.73-0.95). Under H2, E0 albumin-PTA β was -12.94 (-17.49 to -8.40; q < 0.001). Under H3, E0 CAR-PTA β was 6.88 (1.61-12.15; q = 0.039). E0 NLR was unrelated to PTA. Recovery remained null after definition diversification and FDR. After indication-stratified rematching, the NLR onset OR and E0 albumin/CAR-PTA signals were retained. Conclusions: SSNHL blood markers should be reported by clinical axis (A/B/C) and sampling timing (E0/Eb/Δ). Onset and baseline-severity signals persist after indication adjustment, whereas evidence for recovery prediction remains weak.

articles.title: Exercise Stress Test Lactate Curves and Logistic Regression for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Detection: A Quartile-Based Analysis.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the utility of exercise stress test lactate curves combined with logistic regression modeling for the detection of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using quartile-based stratification of maximum speed at the lactate threshold (4 mmol/L). Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted comparing T2DM patients and healthy controls. Lactate levels were measured in participants undergoing standardized exercise stress testing, with the lactate threshold set at 4 mmol/L. Subjects were stratified into quartiles (Q1-Q4) based on their maximum speed at the lactate threshold. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed across 1428 tests examining physiological, biochemical, cognitive, and biomarker variables. Significant predictors identified through variable-selection procedures were incorporated into a logistic regression model. Results: ANOVA revealed 126 significant differences (8.8% overall) between T2DM patients and controls across all quartiles, with Q4 demonstrating the highest significance rate (12.8%, 46/358 tests). Key discriminatory variables included HbA1c (p < 0.01 in Q2, Q3, Q4), fasting glucose (p < 0.05 in Q2, Q3, Q4), systolic blood pressure (DER Systole, p < 0.05 across multiple quartiles), homocysteine (p < 0.01 in Q4), and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF, p < 0.05 in Q4). The logistic regression model, developed on a sample with 68.3% diabetes prevalence, identified three significant predictors: DER Systole (negative association), vitamin D (VIT_D, positive association), and lactate velocity (Vel_Lactato2, positive association). The model achieved moderate performance, with 84.5% accuracy, 97.9% sensitivity, 58.3% specificity, 82.1% precision, 93.3% negative predictive value, an F1-score of 0.882, an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.792, and a Gini coefficient of 0.583. Conclusions: The integration of exercise stress test lactate curves with logistic regression modeling provides an adequate, minimally invasive tool for T2DM detection. The quartile-based analysis reveals that physiological and biochemical differences between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals are more pronounced among those with higher aerobic capacity (Q4). The predictive model demonstrates adequate discriminatory power (AUC = 0.792) and represents an exploratory hypothesis-generating approach for diabetes risk stratification in clinical and sports medicine settings.

articles.title: Multidimensional Outcomes After Carpal Tunnel Release: An ICF-Oriented Network Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is the most common entrapment neuropathy. Clinical assessment, neurophysiological studies, ultrasonography, and patient-reported outcome measures are routinely used to evaluate the condition. However, these domains are usually investigated separately, and the relationships among them remain incompletely understood. We investigated the relationships among clinical, neurophysiological, ultrasonographic, functional, and patient-reported variables in patients with CTS undergoing surgical treatment through a network analysis based on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) model. Methods: Before surgery, patients underwent clinical assessment, handgrip dynamometry, ultrasonographic evaluation of the median nerve, neurophysiological assessment including distal motor latency (DML) of the median nerve, and completion of the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ). Clinical, ultrasonographic, and patient-reported assessments were repeated three months after surgery. Pre-post differences were analysed and correlation analyses between the variables were used to construct the network. Results: Thirty-two adults with neurophysiologically confirmed moderate-to-severe CTS were included. Significant improvements were observed in pain, handgrip strength, and BCTQ scores after surgery, whereas no significant changes were detected in ultrasonographic measurements. In the observed network, BCTQ Functional Status at follow-up showed the highest node strength and eigenvector centrality, while DML remained among the more highly connected variables. Four stable communities showed strong correspondence with the ICF classification, although bootstrap and false-discovery-rate sensitivity analyses indicated limited stability of centrality rankings. Conclusions: Patient-reported outcome measures occupied central positions in the observed CTS network, while the community structure broadly reflected ICF domains. Because centrality rankings showed limited stability, these network findings should be considered exploratory. Network analysis provides a novel framework for understanding the multidimensional nature of CTS.

articles.title: Baseline Prostate Volume and the Magnitude and Durability of the Volumetric Response After Prostatic Artery Embolization: A Retrospective Ultrasound-Based Time-to-Event Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Whether the magnitude and durability of prostate volume reduction after prostatic artery embolization (PAE) depend on baseline gland size is unclear. Methods: Retrospective single-operator study at two institutions (2015-2024): 164 of 177 consecutive men treated by PAE for benign prostatic hyperplasia with evaluable transrectal ultrasound volumetry were stratified as small (30-65 mL, n = 53), medium (>65-100 mL, n = 70) or large (>100 mL, n = 41); median follow-up was 12.8 months. The primary endpoint was relative volume reduction at nadir. Durability was analysed in a 6-month landmark cohort of early responders (n = 87), with regrowth to ≥80% of baseline as an interval-censored event (Turnbull estimator; Cox regression on midpoint-imputed event times). Results: Median reduction at nadir was 41.7%, 40.1% and 39.1% in small, medium and large glands (p = 0.39); 10 patients (6.1%) never fell below 80% of baseline. Regrowth occurred in 27 of 87 landmark patients; the probability of sustained reduction 24 months after the landmark was 0.76 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61-0.88). Baseline volume was not significantly associated with durability (hazard ratio 0.97 per 10 mL, 95% CI 0.86-1.10), consistently across sensitivity analyses and after adjustment for 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor pretreatment, which was more than twice as common in large glands; in an exploratory analysis, deeper reduction by the landmark was associated with longer durability. Conclusions: No association between baseline volume and the magnitude or durability of the volumetric response was detected, but the confidence intervals are wide and do not exclude a clinically relevant effect. The durability estimates are conditional on an early volumetric response and continued follow-up and should not be generalised to the entire treated population; residual confounding by medical therapy cannot be excluded, and the findings concern prostate volume, not clinical efficacy.

articles.title: Geriatric Forensic Cases in the Emergency Department: Clinical and Medicolegal Characteristics and Factors Associated with Same-Calendar-Day Mortality and ICU Admission.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Geriatric forensic cases pose complex clinical and medicolegal challenges; outcome evidence is limited. We characterized these cases and examined factors associated with same-calendar-day mortality and ICU admission. Methods: This single-center retrospective observational study included 243 forensic cases aged ≥65 years presenting to a tertiary emergency department from 1 January to 31 December 2025. Demographic, clinical, and medicolegal data were extracted from hospital records and forensic reports. Multivariable binary logistic regression assessed factors associated with same-calendar-day mortality and ICU admission. Results: Mean age was 74.36 ± 7.05 years; 60.9% were male. Traffic accidents accounted for 53.1% of cases. Fractures, internal organ injuries, and life-threatening injuries occurred in 49.4%, 28.4%, and 40.7%, respectively; same-calendar-day mortality was 16.5%. Among patients aged ≥85 years, suspicion-based forensic reporting, ICU admission, and same-calendar-day mortality occurred in 27.3%, 45.5%, and 36.4%, respectively. In Model A1, suspicion-based forensic reporting (OR 17.68, 95% CI 3.44-90.84), internal organ injury (OR 7.60, 95% CI 2.79-20.70), and multiple bone fractures (OR 12.19, 95% CI 2.92-50.98) were associated with same-calendar-day mortality. In Model A2, surgical intervention was associated with lower odds of same-calendar-day mortality (OR 0.28, 95% CI 0.11-0.75). Internal organ injury (OR 13.97, 95% CI 5.92-32.95) and suspicion-based forensic reporting (OR 24.82, 95% CI 5.89-104.57) were associated with ICU admission. Conclusions: Geriatric forensic cases had complex clinical and medicolegal profiles. Internal organ injury, multiple bone fractures, and suspicion-based forensic reporting were associated with same-calendar-day mortality; internal organ injury and suspicion-based forensic reporting were also associated with ICU admission. Assessments should integrate injury severity and medicolegal circumstances with chronological age.

articles.title: SAM3-SemiSkin: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Heterogeneous Decoders for Semi-Supervised Dermoscopic and Brain-MRI Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Reliable pixel-level segmentation is needed when lesion boundaries are faint, irregular or affected by acquisition artefacts, yet dense annotation is costly. We investigated whether heterogeneous decoders remain complementary when they share a frozen foundation-model representation, and separated this architectural effect from the contribution of unlabelled training. Methods: SAM3-SemiSkin combines a frozen SAM3 image encoder, bottleneck adapters, and convolutional neural network (CNN) and Transformer decoders. Agreement-weighted soft targets provide mutual supervision, supplemented by frequency and morphological objectives; colour compactness is restricted to dermoscopy. Evaluation included ISIC-2018 benchmarks, controls that retain the shared frozen SAM3 encoder and identical adapter stack, component analyses, zero-shot prompt controls, robustness perturbations, and two-dimensional TCGA-LGG brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). MRI data were partitioned by patient and evaluated slice-wise. Training and validation annotation budgets were counted separately. Results: On ISIC-2018, three-seed test means were 0.886/0.811 for mDice/mIoU at nominal 10% training labels and 0.894/0.825 at 30%. In a separate seed-42 checkpoint audit, the epochs with maximal validation mDice were 45 and 40; train/validation/test mDice were 0.964/0.929/0.882 and 0.974/0.942/0.891, respectively. The 30%-label complete ablation reached 0.893/0.827, exceeding a supervised single-CNN reference by 4.1 percentage points (pp) in mDice. Three-seed paired contrasts were 1.53±0.42 pp for heterogeneous versus homogeneous decoders and 0.63±0.38 pp for adding unlabelled objectives. Matched controls and zero-shot prompt evaluations contextualize these gains. At 30% labels, the MRI benchmark yielded mDice 0.833±0.007 and mIoU 0.740±0.007. Approximately 2.2% of the complete model parameters were trainable. Conclusions: The results support parameter-efficient adaptation with heterogeneous decoding as an integrated design for the tested dermoscopic and MRI tasks. The smaller unlabelled-training contrast and competitive matched controls limit the contribution attributable to the particular pseudo-label objective.

articles.title: Improved U-Net for Automated Segmentation of Lung Ultrasound Findings and Assistance with Lesion Assessment in Children with Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate an improved U-Net for automatic segmentation of lung ultrasound (LUS) findings in pediatric community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and its effect on sonographers' contouring performance and efficiency. Methods: This prospective study included 1994 images from 441 children: 1019 with consolidation, 767 with B-lines, and 208 with pleural effusion. The patient-level development and internal held-out set comprised 353 children (1575 images) and 88 children (419 images), respectively. The model used a ResNet34 encoder, dense atrous convolution, residual multi-kernel pooling, and weighted binary cross-entropy losses for multiscale segmentation deep supervision. We evaluated six model configurations by five-fold cross-validation and on an internal held-out test set. The complete model was also compared with sonographers, and two less-experienced readers repeated contouring with model assistance. Image-level paired differences were analyzed using 50,000 patient-cluster bootstrap replicates and within-family Holm adjustment. Results: Development-set Dice similarity coefficients (DSCs) for consolidation, B-lines, and pleural effusion were 0.8411 ± 0.0107, 0.7698 ± 0.0142, and 0.7730 ± 0.0187, respectively; internal held-out set DSCs were 0.8159 ± 0.0134, 0.7467 ± 0.0178, and 0.7498 ± 0.0234. The improved model had higher DSC, intersection over union, and boundary F1 scores and lower 95th-percentile Hausdorff distances than baseline U-Net for all three findings. It exceeded both less-experienced sonographers but remained below senior sonographers. With assistance, both less-experienced readers improved DSC across all findings and exceeded the standalone model in DSC, and reduced mean per-image processing time by 38.3% and 35.8%, respectively. Conclusions: The improved U-Net segmented consolidation, B-lines, and pleural effusion on LUS images from children with CAP and outperformed baseline U-Net on segmentation metrics. Model assistance improved lesion contouring performance in both less-experienced sonographers. These findings highlight the potential of the model as an AI-assisted tool to facilitate lesion delineation and improve the efficiency of LUS assessment in pediatric CAP and may help reduce reliance on operator experience during contouring.

articles.title: Congenital Heart Disease Diagnosis Using Minimax Guided Context Attention (MG-CAT) Transformer Framework.
articles.abstract: Background: Congenital heart disease is a major cause of mortality in small babies and children, where early diagnosis is very important for proper treatment and improving clinical outcomes. Unfortunately, conventional auscultation-based diagnosis methods mostly rely on expert interpretation that limits their scalability in very far and mountain regions having comparatively low-resource environments. To address these major problems, we propose a deep learning-based method with a spectral minimax-guided context attention transformer framework. Methods: The input signal to the framework is phonocardiogram signals. The proposed framework leverages the optimal use of spectral representation of heart sounds to capture time-frequency features and introduces a novel minimax transformation block designed for cardiac sound mapping analysis. The minimax attention block enhances spectral discrimination by mapping features to a relatively high-dimensional space to improve stratification, thereby compressing them to reduce sensitivity to repetition and noise. Additionally, we employ a cosine-oriented contextual attention module to improve feature representation, adaptively adjusting spatial and temporal features. This approach allows the proposed framework to highlight important acoustic differences and more effectively understand interlayer variations in heart sound patterns. The design also incorporates window-based focus and hierarchical feature clustering to efficiently represent local and global correlations. Results: We conducted experiments on the heart sound dataset known as the ZCHSound. We found that the proposed framework outperforms the basic methods on many assessment metrics. Conclusion: Although some challenges remain in multi-class classification with unbalanced datasets, the results demonstrate the potential of simple spectral learning and cosine-oriented attention to improve the automated diagnosis of congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Exposing Patient-Level Data Leakage in Respiratory Sound Classification: A Leakage-Free Benchmark Leveraging Transformer-Based TabPFN-3 and Knowledge Distillation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Many studies on automated respiratory sound classification report near-perfect accuracy. In most of these studies, respiratory cycles are split randomly into training and test sets, so cycles of the same patient can be found in both sets. This patient-level data leakage makes the reported results higher than the real performance. In this study, we show this problem on the ICBHI 2017 dataset and build a leakage-free benchmark. Methods: We compare TabPFN-3, a pretrained tabular foundation model that predicts by in-context learning without task-specific gradient updates, with eight standard machine learning classifiers in a three-stage framework. Results: When the cycle-level split was replaced by a patient-level split (a stratified five-fold split repeated three times, 15 test folds, with every class present in every test fold), the accuracy of TabPFN-3 decreased from 0.9943 to 0.8722, the macro-F1 from 0.9807 to 0.5010 and the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) from 0.9805 to 0.5788. Nadeau-Bengio-corrected t-tests with Holm adjustment over the 15 folds showed that TabPFN-3 had a significantly higher MCC than all eight baselines. SHAP analysis showed that the first MFCC coefficient, the spectral bandwidth and the RMS energy contributed most to the predictions. We also distilled TabPFN-3 into small student models. The best student, a small transformer (276.3 KB), reached an MCC of 0.5140; its MCC difference from the teacher was not significant after Holm correction, but an equivalence test did not show equivalence and its macro-F1 was significantly lower. A shallow distilled decision tree gave readable rules, mainly for COPD and healthy recordings. Conclusions: Performance on several minority diseases remains low, so the models are not ready for clinical use, and the results should be seen as a realistic baseline for future work.

articles.title: Supine Slow Vital Capacity as a Screening Test for Ultrasound-Defined Hemidiaphragm Dysfunction, with Exploratory Right-Versus-Left Comparisons.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: It is uncertain which widely available pulmonary function parameter best identifies hemidiaphragm dysfunction. We assessed how pulmonary function parameters agree with ultrasound-defined dysfunction and explored right-versus-left differences. Methods: We retrospectively studied 125 adults referred for suspected diaphragm dysfunction who underwent diaphragm ultrasound and pulmonary function testing, including seated and supine slow vital capacity (SVC) and maximal respiratory pressures. Dysfunction was defined as a diaphragm thickening fraction below 20%. Analyses included the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), internal validation, fixed thresholds and intention-to-diagnose. Results: Forty-eight patients (38%) had dysfunction. Supine SVC had the highest AUC (0.837; 95% CI 0.761-0.904). Below a fixed threshold of 80% predicted, sensitivity was 98% (47/48), specificity 58% and the negative likelihood ratio 0.036 (95% CI 0.005-0.25). Validated sensitivity of the data-derived 78% cut-off depended on the method, because the Youden index was nearly flat: 95% (65-98%) after optimism correction, 71% by leave-one-out and 94% with a sensitivity-targeted rule. Supine SVC was unobtainable in 23% of encounters; counting these as positive, sensitivity was 98-99% and specificity 38-44%. Right-versus-left differences were inconsistent. Conclusions: In referred adults, a supine SVC above about 80% predicted may identify patients in whom ultrasound-defined dysfunction is unlikely, although a negative likelihood ratio ≤ 0.1 was not demonstrated with confidence; inability to lie flat should itself prompt ultrasound. External validation is required.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal Findings and Malignancy Diagnoses Recorded During the Follow-Up Period in Adults Receiving Intravenous Iron Therapy: A Descriptive Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gastrointestinal findings and malignancy diagnoses recorded during follow-up were evaluated in adults receiving intravenous (IV) iron in routine clinical care. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 1164 adults treated between 2015 and 2025. Hospital and e-Nabız records were reviewed through 22 October 2026. Iron deficiency anemia (IDA) required anemia and ferritin < 30 ng/mL. Physician-confirmed malignancy diagnoses and available pathology documentation were assessed separately. Associations were examined using Firth logistic regression. Results: Among 1116 patients with post-infusion records, median follow-up was 38.2 months. The IDA subgroup included 424 patients. Endoscopy records from any period were available for 341 patients, and post-infusion gastrointestinal mucosal histology for 198. Gastric atrophy was reported in 139/161 evaluable patients and intestinal metaplasia in 63/165. The combined diagnostic outcome was recorded after infusion in 46 patients: 15 gastrointestinal carcinomas, 22 non-gastrointestinal solid malignancies, and nine hematologic neoplasms. Full pathology reports documenting malignancy were available for 15 patients; 23 diagnoses were recorded more than one year after infusion. Among 1099 patients in the comparative analysis, male sex was associated with recorded malignancy diagnoses (adjusted odds ratio, 6.04; 95% confidence interval, 3.29-11.42; q < 0.001). No baseline laboratory variable was significantly associated with recorded malignancy diagnoses after correction for multiple testing. Conclusions: Gastrointestinal findings and malignancy diagnoses were documented in this treatment cohort. The association with male sex requires independent confirmation. These findings do not establish cancer incidence or a causal effect of IV iron.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the HEART, SVEAT, and EDACS Scores for Predicting 30-Day Death or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Emergency Department Patients with Chest Pain.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The HEART and EDACS scores are widely used to risk-stratify emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain, but direct comparison with the newer SVEAT score is limited. We compared all three scores in one cohort with a high event rate, each alone and combined with the same serial high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-cTnT) rule. Methods: In a retrospective secondary analysis of a prospectively collected registry at a Turkish tertiary care ED (April-August 2022), 1263 consecutive adults with non-traumatic chest pain were included. Three investigators who did not collect the outcome data calculated the HEART, EDACS and SVEAT scores from the clinical records. The outcome was 30-day all-cause death or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); myocardial infarction was not recorded as a separate outcome. Low risk was defined as HEART ≤ 3, SVEAT ≤ 4 and EDACS < 16; pathways added hs-cTnT < 14 ng/L at 0 h and 2 h. Results: The outcome occurred in 151 of 1263 patients (12.0%). HEART and SVEAT had similar discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] 0.845 versus 0.842; DeLong p = 0.824), and both exceeded standalone EDACS (0.735; both p < 0.001). Among patients classified as low risk by the score alone, the outcome occurred in 4.5% (HEART), 5.9% (SVEAT) and 7.4% (EDACS). With serial troponin, miss rates were 1.7%, 2.0% and 1.8%, respectively, and no significant difference in sensitivity was detected. Conclusions: In this high-prevalence cohort none of the scores alone reached an acceptable miss rate, and no pathway reached a 1% miss rate at the point estimate. The findings are from a single centre, are not externally validated and are subject to overlap between troponin and the outcome.

articles.title: Do Severity Prediction Models for Paediatric Appendicitis Work in Another Hospital? A Bidirectional External Validation and Local Recalibration Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Models predicting complicated appendicitis in children could support selection for non-operative management, but are rarely validated in a second hospital. We examined how severity models transport between hospitals, why they fail and what local recalibration can achieve. Methods: Using two open paediatric cohorts, we developed models in Regensburg (164 operated children with histology-verified appendicitis, 50 complicated) and validated them in Düsseldorf (229 operated children, 49 complicated), and vice versa. Laboratory, clinical and ultrasound models, random forest, XGBoost and two clinical scores were compared. We examined heterogeneity in case mix, predictor measurement, documentation and outcome definition, and local updating with 25-150 patients. Results: Internal AUCs of 0.81-0.82 fell to 0.71-0.74 externally; calibration slopes were 0.52-0.70 and risks were overestimated (observed/expected 0.61-0.85), whereas the reverse direction underestimated risk (1.40-1.62). The hospitals differed in age range, referral and management pathways, documentation practices and the histological definition of complicated appendicitis. A larger same-hospital development sample did not improve calibration. Recalibration with 50 local patients (11 events) brought the median calibration slope close to 1, but estimates were imprecise; precise estimation would require several hundred events. Including non-operatively managed children without histology inflated internal AUC from 0.82 to 0.88. Conclusions: In operated children, discrimination was partly preserved between hospitals, but calibration was not. Because outcome definitions, patient selection and documentation differed, poor transportability cannot be attributed to the models alone; the comparability of clinical data and outcomes should be established before models are transferred or recalibrated.

articles.title: Fetal Corpus Callosum Length in Routine Practice: Reference Centiles, Operator Differences and Temporal Variation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: A corpus callosum (CC) centile reflects anatomy and the way the CC is measured. We constructed CC length centiles and examined associations of operator, ultrasound system and examination period with measurements and centile classification. Methods: In this retrospective single-center study (2014-2026), CC length was measured in singleton pregnancies without documented prenatal anomalies by three operators using four systems, recorded for each examination. Quantile regression centiles were estimated for the whole period and for a current period with two operators using the same system, and operator-system-period groups were compared with the current-practice chart. Results: The pooled chart included 15,574 pregnancies and the current-practice chart 2468. Group medians at 22 weeks differed from current practice by -0.91 to +2.36 mm; 2.5-14.6% of measurements fell below the current 10th centile. With the same operator, system differences were mostly small (-0.77 to +0.26 mm). With the same E6 system in different years, a junior operator measured 3.18 mm more than a senior operator; two concurrent operators with the same system differed by 2.19 mm (E10) and 0.68 mm (Expert 22; no difference at the 10th centile). Conclusions: The largest group difference (junior operator) reached about 80% of the current P10-P50 interval at 22 weeks; operator-associated differences exceeded system-associated differences in several comparisons; repeatability was not assessed. The current-practice chart applies to 20-24 weeks. Charts should be used with the technique that built them and audited when operators, techniques or systems change; a borderline centile should prompt verification, not a diagnosis.

articles.title: Retrospective Visibility of Metastatic Epidural Extension on Unenhanced CT.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the retrospective visibility of metastatic epidural extension on unenhanced computed tomography (CT) in patients with known spinal metastases. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included 98 patients. Epidural extension, with or without neural compression, was determined from clinical MRI (79 patients) or contrast-enhanced CT alone (19 patients). Two spine surgeons independently reviewed the unenhanced CT closest in date to the reference examination, blinded to the imaging diagnosis and lesion location. CT findings were positive if either reader identified a lesion. Earlier CTs were reviewed only after a positive initial assessment, with knowledge of the identified lesion. Surgical and survival comparisons were secondary, exploratory, and unadjusted. Results: Epidural lesions were retrospectively visible in 39/50 reference-positive patients (78.0%), including 19/23 with Bilsky grades II-III (82.6%). One of the 48 reference-negative patients had a positive CT finding. Interobserver agreement was 92.9% (κ = 0.847). The interval from initial CT to reference imaging was a median of 1 day (range, 0-58) in CT-visible cases and 3 days (range, 0-160) in CT-nonvisible cases. Within 7 days, lesions were visible in 25/33 patients (75.8%). In the selected backward review, lesions were visible before reference diagnosis in 24/50 patients (48.0%); the interval from the earliest positive CT was a median of 30 days (range, 1-542). Exploratory comparisons showed surgical proportions of 48.3% versus 14.3% for Bilsky Ic-III versus Ia-Ib (p = 0.0277), without a statistically significant unadjusted survival difference (p = 0.0911). Conclusions: Metastatic epidural extension was retrospectively visible on unenhanced CT in this selected cohort. Earlier retrospective visibility does not establish prospective detectability or improved treatment or neurological outcomes from earlier recognition.

articles.title: An Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: Extended Analytical Validation and Real-World Hemolysis Assessment.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Automated phlebotomy may improve preanalytical quality and access to venous blood testing. Prior work evaluating the Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD) demonstrated analytical equivalence. This study expanded the initial analytical validation to additional blood collection tubes and analytes and also assessed real-world hemolysis rates. Methods: The study was conducted in three hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments, including a site with a high prevalence of (hemato-)oncology patients. The within-subject analytical validation study included Greiner VACUETTE (Cohort 1) and BD Vacutainer (Cohort 2) serum, lithium heparin, and EDTA tubes. Equivalence of potassium, lactate dehydrogenase, hemolysis index, and complete blood count (CBC) with differential between paired ARPD-collected and manually collected samples was assessed using Passing-Bablok regression. Real-world ARPD hemolysis (>0.5 g/L free hemoglobin) rates were determined in a separate cohort (Cohort 3) and compared with site-specific manual hemolysis rates. Results: In the analytical validation study, 119 patients were included in the analysis (Cohort 1, n = 52; Cohort 2, n = 67). All tests met the predefined acceptability criteria. The hemolysis index was statistically significantly lower in ARPD-collected lithium heparin samples in Cohort 1. In real-world use (1368 ARPD venipunctures), the ARPD hemolysis rate was 0.0% (95% CI: 0.0-0.3%), significantly lower than manual phlebotomy (1.6%, p = 0.025). Conclusions: The study demonstrated analytical equivalence in a clinically complex population and found reduced ARPD hemolysis rates. The results further substantiate that the ARPD could improve patient care by reducing preanalytical errors.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Techniques in Endodontics for Dental Students: Development and Preliminary Technical Assessment of an ERFNet-Based Panoramic Radiograph Interpretation Prototype.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Automated interpretation of panoramic radiographs could provide visual support during dental training, but technical feasibility should not be confused with proven diagnostic accuracy or educational benefit. This study describes the development and preliminary technical assessment of sTUDent Dental Assistant, an educational software prototype. Materials and Methods: The original artificial neural network software was developed and tested using a computer equipped with an AMD Ryzen 7 5800H 3.20Ghz processor (Advanced Micro Devices, California, USA) and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 graphics processing unit (NVIDIA Corporation, California, USA). The system was implemented in Python version 3.11, and no additional hardware accelerators were employed. A collection of 1480 panoramic radiographs was screened, and 1000 were retained for annotation after 480 exclusions. Images were acquired with a KAVO OP 3DPRO system, converted from DICOM to 8-bit images, normalized and cropped. The prototype uses an ERFNet for semantic segmentation, followed by morphological and region-based post-processing. Eleven dental categories were specified. Results: The application produces color-coded localization overlays and PDF reports. A supplied class-wise count table permits descriptive calculation of precision, recall and F1. Conclusions: This work demonstrates an implemented educational-oriented image-analysis workflow, not clinically validated pathology detection or demonstrated educational effectiveness. Reproducible independent evaluation and student-based assessment remain necessary in future.

articles.title: Diagnostic Yield of Endocuff-Assisted Colonoscopy with Double Right-Sided Examination on Adenoma Miss Rate and Detection Rate: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Right-sided colonic polyps are frequently missed during standard colonoscopy (SC). While double right-sided colon examinations reduce the right-sided adenoma miss rate (rAMR), Endocuff-assisted colonoscopy (EAC) enhances mechanical fold-flattening to improve visualization. This trial aimed to evaluate the additive diagnostic efficacy and safety of EAC versus SC, both performed with a mandatory double right-sided examination. Methods: Patients undergoing elective colonoscopy were prospectively randomized (1:1) to either the EAC or SC group. A mandatory second examination of the right colon was performed in both cohorts. Primary outcome was overall adenoma detection rate (ADR). Secondary outcomes included rAMR, serrated lesion detection rate (SDR), procedural metrics, and adverse events. Results: A total of 354 patients (268 females; median age: 55 years) were analyzed (177 per group). Overall cohort ADR was 30.8%. EAC showed no statistically significant difference compared with SC regarding ADR (29.4% [52/177] vs. 32.2% [57/177]; absolute difference: -2.8%; 95% CI: -12.4% to 6.8%; p = 0.645) or rAMR (15.0% [3/20] vs. 5.9% [1/17]; absolute difference: +9.1%; 95% CI: -10.1% to 28.4%; p = 0.610). While EAC retrieved significantly more total polyps (178 vs. 138; p = 0.010), this was driven predominantly by diminutive lesions (<5 mm) without improving patient-level ADR. SDR was 2.3% (4/177) in EAC versus 0% (0/177) in SC (absolute difference: +2.3%; 95% CI: -0.1% to 4.6%; p = 0.131). Minor mucosal lacerations were numerically higher in EAC (17.5% [31/177] vs. 10.7% [19/177]; absolute difference: +6.8%; 95% CI: -0.4% to 14.0%; p = 0.081), with no major complications in either group. Conclusions: Within the framework of a mandatory double right-sided examination, EAC demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to standard colonoscopy for overall ADR, rAMR, and SDR. While EAC enhanced the detection yield of diminutive polyps, its incremental patient-level benefit should be weighed against potential histopathology costs. The observed trends suggest EAC remains a valuable tool for optimizing mucosal exposure, though larger studies are warranted to fully define its clinical role.

articles.title: Visual Acuity Relative to Central Subfield Thickness and Its Association with Optical Coherence Tomography Structural Biomarkers in Diabetic Macular Edema: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Central subfield thickness (CST) correlates only modestly with visual acuity in diabetic macular edema (DME). We described an exploratory CST-normalized index of visual loss (CIVL) and evaluated the association of optical coherence tomography (OCT) structural biomarkers with visual acuity after accounting for CST. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 243 eyes of 243 patients with type 2 diabetes (150 without macular edema, 93 with DME; one eye per patient, randomly selected in the DME group). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR), CST, disorganization of the retinal inner layers (DRIL), ellipsoid zone (EZ) disruption, intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF) and epiretinal membrane (ERM) were assessed on spectral-domain OCT. CIVL was calculated as (logMAR × 300)/CST. Within the DME group, a base regression model of BCVA including CST, age and sex was compared with a model additionally including the five biomarkers. Results: Median CIVL was 0.00 (interquartile range 0.00-0.00) in non-edematous eyes and 0.40 (0.26-0.59) in DME eyes (p < 0.001). Within the DME group, EZ disruption (β = 0.195; 95% CI 0.105-0.285), SRF (β = 0.287; 95% CI 0.152-0.422) and IRF (β = 0.120; 95% CI 0.031-0.210) were associated with worse BCVA independently of CST, age and sex, whereas DRIL was not (p = 0.285); the association with ERM (β = 0.105; p = 0.020) was not robust in sensitivity analyses. Adding the biomarkers increased the explained variance in BCVA from 36.9% to 66.8% (ΔR2 = 0.299; p < 0.001; optimism-corrected R2 = 0.599). Conclusions: In DME, EZ disruption and intraretinal and subretinal fluid were associated with worse visual acuity at a given CST. CIVL is an exploratory descriptive index whose clinical and prognostic value requires longitudinal validation.

articles.title: A Multi-Task ResNet-50 Framework for Simultaneous Classification and Triage of Endometrial Lesions Based on Hysteroscopy Images.
articles.abstract: Background: While histopathological analysis remains the definitive gold standard for diagnosing endometrial pathology, hysteroscopy is the primary clinical tool for direct visualisation of the endometrial cavity and targeted biopsy. Visual interpretation during the procedure remains subjective and highly dependent on experience. Deep learning has been applied to lesion detection, but few studies report performance at the level of individual patients or assess how stable model performance is across different patient groupings. This study aimed to develop and rigorously evaluate a multi-task deep learning system for simultaneous endometrial lesion subtyping and binary clinical triage from hysteroscopic images. Methods: A retrospective, single-centre study was conducted using 1030 hysteroscopic images collected from 130 verified cases between 2021 and 2025. The dataset included images of Endometrial Polyp (n = 269), Hyperplasia without Atypia (n = 303), and a combined High-grade group comprising Atypical Hyperplasia and Endometrial Cancer (n = 458). A Multi-Task ResNet-50 architecture was implemented with dual classification heads to predict both lesion type and a binary triage outcome. To enhance generalisation and reduce overfitting, online data augmentation was implemented during training. Finally, the model was integrated into a Streamlit-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) to demonstrate software integration for research purposes. Results: On the held-out test set (139 images, 26 patients), three-class accuracy was 0.777 (95% CI 0.712-0.842) and macro-F1 was 0.769 (95% CI 0.694-0.838); binary triage accuracy was 0.842 (95% CI 0.784-0.899) with an AUC of 0.845 (95% CI 0.767-0.909). Sensitivity for the high-grade class was 0.65 under the binary head and 0.63 under the three-class head, which is close but not identical, indicating that the two heads, despite sharing a backbone, are reaching their decisions independently rather than one being derived from the other. Specificity was high under both heads. Conclusions: Aggregate accuracy looked similar whether images or patients were treated as the unit of analysis, but the patient-level analysis, the analysis that actually reflects how the model would be judged in practice, revealed both a lower and far less certain sensitivity for high-grade disease than the image-level figures suggested. We report this as a feasibility study and a methodological illustration, not a validated diagnostic aid and argue that patient-level evaluation, at minimum, should be standard practice when reporting hysteroscopy-AI performance on cohorts of this size.

articles.title: Fractal Dimension of Unilateral Edentulous and Contralateral Dentate Posterior Mandibular Regions on Panoramic Radiographs: A Within-Participant Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Tooth loss may be associated with alterations in mandibular trabecular architecture; however, findings from radiographic fractal analysis remain inconsistent. This study aimed to compare the fractal dimension (FD) of unilateral edentulous posterior mandibular regions with contralateral dentate regions within the same individuals and to evaluate potential variations according to molar position and demographic characteristics. Methods: This retrospective, cross-sectional, within-participant study included 150 adults with unilateral posterior mandibular edentulism. Four 30 × 30-pixel regions of interest were evaluated at visually matched first- and second-molar levels immediately superior to the mandibular canal. FD was calculated using ImageJ-based box-counting analysis. Paired-samples t-tests, complementary Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and generalized estimating equations were used to assess differences and adjust for relevant covariates. Results: Mean FD was 1.309 ± 0.044 in dentate regions and 1.280 ± 0.048 in edentulous regions. The mean paired difference (edentulous minus dentate) was -0.029 (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.037 to -0.021; p < 0.001; Cohen's dz = -0.60). Significantly lower FD values were observed in edentulous regions at both molar levels, without a significant dentition-by-position interaction (p = 0.467). The association remained significant after adjustment for sex, age group, and ROI position (β = -0.029; 95% CI, -0.037 to -0.021; p < 0.001). No significant effect modification by sex, age group, or edentulous-side laterality was detected. Conclusions: Edentulous regions showed lower panoramic FD than contralateral dentate regions. The clinical relevance of this radiographic association remains uncertain; causality, diagnostic performance, bone quality, and implant outcomes were not established.

articles.title: Characterization of Plasma Bacterial DNA Signatures in Coronary Disease Patients via Nanopore 16S rRNA Sequencing.
articles.abstract: Background: Although bacterial DNA has been detected in coronary thrombi and atherosclerotic tissue, the clinical significance of plasma sequencing signals is uncertain. We characterised candidate bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences in a clinically defined, PCR-selected coronary disease cohort. Methods: Forty participants (26 in the myocardial infarction [MI] recruitment stratum, 12 with stable angina, and two in a coronary artery disease [CAD] assessment group) contributed to 42 nanopore libraries. The MI stratum included 25 patients with a recorded STEMI or NSTEMI diagnosis and one with an unclassified presentation. Clinical characteristics were linked by study identifier. EPI2ME profiling was followed by length-stratified candidate screening, representative-read BLASTN alignment, and water-control review. Results: Median age was 67 years (interquartile range of 58-75.5; n = 39), 13/40 participants were women and 12/40 had diabetes. Candidate findings occurred in nine participants: eight in the MI stratum (seven with a recorded MI diagnosis) and one with stable angina. Representative-read alignments provided exploratory support for putative genus-level assignments to Cutibacterium in four MI-stratum participants, Pseudomonas in three, and Serratia in one. The Serratia-like candidate accounted for 181 screen-assigned reads (40.3% of the 1200-1800 bp reads in one library). The stable angina participant had candidate bacterial sequences related to Cutibacterium and a borderline Corynebacterium-like candidate. Neither CAD assessment participant had a retained finding. Median target-length fractions in patient libraries were 3.1% and 8.9% in the two runs. Flavobacterium-like sequences occurred in both water controls and Escherichia-like sequences in the second. Conclusions: Plasma-derived libraries from patients with coronary disease yielded candidate bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences with an exploratory genus-level supported by representative-read BLASTN alignments. These findings do not constitute confirmed bacterial identification, and contamination cannot be excluded. Cutibacterium-like sequences were retained in libraries from five participants, making this genus a priority for independent confirmation using separately processed plasma samples and appropriate extraction controls.

articles.title: Cellular Context of Blood Transcriptomic Changes Across Early Kidney Recovery Trajectories in Sepsis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined whole-blood transcriptional dynamics across early kidney recovery trajectories in sepsis and their relationship to cellular sources and composition. Methods: We reanalyzed 755 clinical patients, 456 patients with paired day 1/day 3 whole-blood transcriptomes, and eight patients with paired single-cell profiles. Trajectories were defined using renal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment components and continuous renal replacement therapy. Patient-level expression changes were compared genome-wide. Matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9), selected in exploratory analysis, was examined using single-cell source mapping and composition adjustment with external and internal references. Results: The clinical cohort comprised 313 rapid recovery and 442 persistent dysfunction patients. Persistent dysfunction was associated with greater nonrenal organ dysfunction and longer organ support. Expression changes differed for 612 of 27,237 genes and 22 of 50 Hallmark sets. MMP9 declined less in persistent dysfunction (change difference 0.593 log-transformed counts per million (logCPM); 95% confidence interval 0.225-0.961; candidate-family q = 0.0025; genome-wide q = 0.0628). Neutrophils contributed 96.2% of captured MMP9 transcripts in 148,933 quality-controlled cells. In 450 complete cases, external-reference composition adjustment reduced the trajectory coefficient from 0.668 to 0.221 logCPM and conditional held-out expression error by 20.8%. The internal-reference coefficient was 0.411 logCPM. Under the measurement availability sensitivity analysis, the error reduction was 20.2%, whereas the hospital stay association changed with classification. Conclusions: Early kidney recovery trajectories were associated with coordinated blood transcriptional changes. Cellular source mapping and composition sensitivity help explain the blood signal and its reference-dependent interpretation.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of 96-Channel Magnetocardiography for Angiographically Significant Coronary Stenosis in Patients with Chest Pain and Clinically Suspected Angina: A Two-Center Post Hoc Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We evaluated the diagnostic performance of 96-channel magnetocardiography (MCG) for angiographically significant coronary stenosis in patients with chest pain and clinically suspected angina. Methods: This two-center post hoc analysis included 137 participants with paired resting (Rest) and post-exercise recovery recordings. The anatomical reference required visually assessed stenosis ≥70% in a vessel with a reference diameter ≥ 2.5 mm. A predefined Total Score ≥ 2 indicated a positive MCG test. Results: The cohort included 37 reference-positive and 100 reference-negative participants. Rest and post-exercise AUCs were 0.710 (95% CI 0.612-0.801) and 0.815 (0.730-0.889), respectively. The direct paired AUC difference was 0.106 (95% CI 0.004-0.207; paired DeLong p = 0.041). A separate exploratory fitted-model comparison yielded an AUC difference of 0.097 (95% CI 0.031-0.214). At Total Score ≥ 2, Rest sensitivity and specificity were 64.9% and 74.0%. Post-exercise sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 83.8% (95% CI 68.9-92.3), 77.0% (67.8-84.2), 57.4% (44.2-69.7), and 92.8% (85.1-96.6), respectively. Post-exercise MCG produced six false-negative and 23 false-positive results. Paired sensitivity and specificity differences were not statistically significant. Conclusions: In this selected cohort, post-exercise MCG showed higher discrimination than Rest MCG for the study-defined anatomical target. The findings support further evaluation as an adjunctive electrophysiological test; they do not establish physiological ischemia detection or justify deferring indicated anatomical assessment.

articles.title: Factors Associated with a Final Diagnosis of Sepsis in Emergency Department Patients with Elevated Procalcitonin-A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Introduction: The new definition of sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by an inappropriate host reaction to infection. The existing scoring systems are limited in terms of the performance in an initial evaluation of the patients. Therefore, the diagnosis of sepsis is still largely dependent on clinical training and physician experience. Objectives: We aimed to identify factors associated with a final diagnosis of sepsis among patients admitted to the emergency department (ED) with elevated procalcitonin in a Polish population and to describe how clinical severity scoring systems discriminated between patients with and without this diagnosis. Methods: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, we included adult (≥18 years) patients admitted to the ED in the period 1.01.2018-30.09.2023 who had elevated procalcitonin concentration (>0.5 µg/L) and were hospitalized. Patients were divided into two groups based on whether a final diagnosis of sepsis was made during the index hospitalization. The primary endpoint was the association of the analyzed baseline characteristics with the final diagnosis of sepsis, assessed with simple and multiple logistic regression; the multivariable model was internally validated with bootstrap resampling. The secondary endpoint was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of clinical severity scoring systems, calculated in patients with available scores. Results: Of 620 hospitalizations (580 patients), 143 (23.1%) involved a final diagnosis of sepsis. In the multiple logistic regression (613 patients, 142 events), procalcitonin (OR: 2.51 per 10-fold increase, 95% CI: 1.80-3.48, p < 0.0001), C-reactive protein (OR: 2.39 per 10-fold increase, 95% CI: 1.28-4.47, p = 0.0063), and platelet count (OR: 0.87 per 50 × 103/µL, 95% CI: 0.80-0.95, p = 0.0029) were associated with a final diagnosis of sepsis. The model had an AUC of 0.790 (optimism-corrected AUC: 0.767). SAPS II, APACHE, and SOFA were available for only 37, 37, and 35 patients, respectively, and were lower in the sepsis group; their AUCs were imprecise and were not formally compared with other scores. Conclusions: In patients admitted to the ED with elevated procalcitonin, higher procalcitonin and CRP and a lower platelet count were associated with a final diagnosis of sepsis. These exploratory findings require external validation with standardized diagnostic criteria before they can be used to support the early diagnosis of sepsis.

articles.title: Higher Final-Response Under-Triage with Multi-Turn Patient-Pressure Prompts in Consumer-Facing ChatGPT: A Controlled Postoperative General Surgery Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Postoperative care-seeking advice from consumer chatbots may change when users resist medical evaluation. We compared final recommendations after scripted patient-pressure versus neutral follow-ups. Methods: Forty-eight clinician-authored scenarios across six procedure groups were tested in both conditions and three fresh-chat runs (288 conversations; 1440 responses). Two surgeons established G0-G3 reference grades and coded all 288 Turn-5 responses. Study-defined under-triage was assessed among G1-G3 scenarios (216 responses). A scenario random-intercept logistic model was primary, with paired and marginal analyses. Following peer review, an independent general surgeon characterized all 216 eligible Turn-5 responses post hoc. Results: Final-response agreement was 277/288 (96.2%; Cohen's kappa, 0.945). Study-defined under-triage occurred in 10/108 Neutral responses (9.3%) versus 25/108 Pressure responses (23.1%): absolute risk difference, 13.9 percentage points (95% scenario-cluster bootstrap CI, 5.6-23.1); risk ratio, 2.50 (95% scenario-cluster bootstrap CI, 1.38-8.00). The conditional mixed-effects odds ratio was 5.24 (95% CI, 1.84-14.96), versus a marginal GEE odds ratio of 2.95 (95% CI, 1.33-6.53). In 108 matched pairs, Pressure alone produced under-triage in 18 pairs and Neutral alone in three (McNemar p = 0.00149). Independent characterization found explicit rejection of delay/home-only care in 21/25 (84%) Pressure under-triage responses, including all 12 G3→G2 events. Conclusions: Patient-pressure prompts were associated with more final study-defined under-triage, often reflecting less specific or less directive care pathways rather than explicit acceptance of delay. No patient outcomes were observed.

articles.title: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Evaluation of Gingival Changes Associated with Direct Contact with Fixed Metallic Orthodontic Appliances.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gingival enlargement during fixed orthodontic treatment may involve plaque-associated inflammation, mechanical irritation, and tissue remodeling. This study compared histopathological alterations and MMP-9 and TIMP-1 immunoreactivity between paired appliance-contact and non-contact gingival sites and a separate pre-treatment control group. Methods: This comparative study included 40 participants contributing 60 specimens obtained during clinically indicated gingival surgery. Twenty orthodontically treated participants each provided paired contact and non-contact specimens, while 20 pre-treatment controls each provided one specimen. Six histopathological features were scored from 0 to 3 and summed to produce a total score of 0-18. MMP-9 and TIMP-1 staining intensity was assessed by two independent histologists blinded to group allocation. Paired comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and comparisons with controls used Mann-Whitney U tests, with Bonferroni adjustment across three comparisons per outcome. Results: Median (Q1-Q3) total histopathological scores were 2 (0-2), 9 (8-10), and 16.5 (16-17) in control, non-contact, and contact specimens, respectively. Corresponding MMP-9 scores were 0 (0-0.75), 1.5 (1-2), and 3 (3-3), and TIMP-1 scores were 1 (0-1), 2 (1-2), and 2.5 (2-3). All pairwise comparisons of histopathological and immunohistochemical outcomes were significant (all adjusted p < 0.001). Plaque index was higher at both treated-site conditions than in controls (adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.021), whereas paired contact-non-contact differences in periodontal indices were not significant. Average-measure interobserver ICCs were 0.933 for the total histopathological score, 0.649 for MMP-9, and 0.669 for TIMP-1. Conclusions: Contact sites showed greater histopathological alterations and higher MMP-9 and TIMP-1 immunoreactivity than paired non-contact sites and pre-treatment controls. Plaque-associated inflammation, mechanical irritation, and anatomical differences may contribute to these associations; causal or metal-specific mechanisms cannot be established.

articles.title: Bacterial Profiling of Gingival and Lesional Crevicular Fluid and Saliva in Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a serious condition characterized by persistent exposed necrotic bone in the maxillofacial region for more than eight weeks in patients receiving antiresorptive or antiangiogenic medications. Although its pathophysiology remains unclear, bacterial infection is considered an important contributing factor. This pilot study investigated the bacterial communities in gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) and saliva using 16S rRNA next-generation sequencing (NGS) to identify bacterial taxa potentially associated with MRONJ. Methods: A clinical study was conducted from 2023 to 2025 involving healthy controls, patients receiving antiresorptive medications without MRONJ, and patients with MRONJ. Samples were collected, followed by DNA extraction and NGS. Alpha-diversity, beta-diversity, taxonomic, and statistical analyses were performed, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: 18 samples (nine GCF and nine saliva) were obtained (mean age 73.82 ± 4.10 years; range 68-81 years). Bacillota and Bacteroidota were the predominant phyla across all groups. Streptococcus and Veillonella showed higher relative abundances in MRONJ groups, whereas Haemophilus and Neisseria were relatively reduced. Prevotella was enriched in the saliva of the at-risk patient group. Alpha-diversity and beta-diversity analyses were not statistically significant; however, several bacterial taxa differed significantly in pairwise comparisons. Conclusions: This pilot study demonstrated distinct microbial trends among healthy controls, patients at risk of MRONJ, and patients with MRONJ. Although limited by small sample size, the findings provide preliminary evidence that observed alterations in the oral microbiome may be associated with MRONJ. Larger longitudinal studies are required to validate these findings and identify potential microbial biomarkers.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Predictive Score for Nucleic-Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) Positivity in Suspected Clostridioides difficile Infection (CDI) with Glutamate Dehydrogenase (GDH)-Positive and Toxin A/B Enzyme Immunoassay (EIA)-Negative Tests.
articles.abstract: Background:Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a common hospital-associated infection. Patients with discordant glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH)-positive and toxin A/B enzyme immunoassay (EIA)-negative tests represent a clinically distinct population, with mortality rates comparable to their toxin A/B EIA-positive counterparts. NAAT positivity may suggest asymptomatic colonization with toxigenic strains, partially treated disease, or mild CDI with toxin levels below the assay's detection threshold, in which the diagnosis of CDI must be clinically adjudicated. While NAAT results may complement clinical assessment, their access may be limited in specific resource-constrained settings. We aimed to develop and internally validate the Discordant CDI Score to predict NAAT positivity in GDH-positive, toxin A/B EIA-negative patients. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed the electronic medical records (EMRs) of hospitalized patients suspected of CDI with GDH-positive, toxin A/B EIA-negative results from 2019 to 2025. Twelve candidate predictors were predetermined, but their dichotomization thresholds were defined during exploratory unadjusted univariate analysis. Using a held-out internal validation with a temporal split of 70:30, multivariable logistic regression with stepwise variable selection was conducted to identify significant predictors of NAAT positivity in the training cohort. Factors were then converted into a 5-point scoring system based on their beta coefficients. The model's calibration and discriminatory metrics were assessed, and the optimal score cut-off was selected based on the Youden index. Finally, a paired retrospective treatment-classification analysis was performed to compare model-guided decisions with physicians' treatment decisions made prior to availability of NAAT results in the same patients. Results: Among 229 participants (160 training, 69 validation), four predictors were identified through multivariable analysis: elevated stool WBC ≥ 10/HPF (2 points), Bristol Stool Form Scale (BSFS) Type ≥ 6, diarrhea frequency ≥ 5 times/day, and abnormal WBC count (<4000 or >10,000 /µL) (1 point each). Calibration assessment suggested potential overfitting, with an optimism-corrected calibration slope and intercept of 0.791 and -0.208, respectively, in the training cohort. The apparent calibration in the validation group had a wide confidence band, while its slope and intercept were 1.15 (95% CI: 0.746-2.275) and -0.193 (95% CI: -0.938-0.835), respectively. At a selected cut-off of ≥3 points, the sensitivity and specificity were 77.8% (14/18; 95% CI: 54.8-91.0) and 80.4% (41/51; 95% CI 67.5-89.0), respectively, in the validation cohort. Score-assisted decisions were associated with a higher proportion of untreated patients compared to physician care, regardless of subsequent NAAT status (158/229, 68.9% vs. 73/229, 31.9%, respectively). While a greater number of untreated/NAAT-positive pairs were observed in the model group (13/18, 22.4% vs. 5/18, 8.6%), this difference was not statistically significant (matched OR 2.60, 95% CI: 0.927-7.299, p = 0.096). Conclusion: The Discordant CDI Score may help predict NAAT positivity in GDH-positive, toxin A/B EIA-negative patients. Several limitations, including a small number of outcome events and model overfitting, warrant further validation. While the score cannot independently establish a CDI diagnosis, its use may complement clinical decision making when access to NAAT is limited.

articles.title: Analytical Comparison of Two Real-Time RT-PCR Assays and Development of an External Positive Control for Rotavirus A Laboratory Surveillance in Mexico.
articles.abstract: Background: Rotavirus A causes diarrhea mainly in children under the age of five. Diarrhea is often nonspecific, so rotavirus detection is necessary to provide appropriate clinical care. Real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) is a sensitive, specific method that provides rapid, reliable results. Methods: Two real-time RT-PCR protocols targeting the highly conserved region of the NSP3 gene and widely used for rotavirus A detection were compared based on their analytical verification parameters. An in-house external positive control (consisting of plasmid DNA containing the viral NSP3 gene) was employed throughout the analytical verification of both real-time RT-PCR assays. Results: Reactivity results were consistent across both real-time RT-PCR protocols, showing repeatable and reproducible Ct values, with no statistically significant differences observed in the precision assays (repeatability: ∝ = 0.05, t = -1.6903, p = 0.1218; reproducibility: ∝ = 0.05, t = -1.1246, p = 0.2870). Both real-time RT-PCR protocols also detected between 14.89 and 21.65 copies of the NSP3 gene per reaction. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate equivalent performance of both assays for rotavirus A detection. Therefore, they represent robust and suitable options for technology transfer to National Public Health Laboratories, supporting efforts to strengthen rotavirus surveillance in Mexico.

articles.title: Association of the Lymphocyte/Monocyte Ratio and C-Reactive Protein with Bone Lesion Characteristics: An Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to investigate the associations of the lymphocyte/monocyte ratio (LMR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) with bone lesions and to assess their relationships with lesion characteristics and histopathological subgroups. Methods: This study included 241 participants with bone lesions as the bone lesion group and 60 healthy participants as the control group. Blood cell counts, as well as the ratios and indices derived from these counts, were compared between the groups. Data showing significant differences were subjected to various statistical analyses to evaluate their relationships with demographic and clinical findings. Results: Compared to the controls, monocyte, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratios, pan-immune-inflammation values, systemic inflammation response indices, and CRP levels were higher in the bone lesion group, whereas lymphocyte counts and LMR were lower. LMR and CRP possessed moderate diagnostic discriminatory capacity. The presence, dimensions, and volume of bone lesions showed a negative correlation with LMR levels and a positive correlation with CRP levels. LMR levels in the metastatic subgroup were lower than those in the benign non-neoplastic bone lesion, benign bone tumor, and primary malignant subgroups. Conversely, CRP levels in the metastatic bone lesion subgroup were higher than in the other subgroups. LMR showed a negative association with the presence of metastatic and malignant bone lesions. ROC analysis revealed that LMR demonstrated diagnostic performance in distinguishing both metastatic and malignant bone lesions. Conclusions: CRP and, in particular, LMR are potential markers that could complement clinical and imaging findings in the assessment of bone lesions. Nevertheless, further research is required to confirm these exploratory findings.

articles.title: Associations Between Routine Laboratory Markers and FIB-4 in Adults with Diabetes: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Routine laboratory markers may characterise FIB-4 risk profiles in adults with diabetes. This study examined associations between FIB-4 and an exploratory composite of gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and red cell distribution width (RDW), termed GNR-3, and assessed whether the composite provided measurable discrimination beyond GGT alone. Methods: A cross-sectional secondary analysis included 60 adults with documented diabetes and prospectively collected baseline data. FIB-4 and GNR-3 were recalculated from the supplied anonymised records. Analyses included rank correlations, covariate-adjusted associations, false-discovery-rate adjustment and paired receiver operating characteristic comparisons. Confidence intervals were estimated using 20,000 participant-level bootstrap samples. The binary discrimination endpoint was high FIB-4 (>2.67), not a confirmed diagnosis of liver fibrosis. Results: Low, intermediate and high FIB-4 classifications occurred in 9, 36 and 15 participants, respectively. GNR-3 correlated with FIB-4 (ρ = 0.364, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.093-0.596) and retained an association after adjustment for age and sex (partial ρ = 0.351, q = 0.0274). Apparent areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for high FIB-4 were 0.811 for GNR-3 and 0.753 for GGT. Their paired difference was 0.058 (95% CI -0.048 to 0.166, DeLong p = 0.275), providing no evidence that the composite discriminated high FIB-4 better than GGT alone. Age-adapted classification reclassified nine participants without changing the high category. Conclusions: GNR-3 was associated with FIB-4 in this small exploratory cohort, but its apparent discrimination of high FIB-4 did not demonstrate an advantage over GGT alone. These findings concern FIB-4 risk classification rather than diagnosis of liver fibrosis and do not support clinical use of the composite.
