Independent evaluation using clinically characterised liver outcomes would be required before considering further application.

articles.title: Artificial Neural Network Prediction of Daily Upper Respiratory Tract Infection Burden from Meteorological and Air Pollution Data: An Out-of-Time Test.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) create seasonal emergency department demand. We assessed whether temporal representations of meteorological and air pollution variables improve artificial neural network (ANN) prediction of daily URTI presentations and generalize to a later period. Methods: Daily presentations at a tertiary hospital in Istanbul (October 2022-September 2025) were modelled using 30 combinations of three environmental domains and ten temporal representations. Expanding-window validation on 682 development days selected nine ANN finalists, evaluated on 365 subsequent out-of-time days. Prespecified permutation importance was evaluated; reference-model comparisons, uncertainty estimation, calibration and sensitivity analyses were post hoc. Results: The lowest ANN test mean absolute errors (MAEs) were 38.53 (Combined_D02), 38.78 (Weather_D01), and 39.75 (Pollution_S0) presentations/day; differences between leading models were small and imprecise. Test R2 ranged from 0.039 to 0.168, with negative bias in every model. On 45 high-demand days above the development-derived 90th percentile, all models underpredicted (observed mean 229.0; predicted means 95.6-111.6). A seven-day trailing mean (MAE 34.03), seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (33.51), and autoregressive baseline (33.52) outperformed all ANNs; paired intervals for the two fitted baselines excluded zero. A calendar-only ANN achieved MAE 38.83, outperforming seven environmental models. Seasonally balanced splitting yielded lower MAEs (26.5-29.1), without consistent deterioration after training-size matching. Conclusions: No temporal representation consistently dominated. Environmental ANN models generalized poorly, underestimated peak demand and did not demonstrate gains over calendar predictors; simple outcome-history benchmarks were more accurate. They should not be used as stand-alone forecasting tools.

articles.title: Comparative Diagnostic Performance of Flow Cytometry Analysis Software and Panel Configurations for Measurable Residual Disease Assessment in Pediatric BCP-ALL.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiparameter flow cytometry (MFC) is widely used for measurable residual disease (MRD) assessment in pediatric B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL). The impact of analytical software on diagnostic performance remains underexplored. Methods: We compared BD FACSDiva, FlowJo, and Infinicyt using identical Flow Cytometry Standard (FCS) datasets from 76 bone marrow samples. Routine FACSDiva MRD classification served as the reference classification. Data was analyzed using an 8-color routine panel and a 14-color extended panel. Diagnostic performance was assessed using area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, overall accuracy, and agreement with the reference classification. Results: The 14-color panel showed higher sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), and overall accuracy than the 8-color panel across all evaluated software platforms, whereas specificity varied between platforms. FlowJo with the 14-color panel showed the highest numerical diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.917; overall accuracy = 97.37%) and the strongest agreement with the reference classification (κ = 0.894; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.794-1.000). Its NPV was significantly higher than that of Infinicyt (100% vs. 70.0%, p = 0.047), although other pairwise differences between software platforms were not statistically significant. Conclusions: The findings indicate that both panel dimensionality and analytical workflow influence flow cytometric MRD assessment. The extended 14-color panel improved detection performance across platforms, while software-dependent differences remained evident, highlighting the need for standardized post-acquisition analysis and independent validation.

articles.title: NeuroEdge-X: Explainable Multi-Expert Fusion of Wearable Inertial Motion and Non-Motor Symptoms for Parkinson's Disease Detection and Differential Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Wearable models for Parkinson's disease (PD) often use a single modality, overfit small cohorts, require complete inputs, give unfaithful explanations or suffer from subject leakage. We aimed to develop NeuroEdge-X, an explainable multi-expert model that fuses bilateral smartwatch motion from 11 standardized tasks with the 30-item non-motor symptom questionnaire of the same individuals. Methods: A questionnaire expert, an interpretable spectral tremor expert and a MiniRocket random-convolution motion expert are combined by a stacked meta-learner, with a motion-only meta-learner when the questionnaire is missing. The model was evaluated on 469 participants of the PhysioNet PADS dataset under repeated subject-independent cross-validation, and the motion expert was also tested on an external gait cohort recorded with foot-pressure sensors. Results: NeuroEdge-X reached 91.0% balanced accuracy (BA) and 97.0% AUROC for PD versus healthy controls and 75.0% BA and 82.7% AUROC for PD versus other movement disorders. Its gain over a fused logistic regression was small and not consistently significant; its practical advantages are that it retained 81.8% and 68.7% BA without the questionnaire and that its explanations are exact. The motion expert alone transferred to the external gait cohort (AUROC 83.5%). The explanations highlight tremor frequency, tremor regularity and action tasks; calibration, decision-curve and triage analyses support clinical interpretation. Profiled with PyTorch, ONNX Runtime and scikit-learn on one thread of a general-purpose CPU, the model processed a participant in 48 ms with 2.3 MB of working memory. Conclusions: Because the questionnaire was completed after diagnosis, these estimates may be optimistic for undiagnosed people. The complete framework has not been validated externally, and edge deployment was not verified on an ultra-low-power wearable microcontroller.

articles.title: Pulmonary Iodine Map Defects Across Contrast Phases in Routine Photon-Counting Detector CT: An Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pulmonary iodine maps are routinely available from photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT), including examinations not optimized for pulmonary embolism (PE) assessment. We evaluated the frequency and contrast-phase distribution of pulmonary iodine map defects in routine clinical practice. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 442 contrast-enhanced PCD-CT examinations in 433 patients during March-April 2026, each with whole-lung coverage in at least one postcontrast phase. Examinations were classified as dedicated pulmonary arterial, other whole-lung arterial, or nonarterial-only imaging. Two radiologists independently reviewed iodine maps followed by 70-keV virtual monoenergetic images, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Analyses were descriptive; no independent reference standard was available. Results: Iodine map defects were identified in 4/442 examinations (0.9%; 95% confidence interval, 0.2-2.3%), all corresponding to pulmonary arterial filling defects interpreted as PE. Defects occurred in 2/15 dedicated pulmonary arterial examinations and 2/70 other arterial examinations, versus 0/357 nonarterial-only examinations. In all three iodine-defect-positive examinations with paired later-phase imaging, iodine defects were no longer visible. Overall, PE was identified in 6/442 examinations (1.4%), including three findings absent from the original reports. Interobserver agreement was κ = 0.86 for iodine defects and κ = 0.83 for PE. Conclusions: Arterial-phase iodine maps may provide clues to PE on routine PCD-CT, even when acquisition is not timed to the pulmonary arterial phase. Absence of iodine defects on nonarterial images should not be used to exclude PE. Larger studies are needed to establish diagnostic benefit.

articles.title: Zonal PSA Density Strategies and the Incremental Yield of Systematic Biopsy in Men with PI-RADS 3 Lesions: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) category 3 lesions are equivocal, and the value of prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD) may depend on lesion zone. We compared whole-gland PSAD with transition-zone PSAD (TZ-PSAD) by lesion zone and quantified the yield of systematic biopsy. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 542 men with a PI-RADS 3 index lesion who underwent MRI-targeted and 12-core systematic biopsy. Clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) was defined as ISUP grade group ≥ 2. Discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis; data-derived zonal thresholds were validated by bootstrap optimism correction. Results: csPCa was detected in 86 men (15.9%), in 18 (3.3%) by systematic cores alone. AUCs for PSAD and TZ-PSAD were 0.77 and 0.76 in peripheral-zone lesions (59 csPCa; p = 0.540) and 0.64 and 0.82 in transition-zone lesions (27 csPCa; p < 0.001). A zonal rule (PSAD ≥ 0.12 for peripheral-zone and TZ-PSAD ≥ 0.22 for transition-zone lesions) classified 214 men (39.5%) for deferral and missed four csPCa cases (sensitivity 95.3%; optimism-corrected 93.8%); a uniform TZ-PSAD ≥ 0.22 rule performed similarly. Conclusions: In this derivation cohort, TZ-PSAD performed at least as well as whole-gland PSAD, with the largest difference in transition-zone lesions. Systematic cores detected csPCa that targeted cores alone would have missed in 3.3% of men. The thresholds require external validation.

articles.title: Within-Session Intra-Observer Reproducibility of Spleen Stiffness Measured by Endoscopic Ultrasound Point Shear-Wave Elastography: A Prospective Single-Operator Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endoscopic ultrasound point shear-wave elastography (EUS-pSWE) enables quantitative assessment of spleen stiffness, but the reproducibility of repeated measurements remains poorly established. This study evaluated within-session intra-observer reproducibility and the influence of acquisition-quality indicators. Methods: In this prospective, single-center study, 58 patients underwent ten consecutive splenic EUS-pSWE measurements performed by one operator without echoendoscope repositioning. Agreement between the medians of the first and last five measurements was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Measurement quality was evaluated using velocity signal-to-noise ratio (VSN) and interquartile range-to-median ratio (IQR/median). Results: Overall, 66.6% of individual measurements achieved VSN > 60%, while only 20.7% of measurement series fulfilled the IQR/median < 30% criterion. Overall reproducibility was moderate (ICC 0.66, 95% CI 0.49-0.78), with a mean bias of -0.6 kPa and limits of agreement from -15.9 to 14.8 kPa. Among the 12 series meeting the ten-reading IQR/median < 30% criterion, ICC was 0.92 (95% CI 0.77-0.98). However, when both five-reading blocks separately met this criterion (n = 18), ICC was 0.61 (95% CI 0.23-0.83). Conclusions: Splenic EUS-pSWE demonstrated moderate overall within-session reproducibility. The higher agreement observed after whole-series quality-based selection was not consistently reproduced using an alternative block-level criterion. Therefore, the IQR/median < 30% threshold requires independent validation before it can be recommended for clinical use.

articles.title: OCT-Derived Expected Visual Field Function for Quantifying Directional Structure-Function Discordance in Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To develop an OCT-based framework that estimates the visual field function expected from an eye's structural profile and quantifies the direction and magnitude of disagreement between structure-derived expected function and the actually measured visual field in glaucoma and ocular hypertension. Methods: This retrospective study included 592 patients, 893 unique eyes, and 1100 eye-visit samples with matched Humphrey Field Analyzer 24-2 visual field testing and peripapillary OCT imaging. Separate models estimated the MD and PSD expected from OCT-derived structural measurements and prespecified nonfunctional covariates, without using measured visual field variables or visual field reliability indices as model inputs. For each eye, the measured MD and PSD were compared with these eye-specific structure-derived expectations. Direction-oriented prediction errors were standardized using the training out-of-fold distributions and combined into a continuous discordance score. Training-derived cutoffs were then used to define structure-worse-than-function (SWF), concordant, and function-worse-than-structure (FWS) strata, which were applied unchanged to the independent test set. Results: In the independent test set, 119 eyes (55.9%) were concordant, 43 (20.2%) were SWF, and 51 (23.9%) were FWS. FWS eyes showed substantially worse MD and higher PSD, while patient-cluster-aware analyses identified significant differences in temporal, superior, and inferior RNFL thickness among the directional strata. Random forest was selected as the best-performing classifier. The base model achieved an accuracy of 0.667, balanced accuracy of 0.567, macro-F1 score of 0.582, and one-vs-rest macro AUC of 0.794. Conclusions: Comparing measured visual field function with eye-specific OCT-derived expected function provides a quantitative framework for describing the magnitude and direction of structure-function disagreement. This approach is intended to complement, rather than replace, measured perimetry.

articles.title: Prevalence of Radiographic Errors and Assessment of Diagnostic Image Quality in Panoramic Radiographs: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Panoramic radiography is an important imaging modality for the evaluation of dentoalveolar and maxillofacial structures in dental diagnosis and treatment planning. The diagnostic quality of panoramic images is closely related to appropriate patient preparation and accurate positioning. Positioning errors may adversely affect image quality, leading to misinterpretation and unnecessary repeat examinations. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic quality of panoramic radiographs, determine the frequency of common positioning errors, and identify error types contributing to diagnostically inadequate images. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, a total of 5155 panoramic radiographs obtained at Mardin Oral and Dental Health Center were evaluated. Patients were divided into four age groups: ≤20, 21-40, 41-60, and ≥61 years. The assessed errors included failure to position the tongue against the palate, slumped patient position, positioning the patient too far forward or backward, failure to bite on the bite block, patient movement, forward or backward head tilt, head rotation to one side, foreign bodies, exposure errors, lip positioning errors, and missing image sections. Radiographic quality was classified as "excellent," "diagnostically acceptable," or "unacceptable." The distribution of error types according to age and sex was evaluated using the chi-square test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: At least one error was detected in 40.1% of the panoramic radiographs. The most frequent errors were failure to position the tongue against the palate (10.3%) and head rotation to one side (9.7%). Of the radiographs, 3.6% were classified as excellent, 95.7% as diagnostically acceptable, and 0.6% as unacceptable. The overall error rate was highest in the ≥61-year age group (53.8%) and lowest in the ≤20 year age group (31%), with a significant increase with age (p < 0.05). No significant association was found between sex and overall error frequency (p > 0.05), although significant sex-related differences were observed for some specific error types. Conclusions: Patient preparation and positioning errors may affect the diagnostic quality of panoramic radiographs. Accurate positioning, effective patient communication, and consideration of age-specific error patterns may contribute to improving image quality.

articles.title: Plasma KRAS-Mutated Cell-Free DNA Dynamics and Prognostic Associations During the First Chemotherapy Cycle in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Within-cycle changes in circulating tumor-derived DNA may provide prognostic information in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). This exploratory study investigated KRAS-mutated cell-free DNA (mKRAS cfDNA) dynamics during the first chemotherapy cycle and their associations with disease characteristics, progression, and overall survival. Methods: A total of 40 patients contributed 151 plasma samples collected at Pre-cycle, Early-cycle, Post-infusion, and Late-cycle time points. Droplet digital PCR targeting KRAS codons 12, 13, and 61 quantified mKRAS cfDNA concentration and mutant allele fraction (MAF). Total cfDNA and CA 19-9 were also evaluated. For the analysis of survival associations, patients were followed for up to 4 years. Results: mKRAS cfDNA was detected in at least one sample from 29 patients (72.5%). Pre-cycle mKRAS cfDNA concentration and MAF were higher in patients with metastatic disease (all p < 0.0001). Both parameters decreased between Pre-cycle and Late-cycle (both p < 0.001), whereas total cfDNA showed no significant overall change. mKRAS cfDNA and MAF weakly correlated with CA 19-9 at most investigated time-points (ρ 0.396-0.523). Late-cycle positivity was associated with shorter subsequent overall survival after adjustment for age and metastatic status (adjusted hazard ratio 5.36; 95% confidence interval: 1.54-18.64; p = 0.0083). Clinical sensitivity analyses yielded directionally consistent estimates; however, the association was attenuated and became statistically inconclusive after adjustment for CA 19-9 dynamics. Pre-cycle positivity and early increases in MAF were associated with shorter survival in unadjusted analyses but did not retain significance after adjustment. No significant associations with progression were identified among 31 evaluable patients. Conclusions:Late-cycle mKRAS cfDNA detection warrants further evaluation as an on-treatment prognostic marker in PDAC. Larger studies with standardized sampling and external validation are needed to establish its clinical usefulness and added value beyond established assessments.

articles.title: Preoperative Blood Cell-Derived Inflammatory Indices and In-Hospital Postoperative Outcomes After Incisional Hernia Repair: A Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We compared preoperative complete blood count (CBC)-derived indices for in-hospital postoperative complications after incisional hernia repair. Methods: This single-center retrospective study (January 2020-March 2025) included 106 of 173 eligible patients; an expanded cohort of 115 permitted same-day samples. The first qualifying admission CBC was used. Pretreatment eligibility was established during clinical-record review, but treatment timestamps were unavailable in the analytical extract. Five markers were compared using ROC-AUC, average precision (AP), Firth regression, and nested cross-validation. Results: The strict cohort had 11 complications, nine major outcomes (Clavien-Dindo ≥ III), and five deaths. For any complication, red-cell distribution width (RDW) had the highest numerical AUC (0.757), versus 0.718 for the cumulative inflammatory index (IIC). The major-outcome AUCs were 0.836 for IIC and 0.829 for RDW; the AP difference was 0.209 (95% CI: -0.186 to 0.497), and capture curves crossed. The adjusted IIC odds ratio per standard deviation was 2.96 (95% CI: 1.16-9.08; Holm p = 0.052). Adding IIC to age and emergency presentation increased the out-of-fold AUC from 0.726 to 0.804, but the increment remained uncertain (95% CI: 0.000-0.170). Conclusions: RDW ranked highest numerically for the primary endpoint; IIC showed numerical enrichment for major outcomes without established superiority. Selection, uncertain pretreatment timing, and few nonfatal major events limit generalizability. These exploratory markers require prospective independent validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Using Quantitative Computed Tomography Supports the Detection of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated interstitial lung disease (SLE-ILD) is linked to increased disease burden and adverse outcomes, underscoring the need for its reliable detection. This study explored the use of quantitative computed tomography (CT) to assess pulmonary involvement in SLE-ILD and developed an interpretable machine learning model to identify the disease. Methods: This retrospective analysis included 312 patients with SLE: 135 with ILD and 177 without. It compared quantitative CT parameters, including lung volume (LV), mean lung density (MLD), and the percentage of intrapulmonary vascular volume (PIVV), between the groups. Patients from 2017 to 2022 (n = 219) formed the training set, whereas those from 2023 to 2025 (n = 93) formed the temporal test set. Following feature selection using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) in the entire training set, eight machine learning models were developed, with hyperparameters optimized using a separate 10-fold cross-validation procedure. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and precision-recall curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. The final model's feature contributions to predictions were analyzed using SHapley Additive exPlanations. Results: Compared with the non-ILD group, the ILD group generally showed higher MLD, lower LV, and lower PIVV. LASSO identified nine variables. After considering the performance of all models in both the training and temporal test sets, logistic regression (LR) was selected as the final model. In the temporal test set, the LR model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.926 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.875-0.977] and an average precision of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.97). Its accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score were 0.871, 0.825, 0.906, 0.868, and 0.846, respectively. This model was implemented as a web-based diagnostic calculator. Conclusions: Quantitative CT enables objective quantification of pulmonary abnormalities in patients with SLE-ILD. An interpretable LR model integrating clinical and quantitative CT features may support the objective identification of SLE-ILD, although its performance requires further validation in independent cohorts.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Classification of Mandibular Condylar Position Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Single-Center Internal Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study internally evaluated deep learning models for classifying mandibular condylar position on sagittal cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images using a predefined joint-space-based reference standard. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 1040 temporomandibular joint images from 560 patients were categorized as anterior, centric, or posterior using Pullinger and Hollender's method. Patients were allocated to training, validation, and test sets in an 80:10:10 ratio (448, 56, and 56 patients, respectively), yielding 823, 107, and 110 joint images. Three object-detection models (YOLOv8x, YOLOv8n, and RF-DETR Nano) were evaluated on the same test set for condylar region localization and position classification. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and mean average precision (mAP). Results: YOLOv8x correctly classified 97 of 110 test images, achieving an accuracy of 0.88 (patient-cluster bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.81-0.95) and an mAP@0.5 of 0.89. YOLOv8n and RF-DETR Nano correctly classified 84 and 82 images, with accuracies of 0.76 and 0.75 and mAP@0.5 values of 0.80 and 0.81, respectively. The mAP@0.5:0.95 values for YOLOv8n and RF-DETR Nano were 0.60 and 0.59, respectively. YOLOv8x's mAP@0.5:0.95 was 0.66. For YOLOv8x, recall/F1-score were highest for anterior class (0.94/0.91) and lowest for centric class (0.79/0.83), with precision ranging from 0.88 to 0.89 across classes. Intra- and inter-observer classification agreement in 156 joints was κ = 0.90 and 0.97, respectively. Conclusions: The YOLOv8x-based model achieved the highest overall accuracy among the three models in this comparison, indicating that it can classify mandibular condylar position on sagittal CBCT images according to predefined categories.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of the CALLY Index in Predicting Complicated Acute Appendicitis: A Comparative Study with CAR, HALP, SII, and PIV.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the discriminatory performance of the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index in complicated acute appendicitis and compare it with C-reactive protein (CRP) alone and other inflammatory indices. Materials and Methods: This single-center retrospective study included adults diagnosed with acute appendicitis between January 2021 and December 2025. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, with paired DeLong tests for AUC comparisons. Separate logistic regression models were adjusted for age and sex, and internal validation was performed using 350 bootstrap resamples. Results: Of 1733 patients screened, 1634 were included, of whom 306 (18.7%) had complicated appendicitis. CALLY and CAR each achieved an AUC of 0.782, compared with 0.778 for CRP alone. CALLY did not significantly outperform CAR (p = 0.913) or CRP (p = 0.489). Although CAR showed statistically higher discrimination than CRP (p = 0.006), the absolute AUC difference was small. CALLY demonstrated higher discrimination than HALP, SII, and PIV (all p < 0.001). In age- and sex-adjusted analysis, each doubling of CALLY was associated with lower odds of complicated appendicitis (adjusted odds ratio, 0.623; 95% CI, 0.580-0.670). The optimism-corrected AUC of the CALLY-extended model was 0.795. Conclusions: CALLY showed moderate discrimination of complicated acute appendicitis but no demonstrated advantage over CAR. Whether CALLY adds value beyond simpler laboratory measures requires further evaluation and external validation.

articles.title: Spontaneous Relative T1 Hyperintensity of Vertebral Metastases from Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Retrospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study Using the Spinal Cord as an Internal Standard.
articles.abstract: Background/Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of spontaneous T1 hyperintensity relative to the spinal cord (signal intensity ratio [SIR] > 1) for identifying vertebral metastases from clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) among vertebral metastases of other origins, and to assess the spinal cord as an internal reference standard, as an alternative to the conventional comparison with paravertebral muscle or the intervertebral disc. Methods: This retrospective, single-centre, case-control diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at University Hospital of Messina, Italy, between January 2017 and December 2023. Patients with vertebral metastases who underwent spine MRI for radiotherapy planning were included: 11 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven ccRCC (14 lesions) and 28 patients with metastases from other solid tumours (41 lesions; convenience sample). The index test was the lesion-to-spinal-cord SIR measured on unenhanced sagittal T1-weighted fast spin-echo images acquired at 1.5 T. Two blinded neuroradiologists independently performed the measurements; lesions were classified as hyperintense relative to the spinal cord using the prespecified threshold of SIR > 1. The flow-void sign was assessed as a secondary finding. Diagnostic accuracy was calculated on a per-lesion basis with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: At the SIR > 1 threshold, both readers correctly classified 13/14 ccRCC metastases and 38/41 control metastases (13 true positives, 3 false positives, 1 false negative, and 38 true negatives). Sensitivity was 92.9% (95% CI, 68.5-98.7%), specificity was 92.7% (95% CI, 80.6-97.5%), and accuracy was 92.7%. The positive and negative likelihood ratios were 12.7 (95% CI, 4.2-38.1) and 0.077 (95% CI, 0.011-0.51), respectively. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.960 (95% CI, 0.886-1.000) for reader 1 and 0.953 (95% CI, 0.873-1.000) for reader 2. Categorical inter-reader agreement was perfect (55/55, 100%; Cohen's kappa = 1.00). Continuous SIR measurements showed a concordance correlation coefficient of 0.896, a mean inter-reader difference of 0.003 SIR units, and no systematic bias (p > 0.9). The flow-void sign was present in 7/14 ccRCC lesions; it was not assessed in the control group. The three false-positive lesions originated from thyroid, breast, and lung cancers. Conclusions: In this preliminary series, T1 hyperintensity relative to the spinal cord was frequent in ccRCC vertebral metastases and uncommon in metastases from other tumours. Owing to the case-control design, non-consecutive controls, and small sample size, diagnostic accuracy may have been overestimated; validation in prospective, consecutive, multicentre cohorts is required.

articles.title: Fulminant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Keratitis After Initial Improvement of Acanthamoeba Keratitis Requiring Emergency Large-Diameter Penetrating Keratoplasty.
articles.abstract: A 36-year-old contact lens wearer presented with a five-day history of pain, redness, tearing, and photophobia in the right eye. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 1.0 logMAR. Examination revealed diffuse corneal edema without ulceration. Corneal and conjunctival cultures obtained before antimicrobial treatment showed no bacterial or yeast growth, while in vivo confocal microscopy and clinical findings supported Acanthamoeba keratitis. Following seven days of topical chlorhexidine-based treatment, BCVA improved to 0.3 logMAR, and the epithelium was intact at discharge. Ten days later, the patient was readmitted with extensive stromal melting, central perforation, and light perception without projection. Both corneal and conjunctival cultures yielded Pseudomonas aeruginosa after 48 h, and subsequent antimicrobial treatment was guided by susceptibility testing. Progressive destruction necessitated emergency therapeutic penetrating keratoplasty with a 10.0 mm graft. At two months, BCVA was 1.0 logMAR, the epithelium was fully healed, and no clinical recurrence or graft rejection was observed. The biphasic course supports secondary bacterial superinfection, although initial coinfection cannot be excluded. This case highlights the importance of repeat microbiological sampling after clinical deterioration and documents short-term anatomical salvage; long-term graft survival remains undetermined.

articles.title: InceptionTurkerNeXt: A Compact CNN and Deep Feature Engineering Framework for Image-Level Osteoid Osteoma Classification on Computed Tomography.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Osteoid osteoma (OO) is a painful benign bone tumor whose nidus is best depicted on computed tomography (CT). This exploratory study introduces InceptionTurkerNeXt, a compact convolutional neural network, and evaluates a deep feature engineering (DFE) framework built on it for image-level OO classification. Methods: The backbone was pretrained on a public 26-class multi-cancer dataset of 130,000 images. The DFE framework extracts global and patch features, selects them with cumulative weighted iterative neighborhood component analysis and classifies them with a t-algorithm-based k-nearest neighbors ensemble. The single-center OO set contains 359 axial CT images (184 OO and 175 control) from 82 patients. The primary protocol was patient-grouped 10-fold cross-validation with all selection steps fitted on the training folds. Results: The backbone reached 98.94% accuracy on the 26,000-image multi-cancer test set. Under the primary protocol, the DFE framework reached 90.81% image-level accuracy (95% confidence interval 86.35-94.71%), 91.30% sensitivity and 90.29% specificity. Patient-level voting gave 93.90% accuracy (82 patients), and a separate patient-level hold-out set gave 91.55% image-level accuracy (71 images). The earlier image-level estimate (98.33%) was optimistic by 7.52 percentage points. Four fine-tuned standard backbones reached 83.29-88.02% on the same partitions. Conclusions: The framework separated OO and control CT images with approximately 91% image-level accuracy under patient-grouped validation at one center. External multi-center validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Posterior Lenticonus in a 7-Year-Old Child.
articles.abstract: Posterior lenticonus is a congenital developmental defect of the ocular lens. It is an abnormal conical protrusion of the posterior lens capsule and usually occurs as an isolated defect. The diameter of the conical protrusion is typically between 2 and 7 mm. The pathogenesis of this condition is still not fully understood. Proposed but unconfirmed mechanisms include vitreous inflammation combined with excessive proliferation of posterior lens fibers, leading to lens opacification, traction on the posterior lens capsule by remnants of the hyaloid artery system, abnormalities within the tunica vasculosa lentis. The average age at diagnosis of posterior lenticonus is between 3 and 7 years. The most common complication of posterior lenticonus is amblyopia. Other frequent coexisting conditions include cataract, strabismus, and loss of central fixation. It has been observed that, over time, cataractous changes may develop within the cone and may spread to the adjacent subcapsular lens cortex. We present anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans and a slit-lamp photograph of a 7-year-old child with posterior lenticonus, whose parents brought the patient to the Ophthalmology Clinic due to reduced visual acuity. Best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in the right eye was 0.6. Slit-lamp examination and anterior segment OCT revealed posterior lenticonus. Pharmacological treatment was temporarily initiated, and surgery was withheld.

articles.title: Immune Microenvironment Differences Between Upper Tract and Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma: Insights from Synchronous Disease.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is a rare malignancy that is more aggressive than urothelial bladder cancer (UBC). The mechanisms behind synchronous tumors at both sites remain unclear. The tumor microenvironment (TME) may influence tumor behavior. This exploratory study compares the immune landscape across UTUC-only, UTUC with synchronous UBC (UTUC-sUBC), their paired UBC (sUBC), and UBC-only tumors. Methods: Multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) was performed to quantify CD8+ T cells, FOXP3+ regulatory T cells, CD68+ macrophages, PD-L1+ and PD-1+ cells. Comparisons were performed using Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney U, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results: UTUC-sUBC exhibited significantly lower densities of CD8+ (p = 0.013), FOXP3+, PD-L1+, and PD-1+ cells (all p < 0.001) compared to UBC-only. UTUC-only showed significantly lower densities of FOXP3+, PD-L1+, and PD-1+ cells (all p < 0.001) than UBC-only. Only PD-1+ cell density differed significantly between UTUC-sUBC and UTUC-only (p = 0.005). Paired analysis of UTUC-sUBC and matched sUBC revealed comparable immune profiles (p > 0.05). Conclusions: UTUC-sUBC tumors display an immune-depleted phenotype, distinct from the more inflamed UBC-only environment. Compared to UTUC-only, synchronous disease is distinguished by a higher PD-1+ cell density, raising the hypothesis that qualitative T-cell dysfunction, rather than quantitative infiltration, may be associated with its aggressiveness. These exploratory findings warrant validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Molecular Diagnostic Surveillance, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Comorbidity Profiles in Major WHO-Critical-Priority-List Pathogens in a Saudi Tertiary-Care Hospital.
articles.abstract: Background: Timely integrated diagnostic microbiology combines automated identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) with assay-specific molecular confirmation. This allows final resistance classifications to be interpreted within one clinical workflow. The novelty of this study is the integration of these complementary diagnostic outputs with organism identity, specimen source, care setting, and available host context across a mixed-pathogen tertiary-care cohort. We characterized the distribution of major clinical priority-pathogen resistance profiles and examined clinical factors associated with high-priority resistances. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional laboratory-based study included 847 non-duplicate clinical isolates recovered during routine care from a pre-established surveillance cohort at King Salman Specialist tertiary-care hospital in Saudi Arabia from July 2025 to July 2026. Automated organism identification/AST was combined with assay-specific GeneXpert molecular confirmation where applicable. GeneXpert SA Nasal Complete was used for Staphylococcus aureus/MRSA confirmation and Xpert Carba-R for relevant carbapenemase targets; organisms outside these target panels, including Streptococcus pyogenes and Candida spp., were characterized by routine culture and automated identification. Carbapenem resistance was defined by imipenem and/or meropenem resistance and reported as carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) for Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli, carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA), and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB). Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was classified by cefoxitin resistance with concordant GeneXpert confirmation. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression assessed clinical factors associated with CRE and MRSA detection. Results: Gram-negative organisms accounted for 546 isolates (64.5%), Gram-positive organisms accounted for 281 (33.2%), and fungi accounted for 20 (2.4%). Klebsiella pneumoniae was most frequent (176/847; 20.8%), followed by Staphylococcus aureus (169/847; 20.0%) and Escherichia coli (156/847; 18.4%). Priority resistance was highest in Acinetobacter baumannii, with CRAB in 73/74 isolates (98.6%), followed by CRPA in 38/83 P. aeruginosa (45.8%), MRSA in 68/164 S. aureus (41.5%), CRE in 57/176 K. pneumoniae (32.4%), and CRE in 10/156 E. coli (6.4%). In the complete-case CRE model (n = 246; 38 events), K. pneumoniae had higher adjusted odds of CRE than E. coli (aOR 3.91, 95% CI 1.74-9.73; p = 0.002). In the MRSA model (n = 160; 68 events), non-urinary specimens (aOR 3.31, 95% CI 1.21-10.16; p = 0.025) and recorded comorbidity (aOR 3.40, 95% CI 1.26-9.64; p = 0.017) were independently associated with MRSA detection. Conclusions: The integrated diagnostic workflow revealed marked organism-specific differences in resistance, led by a very high CRAB burden and substantial CRPA, MRSA, and K. pneumoniae CRE. Interpreting the final laboratory classification together with organism identity, specimen source, and care setting provides a practical framework for focused diagnostic reporting, antimicrobial stewardship, and infection-control prioritization in tertiary care.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Angiography-Derived MPFFR for Predicting Hemodynamically Significant Coronary Stenosis: A Multicenter Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) methods offer noninvasive alternatives to wire-based FFR for functional assessment of coronary stenosis, but their diagnostic performance requires validation. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven angiography-based FFR for detecting hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis, as compared with percentage diameter stenosis (%DS) from quantitative coronary angiography (QCA), using invasive FFR as the reference standard. Methods: In this prospective, multicenter study, 189 patients (211 lesions) undergoing clinically indicated angiography were enrolled. AI-driven angiography-based FFR and %DS were derived from angiographic images and compared with invasive FFR (cutoff ≤ 0.80). Diagnostic performance was assessed using AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values, along with correlation analysis and analysis time. Results: AI-driven angiography-based FFR showed significantly greater diagnostic performance than %DS (per-patient AUROC: 0.87 vs. 0.63, p < 0.001; per-lesion AUROC: 0.89 vs. 0.65, p < 0.001). AI-driven angiography-based FFR demonstrated higher specificity (92.7%) and positive predictive value (86.7%) than %DS (64.2% and 51.9%, respectively). AI-driven angiography-based FFR correlated strongly with invasive FFR (r = 0.746), whereas %DS showed a weak inverse correlation (r = -0.250). Median analysis time for AI-driven angiography-based FFR was 20.9 s. A gray-zone hybrid strategy (thresholds 0.73-0.83) yielded 89.8% accuracy and could reduce invasive FFR use by 57.1%. Conclusions: AI-driven angiography-based FFR demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy, strong correlation with invasive FFR, and rapid analysis time. These findings support AI-driven angiography-based FFR as a pressure-wire-free tool for physiological assessment during coronary angiography.

articles.title: Prognostic Association of PET/CT-Defined Low Skeletal Muscle Mass in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Treated with Second-Line or Later Nivolumab: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Low skeletal muscle mass (LSMM) may be associated with outcomes in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. We evaluated CT-defined LSMM and survival in patients treated with second-line or later nivolumab. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 62 patients with pretreatment 18F-FDG PET/CT. Skeletal muscle index (SMI) was measured at L3, and LSMM was defined as SMI <34.4 cm2/m2 in women and <45.4 cm2/m2 in men. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. Results: LSMM was present in 32 patients (51.6%). Age ≥65 years (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.19-10.75; p = 0.021) and BMI <25 kg/m2 (OR = 5.67, 95% CI 1.73-18.53; p = 0.003) were associated with LSMM. Median OS was 14.23 versus 22.28 months (log-rank p = 0.049), and median PFS was 6.64 versus 14.42 months (p = 0.058), for LSMM versus no LSMM. Adjusted HRs for LSMM were 2.08 (95% CI 0.97-4.48; p = 0.062) for OS and 1.87 (95% CI 0.93-3.77; p = 0.078) for PFS. Martin and Prado SMI definitions did not reproduce these survival associations. Continuous SMI was also not associated with OS or PFS in adjusted analyses. Conclusions: The primary binary LSMM definition showed an unfavorable survival pattern, but this was not robust across alternative thresholds or continuous SMI and did not establish an independent prognostic association.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Infarct-Zone Circumferential Strain by CMR Feature Tracking After Acute Myocardial Infarction Treated with Primary PCI.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the prognostic significance of CMR feature-tracking-derived peak infarct-zone circumferential strain (CSinfarct) in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI). Methods: Among 450 consecutive patients with AMI screened between February 2017 and March 2020, 356 patients with analyzable CMR and available follow-up were included. Global and regional myocardial strain were quantified using CMR feature tracking. Infarcted and remote myocardial segments were defined according to LGE. The primary endpoint was defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, reinfarction, and hospitalization for heart failure. Results: During a median follow-up of 44 months, 102 patients (28.7%) experienced MACE. Patients with MACE showed impaired global and regional myocardial strain and greater infarct size. In multivariable analysis, peak CSinfarct (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.02-1.15; p = 0.008), GLS (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.03-1.25; p = 0.008), and infarct size (HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 1.00-1.04; p = 0.046) remained independently associated with MACE. CSinfarct > -7.95% was associated with lower MACE-free survival (log-rank p < 0.001). An exploratory CMR score integrating LVEF, GLS, infarct size, and CSinfarct showed a graded increase in observed MACE rates across risk categories (9.46% to 67.65%). Conclusions: Peak CSinfarct was independently associated with long-term MACE after AMI and may provide complementary prognostic information when considered alongside conventional CMR markers.

articles.title: Word-Anchored Eye-Movement Measures for Interpretable and Calibration-Robust Dyslexia Screening on the ETDD70 Dataset.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Eye-tracking models for dyslexia screening usually describe gaze in screen coordinates, although dyslexia is a difficulty with words and letters. We aimed to develop an interpretable word-anchored screening approach that is robust to calibration error. Methods: We analysed the public ETDD70 dataset (70 Czech children, 35 with dyslexia). The position of all 292 stimulus words was recovered exactly from the released landing positions, and every fixation was assigned to a word and letter. Each child was described by word-level reading measures, linguistic sensitivities and saccade geometry in letters (LexiGaze), complemented by empirical-Bayes profiles and a generative likelihood-ratio classifier. Models were evaluated by nested participant-level cross-validation and under simulated gaze error. Results: The resulting word assignment matched the dataset labels for 99.99% of fixations. Dyslexia was associated with 42% longer gaze durations on meaningful text and with an exaggerated word-length effect on fixation counts. LexiGaze reached a balanced accuracy of 82.57% (AUC 0.913) and the generative classifier an AUC of 0.938, comparable to existing descriptors. Under gaze noise of 30 pixels, pixel-based geometry lost 23.4 points of balanced accuracy and LexiGaze 6.0 (direct comparison p = 0.053); with the recorded vertical coordinates, without drift correction, they lost 5.1 and 0.3 points. Conclusions: Word-anchored measures match existing accuracy while being interpretable in psycholinguistic terms and less sensitive to calibration error.

articles.title: Machine-Learning Prediction of Pediatric Thyroid Nodule Malignancy Using Structured Nodule and Cervical Lymph-Node Ultrasonographic Features.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pediatric thyroid nodules carry a higher malignancy risk and more frequent regional cervical lymph-node involvement than adult nodules, making individualized pre-biopsy risk assessment particularly important. We aimed to develop and temporally validate a machine-learning model integrating routinely available thyroid-nodule and cervical lymph-node ultrasonographic features for malignancy-risk estimation in children. Methods: This retrospective single-center study at a tertiary pediatric referral center included consecutive patients aged 18 years or younger undergoing biopsy-based diagnostic evaluation between January 2019 and August 2025. The cohort comprised 195 patients with 221 nodules. Six candidate algorithms were evaluated using patient-grouped nested cross-validation. The selected XGBoost model integrated structured nodule and regional cervical lymph-node ultrasonographic features and was evaluated using discrimination, precision-recall performance, probability accuracy, calibration, and threshold-dependent operating characteristics. ACR TI-RADS served as a secondary standardized comparator. Results: Overall, 151 of 221 nodules (68.3%) were malignant, including 32 of 48 nodules (66.7%) in the temporal validation cohort. The final model achieved an AUROC of 0.973 (95% CI, 0.919-1.000), an AUPRC of 0.986 (95% CI, 0.954-1.000), a Brier score of 0.071 (95% CI, 0.030-0.126), a sensitivity of 84.4%, and a specificity of 87.5%. For comparison, the ACR TI-RADS total score yielded an AUROC of 0.906, while the TR5-positive and TR4/5-positive strategies yielded sensitivities of 84.4% and 93.8% and specificities of 87.5% and 56.2%, respectively. Conclusions: Integrating thyroid-nodule and cervical lymph-node ultrasonographic features enabled individualized malignancy-risk estimation in this selected pediatric biopsy-evaluation cohort. The continuous risk estimate may complement established sonographic assessment as an adjunct to comprehensive diagnostic evaluation. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before broader clinical application.

articles.title: Dual-Timepoint 18F-FDG PET/CT Radiomics for Treatment Response in Breast Cancer: A Two-Center External Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Background: This study investigated the incremental value of radiomic features derived from 18F-FDG PET/CT over clinicopathological characteristics and conventional PET parameters for predicting and assessing metabolic treatment response in breast cancer, using independent external validation. Materials and Methods: This retrospective, two-center study included 153 patients with metastatic or non-metastatic breast cancer representing different biological subtypes, all of whom underwent systemic treatment and paired pretreatment and post-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT. The development cohort comprised 115 patients, while 38 patients from a second institution formed the external validation cohort. The endpoint was complete metabolic response (CMR) of the primary breast tumor. Scenario A examined pretreatment prediction of CMR using baseline variables, whereas Scenario B assessed imaging-defined CMR using post-treatment and longitudinal PET/CT parameters. Models were developed using L1-regularized logistic regression with five-fold stratified cross-validation and evaluated in the external cohort without refitting. Results: Primary-tumor CMR was observed in 14 of 115 patients (12.2%) in the development cohort and 18 of 38 patients (47.4%) in the external cohort. In Scenario A, the multimodal model incorporating radiomics achieved an external validation AUC of 0.747 (95% CI, 0.577-0.887), compared with 0.636 for the model combining clinicopathological variables and conventional PET parameters (ΔAUC = 0.111). Compared with the clinical-only model (AUC = 0.658), the multimodal model improved discrimination by 0.089, although the difference was not statistically significant (DeLong p = 0.146). In Scenario B, conventional post-treatment PET parameters achieved an AUC of 0.986 (95% CI, 0.953-1.000). Adding radiomic features did not improve discrimination (AUC = 0.986). Conclusions: Pretreatment radiomics showed potential additional value for predicting primary-tumor CMR, although the improvement in discrimination was not statistically significant. After treatment, conventional PET parameters provided high discrimination for imaging-defined primary-tumor CMR, with no further improvement from radiomics. These findings require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts before their clinical application.

articles.title: Enhancing HCC Surveillance with GPTs: Computational, Prompt Engineering, and Multimodal Strategies.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Research on applying Large Language Models to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance is limited. We aimed to develop customized GPTs for HCC surveillance and evaluate their performance in predicting HCC risk and providing surveillance recommendations. Materials and Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 376 patients with 797 surveillance visits between January 2014 and March 2023 for evaluation. We developed GPTs by integrating medical expert knowledge and optimized it through three strategies: (1) boosting computational capabilities via code enhancements and in-context learning; (2) enhancing reasoning abilities through prompt engineering; (3) increasing clinical applicability by integrating multimodal clinical data. We assessed the predictive performance of GPTs across different modalities and the efficiency and clinical appropriateness of their surveillance recommendations. Results: Combining in-context learning with code instruction improved HCC risk score calculation accuracy to 97.4%, compared with 90.2% using code instruction alone and 31.1% using default calculation (both p < 0.001). For the five-year HCC prediction, the second chain-of-thought (CoT2) strategy improved sensitivity from 65.3% to 77.6% (p = 0.037), with a numerically higher AUC compared with original GPTs (0.782 vs. 0.731, all p = 0.095). Dual-modality and multi-modality GPTs outperformed traditional scores in predicting HCC (AUC: 0.839 and 0.840 vs. 0.737-0.762, all p < 0.05). Among patients who developed HCC, multi-modality GPTs achieved the highest surveillance efficiency index (2.34) and an estimated earlier detection time of 5.43 months, compared with 2.22 and 4.49 months, respectively, under AASLD-based surveillance, with a higher estimated annual CT/MRI examination frequency (1.46 vs. 0.98). Conclusions: Customized GPTs showed promise for HCC risk prediction and individualized surveillance, warranting further prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: The Impact of MTHFR Gene Polymorphisms on Cerebral Small and Large Vessel Disease, Vascular Cognitive Impairment and Cerebral Volumetric Reduction.
articles.abstract: Objective: The study aims to evaluate the association of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) C677T and A1298C polymorphisms with cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD), cerebral large vessel disease (CLVD), vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) and global and regional brain volumes. Methods: Clinical, laboratory, neuroimaging, volumetric, cognitive and MTHFR genotyping data were retrospectively collected from 62 patients with CSVD (n = 40) or CLVD (n = 22), all carriers of at least one MTHFR variant. Brain volumes were compared between patients with VCI carrying C677T (n = 30) and patients without VCI (n = 32). Analyses were repeated in the open-source platform jamovi and p-values were corrected for multiple comparisons with the Holm procedure. Results: The cohort comprised 41 women and 21 men (mean age 56.9 years). The CT and TT genotypes of C677T, the AC and CC genotypes of A1298C, blood pressure, total cholesterol and triglycerides differed between CSVD and CLVD at the unadjusted level (p < 0.05), but none of these differences remained significant after Holm correction. VCI carriers of C677T showed lower white matter (332.9 ± 25.5 vs. 437.9 ± 35.7 cm3) and gray matter volumes (626.0 ± 45.7 vs. 699.7 ± 51.5 cm3), higher cerebrospinal fluid volume (238.3 ± 42.2 vs. 197.1 ± 24.8 cm3) and reduced hippocampal, amygdalar, thalamic, superior frontal, middle temporal, entorhinal, parahippocampal and middle occipital volumes (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.05). Conclusions: Differences in MTHFR genotype distribution between CSVD and CLVD were not robust to correction for multiple testing, whereas VCI carriers of C677T showed global and selective regional volume loss that withstood correction. MTHFR variants are susceptibility markers rather than direct causes of vascular injury; these associations, which could not be adjusted for comorbid vascular risk factors or for concomitant neurodegenerative pathology, require confirmation in prospective, controlled studies with homocysteine measurements.

articles.title: Beyond Epithelial Thickness: Comprehensive Profiling of Corneal Epithelial Remodeling and Its Diagnostic Value Across Keratoconus Severity: The Noor Multimodal Corneal Imaging Study (NMCIS).
articles.abstract: Background: Keratoconus causes characteristic spatial epithelial remodeling that may not be captured by conventional thickness measurements. Novel morphometric indices from MS-39 AS-OCT may better characterize these changes. Purpose: We aimed to evaluate novel MS-39 AS-OCT epithelial remodeling indices and compare their diagnostic accuracy with epithelial thickness and Pentacam tomography across the keratoconus spectrum, using an objective reference standard. Methods: This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 1319 eyes of 1286 patients with same-day Pentacam and MS-39 imaging at Noor Eye Hospital (2023-2025). Eyes were classified from the clinical records and Pentacam front-surface indices, without use of any epithelial data, as normal (n = 861), forme fruste keratoconus (FFKC; topographically normal fellow eye of very asymmetric ectasia; n = 40) or definite keratoconus (n = 418), graded mild, moderate or severe with the ABCD system. Generalized estimating equations, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with DeLong confidence intervals and cross-validated cut-offs, and bootstrap-validated logistic models were used. Results: The central epithelial remodeling index (CERI) and central epithelial thickness range (CETR) increased with severity (+0.137 and +6.13 µm per severity grade; both p < 0.001). For definite keratoconus, CERI (AUC 0.932; 95% CI 0.913-0.948) and CETR (0.930) outperformed central minimum epithelial thickness (0.839; p < 0.001) but not BAD-D (0.972). Their AUCs rose from 0.666-0.677 in mild to 0.993-0.995 in severe keratoconus, a gradient that partly reflects the disease spectrum. For FFKC, the best epithelial AUC was 0.668 (6 mm epithelial thickness range) versus 0.728 for BAD-D, and adding five epithelial indices to tomography did not improve validated discrimination (out-of-bag AUC gain +0.000 for definite keratoconus and +0.012, 95% interval -0.080 to +0.083, for FFKC). Conclusions: CERI and CETR quantify epithelial remodeling and discriminate established keratoconus well, but they add little validated discrimination to Pentacam tomography; in FFKC, their discrimination was modest and any added value remains uncertain. They may complement, but not replace, tomography and biomechanics.

articles.title: Developmental Disabilities and Subsequent Asthma Diagnosis in Children: Diagnostic Implications from a Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: The longitudinal risk of asthma among children with developmental disabilities (DDs) remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between DD and subsequent asthma risk. Methods: We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database from 2009 through 2019. Children younger than 18 years with a claims-based DD diagnosis were propensity-score-matched 1:1 with children without DD. Children with asthma before the index date were excluded. Incident recorded asthma was defined using ICD-9-CM code 493.- or ICD-10-CM code J45.-; ICD-10-CM J44.- was excluded. Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs). Prespecified subtype analyses addressed DD heterogeneity. Results: The study included 213,759 children in each cohort. The DD cohort had 43,782 recorded asthma diagnoses during 1,503,077 person-years (29.13 per 1000 person-years), compared with 30,559 diagnoses during 1,620,645 person-years among controls (18.86 per 1000 person-years). DD was associated with a higher rate of subsequent recorded asthma diagnosis (aHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.67-1.72), with associations present in both sexes and all age strata. Subtype-specific aHRs ranged from 1.65 for developmental delay or speech and language disorders to 1.94 for autism spectrum disorder. Exploratory post-index therapy and medication estimates were not interpreted as causal treatment effects. Conclusions: In this administrative claims cohort, a pre-existing DD diagnosis was associated with an approximately 70% higher adjusted rate of a subsequent recorded asthma diagnosis. The finding may support careful respiratory assessment when symptoms occur. Prospective studies incorporating healthcare-utilization measures, standardized asthma confirmation, and objective pulmonary testing are needed.

articles.title: FetalSANet: A Lightweight Spatial-Attention MobileNetV2 Framework for Fetal Ultrasound Plane Classification.
articles.abstract: Reliable identification of standard fetal ultrasound planes underpins prenatal biometry and screening, but manual identification depends on the operator. This study evaluates FetalSANet, a lightweight MobileNetV2 classifier with a 98-parameter spatial-attention module, against channel-attention, dual-attention and no-attention variants on FETAL_PLANES_DB. On the released split (five classes, one seed), spatial attention reached 93.70% accuracy, but its difference from the no-attention baseline was not significant (McNemar p=0.429), and a perceptual-hash audit found near-duplicate images across the training, validation and test partitions, mainly in Fetal Thorax and Maternal Cervix. We therefore re-evaluated the baseline and FetalSANet on a patient-disjoint, deduplicated split (six classes) with three seeds: accuracy was 88.13±0.37% and 88.29±0.79%, with no significant difference in paired tests (not evidence of equivalence). The module adds 9.6 KFLOPs to a 0.60 GFLOP network. In an external-domain evaluation without fine-tuning (two classes, two sources, N=2588), unrestricted five-class accuracy was about 87% (96.64% when restricted to the two present classes), and 11.51% of predictions fell into absent classes; class and data source are confounded. Grad-CAM++ maps are qualitative examples only. Spatial attention is therefore a nearly free but not demonstrably beneficial addition, and released-split accuracy should not be read as patient-level performance.

articles.title: Cancer Therapy-Induced Right Ventricular Systolic and Diastolic Dysfunction Assessed Using Conventional Echocardiographic Indices: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer treatment can impair right ventricular (RV) systolic and diastolic function by altering cardiomyocyte metabolism and inducing cell death. The incidence and prognosis of cancer therapy-induced RV involvement remain uncertain. We assessed RV diastolic changes and their association with systolic RV and LV dysfunction in cancer patients. Methods: We prospectively observed 60 adults (91.7% female, aged 31 to 74 years) with breast or gastrointestinal cancer receiving chemotherapy for a median of 381 days (IQR 187, 464), excluding those with cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. RV diastolic function was assessed using the 2010 right heart echocardiographic guidelines. RV systolic dysfunction was defined by abnormal values in at least two of the following RV indices: fractional area change (RVFAC), systolic tissue Doppler velocity (RVS'), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, or myocardial performance index. LV dysfunction was defined by abnormal LV ejection fraction or average systolic LV tissue Doppler velocity. Results: RV systolic dysfunction was found in 7 patients (11.7%), RV diastolic dysfunction in 12 (30.7%), and LV dysfunction in 11 (18.3%). Generalised estimating equations showed early decreases in RVS' and RVFAC at the first month (β = -0.68, p = 0.016; β = -2.2, p = 0.006), and later changes in RV early diastolic tissue velocity (RVe') and the ratio of early RV filling velocity (RVE) to RVe' (RVE/e') at the third month (β = -1.03, p = 0.005; β = 0.35, p = 0.034). Higher RVFAC values were linked to lower odds of LV dysfunction (OR 0.88, p = 0.002). RVe' was associated with RV systolic dysfunction (OR 0.61, p < 0.001), with a threshold of 10 cm/s (AUC 0.81; 95% CI: 0.69, 0.93). Conclusions: Conventional echocardiographic parameters may facilitate the detection of RV systolic and diastolic dysfunction during cancer therapy. Early alterations and the prognostic value of RV parameters support the necessity for their routine monitoring.

articles.title: Microbiological Assessment of Halitosis in Users of E-Cigarettes, Heated Tobacco Products, and Combustible Cigarettes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The diagnostic value of oral microbiological testing in users of different nicotine products remains uncertain. We compared tongue-coating dysbiosis, salivary cultures, and chairside enzymatic activity across product groups and evaluated their discrimination of objective halitosis. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 225 adults: 60 never-users, 55 combustible cigarette users, 52 heated tobacco product users, and 58 e-cigarette users. Six tongue-coating taxa and total bacterial load were quantified by quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Salivary cultures and the benzoyl-DL-arginine-naphthylamide (BANA) test complemented organoleptic assessment and volatile sulfur compound measurement. Analyses included adjusted regression, compositional analysis, exploratory profiling and mediation, and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results: Adjusted dysbiosis-index differences versus never-users were 1.82, 1.50, and 2.08 units for combustible cigarette, heated tobacco product, and e-cigarette users, respectively (all p < 0.001). E-cigarette users had the highest Solobacterium moorei load and Candida carriage, whereas combustible cigarette users had the highest Porphyromonas gingivalis load and BANA positivity. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) R2 was 15.8%, with heterogeneous dispersions. Objective halitosis prevalence ranged from 10.8% to 66.7% across microbial profiles. The chairside/culture panel and dysbiosis index had areas under the curve of 0.72 and 0.71, respectively. Conclusions: Microbial differences were associated with product use, but exposure history and oral conditions may confound these associations. Moderate discrimination and absent external validation preclude diagnostic interchangeability or routine implementation of these adjunctive tests.

articles.title: LQ-HybridNet: A Parameter-Compact Classical Architecture with Quantum-Inspired Feature Transformations for Skin Lesion Classification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluates LQ-HybridNet, a parameter-compact classical architecture for skin-lesion classification. Methods: MobileNetV2 is augmented with amplitude-phase channel gating and a four-qubit variational circuit feature transformation. Crucially, all evaluations enforce a rigorous, leakage-resistant stratified lesion-level split to prevent data contamination. Here, quantum-inspired denotes a classical mathematical inductive bias, not quantum hardware execution or computational advantage. Results: On HAM10000, LQ-HybridNet achieved 90.80±0.25% accuracy, 0.7714 macro precision, 0.7257 macro recall, and 0.7428 macro F1-score, compared with 88.50±0.30% accuracy for MobileNetV2. The 2.30 percentage-point gain required 45.9K additional parameters. Across the evaluated backbones, accuracy gains ranged from 1.10 to 2.40 percentage points on HAM10000 and 1.77 to 4.00 points on ISIC 2018. Latency increased from 12.4 to 48.7 ms per batch of 32 images. Conclusions: The structured classical transformations yielded incremental benchmark improvements with small parameter overhead but approximately 3.9-fold higher latency. These results concern the evaluated architectures and benchmark distributions; parameter compactness does not imply inference efficiency.

articles.title: Synthetic Haematocrit for Myocardial Extracellular Volume Mapping in Clinical Practice at 1.5 T and 3 T.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Synthetic haematocrit (HCT) permits cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) extracellular volume fraction (ECV) estimation without contemporaneous laboratory HCT. We evaluated four published equations in a clinical referral cohort. Methods: This retrospective audit included 67 adults scanned at 1.5 T (n = 34) or 3 T (n = 33), with laboratory HCT within 24 h. Two equations per field strength were assessed using correlation and Bland-Altman analysis with confidence intervals. Observer reproducibility of T1 and calculated synthetic ECV was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Post hoc exploratory analyses examined classification at ECV ≥ 30%, estimation-error associations and proportional bias. Results: Absolute mean ECV bias was below one percentage point for all equations, but model-specific limits of agreement extended from -4.47 to 4.19 percentage points. At the exploratory 30% threshold, classification agreement was 85.3% and 88.2% at 1.5 T and 75.8% for both equations at 3 T. Synthetic ECV intraobserver ICCs ranged from 0.853 to 0.949; interobserver ICCs were 0.936-0.944 at 1.5 T and 0.842-0.851 at 3 T. Shang HCT showed magnitude-dependent disagreement. Conclusions: Synthetic ECV may help assess myocardial tissue when timely laboratory haematocrit is unavailable, with low average differences from conventional ECV. However, the small groups limit precision and generalisability, and individual and observer differences prevent assuming interchangeability. Local validation is needed before using synthetic ECV for clinical decisions or monitoring changes over time.

articles.title: Integrated Urinary Metabolomics and Artificial Intelligence for the Identification of Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Progression Biomarkers in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 10% of the global population, and it is a critical challenge for public health worldwide. The integration of metabolomics with machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising approach to enhancing disease diagnosis and prognosis. Objective: This study characterized the urinary metabolomic profiles of individuals with intermediate-to-advanced CKD and developed predictive models for disease diagnosis and prognosis. Methods: Urine samples from 129 participants, including healthy individuals and patients with CKD, were analyzed using liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Multivariate analysis was performed to identify differences between groups. ML algorithms were the best for developing predictive models for the diagnosis, prognosis, and progression of CKD. Results: The results show the identities of 1499 metabolites. They also indicate that ML models effectively differentiated between healthy individuals and CKD patients, demonstrating high accuracy and specificity. The RF model was effective for diagnostic purposes, while the SVM showed superior performance in prognostic and disease progression predictions. The differentially expressed metabolites found, predominantly lipids, may serve as potential biomarkers for the detection and progression of CKD. Conclusions: The combination of urinary metabolomics with ML algorithms represents a promising, non-invasive approach for CKD diagnosis and follow-up, offering an alternative that may improve both the precision and personalization of disease management.

articles.title: Uncertainty and Geometric Image-Region Ranking in Artificial Intelligence-Based Panoramic Tooth Segmentation: A Multi-Source External Benchmark.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This retrospective benchmark evaluated scores for selecting regions of panoramic tooth segmentations for review. Methods: Three-member U-Net ensembles trained on UFBA-425 were evaluated on 590 held-out images and subsequently on 329 photographed radiographs. The original mixed-granularity pipeline comparison used the calibrated residual ensemble on 100 pediatric images. Cells in a 2 × 4 grid received regional mutual information (MI) scores but shared one whole-image soft Dice confidence (SDC) value. A lower Dice-risk area under the risk-coverage curve (AURC) indicated better ranking against source masks. Interaction tests, quality subset analyses, and prediction-positive sensitivity analyses were post hoc. Image-key bootstrap intervals may be too narrow for patient-level inference because patient independence was unverified. Results: The primary MI-minus-SDC AURC difference was +0.007 (95% confidence interval -0.033 to +0.041), leaving the comparison inconclusive. Subsequent evaluations were exploratory. Analyses of reference-positive cells (containing reference tooth pixels) received co-principal emphasis after outcomes were known. MI had a higher Dice-risk AURC than the replicated SDC in the pediatric main subset (+0.238) and the local SDC in AKUDENTAL (+0.157 residual, +0.134 ResNet18). When 20% of grid cells were reviewed, the mean maximum pixel probability (MSP) captured more error pixels than MI in seven of ten source/model comparisons, including both AKUDENTAL ensembles. On photographed radiographs, the MSP led by 15.73 percentage points for the residual ensemble and MI by 3.66 for ResNet18. For ResNet18, equal weighting of false-positive and false-negative capture favored MSP by 6.59 points. Conclusions: The primary comparison established neither superiority nor equivalence. Exploratory capture varied by source, model, and error mix.

articles.title: Super-Resolution Ultrasound Microvascular Features in Breast Invasive Ductal Carcinoma: Associations with Ki-67 Status and Stromal Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte Categories.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) depicts tumor microvascular structure and flow. We examined associations with Ki-67 status, stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (sTIL) categories, and immunohistochemistry-based surrogate subtypes in untreated breast invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). Methods: This single-center retrospective secondary analysis included 72 surgically confirmed IDCs. Ki-67 was categorized as low (<20%; n = 31) or high (≥20%; n = 41) and sTILs as three ordered categories. Eight SRUS fields underwent endpoint-specific false-discovery-rate correction. Revision-stage logistic and ordinal logistic models examined four selected features separately, adjusting for age and log-transformed lesion volume. Results: Complexity levels and vessel ratios were higher in high-Ki-67 tumors (both q < 0.001). Maximum curvature based on the sum-of-angles metric (MaxCurvatureSOAM) and density entropy (DenEntropy) were inversely associated with the sTIL category (Spearman ρ = -0.475 and -0.411; both q < 0.001). These four association directions persisted after age/volume adjustment (all q < 0.001), although Ki-67 effect estimates were imprecise and sensitive to individual observations. Subtype differences were exploratory, with the two smallest groups containing nine and six tumors. A supplementary two-feature analysis did not establish incremental clinical value over the vessel ratio alone. Conclusions: SRUS features showed exploratory imaging-pathology associations that persisted after limited clinical adjustment. Residual confounding, small subtype groups, platform-specific measurements, and the absence of external validation preclude claims of independent biological effects or clinical decision utility.

articles.title: Early-Term Pneumopericardium After Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract: Free air in the pericardial space is called pneumopericardium, a rare phenomenon. Increased intra-alveolar pressure may cause alveolar rupture, releasing air that travels to the pericardial space. This condition can occur following trauma or surgical interventions. In this case, we present a young female patient with pneumopericardium that developed early after open-heart surgery. Interestingly, the pleural spaces were not opened during the initial operation, and hemodynamic stability was maintained despite the massive mediastinal air that developed. The case was treated surgically due to the possible risk of infection associated with the Dacron graft in the mediastinum.

articles.title: Clinical Significance of Abnormal First-Trimester Chorionic Villus Sampling After Mosaic Embryo Transfer: A Prospective Study with Confirmatory Amniocentesis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Prenatal outcomes after mosaic embryo transfer are generally reassuring. However, evidence remains limited on how an abnormal first-trimester chorionic villus sampling (CVS) result should be interpreted. We evaluated first-trimester CVS findings after mosaic embryo transfer and examined their relationship with the original preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) results and subsequent amniocentesis. Methods: This prospective observational study included 183 CVS specimens obtained from placentas corresponding to PGT-A-designated mosaic embryos. Uncultured chorionic villi were analyzed using the same next-generation sequencing platform used for PGT-A. Abnormal CVS findings were compared with the original PGT-A results, and all nine pregnancies with an abnormal CVS result underwent diagnostic amniocentesis. Results: Of the 183 CVS specimens, 174 (95.1%) were euploid and nine (4.9%; exact 95% confidence interval, 2.27-9.13%) were abnormal. Among the nine abnormal findings, three involved the same chromosome or chromosomal region reported by PGT-A, whereas six involved a different chromosome or region. Amniocentesis showed a euploid result in eight cases, which were classified as confirmed confined placental mosaicism. In the remaining case, mosaicism was also detected in amniotic fluid and was classified as confirmed fetal mosaicism. Conclusions: This is the largest published series specifically evaluating first-trimester CVS after mosaic embryo transfer. Abnormal CVS findings were uncommon, and eight of the nine abnormal findings were confined to the placenta. Furthermore, six involved a chromosome or chromosomal region different from that reported by PGT-A. Therefore, an abnormal CVS result does not necessarily indicate fetal involvement or persistence of the original PGT-A abnormality. Amniocentesis is required to clarify the fetal chromosomal status.

articles.title: Robustness of U-Net Retinal Layer Segmentation to Controlled OCT Image Degradation.
articles.abstract: Background: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) retinal layer segmentation supports quantitative clinical assessment, but its robustness to different image degradation has not been systematically characterized. Methods: This study evaluates a U-Net trained on unmodified OCT5k scans under seven synthetic degradation families at five family-specific severity levels. The test set included 315 held-out B-scans from nine cases, with three cases each of age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and healthy retinas. After ordered boundary decoding, two primary outcomes were calculated: boundary mean absolute error (MAE, pixels) and internal-layer Dice. Results: Clean images yielded macro-MAE of 3.66 pixels and macro-Dice of 0.934. At severity 5, MAE increased in five families and Dice decreased in all seven.
