Gaussian noise, contrast reduction, and global attenuation produced the largest deterioration, with macro-MAE/macro-Dice values of 94.35/0.715, 236.81/0.044, and 112.32/0.0004, respectively. Adjusted paired tests showed statistically significant deterioration in both outcomes for these three families; macro-Dice also showed declines under defocus, shadowing, and axial-resolution reduction, while speckle showed no significant change. Conclusions: These results indicate corruption- and metric-specific vulnerability in the tested U-Net. This study may inform the development of automated OCT image-quality screening. Before clinical use, these findings may be evaluated on other segmentation models, larger datasets, additional OCT devices, and with naturally occurring acquisition artifacts.

articles.title: Explainable Transfer Learning for Brain Tumor MRI Classification: Leakage-Aware Evaluation, Grey Wolf Optimizer-Based Hyperparameter Tuning, and Quantitative Attribution Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate MRI-based brain tumor classification requires leakage-free performance estimates and inspectable decisions. We compared pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs), evaluated Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO)-based hyperparameter tuning against alternative search strategies, and quantified Grad-CAM explanations. Methods: Seven ImageNet-pretrained CNNs were compared with duplicate-aware 10-fold cross-validation on 5966 images of a public four-class dataset; 1057 images were held out. GWO tuning of VGG16 was compared with five other search strategies at an equal budget. Ablation, cost-sensitive training, external validation (BDNeuro-MRI), and Grad-CAM analyses of all test images were performed. Results: VGG16 had the highest cross-validation accuracy under the original protocol (96.73 ± 1.24%) but not under full fine-tuning. GWO-VGG16 reached 98.68% hold-out accuracy (95% CI 97.92-99.34%). Because 39.7% of test images had a duplicate in the development data, accuracy was also assessed on 637 duplicate-free test images (98.27%; 95% CI 96.93-99.03%) and on 1888 non-overlapping external images (87.29%; 95% CI 85.75-88.77%). GWO was not superior to alternative search strategies. Grad-CAM maps showed little border attention and were model-dependent, but lesion localization remained unverified. Conclusions: High internal accuracy did not fully transfer to external data; without patient-level validation and expert annotations, the framework remains a research-stage tool, not a validated diagnostic system.

articles.title: Genetic Polymorphisms in Apoptosis-Related Genes XAF1 and XIAP Are Associated with Clinical Outcomes in Pediatric Ewing Sarcoma.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ewing sarcoma (ES) is an aggressive malignant cancer with a higher incidence in adolescents and young adults. Despite multimodal therapy, prognosis remains poor, particularly in metastatic and recurrence cases. Dysregulation of apoptosis is central to ES tumorigenesis; however, the impact of polymorphisms in apoptotic regulators on clinical outcomes remains unclear. This study investigated the association between single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the apoptotic pathway genes XAF1 and XIAP and their respective protein expression in ES outcomes. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted on ES samples from paraffin blocks (n = 55). Genotyping for selected SNPs and immunohistochemistry for XAF1 and XIAP expression were performed. The cohort included 41 pediatric and 14 non-pediatric cases. Statistical associations were analyzed between genotypes, age groups, protein expression, and recurrence. Results: The male sex (61.8%) and bone site (75.5%) were prevalent, while recurrence (30.9%) and metastasis (14.5%) were frequent outcomes. There was low or absent XAF1 expression (<1.2 μm2) in 75.5% of all ES cases, and 54.9% showed higher XIAP expression (≥16.4 μm2). The A allele present in the dominant group (AA + AG) of the rs3785793 [A/G] XAF1 gene, showed significantly lower XAF1 expression (p = 0.043) and was associated with recurrence in comparison to the GG genotype in pediatric ES. Conclusions: ES showed low or absent protein XAF1 expression and high XIAP expression. The wild-type A-allele of XAF1 rs3785793 was associated with decreased protein expression and increased recurrence outcome in pediatric ES. These findings suggest XAF1 polymorphism might be a potential biomarker for outcomes in ES, warranting further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Association of the Cholesterol-High-Density Lipoprotein-Glucose Index with Large-Artery Atherosclerotic Versus Cardioembolic Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We aimed to assess the association of the cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein-glucose index (CHG) with large-artery atherosclerotic stroke (LAA) versus cardioembolic stroke (CE), and to compare its discrimination and incremental value beyond a clinical model with those of the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG). Methods: This single-center retrospective study consecutively screened patients hospitalized with ischemic stroke at Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University, from September 2024 to August 2025 and included eligible patients with acute LAA or CE. CHG and TyG were calculated from the first examination results after admission. Missing BMI values were handled using 20 multiple imputations. Logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and exploratory subgroup analyses were used to evaluate associations, with further adjustment for lipid-lowering and glucose-lowering medication use before the current stroke onset. Firth-penalized regression was also used to assess the robustness of the association estimates. Model performance was evaluated using 1000 paired outcome-stratified bootstrap resamples, comparing CHG, TyG, and joint modeling of the three component indicators and estimating differences in corrected AUC and their 95% confidence intervals. Results: The study included 921 patients, comprising 790 with LAA and 131 with CE. After multivariable adjustment, each 1-standard-deviation increase in CHG was associated with an odds ratio of 2.83 for LAA versus CE (95% confidence interval: 2.20-3.65, p < 0.001), with a nonlinear association (p for nonlinearity = 0.003). The OR in the Firth sensitivity analysis was 2.77 (95% confidence interval: 2.17-3.59). The single-index AUCs of CHG and TyG were 0.725 and 0.662, respectively (paired DeLong p < 0.001). Adding CHG increased the bootstrap-corrected AUC of the clinical model from 0.647 to 0.743 and reduced the corrected Brier score from 0.119 to 0.105. The difference in corrected AUC between the CHG-enhanced model and the TyG-enhanced model was 0.051 (95% confidence interval: 0.025-0.079), whereas its difference from the model jointly including the three component indicators remained uncertain. The direction of the main associations was consistent in sensitivity analyses, and no clear subgroup interactions were identified. Conclusions: In this cohort, higher CHG was positively associated with LAA versus CE after adjustment for measured covariates. Its enhanced model had higher discrimination than the TyG-enhanced model in internal validation, but its advantage over joint modeling of the component indicators remained uncertain. This was a single-center retrospective study with a substantial imbalance in group sizes, and residual confounding may remain. All performance estimates were derived from internal validation. The clinical utility of CHG and its applicability across centers have not been established and require independent external validation.

articles.title: Calibration and Cross-Dataset Behavior in Malaria Microscopy with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: A Matched LoRA-PiSSA Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Reliable evaluation of deep-learning methods for malaria microscopy requires assessing both classification performance and the quality of predicted infection probabilities across datasets. We compared low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and principal singular values and singular vectors adaptation (PiSSA) under matched parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). Methods: An ImageNet-pretrained vision transformer (ViT-B/16) was adapted at ranks 2, 4, 8, and 16 using 27,558 National Institutes of Health (NIH) malaria cell images. One NIH grouped partition was held fixed across paired training seeds 42, 123, and 456. Models were evaluated on the NIH test split and, without target-domain adaptation, on BBBC041 P. vivax cell crops. The analysis was also replicated in invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) histopathology. External probability and threshold-transfer analyses were post hoc. Results: Across LoRA and PiSSA configurations, NIH area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) ranged from 0.9960 to 0.9970. PiSSA had lower rank-level mean Brier scores and expected calibration error (ECE) at every evaluated rank in NIH and IDC, although paired-run differences varied. On BBBC041, PiSSA-r16 achieved the highest PEFT ROC-AUC (0.8451) and area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC, 0.1588), while fully trained reference models performed better. Across all 12 matched external comparisons, PiSSA had lower overall Brier scores and ECE but higher infected-cell Brier scores. PiSSA had lower sensitivity at NIH-derived thresholds in 11 of 12 comparisons. All PEFT models overpredicted infection relative to the observed 2.70% prevalence. Conclusions: Nearly identical internal discrimination concealed differences in external probability behavior and class-specific errors. PiSSA reduced overprediction, but neither adapter achieved adequate external calibration.

articles.title: Association Between Trapezius Lateral Shear Strain and Perceived Stiffness Assessed with Continuous Shear Wave Imaging: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We explored whether lateral shear strain (L-str), an imaging-derived parameter estimated from oscillatory displacement in continuous shear wave imaging (C-SWI), was associated with perceived shoulder stiffness. Methods: In this prospective observational study, 12 adults with chronic shoulder stiffness underwent bilateral C-SWI of the upper and lower trapezius and symptom evaluation at baseline and 4-week follow-up. During follow-up, participants undertook a general exercise routine provided independently of the study. Results: No C-SWI parameter changed significantly at the group level after multiplicity correction. Change in bilateral averaged all-muscle L-str was inversely associated with change in stiffness assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS) (Pearson r = -0.804, 95% confidence interval -0.94 to -0.43, p = 0.0016). The false-discovery-rate q value was 0.029 within 18 L-str-symptom comparisons, 0.058 with 36 pooled symptom comparisons, and 0.109 with all 68 comparisons; the Spearman correlation did not remain significant (ρ = -0.77, q = 0.063). After adjustment for baseline stiffness, the partial correlation was -0.51 (p = 0.11). Conclusions: These exploratory findings are sensitive to analysis choices and baseline adjustment, and regression to the mean cannot be excluded. L-str has not been independently validated as a measure of tissue deformation; confirmation is required.

articles.title: Bench Agreement of Two Units of a Low-Cost Digital Manometers with a Clinical Respiratory Pressure Comparator: A Laboratory-Based Comparison.
articles.abstract: Background: Maximal inspiratory (MIP) and expiratory (MEP) pressures are widely used indices of respiratory muscle strength, but clinical manometers are costly. We evaluated the bench agreement of two units of a low-cost digital manometer with a clinical respiratory pressure comparator. Methods: Two BioPimo 101® units and a Vitalograph Pneumotrac 6800® were connected simultaneously to a mechanical insufflation-exsufflation device coupled to a test lung. Pressures of 5-70 cmH2O were applied in 5-cmH2O steps under two compliance conditions, in triplicate (56 conditions; 336 paired differences analyzed as repeated measurements). Agreement was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis, condition-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals, regression-based limits of agreement and ICC (2,1). Results: For MIP, mean differences were -0.03 to 0.21 cmH2O (limits of agreement -0.42 to 0.72 cmH2O). For MEP, both units showed higher readings than the comparator (mean differences 0.52-0.72 cmH2O), and differences increased with pressure; at 70 cmH2O under low compliance, the predicted upper limit of agreement reached 2.44-2.64 cmH2O. ICCs exceeded 0.999. Conclusions: Both units agreed closely with the comparator under bench conditions, particularly for MIP, whereas MEP showed positive, pressure-dependent differences. Without a traceable pressure standard and with only two units tested, these findings do not establish absolute accuracy or clinical interchangeability.

articles.title: Calprotectin Measurement in Rectal Mucus Collected with the OriCol™ Sampling Device: A Method-Comparison Study Against Faecal Calprotectin Reference Tests.
articles.abstract: Background: Faecal calprotectin is recommended by the UK National Institute of Health and Care Excellence (NICE) HealthTech guidance HTG320 (2013) to distinguish inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from functional bowel disorders, including irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), when cancer is not suspected, and to monitor IBD activity. Stool collection can limit adherence. Home-based and smartphone-enabled assays partly address this gap, but clinic-acquired sampling could provide results soon after consultation. We compared calprotectin in OriCol™ Sampling Device-collected rectal mucus with matched faecal calprotectin. Methods: Sixty-six adults were prospectively recruited from three NHS gastroenterology clinics. Each provided a clinic-acquired rectal mucus sample and matched stool sample. Calprotectin was measured using two CE-marked ELISAs (IDK® Calprotectin and fCAL®), with laboratory staff blinded to clinical category. The primary endpoint was categorical agreement at the 50 µg/g faecal threshold; secondary analyses included Bland-Altman analysis, Cohen's κ and patient acceptability. Results: Calprotectin was detected across both assays' working ranges and correlated positively between matrices. Forty-eight participants were eligible for threshold analysis. Regression-derived rectal mucus equivalents produced positive percent agreement of 79% (95% CI 61-91) for IDK® and 68% (51-82) for fCAL®, and negative percent agreement of 53% (27-79) and 40% (12-74), respectively. Chance-corrected agreement was fair for IDK® (κ 0.32, 95% CI 0.02-0.62) and slight for fCAL® (κ 0.07, 95% CI -0.27-0.41), and Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement between matrices were wide (spanning roughly two orders of magnitude). Among IBD patients, paired results were above threshold in 93% and 86%, respectively. Of 60 respondents, 96.7% would repeat sampling, 55.6% of those expressing a preference (30 of 54) chose OriCol™, and no OriCol™ Sampling Device-related adverse events occurred. Conclusions: OriCol™ enabled acceptable clinic-based rectal mucus calprotectin measurement with positive correlation to faecal results. Above-threshold agreement was encouraging, but the low negative agreement, the fair-to-slight κ values and the wide between-matrix limits of agreement indicate that rectal mucus calprotectin is not equivalent to faecal calprotectin. Below-threshold agreement, in particular, requires confirmation in larger independent cohorts with pre-specified thresholds before clinical implementation based upon current diagnostic platform threshold.

articles.title: Preterm Small-for-Gestational-Age Risk Estimates Using Large Language Models Versus the FMF Competing-Risks Model.
articles.abstract: Introduction: The midgestation prediction of preterm small-for-gestational-age (SGA) birth could use the externally validated Fetal Medicine Foundation (FMF) competing-risks model, integrating maternal characteristics and obstetric history with fetal biometry and biophysical markers. Large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly used for pregnancy-related health information, but how their numerical risk estimates respond to clinical inputs compared with this model is not known. Objective: To compare the direction and relative magnitude of changes in numerical estimates of preterm SGA risk from eight LLMs and the FMF competing-risks model when individual predictors are varied, and examine how agreement relates to the calculation methods reported by the LLMs. Methods: We generated 108 synthetic singleton pregnancy scenarios by varying one of 16 clinical variables (19 encoded predictors) at a time around low-risk multiparous and nulliparous profiles assessed at 22 weeks. Each LLM was queried once through its consumer interface for the probability of birthweight below the 10th percentile with delivery before 37 weeks; temperature and tool use could not be controlled. FMF probabilities were calculated from the published equations. Local interpretable model-agnostic explanation (LIME)-inspired weighted linear surrogates were fitted to logit-transformed probabilities and compared with FMF using an exploratory composite alignment score, combining directional concordance, Spearman correlation, cosine similarity, and normalized root mean squared error similarity. Absolute agreement was assessed on the logit scale. Results: The largest FMF surrogate coefficients were chronic hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and smoking among binary predictors, and uterine artery pulsatility index, estimated fetal weight Z-score, and gestational age at the previous delivery among continuous predictors. Composite alignment with FMF was highest for GPT-6 (0.999), Mistral (0.988), and Grok (0.917), followed by Claude (0.894), DeepSeek (0.769), Meta (0.752), Qwen (0.600), and Copilot (0.492). Diabetes mellitus received a negative surrogate coefficient in four LLMs, although only DeepSeek returned a lower probability with diabetes than without. Predicted probabilities agreed closely with FMF only for GPT-6; the other LLMs predicted higher risks, with odds on average 1.2 to 9 times those of FMF. GPT-6, Mistral, and Grok reported implementing the published FMF algorithm, although this cannot be verified; Claude, DeepSeek, and Qwen described approximate logistic models; and Copilot and Meta displayed no process messages. Conclusions: Under a single prompt and uncontrolled consumer access conditions, similarity to the FMF model varied widely and was highest for LLMs reporting use of the published algorithm, while predicted risks often diverged, even when the effects of individual risk factors were similar. Verification of the calculations and validation against observed pregnancy outcomes are required before clinical application.

articles.title: Microscopic Fat on Chemical-Shift MRI in Solid Renal Tumours: Clear Cell Carcinoma, Fat-Poor Angiomyolipoma and the Added Value of T2-Weighted Heterogeneity and Necrosis.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: To assess whether microscopic fat on chemical-shift MRI, T2-weighted heterogeneity and necrosis separate clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and fat-poor angiomyolipoma (AML) from other solid renal tumours and from each other. Methods: Seventy pathologically proven solid renal tumours without macroscopic fat (38 ccRCCs, 17 papillary RCCs, five chromophobe RCCs, six AMLs, and four oncocytomas) consecutively imaged at 1.5 T between 2017 and 2021 were reviewed retrospectively by one radiologist blinded to histology. Visual signal loss, the chemical-shift index (CSI) and a tumour-to-kidney signal-intensity drop ratio were recorded; signal loss > 20% defined microscopic fat. T2-weighted heterogeneity and necrosis/cystic degeneration (T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images) were recorded. Groups were compared with non-parametric and Fisher's exact tests. Results: Median CSI was 43.8% in AML, 14.3% in ccRCC and ≤11.7% in the other subtypes (p < 0.001). A CSI > 20% was observed in 20 of 44 ccRCCs or AMLs and in 1 of 26 other tumours (p < 0.001; sensitivity 45.5%, specificity 96.2%); the tumour-to-kidney ratio and visual assessment performed similarly. AML had higher CSI than ccRCC (p = 0.033), but threshold positivity did not differ significantly (5/6 vs. 15/38; p = 0.077). T2-weighted heterogeneity (84% vs. 17%; p = 0.002) and necrosis/cystic degeneration (82% vs. 0%; p < 0.001) were more frequent in ccRCC than AML. An exploratory AML-positive criterion combining CSI > 20% with T2 homogeneity increased specificity from 60.5% to 92.1%, while sensitivity decreased from 83.3% to 66.7%. A negative CSI was more frequent in papillary RCC (59% vs. 19%, p = 0.004). Conclusions: Opposed-phase signal loss > 20% is a specific but insensitive marker of ccRCC or AML. Morphology provided exploratory complementary information, but the six-AML subgroup limits precision.

articles.title: PulmonaryAspergilloma Developing in a Giant Emphysematous Bulla.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary aspergilloma usually develops in a pre-existing pulmonary cavity and may present with hemoptysis. We report a 51-year-old former smoker with bilateral apical post-tuberculous sequelae, severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic respiratory failure requiring long-term oxygen therapy, and a three-month history of worsening dyspnea, productive cough with intermittent mild hemoptysis (blood-streaked sputum), and right-sided pleuritic pain. Chest computed tomography demonstrated bilateral giant emphysematous bullae and a round intracavitary soft-tissue mass within a right upper-lobe cavity of uncertain origin, partially outlined by a crescent of air. Bronchoscopy showed marked traction-related bronchial distortion without an endobronchial lesion. Bronchial aspirate was positive for Aspergillus spp. by polymerase chain reaction and fungal culture, while investigations for active tuberculosis were negative. Surgical resection was considered unsuitable because of severely impaired pulmonary function and extensive parenchymal destruction. Itraconazole was initiated; during approximately eight months of therapy, two admissions for mild hemoptysis were followed by resolution, and the patient was otherwise reported to be clinically stable; no follow-up data were available after this period. This case illustrates an uncommon site of aspergilloma formation and emphasizes the diagnostic value of correlating characteristic imaging findings with microbiological results in patients with advanced structural lung disease.

articles.title: Diagnostic Spectrum and Temporal Trends of Necrotic and Inflammatory Jawbone Lesions: A 22-Year Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), osteoradionecrosis (ORN), and osteomyelitis exhibit overlapping histopathological features, making clinical context essential for etiological differentiation. This study aimed to evaluate the clinicopathological characteristics and temporal distribution of four diagnostic categories of necrotic and inflammatory jawbone lesions over a 22-year period. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study reviewed 25,133 oral and maxillofacial pathology reports from 2004 to 2025. A total of 650 patients were included and categorized using clinicopathological diagnoses and available medication history. Demographic, clinical, anatomical, and temporal characteristics were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with MRONJ. Results: MRONJ was the most frequent diagnosis (51.5%), followed by osteomyelitis (39.2%), ORN (4.9%), and sclerosing osteomyelitis (4.3%). The proportion of MRONJ increased from 24.7% in 2004-2010 to 61.7% in 2018-2025, whereas osteomyelitis declined from 58.1% to 30.0% (p < 0.001). Calendar year was associated with MRONJ classification in the linear regression model (adjusted odds ratio = 1.114; 95% CI: 1.079-1.149; p < 0.001), although sensitivity analyses indicated a nonlinear temporal association. Among MRONJ patients with documented underlying disease, 37.5% had osteoporosis. The number of recorded osteoporosis-associated MRONJ cases increased from 3 in 2004-2010 to 75 in 2018-2025. Conclusions: The distribution of recorded clinicopathological diagnoses of jawbone lesions has shifted substantially, with MRONJ becoming increasingly prominent, including among patients treated for osteoporosis. These findings highlight the importance of integrating biopsy findings with clinical history and medication exposure for etiological differentiation. Changes in diagnostic recognition, terminology, referral patterns, and biopsy practices may have influenced these trends, which do not establish changes in disease incidence.

articles.title: Incremental Value of Systematic Biopsy in Patients with Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System 5 Lesions Undergoing MRI-Ultrasound Fusion Biopsy: A Single-Operator Study in a Secondary-Care Setting.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the incremental value of systematic biopsy (SB) in addition to targeted biopsy (TB) and its impact on Grade Group (GG) reclassification in patients with Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) 5 lesions. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed data from 32 patients with PI-RADS 5-only lesions who underwent magnetic resonance imaging-ultrasound fusion transrectal biopsy by a single operator. Based on the patient-level maximum GG, we evaluated the detection of any prostate cancer (GG ≥ 1), clinically significant prostate cancer (GG ≥ 2), and high-grade prostate cancer (GG ≥ 3). An exploratory subgroup analysis was performed according to prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD; <0.15 vs. ≥0.15 ng/mL/mL). Results: Any prostate cancer was detected in 24 patients (75.0%) using TB, with no incremental detection using SB (0.0%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.0-10.9). Clinically significant prostate cancer was detected in 21 patients (65.6%) using TB, with incremental detection using SB in one patient (3.1%; 95% CI, 0.1-16.2). High-grade prostate cancer was detected in 17 patients (53.1%) using TB, with incremental detection using SB in one patient (3.1%; 95% CI, 0.1-16.2). The maximum GG was higher in three patients (9.4%) when TB and SB were combined. Among the 20 patients with PSAD ≥ 0.15 ng/mL/mL, no incremental detection of clinically significant prostate cancer or high-grade prostate cancer was observed using SB (0.0%; 95% CI, 0.0-16.8). Conclusions: In this cohort of patients with PI-RADS 5 lesions, the incremental value of SB for cancer detection was limited, although the upper limit of the 95% CI for incremental detection of clinically significant prostate cancer was 16.2%. Nevertheless, SB provided additional grading information in a small number of patients. Larger studies are needed to evaluate the clinical value of selective SB omission in patients with PI-RADS 5 lesions.

articles.title: TriHG-XAI: A Human-Grounded Framework for Triangulated Explainability Evaluation in Ordinal Clock Drawing Test Quality Prediction.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning models can score the Clock Drawing Test (CDT) accurately, but their explanations are usually judged by looking at saliency maps. We asked whether complementary quantitative explainability criteria, evaluated against independent human annotations, give convergent evidence that a CDT model has learned interpretable drawing abnormalities. Methods: An image-only ResNet50 was trained to predict five-level CDT scores from the National Health and Aging Trends Study (7708 observations; participant-level split). In 200 separate, participant-unique drawings annotated for seven abnormalities, we evaluated Grad-CAM attribution alignment, matched-ink perturbation sensitivity, and linear probing of frozen representations. Sensitivity analyses covered region-of-interest definitions, data quality, and adjustment for CDT score. Results: On 1181 test observations, the quadratic weighted kappa was 0.740 and accuracy 0.678. Unadjusted analyses suggested abnormality-specific effects, including reduced hand-region attribution for missing or incorrect hands (q < 0.001) and significant perturbation sensitivity for three abnormalities. However, perturbation effects were as large in drawings without the abnormality. Within score levels, neither attribution nor perturbation sensitivity distinguished drawings with and without abnormalities. Within-score linear decodability remained for five abnormalities (AUROC 0.64-0.93), but not for uneven number spacing or same-length hands. Inter-rater agreement varied (κ 0.27-0.85). Conclusions: In this model and dataset, attribution and perturbation sensitivity mainly reflected overall drawing quality and the presence of intact hands and numerals. Abnormality-specific information was detectable only in the learned representation. Feature-level explainability evaluations should control for the prediction target, and saliency maps alone do not show that a model has learned interpretable abnormalities.

articles.title: Intestinal Behçet's Disease Presenting as Recurrent Gastrointestinal Perforation: A Diagnostic Pitfall Mimicking Crohn's Disease.
articles.abstract: A 24-year-old man underwent four emergency surgeries for gastrointestinal perforation over a six-year period. Surgical pathology repeatedly suggested transmural inflammation with fissuring ulcers, favoring Crohn's disease. However, the acute onset of each episode and the lack of typical Crohn's disease-related chronic inflammatory symptoms between episodes were incompatible with the chronic course of Crohn's disease. The histopathological finding of a tunnel-like ulcer, together with recurrent oral ulcers and acneiform folliculitis, led to a diagnosis of intestinal Behçet's disease after multidisciplinary review. This case illustrates that when pathological morphology and clinical rhythm conflict, a comprehensive evaluation integrating the clinical history, extraintestinal manifestations, and histopathological findings is essential.

articles.title: Computed Tomography-Derived Myosteatosis and Diaphragmatic Crus Morphology Are Associated with Radiologically Documented Recurrence Following Sliding Hiatal Hernia Repair: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Systemic muscle composition and local diaphragmatic crus morphology may be associated with recurrence after sliding hiatal hernia repair. This study evaluated the associations of preoperative CT-derived muscle measurements with radiologically documented recurrence after primary type I sliding hiatal hernia repair. Methods: This retrospective single-center study identified 132 patients who underwent repair between January 2015 and July 2024. The primary recurrence analysis was restricted to 48 patients with postoperative CT. Preoperative measurements included L3 skeletal muscle attenuation and diaphragmatic crus thickness and attenuation. Associations were evaluated using between-group comparisons and separate univariable Firth penalized logistic regression models. Multivariable models and analyses involving the overall cohort were retained as exploratory supplementary analyses. Results: Among the 48 CT-imaged patients, 15 had radiologically documented recurrence and 33 had no recurrence detected on available CT. Myosteatosis was more frequent in patients with recurrence (80.0% versus 18.2%; p < 0.001). Mean crus attenuation (31.53 ± 4.69 versus 37.21 ± 3.61 HU) and thickness (5.51 ± 0.61 versus 6.39 ± 0.71 mm) were lower in patients with recurrence (both p < 0.001). In separate univariable models, myosteatosis (OR, 15.11; 95% CI, 3.84-75.00), lower crus attenuation (OR per 1-HU decrease, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.15-1.72), and reduced crus thickness (OR per 1-mm decrease, 8.02; 95% CI, 2.42-44.33) were associated with documented recurrence. These estimates were unadjusted and imprecise. Conclusions: Among selectively CT-imaged patients, myosteatosis and adverse crural muscle measurements were associated with documented recurrence. Limited events, nonstandardized imaging, and uncontrolled confounding preclude definitive prognostic conclusions. Larger studies with standardized postoperative imaging are required.

articles.title: Multi-Parametric Spectral Detector CT for the Assessment of Focal Liver Lesions: Evaluation of Readers' Diagnostic Confidence and Economic Effects.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Characterization of small liver lesions on computed tomography (CT) remains challenging. This study evaluated whether spectral detector CT (SDCT) improves subjective diagnostic confidence in the characterization of focal hypoperfused liver lesions using additional spectral information and assessed its potential economic impact. Methods: In this IRB-approved retrospective study, 100 patients with 229 focal hypoperfused liver lesions who underwent SDCT were included. Images were evaluated in three consecutive reading sessions using (1) conventional polychromatic images (conv), (2) conventional plus monoenergetic images at 40, 50, and 60 keV (monoE), and (3) a multiparametric SDCT approach (mSDCT) combining conventional and spectral reconstructions, including iodine density (ID) and effective atomic number (Zeff) images. Lesions were characterized, and subjective diagnostic confidence was rated on a 5-point scale. Diagnostic performance was compared, and potential economic savings were estimated. Results: mSDCT yielded the highest diagnostic confidence in 130 lesions, compared with 36 lesions for conventional CT. Diagnostic confidence increased significantly from conventional CT through monoE to mSDCT (median scores: 3, 4, 4, 4, and 5 for conventional CT, 40-, 50-, and 60-keV monoE, and mSDCT, respectively; all p < 0.001). For lesions ≤ 10 mm, sensitivity was comparable between conventional CT and mSDCT, whereas mSDCT significantly improved specificity (85.0% vs. 97.9%) and diagnostic accuracy (86.4% vs. 96.7%; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Multiparametric SDCT significantly improves radiologists' diagnostic confidence in characterizing focal hypoperfused liver lesions, particularly lesions ≤ 10 mm in oncologic patients. Increased diagnostic confidence may reduce the need for additional imaging or biopsy, potentially enabling faster and less costly diagnostic workups.

articles.title: Exploratory Evaluation of TBR Thresholds for Arterial [18F]F-FAPI-74 PET/CT.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI)-directed PET/CT has emerged as a promising approach for non-invasive assessment of arterial wall pathology. While a target-to-background ratio (TBR) threshold of 1.6 has previously been applied for vascular [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 imaging, no established threshold exists for [18F]F-FAPI-74. Given differences in physical imaging characteristics and tracer kinetics, this study systematically evaluated candidate TBR thresholds for arterial [18F]F-FAPI-74 uptake, using CT-derived calcification as a morphological comparator. Methods: Seventy-two oncological patients undergoing [18F]F-FAPI-74 PET/CT were retrospectively analyzed. Six vascular territories were assessed for focal vessel wall-associated tracer uptake and CT-derived calcification. Three primary candidate TBR thresholds (1.2, 1.4, and 1.6) were selected for focused comparison, while complementary thresholds from 1.0 to 2.0 in increments of 0.1 were assessed descriptively. For each threshold, the number of FAPI-positive sites, proportion of FAPI-positive sites with concomitant calcification, and proportion of calcification-positive sites with concomitant FAPI uptake were determined. All co-localization measures were interpreted as descriptive morphological comparisons and not as measures of biological FAP expression, diagnostic sensitivity, or diagnostic accuracy. Results: Focal arterial uptake was detected in 69/72 patients (95.8%) at a TBR threshold of 1.2, 61/72 (84.7%) at 1.4 and 38/72 (52.8%) at 1.6. The corresponding numbers of FAPI-positive sites were 896, 452 and 220. Among the three primary candidate thresholds, the proportion of FAPI-positive sites with concomitant calcification remained broadly comparable (66.7%, 60.2%, and 68.2%, respectively), whereas the proportion of calcification-positive sites with concomitant FAPI uptake decreased from 23.4% at a TBR threshold of 1.2 to 10.7% at 1.4 and 5.9% at 1.6. Across the broader TBR range, lower thresholds, including 1.0 and 1.1, yielded greater site detection and numerically higher calcification co-localization than the TBR threshold of 1.2, and no unique empirical optimum was identified. Conclusions: A TBR threshold of 1.2 represents a pragmatic candidate threshold within the predefined primary range rather than an empirically optimized cut-off. Prospective validation in dedicated cardiovascular cohorts using standardized imaging protocols and biological reference standards is required before a generally applicable threshold for arterial [18F]F-FAPI-74 imaging can be established.

articles.title: Lifestyle and Clinical Correlates of Myosteatosis Among African Caribbean Men and Women.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Myosteatosis, i.e., adiposity in and around skeletal muscle, is a hallmark of adverse muscle aging, more common among women than men, and associated with several major health outcomes, including cardiometabolic diseases and functional decline. We investigated lifestyle and clinical correlates of skeletal muscle adiposity among an understudied cohort of Afro-Caribbean men and women. Methods: Among 213 men and 530 women aged 50-80 from the Tobago Health Study, several lifestyle and clinical factors were assessed, including accelerometry-derived physical activity and sleep duration, diet, and medications. Lifestyle risk scores were based on smoking, alcohol, physical activity, and body mass index. Calf muscle density was measured using peripheral quantitative computed tomography, with lower values suggesting more muscle adiposity. Results: Women were more likely to abstain from cigarettes and alcohol, but less physically active, with more sugar intake and lower muscle density than men. Using Isotemporal Substitution, cross-sectionally replacing sedentary time with sleep or light-intensity physical activity was significantly associated with higher muscle density. In multivariable models, older age, larger waist circumference, and taking diabetes medications were cross-sectionally associated with lower muscle density, as well as shorter sleep among men and taking anti-hypertensive medications among women. Conclusions: Older Afro-Caribbean women vs. men had healthier substance habits, but lower activity and muscle density, suggesting more muscle adiposity. Modifiable behaviors, particularly sedentary time, sleep duration, and light-intensity physical activity were strongly associated with muscle density. Interventions that replace sedentary time with light-intensity physical activity and sleep may be feasible and sustainable approaches to reduce myosteatosis.

articles.title: Comparison of Cone-Beam CT, Photon-Counting Detector CT and Micro-CT for Imaging Bone Graft Biomaterials and Three-Dimensional Printed Calcium Phosphate Scaffolds: An Ex Vivo Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used in dentomaxillofacial imaging for evaluating bone grafts and implant-related procedures; however, image quality is often compromised by metal-induced artefacts. This study compared CBCT, photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT), and micro-computed tomography (µCT) for imaging clinically relevant bone graft materials and three-dimensional printed calcium phosphate scaffolds, focusing on biomaterial visualisation and titanium artefact reduction. Methods: Four bovine mandibles were prepared with standardized cylindrical defects containing eight bone substitute materials and 3D-printed calcium phosphate scaffolds, with or without surrounding titanium cages. Specimens were imaged using CBCT and PCD-CT with low-dose and maximum-dose ultra-high-resolution acquisition protocols, and µCT. Two readers independently assessed image interpretability, biomaterial visualisation, and metal artefact severity using a five-point scoring system. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated using weighted Cohen's kappa. Results: µCT provided the highest spatial resolution and served as the ex vivo reference standard. Under the acquisition and reconstruction protocols evaluated, PCD-CT provided favorable visualization of scaffold architecture and reduced the visual impact of titanium-induced artefacts compared with CBCT. High-energy virtual monoenergetic reconstructions (≥130 keV) further reduced beam-hardening and streak artefacts, although the optimal reconstruction energy may depend on the biomaterial and diagnostic task. Without titanium cages, PCD-CT and µCT achieved higher image interpretability scores than CBCT. With titanium cages, CBCT frequently became non-diagnostic, whereas PCD-CT maintained good visualisation of most biomaterials. Inter-reader agreement ranged from substantial to almost perfect. Conclusions: In this exploratory ex vivo study, the evaluated PCD-CT protocols provided favorable qualitative visualization of several bone graft materials and three-dimensional printed calcium phosphate scaffolds compared with the evaluated CBCT protocol, particularly in the presence of titanium cages. However, the protocols were not dose-matched, and differences in acquisition and reconstruction parameters prevent attributing the observed findings exclusively to detector technology. The study does not establish PCD-CT superiority at equivalent radiation doses or demonstrate clinical performance in longitudinal bone-regeneration monitoring. Further dose-matched studies incorporating objective image-quality measurements and clinical validation are required.

articles.title: Unprotected TAVI with Critically Low LMCA Height: The Importance of Individualized Anatomical Assessment.
articles.abstract: A 66-year-old woman with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis (STS-PROM 5.15%; EuroSCORE II 3.66%), right carotid occlusion, 50% left carotid stenosis, and a preference for TAVI underwent multidisciplinary assessment. Computed tomography demonstrated a 6 mm left main coronary artery (LMCA) ostial height, hypoplastic right coronary artery, 31 mm left coronary sinus, and no bulky calcification facing the LMCA. Following Heart Team assessment of obstruction risk and the potential complications of prophylactic stenting, transfemoral TAVI was performed without coronary protection using a 29 mm recapturable self-expanding valve, with emergency revascularization, hemodynamic support, and surgical backup available. Preserved left coronary perfusion after 18 mm balloon predilatation provided reassurance but could not exclude obstruction during valve deployment. Recovery was uneventful, with no reported adverse cardiovascular events during approximately 18 months of follow-up. Favorable sinus anatomy may inform procedural planning but cannot independently establish protection against coronary obstruction. This single case illustrates individualized anatomical assessment and Heart Team decision-making, not the general safety of omitting coronary protection in similarly high-risk patients.

articles.title: Longitudinal SPECT Assessment of Regional Cerebral Perfusion Associated with Nicergoline Use in Parkinson's Disease Without Dementia: An Exploratory Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cerebral hypoperfusion has been reported in Parkinson's disease (PD), including in patients without dementia. We explored whether long-term nicergoline use was associated with longitudinal changes in relative regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and clinical outcomes in non-demented PD. Methods: Thirty patients with idiopathic PD without dementia underwent Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) assessment and 99mTc-ethyl cysteinate dimer brain perfusion SPECT at baseline and again after 2-4 years. Eighteen patients received nicergoline (30 mg twice daily) with standard dopaminergic treatment, whereas 12 received dopaminergic treatment without nicergoline. Treatment allocation was non-randomized. Longitudinal SPECT change images were analyzed in SPM12. The voxel-wise group comparison used p < 0.001 uncorrected with a cluster extent threshold of ≥50 voxels and was considered exploratory because no correction for multiple comparisons was applied. Results: Baseline clinical characteristics did not differ significantly between groups, although age was numerically higher in the nicergoline group (72.4 ± 6.44 vs. 66.8 ± 9.14 years; p = 0.057). Changes in UPDRS scores, Hoehn and Yahr stage, and levodopa equivalent daily dose did not differ significantly between groups. A single 76-voxel cluster showed a greater relative perfusion increase in the right temporal fusiform cortex (Brodmann area 37; peak MNI coordinate 34, -40, -22; t = 4.07; uncorrected p < 0.001) in the nicergoline group. Conclusions: Long-term nicergoline exposure was associated with an uncorrected group-level difference in right fusiform relative perfusion without corresponding clinical improvement. Because the finding was based on a small, non-randomized cohort and an uncorrected voxel-wise threshold, it should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic efficacy or a cholinergic/cognitive benefit. Larger randomized studies with multiplicity control and clinically relevant cognitive outcomes are required.

articles.title: A Source-Traced PET/CT Scanner Performance Database (2004-2024): The Sphere-Size Dependence of Time-of-Flight Contrast Recovery.
articles.abstract: Background: Small-lesion quantification is a key task in diagnostic PET/CT. However, published performance data span two decades and multiple NEMA NU 2 revisions, complicating comparisons. We developed a source-traced database to examine how reconstruction-associated improvements in hot-sphere contrast recovery vary with sphere diameter, providing reference data for phantom-based protocol optimisation. Methods: Published NEMA and phantom measurements were source-verified, linked to scanner geometry, and annotated with acquisition and reconstruction conditions. Contrast recovery at a 4:1 sphere-to-background activity ratio (151 measurements; 13 scanners) was analysed using mixed-effects meta-regression with a scanner random intercept. Results: The database included 28 scanner models (2004-2024), 610 measurements and 43 publications. Descriptively, sensitivity was 3.8-10.9 cps/kBq for lutetium-based analogue scanners, 12.1-47.6 for conventional-geometry digital scanners and 176-192 for total-body scanners. Time of flight (TOF) was associated with a 7.9-percentage-point-higher contrast recovery (95% CI 4.8 to 11.1), but the association varied with sphere diameter (p < 0.001) and was significant only at 10-17 mm (11.4, 9.9 and 7.0 points); estimates at 28 and 37 mm rested on four to five scanners and were imprecise. The median between-laboratory difference under matched conditions was 5.7 points. Point-spread-function and regularised-reconstruction effects were not robust. Conclusions: In phantom measurements, TOF-associated gains were concentrated at 10-17 mm. These data provide reference values for phantom-based protocol optimisation, harmonisation and acceptance testing; they do not measure lesion detectability or diagnostic accuracy, which require patient-based validation.

articles.title: Body Size, Radiation Dose and Exposure Index in Conventional Radiography: A Multicentre Prospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Exposure index (EI) reflects detector exposure rather than patient dose, but its behaviour as patient size increases remains incompletely characterised across radiographic examinations. We evaluated continuous associations of body mass index (BMI) and regional body thickness proxy with dose-area product (DAP), entrance surface dose (ESD), and EI, and tested whether associations differed by examination and institution. Methods: This prospective multicentre observational study included 572 exposures from 331 adults undergoing nine projections at three institutions. Generalised estimating equations with a Gamma distribution and log link accounted for repeated exposures. Total-association models adjusted for examination, institution, age, and sex; technical-adjusted models additionally included log mAs and kVp, with SSD included only in BMI-based models. Results: In total-association models adjusted for examination, institution, age, and sex, each 1 kg/m2 increase in BMI was associated with 4.31% higher DAP, 3.25% higher estimated ESD, and 3.45% lower EI (all p < 0.001). Each 1 cm increase in geometrically derived regional-thickness proxy was associated with 3.03% higher DAP, 2.97% higher estimated ESD, and 2.51% lower EI (all p < 0.001). Technical adjustment substantially attenuated the associations with DAP, whereas inverse associations with EI persisted. Conclusions: Body-size associations were outcome- and examination-specific. Direct EI-dose associations were generally positive but substantially attenuated after accounting for exposure technique and regional thickness, indicating that their relationship is strongly influenced by patient attenuation and technical exposure factors. These findings support further examination- and system-specific evaluation of EI behaviour alongside body size, technical factors, and patient-dose indicators.

articles.title: Unexpected Immune Biomarker Separation by Recorded Long COVID Status in an Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Long COVID is clinically and immunologically heterogeneous. We describe unexpected biomarker separation between recorded groups and limitations that prevent a disease-specific interpretation. Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional secondary analysis included 191 post-COVID records: 158 labeled long COVID and 33 originally designated "No adverse events." The comparator designation did not establish a clinically verified absence of post-COVID sequelae. Eight biomarkers were evaluated after correction of confirmed reporting errors at common assay lower limits. Analyses included rank-based comparisons, Firth penalized logistic regression, internal resampling, censoring sensitivity analyses and exploratory clustering. Results: Seven biomarkers were higher in the recorded long COVID group (all false-discovery-rate q < 0.001). Apparent areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.9942 for CXCL9 and 0.9914 for IL-6. The seven-marker model had an apparent AUC of 1.0000 and a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.9989. CXCL9 was at or below the reporting limit in 30/33 comparator records versus 1/158 long COVID records. All individual coefficients in the full model had 95% profile intervals including the null. Clustering did not establish distinct biological subtypes. Conclusions: The unexpectedly strong separation is a hypothesis-generating observation requiring independent investigation. Incomplete verification of group definitions and sampling times limits disease-specific interpretation. These findings do not establish a long COVID-specific immune signature or a clinically applicable diagnostic test.

articles.title: Not All That Hurts Is Fibromyalgia: The Challenges of Differential Diagnosis of Patients Referred to a Tertiary Care Center.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a complex and disabling condition characterized by chronic widespread pain, fatigue and multiple somatic symptoms, often overlapping with rheumatic (RMD) and non-rheumatic diseases. Since objective biomarkers are lacking, diagnosis relies on validated criteria and careful clinical assessment. This study aimed to describe a referral cohort including patients with either a previous diagnosis or suspicion of FM and to identify the proportion of patients fulfilling FM criteria, the severity of their FM, and to identify alternative or associated conditions. Methods: A prospective cohort of consecutive patients referred to our Center between June 2023 and October 2025 was assessed according to the 2016 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) diagnostic criteria for FM. Demographic data, medical history, and clinical findings were collected. Additional laboratory or imaging investigations were performed when clinically indicated. FM severity was evaluated using validated tools included in the 2016 ACR diagnostic criteria. Results: Overall, 247 patients were enrolled: 44 with a certified previous FM diagnosis, 145 referred by physicians for suspected FM and 58 self-referred. Among patients without a previous certified diagnosis, FM was newly diagnosed in 75% of physician-referred and 77% of self-referred patients. A substantial proportion was also diagnosed with an RMD. Longer symptom duration, higher fatigue and worse global health were associated with FM. Conclusions: Among patients who reached our referral center because of suspected FM, a high proportion fulfilled the 2016 ACR criteria. Careful application of FM criteria and evaluation of coexisting conditions may improve timely diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Detection of Residual or Recurrent Filling in Endovascularly Treated Intracranial Aneurysms on TOF-MRA: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Background and Purpose: Surveillance TOF-MRA is a non-invasive alternative to digital subtraction angiography (DSA) for detecting aneurysm residual/recurrence after endovascular embolization but is limited by coil/WEB device-related susceptibility artifact and inter-reader variability. We evaluated a supervised machine-learning classifier for detecting residuals and/or recurrence on surveillance TOF-MRA obtained 3-6 months after endovascular embolization, referenced against the Raymond-Roy Occlusion Classification (RROC) class assigned on the surveillance TOF-MRA itself by a single, non-blinded neuroradiologist who had access to the completion DSA and 24-48 h post-procedural MRA. Materials and Methods: In this single-center retrospective pilot study, 53 of 55 eligible adults with intrasaccular endovascular embolization (coiling or WEB device, 2020-2024) were analyzed after excluding 2 for suboptimal MRA quality (RROC I: n = 13, II: n = 18, III: n = 27); the final analytical cohort comprised 58 aneurysms from 53 unique patients. Radiomic features from a class-agnostic 3 mm peri-device region were extracted with PyRadiomics and evaluated using L1-regularized logistic regression, calibrated linear SVM, and random forest. Model evaluation used 100 repetitions of 5-fold patient-grouped nested cross-validation, with all aneurysms from the same patient kept within the same fold and preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model fitting confined to training data. A post hoc exploratory subgroup analysis excluded the morphologically intermediate Class II cases. Results: In the primary analysis of 58 aneurysms from 53 patients, L1-regularized logistic regression yielded an aggregated repeated out-of-fold AUC of 0.716 (95% patient-cluster bootstrap CI 0.566-0.856), sensitivity 0.800, specificity 0.462, negative predictive value 0.400, and balanced accuracy 0.631 at a 0.50 threshold. The mean AUC across the 100 individual cross-validation repetitions, which is a different estimate, was 0.601 (SD 0.088) for logistic regression, 0.631 (SD 0.056) for random forest and 0.555 (SD 0.097) for the calibrated linear SVM. In the post hoc exploratory Class I versus III analysis (40 aneurysms from 38 patients), L1 logistic regression yielded AUC 0.832 (95% CI 0.704-0.946), sensitivity 0.852, specificity 0.692, and balanced accuracy 0.772. The subgroup represents a different, more separated classification task and is not directly comparable with the full cohort. Of 45 outcome-positive aneurysms, 42% were persistent residual filling and 58% interval recurrence. Conclusions: This pilot analysis demonstrates the technical feasibility of the patient-grouped radiomics-based classification of post-treatment surveillance TOF-MRA. The performance estimates remain preliminary because of the small single-center cohort, limited number of negative cases, scanner/device heterogeneity, and absence of external validation. The exploratory Class I versus III results should not be interpreted as evidence of improved clinical performance and warrant external multicenter validation. The specificity and negative predictive value were low, the incremental value of radiomics beyond simpler device- or morphology-based approaches has not been established, and the model is not ready for clinical use.

articles.title: Maternal Cardiovascular Phenotyping in Fetal Growth Restriction: Integrating Hemodynamics, Echocardiography, Circulating Biomarkers and Fetoplacental Doppler Assessment.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with maternal cardiovascular maladaptation, but its relationship with cardiac function, biomarkers and fetoplacental dysfunction remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize the maternal cardiovascular phenotype associated with FGR and its variation according to onset. Methods: This prospective study included 140 singleton pregnancies: 59 with FGR (10 early-onset; 49 late-onset) and 81 controls. Assessments included maternal hemodynamics, echocardiography, circulating biomarkers, fetoplacental Doppler indices and neonatal outcomes. Analyses comprised group comparisons, multivariable regression, correlations and exploratory biomarker ROC analyses. Results: After adjustment for gestational age at the corresponding assessment, maternal age, body mass index, preeclampsia and chronic hypertension, FGR was associated with lower cardiac output (-1.84 L/min; 95% CI, -2.13 to -1.55), higher systemic vascular resistance (+530 dyn·s·cm-5; 95% CI, 429-632) and altered relaxation indices. NT-proBNP and GDF-15 concentrations were 191% (95% CI, 141-250%) and 125% (95% CI, 92-164%) higher, respectively. Early-onset FGR showed greater abnormalities in selected hemodynamic and relaxation parameters and higher GDF-15 than late-onset FGR; e', E/e', and NT-proBNP did not differ significantly. Apparent within-cohort AUCs for FGR discrimination were 0.991 for NT-proBNP and 0.961 for GDF-15. Selected cardiovascular parameters correlated with fetoplacental Doppler indices and perinatal outcomes. Early-onset FGR had the highest NICU admission rate and longest neonatal hospitalization among survivors, alongside substantially earlier delivery. Conclusions: FGR was associated with a low-output, high-resistance maternal cardiovascular phenotype and elevated biomarkers. Onset-related comparisons remain exploratory and were not validated by the gestational-age-restricted sensitivity analysis, which included only late-onset FGR. Incremental predictive value beyond fetal biometry and Doppler assessment and benefits for clinical management remain to be established.

articles.title: Fetal Ventriculomegaly Across the Severity Spectrum: Prenatal Ultrasound Features, Longitudinal Evolution, and Additional Fetal MRI Findings.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fetal ventriculomegaly is a heterogeneous prenatal finding with variable severity, evolution, and risk of associated cerebral abnormalities. Prenatal ultrasound is the primary diagnostic and follow-up modality, while fetal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may provide additional anatomical information. This study evaluated ultrasound features and longitudinal evolution across the ventriculomegaly severity spectrum and investigated prenatal features associated with additional MRI abnormalities. Methods: This single-center observational cohort included 62 fetuses who underwent detailed prenatal ultrasound, fetal MRI, and serial ultrasound follow-up. Ventriculomegaly was classified as mild (10-12 mm), moderate (>12-15 mm), or severe (>15 mm). Multivariable logistic regression assessed prenatal features associated with additional MRI abnormalities, and receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated its discriminatory performance. Results: Mild, moderate, and severe ventriculomegaly were present in 12 (19.4%), 22 (35.5%), and 28 (45.2%) fetuses. Additional MRI abnormalities increased with severity (16.7%, 40.9%, and 71.4%; p = 0.004). Longitudinal evolution differed across severity groups (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.013), with progression observed in 25.0%, 45.5%, and 71.4% of mild, moderate, and severe cases, respectively. Greater ultrasound ventricular diameter (OR 1.19 per 1 mm increase, 95% CI 1.03-1.37; p = 0.021) and bilateral asymmetric ventriculomegaly (OR 3.82, 95% CI 1.04-13.96; p = 0.043) were independently associated with additional MRI abnormalities. Ventricular diameter showed moderate discriminatory performance (AUC 0.768, 95% CI 0.651-0.886); an exploratory, data-derived 13.5 mm threshold yielded 83.9% sensitivity and 54.8% specificity. Conclusions: Increasing ventricular severity was associated with more frequent progression and additional MRI abnormalities. The associations of ventricular diameter and bilateral asymmetric ventriculomegaly with additional MRI abnormalities should be considered exploratory and require further validation. The identification of additional abnormalities even in mild cases supports the complementary role of fetal MRI alongside longitudinal ultrasound assessment.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Nurse-Led Sepsis Risk Score Using AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Data in Adult Febrile Neutropenia: A Nested Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Febrile neutropenia (FN) in hematologic malignancies carries a high risk of sepsis. We developed a regression model and a simplified nurse-led sepsis risk score using artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled remote patient monitoring (RPM) measurements and routine clinical and laboratory variables. Methods: A nested case-control study included 120 adult FN episodes (40 Sepsis-3-defined cases within 14 days of FN onset; 80 matched controls) in a hematology/bone marrow transplantation unit (BMT) in India (December 2021-December 2024). Heart rate and respiratory rate were obtained by ballistocardiography; blood pressure (BP), peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), and temperature were obtained using connected probes. Only a single set of FN-onset measurements was analyzed; longitudinal RPM trends and platform-generated alerts were excluded. Conditional logistic regression identified independent predictors and supplied coefficients for an integer-weighted score. Regression-model validation used two 1000-resample bootstrap analyses: one holding cut-offs and predictors fixed, the other repeating cut-off determination and backward selection. Integer-score discrimination was assessed separately. Results: Six predictors-tachycardia, hypotension, ≥2 comorbidities, absolute neutrophil count <99.5 cells/μL, chills, and elevated procalcitonin-formed an 8-point score. The regression model area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.847, with fixed-specification optimism of 0.028 and a corrected AUC of 0.819. Repeating cut-off determination and predictor selection yielded an apparent AUC of 0.855, optimism of 0.036, and corrected AUC of 0.819. The integer-score apparent AUC was 0.654 (95% CI 0.567-0.740), without optimism correction. Conclusions: Regression-model discrimination remained similar after accounting for cut-off determination and predictor selection. Integer-score performance remains uncorrected for optimism and requires independent temporal validation before clinical use. RPM's AI functions and continuous-monitoring benefits were not evaluated. Temporal validation is planned in Phase II. Trial registration: Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2025/06/088290).

articles.title: Lightweight Calibration-Based Blood Pressure Tracking from Photoplethysmography Features for Smart Devices: Accuracy, Model Size and Recalibration Interval.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Smart devices estimate blood pressure (BP) from photoplethysmography (PPG), but models trained on other people generalize poorly, and device constraints limit model size. This study compared calibration strategies and model sizes for PPG-based BP estimation. Methods: We used 65 hand-crafted PPG features with MIMIC-BP (1295 training and 229 subject-disjoint test subjects, ten repeats) and 17 external VitalDB surgical cases. We compared calibration-free regressors, calibration with one to five cuffs, recalibration policies and calibration models of decreasing size. Results: Without calibration, six regressors reached a systolic BP (SBP) mean absolute error (MAE) of 13.0-13.3 mmHg on unseen subjects, close to a constant predictor (14.2 mmHg). A delta model that predicts the change from the cuff reading reduced the SBP MAE to 11.8 mmHg with one cuff and 10.8 mmHg with five, but followed only 30-50% of large changes. With five calibration readings, the model achieved a pooled area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94 for new-onset SBP ≥160 mmHg on MIMIC-BP, but sensitivity was zero at an estimated-SBP threshold of 160 mmHg. Accuracy was governed by the recalibration interval: recalibration nominally every 15 min gave 10.3 mmHg on VitalDB, and event-triggered cuffs were not better than periodic ones. A 47 KB tree model lost 0.2 mmHg against a 1.5 MB reference. Conclusions: For these data, calibration was required, the recalibration interval mattered more than model complexity, and a compact tree model was sufficient; on-device use requires further validation. Accuracy remained poor at blood-pressure extremes, and external validation in only 17 VitalDB cases remains preliminary.

articles.title: First-Line CDK4/6 Inhibitor Outcomes in HER2-Low Versus HER2-Zero Hormone-Receptor-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Single-Centre Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: A CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy is the standard first-line treatment for hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. Post hoc analyses of randomised trials have raised the possibility that HER2-low status influences CDK4/6 inhibitor benefit, whereas real-world data are limited. We compared outcomes between patients with HER2-low and HER2-zero disease treated with first-line CDK4/6-inhibitor-based therapy in a real-world cohort. Methods: In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, we identified 137 patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer who received first-line ribociclib or palbociclib plus endocrine therapy between January 2017 and December 2024. HER2-zero was defined as an immunohistochemistry (IHC) score of 0 and HER2-low as IHC 1+ or 2+ without gene amplification. Objective response, progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and neutropenia were compared; Cox models were adjusted for recognised prognostic factors. Results: Of 137 patients, 98 (71.5%) had HER2-zero and 39 (28.5%) HER2-low disease; median follow-up was 29.5 months. Objective response rates were 63.9% versus 56.4% (p = 0.44). Median PFS was 31.4 versus 28.5 months (63 events in 134 evaluable patients; log-rank p = 0.70), and median OS was 69.7 months versus not reached (34 deaths in 127 evaluable patients; p = 0.95). Adjusted hazard ratios for HER2-low versus HER2-zero were 1.01 (95% CI 0.57-1.80) for PFS and 1.04 (95% CI 0.49-2.19) for OS. Any-grade and grade ≥3 neutropenia and dose reductions did not differ. Results were consistent across IHC categories (0, 1+, 2+) and in propensity-score-weighted and misclassification bias analyses, all with wide confidence intervals. Conclusions: In this single-centre real-world cohort, response, survival and tolerability of first-line CDK4/6-inhibitor-based therapy did not differ significantly between HER2-low and HER2-zero disease. However, with only 39 HER2-low patients the study was underpowered: it had 80% power to detect only a PFS hazard ratio of approximately 2.2, so clinically relevant differences cannot be excluded. Because all patients received a CDK4/6 inhibitor, these prognostic data cannot show whether HER2-low status modifies the CDK4/6 inhibitor benefit. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies.

articles.title: Early Metabolic and Microstructural Responses of the Rat Hippocampus to BED-Matched Single-Fraction and Fractionated Whole-Brain Irradiation: A Multimodal MRI Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The biologically effective dose (BED), based on the linear-quadratic model, is widely used to equate different irradiation schedules. However, whether BED equivalence holds for early brain responses is unclear. We compared single-fraction and fractionated whole-brain irradiation (WBI) under BED-matched conditions in a rat model, using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and histology to characterize early hippocampal responses. METHODS: We randomly assigned 27 male Wistar rats to three groups: Sham, WBI-Single (15 Gy × 1), and WBI-Fraction (6.2 Gy × 5), the latter designed to achieve a comparable BED (α/β = 2 Gy). Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), glutamate chemical exchange saturation transfer (Glu-CEST), and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) of the hippocampus were performed pre-irradiation and at 1 and 2 wk post-irradiation on a 7-T scanner. Hematoxylin-eosin staining, Luxol Fast Blue staining, and immunohistochemistry (glial fibrillary acidic protein, ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1) were evaluated. Longitudinal MRI data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction across imaging endpoints. RESULTS: Among the MRI endpoints, only myo-inositol exhibited a significant group-by-time interaction after FDR correction (p = 0.0026, q = 0.0342). At 1 wk, myo-inositol was higher in the WBI-Fraction group than in the Sham group (Tukey-adjusted p = 0.0217). At 2 weeks, glutamine was lower in the WBI-Single group than in the Sham group in an exploratory post hoc comparison (Tukey-adjusted p = 0.0382). For DTI, radial diffusivity was higher in the WBI-Single group than in the Sham and WBI-Fraction groups at 1 wk (Tukey-adjusted p = 0.0460 and 0.0110, respectively), although no significant group-by-time interactions were observed for DTI metrics. Glu-CEST showed no significant group differences or group-by-time interaction. CONCLUSIONS: Under irradiation conditions designed to achieve comparable BED, early hippocampal MRI revealed a significant group-dependent temporal pattern in myo-inositol and exploratory differences in diffusion metrics. These findings suggest that multimodal MRI may provide complementary information on early hippocampal responses to WBI, although distinct biological effects of the two irradiation schedules remain to be established.

articles.title: Assessment of the Association Between Tooth Loss Patterns and CBCT-Derived Gray Values of the Mandibular Condyle: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between tooth loss and mandibular condylar cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-derived gray values according to different patterns of edentulism. Methods: This retrospective study was conducted using the CBCT archive of the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology, Faculty of Dentistry, Harran University. All CBCT examinations were obtained using a single CBCT scanner and a standardized acquisition protocol. Demographic variables such as age and gender, along with edentulism status based on the Kennedy classification, were recorded to assess their relationship with mandibular condylar CBCT-derived gray values. The collected data were statistically analyzed using the independent t-test, Pearson's chi-square test, one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons, paired samples t-test, and multivariable linear regression analysis. Results: A total of 371 CBCT scans (144 males and 227 females) were included. The mean age was 41.67 years for females and 41.87 years for males. The mean CBCT-derived gray values of the right and left mandibular condyles were lower in males (right: 577.08 ± 161.18; left: 353.89 ± 181.41) compared to females (right: 702.02 ± 137.59; left: 460.47 ± 163.65) (p < 0.001 for both sides). In a secondary analysis, the mean CBCT-derived gray value of the right condyle (653.53 ± 159.13) was higher than that of the left condyle (419.10 ± 178.27) (unadjusted p < 0.001). A nominal overall association between maxillary dentition status and right condylar CBCT-derived gray values was observed after adjustment for age, sex, and mandibular dentition status (p = 0.024). However, this association was not corrected for multiple testing across study outcomes and should therefore be interpreted as exploratory. No significant overall adjusted associations were observed for mandibular dentition status or for left condylar gray values. Conclusions: Descriptively lower CBCT-derived gray values were observed in completely edentulous individuals; however, these differences were not statistically confirmed and were not consistent across all dentition classifications. These findings should also be interpreted cautiously, as CBCT-derived gray values are scanner- and protocol-dependent and do not represent absolute Hounsfield units or direct measurements of bone mineral density. Further longitudinal and calibrated imaging studies are needed to clarify the relationship between tooth loss and mandibular condylar bone changes.

articles.title: Patterns of Computed Tomography Use, Diagnostic Yield and Radiation Dose in Pediatric Trauma Patients: A Single-Center Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Computed tomography (CT) is central to pediatric trauma imaging but involves radiation exposure. This study evaluated CT use patterns, diagnostic yield, and radiation dose relative to diagnostic reference levels (DRLs). Methods: This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included patients younger than 18 years who underwent CT for blunt trauma in 2025. Findings were classified as major pathology positive or negative. CTDIvol and DLP were retrieved from the picture archiving and communication system, and institutional medians were compared with registry-based and European DRLs. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized estimating equations were used. Results: Among 1686 patients (66.3% male; median age, 9.92 years; 2209 examinations), major pathology was detected in 9.0% of patients (152/1686) and 7.2% of examinations (160/2209). No major pathology was found on single-region spine CT. Yield was lowest at 1-<5 years (1.9%) and highest at 15-<18 years (16.2%); older age and multiple CT examinations were independently associated with major pathology. Median cumulative DLP per patient was 583.0 mGy·cm. Institutional median DLP exceeded phantom-matched registry DRLs in 5 of 22 adequately sampled region-age groups, mainly abdominal CT at ≥10 years; head CT medians exceeded the DRL only in infants. Combined chest-abdomen CT, mostly referenced to the 16 cm phantom, was excluded. Conclusions: Low diagnostic yield in several regions and doses above reference levels in selected regions identify areas for optimizing pediatric trauma CT. Whether decision rules, selective imaging, and protocol optimization can reduce exposure without compromising diagnostic safety should be assessed prospectively.

articles.title: Evaluation of a Deep Learning Reconstruction Technique for Accelerated Brain MRI Scans.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone of diagnostic imaging, providing exceptional soft tissue contrast and enabling detailed characterization of neurological, vascular, and musculoskeletal diseases. Despite its clinical utility, prolonged acquisition times remain a primary limitation of MRI. Extended scan durations increase patient discomfort, particularly in vulnerable populations, which elevate the risk of motion artifacts that can degrade image quality and necessitate repeat imaging. Recent advances in machine learning, especially deep learning (DL), promise to ameliorate these limitations by enabling high-quality MRI reconstruction from heavily undersampled data, increasing throughput capacity and improving healthcare delivery efficiency. This work describes an FDA-cleared DL algorithm known as DeepFoqus-Accelerate for the reconstruction of deliberately under-sampled magnetic resonance imaging data. METHODS: Fully sampled k-space from 408 brain MRI volumes (108 from 18 healthy volunteers and 300 from the public fastMRI dataset) was retrospectively undersampled. A detailed comparison of reconstructed images using DeepFoqus-Accelerate with corresponding fully sampled clinical images is presented using expert evaluation of overall image quality and quantitative similarity metrics. The only conventional comparator included in the study was GE's parallel imaging reconstruction (ARC) at matched retrospective undersampling; comparisons with compressed sensing and vendor-specific deep-learning reconstruction methods were outside the study design. RESULTS: This algorithm can allow for a four-fold reduction in brain imaging times relative to a fully sampled acquisition while preserving image quality. No reader rated any reconstruction below the acceptability threshold, and DeepFoqus-Accelerate exceeded ARC on all metrics at 4×. CONCLUSIONS: The findings characterize image quality and structural fidelity relative to fully sampled references and support further evaluation of diagnostic performance, with the potential to improve imaging efficiency and patient experience.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery CT Angiography on Photon-Counting Detector CT: A Practical One-Stop Acquisition, Reconstruction, and Reporting Protocol.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is the first-line test for suspected acute pulmonary embolism (PE), yet respiratory and cardiac motion artifacts, non-diagnostic opacification, subsegmental interpretive uncertainty, contrast medium and radiation dose burdens, and historically variable reporting persist. Photon-counting detector CT (PCCT), together with the newly released Pulmonary Embolism Reporting and Data System (PE-RADS) v2026, creates the opportunity for a standardized one-stop examination. This technical note consolidates the PCCT-CTPA evidence base into a practical acquisition, reconstruction, and reporting protocol. METHODS: The protocol was developed as a narrative, literature-informed synthesis of the PCCT-CTPA evidence base, identified by searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from January 2021 (first clinical PCCT installation) to July 2026; sources included randomized and comparative clinical studies, phantom experiments, and a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis pooling 12 studies and 950 patients. This technical note is not itself a systematic review, and pooled effect sizes are quoted from that existing meta-analysis rather than newly derived.
