RESULTS: The protocol specifies a sub-second (<1 s), free-breathing, dual-source high-pitch acquisition in QuantumPlus multi-energy mode, 25-40 mL of contrast medium as evidence-based example regimens rather than fixed volumes, routine reading on 50-55 keV virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) with 40 keV bolus salvage and 90-120 keV streak suppression, iodine distribution (perfused-blood-volume surrogate) maps from the same scan at no additional dose, an optional ultra-high-resolution (UHR) problem-solving tier that replaces, rather than adds to, the standard acquisition in selected patients, and reporting aligned with PE-RADS v2026 categories, designations, and accessory findings. Effective doses of 1.3-1.4 mSv have been reported for low-dose PCCT protocols (including the free-breathing ultra-high-pitch protocol) under specified conditions; 89% of routine PCCT examinations were entirely artifact-free versus 28.6% on energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT); and iodine maps diagnosed chronic thromboembolism with sensitivity 0.94 and specificity 0.84 at 1.3 mSv. Reported dose and contrast savings are protocol-dependent and did not retain meta-analytic significance after conservative adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: PCCT enables an evidence-supported, PE-RADS-ready one-stop CTPA protocol delivering morphology and iodine-distribution (perfused-blood-volume surrogate) maps in every patient. It complements rather than replaces conventional CTPA, and local validation of dose, contrast use, and reporting outcomes is advised. Whether improved peripheral visibility translates into improved diagnostic accuracy for subsegmental PE remains unproven.

articles.title: MRI Morphometry of the Pediatric Olfactory Bulb and Sulcus: Age-Related Changes and Reference Morphometric Values.
articles.abstract: Background: Reference morphometric data for the olfactory sulcus (OS) and olfactory bulb (OB) in the pediatric population are scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the age-related morphometric characteristics of these structures using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included pediatric patients with normal brain MRI findings. Olfactory bulb diameters and olfactory sulcus depth were measured. Patients were grouped by age, and correlation, group comparison, and regression analyses were performed to evaluate associations with age. Results: A total of 248 children were enrolled. The mean olfactory bulb transverse and craniocaudal diameters were 2.69 ± 0.67 mm and 2.15 ± 0.65 mm on the right and 2.85 ± 0.71 mm and 2.25 ± 0.63 mm on the left, respectively. The mean olfactory sulcus depth was 10.08 ± 1.76 mm on the right and 9.72 ± 1.65 mm on the left. Sulcus depth showed a weak positive correlation with age (right: r = 0.277, p < 0.001; left: r = 0.259, p < 0.001), whereas bulb measurements demonstrated weaker associations (e.g., right bulb craniocaudal diameter: r = 0.153, p = 0.016). Quadratic regression analyses indicated that age significantly predicted sulcus depth (explaining 27.1% and 25.5% of the variance on the right and left sides, respectively, p < 0.001), whereas bulb measurements remained relatively stable. Conclusion: OB dimensions are relatively stable across childhood, whereas OS depth increases with age in the pediatric population. These data provide reference morphometric parameters to support the radiological evaluation of olfactory system development in children.

articles.title: Limitations of clDice for Evaluating Pancreatic Duct Segmentation in CT.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Centerline Dice (clDice) emphasizes skeleton overlap, but a high score does not establish connectivity. This empirical study, which proposes no new metric, measured how often high-scoring pancreatic-duct segmentations on computed tomography (CT) differ from their references in connected-component count, and what changes that frequency. Methods: Dice, clDice and component counts were compared for 235 held-out PANORAMA CT predictions of a public model. The references were algorithm-generated, so a difference shows disagreement, not anatomical correctness. Thresholds, small-component cleanup and skeleton-based counting were varied. Further tests used a second model, known cuts, synthetic tubes and retinal labels. Synthetic-tube radii illustrate the mechanism, not clinical thresholds. Results: Among 81 predictions with both scores above 0.85, 51 (63.0%; 95% CI 52-73%) differed in component count; a second model gave 32 of 55 (58.2%). Among 86 predictions with Dice above 0.85, cleanup alone moved discordant cases between 25 and 60, and skeleton-based counting reclassified seven cases. After one known cut, 194 of 199 references kept both scores above 0.85 despite the break. Conclusions: High clDice does not ensure matching connectivity. Studies should report a direct connectivity measure alongside clDice and state their cleanup and skeletonization conventions, because these conventions alone changed the reported frequency.

articles.title: Prognostic Factors for Progression-Free Survival in Patients with Advanced Gastric Cancer Treated with First-Line Nivolumab Plus Oxaliplatin-Based Chemotherapy: Combined Clinical and Baseline CT Features.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although nivolumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy has been approved as a first-line systemic treatment for advanced gastric cancer (AGC), the pretreatment imaging and clinical factors associated with disease progression remain incompletely understood. METHODS: This retrospective study included 172 patients with AGC who underwent baseline CT and were treated with nivolumab plus chemotherapy. Factors associated with progression-free survival (PFS) were analyzed using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. The performance of the selected variables was evaluated using Harrell's concordance index (C-index) and the time-dependent area under the curve (AUC). RESULTS: Progression or death occurred in 79.1% of patients (136/172). The number of metastatic sites (hazard ratio [HR], 1.60; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.28-1.99; p < 0.001), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) (HR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.29-3.16; p = 0.003), macroscopic tumor morphology (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.00-2.84; p = 0.049), and seeding score (HR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.00-1.36; p = 0.049) were significant prognostic factors for PFS. Together, these four selected variables yielded a C-index of 0.69 (0.64-0.74) and a 12-month time-dependent AUC of 0.73 (0.66-0.81). Median PFS differed significantly between the low- and high-risk groups (9.6 months, 95% CI, 8.0-17.3 vs. 5.2 months, 95% CI, 4.1-6.6; p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Combined clinical and CT imaging features, including the number of metastatic sites and ECOG PS, were independent prognostic factors for PFS in patients with AGC receiving first-line nivolumab plus chemotherapy.

articles.title: 3D M-FFE Sequence for Assessment of Osseous Abnormalities in the Knee.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the potential complementary value of the 3D multi fast field echo (M-FFE) sequence for knee bone assessment at 1.5T MRI, focusing on the visualization of osseous abnormalities and its potential to complement a standard knee MRI protocol. METHODS: A standard knee MRI protocol supplemented with a 3D M-FFE sequence was performed at 1.5T MRI in 49 outpatients. Two observers independently evaluated image quality, visualization of six anatomical knee structures, and osseous abnormalities using a 5-point Likert scale. Intra- and interrater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Cohen's kappa. Eleven examinations were reassessed for intra-rater reliability. Diagnostic confidence with the 3D M-FFE sequence was evaluated. RESULTS: Image quality was consistently high, with sharpness and artifact scores of 4-5 in >95% of examinations, while contrast showed greater variability, and no examinations scored below 3. Osseous abnormalities were identified in 18/49 patients by each observer, with agreement in 12 cases. A total of 28 and 25 abnormalities were identified by the observers, most commonly osteochondral lesions and bone islands. Abnormalities were assigned visualization scores of 4-5. Inter-rater agreement for osseous abnormalities ranged from fair to substantial (kappa = 0.40-0.76), while intra-rater agreement varied from slight to almost perfect depending on anatomical location. Both observers reported increased perceived diagnostic confidence in osseous abnormalities with the addition of the 3D M-FFE sequence. CONCLUSIONS: The 3D M-FFE sequence demonstrated high image quality, robust anatomical visualization, and potential complementary value for osseous assessment at 1.5T MRI. Further studies using an appropriate reference standard are needed to establish diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: In Vitro and in Vivo Characterization of a Miniature Histotripsy Platform Developed for Endoscopic or Laparoscopic Cancer Applications.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Extracorporeal histotripsy is limited by poor acoustic transmission across air-tissue interfaces, restricting broader therapeutic applications. This study evaluates in vitro and in vivo feasibility of a miniature histotripsy device designed for endoscopic and laparoscopic oncology applications. METHODS: A custom-designed 10 mm histotripsy transducer was tested in vitro on MC38 and Neuro2a cells at 160-240 V, with the samples assessed after 1 and 2 minutes of cumulative treatment and compared with untreated controls. Subsequent studies in MC38, Neuro2a, A549, and MDA-MB-231 cells were performed at 240 V for 2 minutes. Cell viability was quantified using trypan blue exclusion assay and flow cytometry with propidium iodide staining. Histotripsy-derived MC38 lysate was used to assess RAW 264.7 macrophage polarization. Preliminary in vivo feasibility was assessed in bilateral MC38 murine tumors at 240 V for up to 90 minutes, with post hoc mean grayscale intensity analysis performed. RESULTS: In vitro studies demonstrated cytotoxic effects in MC38 and Neuro2a cells that varied with driving voltage and treatment duration. Macrophages exposed to histotripsy-derived MC38 lysate exhibited increased M1 polarization (p < .01). Additionally, MDA-MB-231 cells exhibited lower propidium iodide positivity than MC38 and Neuro2a cells (p < .01). Histotripsy-treated regions of MC38 murine tumors demonstrated lower mean grayscale intensity than untreated regions (p < .001). CONCLUSION: These findings support the feasibility of a miniature histotripsy device for tumor cell lysis and pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization in vitro and provide initial in vivo evidence of localized tumor disruption, supporting further investigation for endoscopic and laparoscopic applications.

Leiomyomatosis Peritonealis Disseminata Presenting with Tumor Torsion After Laparoscopic Myomectomy: A Case Report and Focused Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background: Leiomyomatosis peritonealis disseminata (LPD) is a rare benign condition characterized by multiple smooth-muscle nodules throughout the peritoneal cavity. Increasing evidence suggests that uncontained morcellation during laparoscopic myomectomy represents a clinically relevant mechanism of iatrogenic dissemination. Because LPD frequently mimics advanced intra-abdominal malignancy, preoperative diagnosis remains challenging, particularly in emergency settings. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 46-year-old nulligravid woman presenting with progressive abdominal pain, abnormal uterine bleeding, and acute abdominal deterioration thirteen years after laparoscopic myomectomy performed with uncontained power morcellation. Ultrasound and contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a large, complex abdominopelvic mass with multiple associated lesions but failed to determine its precise origin or establish a definitive diagnosis. Emergency exploratory laparotomy revealed torsion of a giant parasitic leiomyoma together with multiple disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatous implants involving the broad ligament, paracolic fat, and paraintestinal peritoneum. Complete surgical excision, including hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and removal of all visible implants, was performed successfully. Histopathological examination confirmed benign LPD without evidence of malignant transformation. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and pelvic magnetic resonance imaging performed one month after surgery showed no residual disease at that time. Conclusions: This case illustrates an delayed presentation 13 years after laparoscopic myomectomy of LPD manifesting as an acute abdomen caused by torsion of a giant parasitic leiomyoma. It highlights the diagnostic limitations of preoperative imaging and the need to consider LPD in women presenting with abdominal masses years after laparoscopic myomectomy. Although the timing and distribution of the lesions are compatible with dissemination following uncontained morcellation, causality cannot be established from this case, and the possible contribution of the coexisting FH-deficient leiomyoma remains uncertain. Long-term postoperative surveillance and meticulous tissue containment techniques during minimally invasive gynecologic surgery remain essential strategies to reduce delayed complications.

articles.title: Eculizumab Therapy in Suspected Late-Onset Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome in an Adult Kidney Transplant Recipient: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, life-threatening, complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) that may occur de novo after kidney transplantation. Because its manifestations overlap with more common causes of allograft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection, diagnosis can be challenging. The disease may progress rapidly, making early clinical suspicion and timely etiologic evaluation essential. Case Presentation: We report a 52-year-old man who developed abrupt, severe graft dysfunction approximately 10 years after ABO-incompatible living-donor kidney transplantation. His serum creatinine had remained approximately 2.0 mg/dL after treatment for suspected chronic active antibody-mediated rejection but increased to 6.57 mg/dL at outpatient follow-up and to 8.47 mg/dL on admission after a recent norovirus infection. Initial evaluation considered common post-transplant causes of graft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection-related injury. However, as renal dysfunction progressed and concurrent anemia and thrombocytopenia became evident, TMA was suspected, and a targeted workup was undertaken. Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, decreased haptoglobin, fragmented red blood cells, and allograft biopsy findings supported TMA. No HLA class I or II antibodies were detected, C4d staining was negative, ADAMTS13 activity was preserved, and testing for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli was negative. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous CFH variant (c.3329G>C, p.Gly1110Ala), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Based on the clinical, hematologic, and histopathologic findings, suspected aHUS was considered the most likely diagnosis. However, ABMR-associated TMA could not be completely excluded. Plasma exchange was complicated by anaphylaxis, and eculizumab was initiated. Hematologic abnormalities subsequently resolved, although renal function did not recover and the patient remained dialysis-dependent. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of considering TMA when graft dysfunction progresses rapidly or remains unexplained, even many years after kidney transplantation. Early recognition of microangiopathic features and prompt evaluation for the underlying etiology are particularly important when complement-mediated aHUS is suspected, because established acute-on-chronic allograft injury may limit renal recovery despite hematologic response to C5 inhibition.

articles.title: Congenital Mesenteric Lymphatic Malformation with Severe Hypertriglyceridemia in Infancy-Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenges.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Mesenteric lymphatic malformations (LMs) are rare congenital anomalies that may involve extensive visceral structures and present significant therapeutic challenges. We report an unusual case of congenital mesenteric LM complicated by recurrent intra-abdominal disease and severe hypertriglyceridemia during infancy. Case Presentation: A female infant with an antenatally diagnosed mesenteric LM underwent surgical excision on the second day of life, with histopathology confirming cystic lymphangioma. Despite surgery and treatment with sirolimus and propranolol, further intra-abdominal cystic lesions were identified. At 10 months, intestinal obstruction required repeat laparotomy, revealing milky peritoneal fluid suggestive of chylous leakage. During a January 2026 admission at 14 months of age, following a recent viral infection (varicella/influenza A), severe hypertriglyceridemia (990 mg/dL) was documented, and sirolimus was withheld following recognition of dyslipidemia because of its known lipid-related adverse effects. Temporary bowel rest, intravenous hydration, a short insulin infusion, and low-fat MCT-based nutritional management were followed by declining triglycerides-391 mg/dL on day 9 and 192 mg/dL on day 15. Conclusions: This case highlights the challenges of managing extensive mesenteric LM and sirolimus-associated hypertriglyceridemia, potentially accompanied by additional precipitating factors. The response cannot be attributed to a single intervention; careful longitudinal metabolic and nutritional monitoring is essential.

articles.title: The Role of SPECT/CT in Localizing Lymphorrhea Following Great Saphenous Vein Harvesting for CABG Surgery: Case Report and Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Postoperative lymphorrhea is an uncommon complication of great saphenous vein harvesting for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and accurate localization of the leakage site may be challenging. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 79-year-old man who developed persistent lymphorrhea following great saphenous vein harvesting for CABG. Notably, a Pseudomonas aeruginosa surgical site infection preceded the clinically apparent lymphatic leakage and required surgical wound debridement. Following the onset of lymphorrhea, compression therapy was applied for two weeks, accompanied by frequent dressing changes, without improvement. Due to persistent lymphatic leakage, planar lymphoscintigraphy using 99mTc-nanocolloid was performed, demonstrating active lymphatic leakage. Subsequent hybrid single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) localized the suspected region approximately 3.5 cm above the medial femoral condyle, providing anatomical information that guided targeted suture ligation. Conclusions: External lymphorrhea ceased immediately following the intervention and the patient was discharged the following day in good clinical condition, with instructions to wear compression stockings. We also reviewed the relevant English-language literature on this topic.

articles.title: Silent but Aggressive: A Case of Cervical Large-Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma with Repeatedly Normal Cytology in a 22-Year-Old Postpartum Patient.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix (NECC) is a rare, aggressive variant of cervical cancer (approximately 1-1.5% of cases), and large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is an even rarer subtype. Diagnosis is often delayed because symptoms are non-specific and cytology may fail to detect the disease. We report this case to highlight the diagnostic challenge posed by LCNEC in a young patient with repeatedly normal cytology. Methods: We describe the diagnostic work-up and multimodal management of a 22-year-old woman who presented with post-coital bleeding nine months after her second full-term vaginal delivery. Results: Two Babeș-Papanicolaou smears obtained three months apart were negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. Persistent bleeding prompted a loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP), which revealed a poorly differentiated (high-grade) LCNEC. Clinical examination and MRI showed proximal parametrial involvement and a left external iliac lymph node metastasis (FIGO 2018 stage IIIC1r, cT2bN1M0). The patient received definitive chemoradiotherapy (external beam radiotherapy with a simultaneous integrated boost and high-dose-rate brachytherapy) with six cycles of platinum-etoposide chemotherapy (two concurrent, four adjuvant), achieving a complete response with no evidence of disease approximately three years after treatment. Conclusions: This report illustrates that cytology can be repeatedly negative in NECC and that persistent symptoms or a visible cervical lesion warrant histological evaluation. Given its aggressive clinical course, LCNEC requires the rapid initiation of combined local and systemic therapy.

articles.title: Massive Transfusion-Associated Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome After Liver Transplantation: A Case Report and Retrospective Estimate of the Sodium Load.
articles.abstract: A 67-year-old woman with acute-on-chronic liver failure and profound preoperative hyponatraemia (central-laboratory serum sodium 116 mmol/L preoperatively; 120.3 mmol/L on the first intraoperative blood gas) underwent emergency living-donor liver transplantation complicated by an estimated blood loss of 6200 mL. Resuscitation comprised 20 units of packed red blood cells (PRBC), 12 units of fresh frozen plasma (FFP), 34 units of cryoprecipitate, three units of apheresis platelets, approximately 7.7 L of crystalloid and albumin, 60 mL of 7% sodium bicarbonate and 70 mEq of potassium chloride, with no hypertonic saline. Serum sodium measured on the operating-room blood gas analyser rose from 120.3 to 132.5 mmol/L over 7 h (+12.2 mmol/L), and by 18 mmol/L between the preoperative central-laboratory value and arrival in the intensive care unit, exceeding the 8-10 mmol/L per 24 h limit recommended by the European Renal Best Practice guideline. She developed dysarthria and dysphagia after extubation on postoperative day (POD) 6 and severe tetraparesis with decreased consciousness on POD 7. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on POD 7 (rapid protocol) reported no pontine lesion, whereas MRI on POD 19 showed T2 hyperintensity in the central pons and both thalami, consistent with osmotic demyelination syndrome with extrapontine involvement. A simple pooled Adrogué-Madias calculation, with its assumptions stated, estimated the sodium contributed by the infused products at roughly +10 to +17 mmol/L, the same order of magnitude as the observed rise. This case illustrates that blood products, isotonic crystalloids and sodium bicarbonate together can deliver a substantial sodium load during massive transfusion, that the load can be estimated approximately, and that an early MRI without a reported pontine lesion does not exclude osmotic demyelination.

articles.title: Hepatic Hydatid Cyst with Rupture into the Biliary Tract: Diagnostic Challenges and Combined Endoscopic-Laparoscopic Management.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Intrabiliary rupture is one of the most frequent complications of hepatic hydatid disease and may lead to cholangitis, obstructive jaundice, and, rarely, anaphylaxis. Case Presentation: We report a 52-year-old man in whom a hepatic cystic lesion of probable parasitic origin was discovered incidentally in 2023; he received albendazole for three months but declined surgery. Two and a half years later he presented with abdominal pain and cholestasis, two days after an episode of near-syncope. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a multivesicular, partially calcified hydatid cyst with an ill-defined wall segment and left intrahepatic bile duct dilation, suggesting rupture with biliary communication; ELISA was positive. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with sphincterotomy was performed first, followed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy, cyst evacuation with hypertonic saline inactivation, partial pericystectomy, and drainage, under albendazole therapy. Histopathology confirmed hepatic echinococcosis. A persistent low-output biliary fistula, due to communication between the cyst and the left hepatic duct, required a second ERCP with two plastic biliary stents, removed four months after surgery without incident; the evolution was favorable. Conclusions: Combined endoscopic-laparoscopic management is feasible but may require staged re-intervention, and a presyncopal episode in a patient with known hydatid disease should raise suspicion of cyst rupture.

articles.title: CBCT-Guided Diagnosis and Conservative Nonsurgical Management of a Trauma-Associated Non-Perforating Internal Root Resorption: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Internal root resorption (IRR) is an uncommon destructive process that may compromise tooth structure, particularly after dental trauma. This case report describes cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-guided diagnosis and nonsurgical management of a non-perforating internal resorptive defect in a maxillary central incisor. Case Presentation: A 33-year-old man with childhood trauma and discoloration of the maxillary left central incisor underwent clinical examination, periapical radiography, and CBCT assessment. CBCT demonstrated an internal defect in the cervical and middle thirds, marked circumferential dentin-wall thinning, no detectable external communication, and a periapical radiolucency. The tooth was treated with conservative preparation, supplementary XP-endo instrumentation, activated irrigation, a two-week calcium hydroxide dressing, and warm vertical compaction with a bioceramic sealer, followed by direct composite restoration without an intracanal post. Discussion: CBCT supported differentiation of IRR from external cervical resorption by demonstrating a canal-centered defect without detectable communication with the external root surface. These CBCT findings informed conservative nonsurgical treatment and highlighted the associated structural risk. Post-space preparation was avoided to preserve the thinned radicular dentin, as clinical assessment confirmed sufficient coronal tooth structure to retain a direct composite restoration. At 12 months, the patient was asymptomatic with periapical healing on periapical radiography and CBCT; at 18 months, the tooth remained asymptomatic and the periapical radiolucency had resolved radiographically. Conclusions: In this patient, CBCT-informed diagnosis and conservative management were associated with favorable clinical and radiographic findings at 18 months. Continued clinical monitoring and appropriately justified radiographic assessment are required because short-term healing does not establish long-term structural survival.

articles.title: Polypoid Colonic Leiomyosarcoma with Occult Regional Lymph Node Metastasis: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Primary colonic leiomyosarcoma (LMS) is rare, and regional nodal involvement can be clinically occult. We describe nodal metastasis from a small polypoid lesion and review relevant colorectal cases. Case Presentation: A 61-year-old man underwent endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) of a 30-mm ulcerated lesion at the hepatic flexure following a positive fecal occult blood test. Histology showed an atypical spindle-cell tumor involving the submucosa, approximately 30 mitoses per 10 high-power fields, and a Ki-67 index of approximately 50%. Tumor cells expressed desmin and were negative for DOG1, CD34, and S-100. The deep margin was involved. Abdominal computed tomography showed no enlarged nodes. Right hemicolectomy 18 days later showed no residual malignancy in the bowel but metastatic LMS in 1 of 44 lymph nodes. The nodal deposit showed a concordant desmin-positive, DOG1-negative phenotype. Discussion: The paired specimens document nodal involvement despite apparent local clearance and no radiological lymphadenopathy. The nodal deposit retained the desmin-positive smooth muscle phenotype of the primary and lay at the periphery of the node, indicating that regional spread occurred without overt loss of differentiation. The route and timing of spread could not be determined, and the positive deep margin precluded assessment of the original depth of invasion. Conclusions: Regional nodal disease can accompany a small polypoid colonic LMS. Following unexpected LMS diagnosis on EMR, staging and further surgery, including the extent of regional nodal assessment, should be discussed by a multidisciplinary sarcoma team.

articles.title: Linear IgA Disease with Oral and Laryngeal Mucosal Involvement in an Elderly Denture Wearer: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Linear IgA disease (LAD) is a rare autoimmune subepithelial blistering disorder characterized by linear IgA deposition along the basement membrane zone (BMZ). Oral and laryngeal involvement is exceptionally rare and can mimic other autoimmune blistering diseases. We report such a case and review previously published cases. Case Presentation: An 85-year-old denture-wearing woman with ulcerative colitis (UC) and chronic oral erosions since 2019 underwent clinical, histopathological, immunofluorescence, and serological evaluations, as well as laryngoscopy. Medication exposure and denture-related injury were reviewed as possible triggers. Previously diagnosed as oral lichen planus (OLP) and bullous pemphigoid (BP), the lesions showed strong linear IgA (3+) and moderate C3 (2+) deposition along the BMZ on direct immunofluorescence (DIF); serological tests for pemphigoid and pemphigus antigens were negative. Laryngoscopy revealed edema, fibrinous deposits, and early scarring. After drug-related and denture-related causes were considered unlikely, a clinicopathologic diagnosis of mucosal-predominant LAD was made; because salt-split skin indirect immunofluorescence (IIF) and antigen-specific testing were unavailable, IgA-predominant mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) could not be completely excluded. Dapsone produced marked improvement but was discontinued because of severe hemolytic anemia; laryngeal edema later caused respiratory insufficiency. A structured literature review of English-language reports published since 2016 identified three previously reported cases of LAD limited to the oral mucosa. No prior case with simultaneous oral and laryngeal involvement without skin disease was identified, although one report described LAD confined to the hypopharyngeal and laryngeal mucosa. Conclusions: DIF is essential for diagnosis, LAD must be distinguished from IgA-predominant MMP, and laryngeal involvement requires early recognition. Because linear IgA deposition in adults may be reactive, drug-induced and denture-related injury should be excluded, and dapsone toxicity monitored.

articles.title: Intradermal Hyaluronic Acid Deposits in the Chin and Lower Eyelid: A High-Frequency Ultrasound Case Series.
articles.abstract: This retrospective, descriptive case series reports 10 nonconsecutive patients presenting with delayed-onset clinical changes in the chin and/or lower eyelids following hyaluronic acid (HA) filler injections. Intradermal pseudocystic deposits were identified, a pattern first recognized in our clinical practice following the introduction of a 33-MHz transducer. All 10 patients were examined using both 24- and 33-MHz transducers to characterize the deposits and their anatomical relationships, with clearer delineation at 33 MHz. The deposits followed the orientation of mentalis or orbicularis oculi fibers and their cutaneous or fibrous attachments. Patients reported that their complaints first arose years after HA filler injection. The intradermal deposits corresponded to the sites of the reported complaints, and high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) revealed no other findings that could account for them. The late onset of complaints and the recurring anatomical distribution of the deposits raise the possibility of superficial filler redistribution, potentially influenced by repetitive muscle contraction, muscle-skin coupling, and shear forces. However, without immediate post-injection or interval ultrasound examinations, neither the initial location of the filler nor whether or when it redistributed could be established.

articles.title: Comment on Bulbul, C.B.; Yakistiran, B. First Trimester Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Lipid Profile as Predictive Factors in the Diagnosis of Late-Onset Preeclampsia: Can We Prevent It? Diagnostics 2025, 15, 3141.
articles.abstract: This comment addresses methodological and interpretive limitations in Bulbul and Yakistiran's study of first-trimester triglyceride-glucose index and lipid parameters as predictors of late-onset preeclampsia. Although the topic is clinically relevant, largely unadjusted analyses, unvalidated ROC-derived cut-offs, incomplete precision reporting, possible multiple-comparison issues, and ambiguity between disease-onset and delivery timing limit the strength of the conclusions. The findings should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than clinically actionable, pending prospective validation in adequately powered cohorts.
